title: [ROCm][Bugfix][Spec Decode] Add compact_topk_indices to the ROCm DSA MTP drafter
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm, MTP speculative decoding crashes for every GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3 checkpoint on
current `main`, out of the box:

```bash
vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 -tp 4 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}'
```

```
File "vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py", line 613, in propose
    self.model.model.compact_topk_indices(token_indices_to_sample)
AttributeError: 'DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor' object has no attribute
'compact_topk_indices'
```

The engine starts, and the first draft step fails on every TP worker.

### Cause

GLM-5.x checkpoints set `index_share_for_mtp_iteration: true`. With that set, the legacy
proposer checks the drafter for `set_skip_topk` and then calls both methods:

```python
if self._share_mtp_indices and hasattr(self.model.model, "set_skip_topk"):
    self.model.model.set_skip_topk(True)
    self.model.model.compact_topk_indices(token_indices_to_sample)
```

On ROCm, `deepseek_v32` and `glm_moe_dsa` are dispatched to
`vllm/models/deepseek_v32/amd/` (#51915). That module's `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor`
implements `set_skip_topk` but not `compact_topk_indices`, which #47238 added only to the
generic drafter in `deepseek_mtp.py`. It is the only drafter on `main` with one method and
not the other. The generic, NVIDIA DSA, GLM-5-Next, HY-V4 and both Qwen4-Exp drafters
have both.

### Change

- `amd/mtp.py`: add `compact_topk_indices` to `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictor`. It
  follows the amd drafter's own layout: `topk_indices_buffer` lives on `self_attn`
  itself, where `set_skip_topk` already looks for `skip_topk`, not under
  `self_attn.mla_attn`. Copying the generic method body would find no buffer. It would
  silently leave the buffer uncompacted, and steps 1+ would reuse the wrong rows instead
  of crashing.
- `llm_base_proposer.py`: decide index sharing once, after the draft model is loaded, and
  require both methods. This is what the V2 MTP speculator already does
  (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/mtp/speculator.py`). A future drafter with only
  `set_skip_topk` then falls back to not sharing instead of crashing.

Every other drafter on `main` has both methods, so their behaviour does not change. Until
this lands, `"index_share_for_mtp_iteration": false` in `--speculative-config` avoids the
crash on `main`.

### Affected checkpoints

Each checkpoint's real `config.json` was resolved through the draft-model registry on both
`main` and this branch. Each one then ran on ROCm with its architecture truncated and
dummy weights.

| checkpoint | `model_type` | drafter on ROCm | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3 (fp8), GLM-5.3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8, GLM-5.2-FP8, GLM-5.2-MXFP4 | `glm_moe_dsa` | `deepseek_v32/amd/mtp.py` | `AttributeError` on the first draft step | runs, index sharing on |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 | `deepseek_v32` | `deepseek_v32/amd/mtp.py` | runs, no sharing (config does not ask) | same |
| GLM-5.3-Flash | `glm5_next` | V2 model runner's MTP speculator | runs | same — never reaches this proposer |

GLM-5.3-BF16 has the same config as GLM-5.3 and was not run separately. The other
first-tier checkpoints (DeepSeek-V4 line, Kimi, MiniMax, Qwen, gpt-oss, gemma-4, Llama)
have no DSA indexer or no MTP drafter, and they resolve identically on both trees.

Two open PRs touch the same file, and both are in different hunks: #55081 edits the
`DeepseekV32MTP` wrapper, and #53953 edits `DeepseekV32MultiTokenPredictorLayer`. Neither
adds this method.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/models/deepseek_v32/test_amd_mtp.py   # ROCm only; skipped elsewhere
```

The new tests build the amd predictor with real `topk_indices_buffer` tensors. They check
that `compact_topk_indices` gathers the requested rows to the front, leaves the rest
alone, covers every MTP layer, and compacts identically to the generic drafter given the
same buffer and slots.

End to end: GLM-5.3 (official fp8 weights), TP=4, `num_speculative_tokens=3`. The baseline
is `main` with `"index_share_for_mtp_iteration": false`, because that is the only way it
runs on `main`. It is compared against this PR with the checkpoint's own setting, using
GSM8K (`lm_eval`, 5-shot, all 1319 items) and `vllm bench serve` with a fresh server per
run.

## Test Result

MI355X (gfx950), ROCm, against `main@94f4170df3`.

### The crash is fixed

GLM-5.3 (official fp8 weights), TP=4: on `main`, the first draft step fails on all four TP
workers with the `AttributeError` above. The same happens for the other three
`glm_moe_dsa` checkpoints in the table. With this PR every one of them runs, with
`compact_topk_indices` and `set_skip_topk(True)` called on every draft step.

Each unit test was run against three trees, to show that the assertions discriminate
rather than merely pass:

| tree | result |
|---|---|
| `main` | 4 failed — the method does not exist |
| the generic drafter's body copied in (`self_attn.mla_attn` path) | 3 failed, 1 passed — the method exists but compacts nothing |
| this PR | 4 passed |

These were run from a directory outside the repository, with the imported module's
`__file__` checked for each tree.

### No accuracy or performance regression

GLM-5.3 (official fp8), TP=4, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, this PR against the `main`
workaround:

| | `main`, sharing off | this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| GSM8K strict-match | 0.9181 (repeat: 0.9196) | 0.9174 | within the base-repeat drift |
| Total tok/s | 2673.1 | 2676.5 | +0.1 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 63.79 | 64.04 | +0.4 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 369.6 | 370.5 | +0.2 % |

All three bench metrics are inside their own within-arm spread. On the drafter alone,
`propose()` time does not move beyond the spread between two identical baseline runs at
`num_speculative_tokens` 1, 2 and 3, for context up to 97k and batch up to 83. So index
sharing costs nothing measurable, and it gives no speedup either. Full tables and per-sample
GSM8K agreement are in the comment below.

---

Found by [Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom); reviewed and measured by hand.

title: [Feature] Add fixed-token prefill scoring
body:
## Summary

This PR adds request-wise fixed-token prefill logprob scoring for OPD / top-k distillation:

- `SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_token_ids`: candidate token IDs to score.
- `SamplingParams.prompt_logprob_start`: absolute first causal prompt row to score.

The result is returned through the existing engine-core and `RequestOutput` paths for the V2 GPU runner.

This is M1 of RFC #56860. Per-position candidate lists (M2) are tracked there.

## Design

For a prompt of length `C` followed by student-generated output tokens, the hidden state at row `i` predicts token `i + 1`. Therefore the first output token is predicted by row `C - 1`. An OPD request sets:

```python
prompt_logprob_token_ids=teacher_topk_union
prompt_logprob_start=C - 1
```

This returns exactly the student probabilities needed for the output suffix. It does not score the earlier context rows. The dedicated result is source-row aligned and contains only requested rows; unlike `prompt_logprobs`, it does not add a leading `None` sentinel.

The candidate IDs are request-wise and fixed across positions, matching M1 of #56860. For each scheduled prefill chunk, the runner converts the absolute start into the chunk-relative row range, runs the lm-head only on that range, and gathers the requested IDs. The worker keeps one `[num_scored_rows, num_ids]` buffer per request, allocated on the first prefill chunk and written in place chunk by chunk, and emits it on the last chunk. Nothing is concatenated, and a request whose start is past the last scorable row emits an empty buffer rather than nothing.

This bounds intermediate memory by the requested suffix and candidate width rather than the full prompt. With `prompt_logprob_start=C-1`, the retained result is proportional to the generated output length. The implementation intentionally keeps the existing chunking and output plumbing instead of adding a new sparse protocol.

### Scoring reuses the sampler's kernel

Scoring calls the existing `compute_token_logprobs()` rather than computing `gather - logsumexp` in the logits' own dtype. That kernel already does exactly this gather: it accumulates max and logsumexp in fp32 and emits only the requested columns, so it materializes no `[tokens, vocab]` tensor either.

The kernel indexed `token_ids` as contiguous rows. It now takes a row stride for `token_ids`, as it already did for `logits`, so the request-wise IDs are passed as a broadcast `[rows, num_ids]` view (stride 0) and are never copied out per row. Existing callers pass contiguous tensors and are unaffected.

This matters numerically. Reducing over a 151936-entry bfloat16 vocabulary loses about 1e-1 of accuracy; against vLLM's own `prompt_logprobs` on the same forward pass, an in-dtype reduction disagreed by up to 7.78e-02. Through the shared kernel the values are bit-identical to `prompt_logprobs` (see Verification).

## Naming

The request-side parameters follow the existing `logprobs` / `prompt_logprobs` prefix convention: `SamplingParams.logprob_token_ids` already exists on main (#43463) and scores caller-supplied token IDs at sampled positions, so `prompt_logprob_token_ids` is its prefill counterpart.

The result is named after that parameter: `RequestOutput.prompt_token_id_logprobs`, a plain `[num_scored_rows, len(prompt_logprob_token_ids)]` float32 array whose columns follow the order the IDs were requested in. The IDs are not echoed back: the caller supplied them, so a container pairing them with the scores would carry nothing the caller does not already have, and nothing between the worker and the output needs them either.

Returning `list[dict[int, float]]` instead would cost ~22 MB of Python objects for a 1000-row, 242-ID request against ~1 MB for the array, and callers doing top-k distillation want the array rather than dicts they have to re-flatten.

## Token-in/token-out HTTP and the Rust frontend

`/inference/v1/generate` takes raw `SamplingParams`, so it accepts both parameters; the non-streaming response returns the scores as `prompt_token_id_logprobs`, a base64 `.npy` float32 array (`np.load(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(s)))`), the encoding `routed_experts` already uses on this endpoint. Streaming follows `prompt_logprobs`: the Python frontend omits the field, the Rust frontend rejects the request.

`EngineCoreOutput` is `array_like` on the Python side and decoded positionally by the Rust engine-core client (`Deserialize_tuple`), so the field is appended last there too, kept as the wire ndarray with its aux frame resolved in place; the server writes its float32 bytes straight into the `.npy`. The Rust frontend forwards `prompt_logprob_token_ids` / `prompt_logprob_start` and, since it bypasses `InputProcessor`, checks the candidate count against `max_logprobs` and the ids against the vocabulary, as it does for `logprob_token_ids`. Its `.npy` encoder is byte-identical to `numpy2base64`. OpenAI routes are unchanged.

## Limits

The candidate count is bounded by the existing `max_logprobs` (`--max-logprobs`, default 20), not by a new constant. One logprob per requested ID is returned per scored row, which is exactly the quantity that setting already bounds for `logprobs` and `prompt_logprobs`, and `-1` opens it to the whole vocabulary here too. A distillation workload wanting a few hundred candidates therefore needs the operator to raise `--max-logprobs`, the same opt-in the existing full-vocabulary path requires.

Because the default rejects any realistic candidate set, this is the first error most callers of the parameter will meet, so it names the value to set rather than just the setting:

```
Requested prompt_logprob_token_ids of length 242, which is greater than
max allowed: 20. Set max_logprobs (--max-logprobs) to at least 242.
```

Both spellings appear because `--max-logprobs` is not what a caller using `LLM(...)` sets. The sibling errors in `_validate_logprobs` carry no such hint; the asymmetry is deliberate, and easy to drop if reviewers would rather keep them uniform.

The parameter is implemented for the V2 GPU runner only, so the input processor rejects it with a `VLLMValidationError` naming `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` when that runner is not in use, rather than letting the V1 runner return `None`. `prompt_logprob_start` without `prompt_logprob_token_ids` is likewise rejected instead of being silently ignored.

`logprob_token_ids` keeps its own `MAX_LOGPROB_TOKEN_IDS = 128` because that number is physical: it is the row width `LogprobTokenIdsState` preallocates. Prompt scoring allocates per request, so it has no such structural bound and does not need a constant of its own.

On the output path the result is owned by `LogprobsProcessor` alongside sample and prompt logprobs, and reached through the same single `update_from_output` call. That also gives it the same `RequestOutputKind.DELTA` handling: like prompt logprobs it is popped, so a streaming request carries it on exactly one output at the end of prefill instead of re-attaching the array to every later delta.

It is kept out of `prompt_logprobs_dict` deliberately: `LogprobsTensors` carries an implicit target-token column and a rank column, neither of which is meaningful for a caller-fixed ID set, and `prompt_logprobs` prepends a `None` sentinel for position 0 that this result must not have. Reusing that container would mean populating two columns with placeholder values and then documenting that they are meaningless.

## Relationship to SGLang

SGLang main uses the same two concepts: request-wise `token_ids_logprob` and an absolute `logprob_start_len`. Its scheduler converts the absolute position to a per-chunk pruned range, and its logits processor applies the lm-head only to suffix hidden states. This V2 implementation follows that lifecycle and offset model while reusing vLLM's existing chunk helper and logprob kernel.

SGLang main does not currently expose a per-position candidate-ID API; this PR therefore does not add one. Per-position candidates are proposed as M2 in #56860.

## Scope / non-goals

This is M1 of #56860. It does not add per-position candidate lists (M2 in #56860), streaming updates, a scoring-only lifecycle, speculative/beam support, multimodal scoring, prefix-cache reads, or an OpenAI protocol field. Those can be evaluated separately if a concrete caller requires them.

This is complementary to open PR #39351 (generative scoring with `max_tokens=0`, which targets next-token scoring) and #49171 (skipping logits for unfinished chunk prefills). This PR scores arbitrary fixed IDs at selected prefill positions. No other open PR adds fixed-ID prefill scoring.

## Verification

All runs used the vLLM nightly container (`0.28.1rc1.dev388+g8a728663c`) on 4x GB200, with this branch's Python layer overlaid on the image's compiled package. Performance runs used a dedicated node with the checkpoint staged in `/dev/shm`.

### Correctness

`Qwen3-0.6B`, 193-token prompt (`193 % 64 == 1`, so the final prefill chunk holds a single token), 10 checks, all passing:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Chunked prefill (64 tokens/chunk) row count vs unchunked | identical |
| Chunked values vs unchunked | max abs diff `0.00e+00` |
| Values vs vLLM's own `prompt_logprobs=-1`, same request | max abs diff `0.00e+00` |
| Full-vocab `prompt_logprobs=-1` row normalizes | logsumexp over 151936 entries = `+1.24e-07` |
| Row alignment (scan row offsets -2..+2 against HF) | offset 0 median `0.051`; ±1 median `2.43` / `2.43` |
| Result shape / dtype | `(92, 7)` float32 |
| vs HuggingFace `log_softmax` reference | median `5.12e-02` |

The last row needs a control, since vLLM and HuggingFace disagree on this model regardless of this feature. Running vLLM's own `prompt_logprobs` against the same HF reference on the same prompt gives median `4.95e-02`. The residual is the pre-existing vLLM-vs-HF gap (TRTLLM attention, bfloat16), not this path: the two agree to within 3%.

Row alignment is worth calling out separately: a ±1 row shift would still look plausible on a single-number comparison, but scanning offsets shows offset 0 fitting 47x better than its neighbours.

### Preemption

Preemption in the middle of a chunked prefill needs no special handling: the V2 scheduler reports a resumed request as a new one, and the runner drops the worker's state on preemption (`finish_requests` runs before `add_requests`), so the partial buffer is discarded and the re-prefill rebuilds it from the first chunk and emits it once. A resumed request whose prefill had already completed is the case that does need a guard:

A request resumed after preemption re-prefills its prompt plus the tokens it already generated. Those rows are not prompt positions, and its scores were emitted before the preemption, so the accumulator has to skip the resumed prefill — the same condition `compute_prompt_logprobs` already guards with `prompt_lens < prefill_len`. An earlier revision of this PR did not, which is not a silent numerical error: the resumed request emits a result on a step that must produce none, and the engine dies on the scheduler's own invariant.

```
File "vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py", line 2131, in update_from_output
    assert not prompt_token_id_logprobs
AssertionError
```

`test_prompt_logprob_token_ids_with_chunking_and_preemption` is added to `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py`, next to the existing prompt-logprobs preemption test and reusing its setup for forcing chunking and preemption. Verified as a regression test in both directions: it fails with the above assertion against the pre-fix code and passes with the guard in place.

### Performance

`Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507`, TP4, 8192-token context, median of 5 reps, `prompt_logprob_start` set to score the last N rows:

| Scored rows x candidate IDs | median | vs baseline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline (no scoring) | 75.2 ms | — |
| 1000 x 64 | 77.1 ms | +2.0 ms |
| 1000 x 242 | 77.7 ms | +2.6 ms |
| 1000 x 1024 | 80.6 ms | +5.5 ms |
| 4000 x 64 | 80.7 ms | +5.6 ms |
| 4000 x 242 | 81.7 ms | +6.6 ms |
| 4000 x 1024 | 88.9 ms | +13.7 ms |
| `prompt_logprobs=0`, all 8192 rows | 146.2 ms | +71.0 ms |

Row count dominates: at a fixed 64 IDs, going 1000 -> 4000 rows costs +3.6 ms, while at 1000 rows a 16x increase in candidates (64 -> 1024) costs +3.5 ms. In the intended distillation range the feature is roughly 10x cheaper than the existing full-row path while returning far more per row.

Cost grows with `rows x ids`, and at a wide candidate set it crosses over (separate run, baseline 76.6 ms):

| Scored rows x candidate IDs | median | vs baseline |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4000 x 1024 | 89.6 ms | +13.0 ms |
| 4000 x 4096 | 108.4 ms | +31.7 ms |
| 4000 x 16384 | 176.0 ms | +99.4 ms |
| `prompt_logprobs=0`, all 8192 rows | 146.1 ms | +69.5 ms |

So 16384 candidates over 4000 rows costs more than scoring every row with `prompt_logprobs=0` — though it returns 16384 candidates per row rather than one target token. The crossover is around 40M `row x id` pairs; beyond that, callers should compare against the full-row path. This is another reason the ceiling is `max_logprobs` rather than a constant of our own: the operator who opens that gate is the one accepting the cost.

### Commands

```bash
# correctness (11 checks) and the two sweeps above
MODEL=/models/Qwen3-0.6B ./_bench/run.sh test_correctness.py
MODEL=/models/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 TP=4 CONTEXT=8192 ./_bench/run.sh test_perf.py

# upstream tests covering the changed kernel and the preemption path
pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_prompt_logprob_token_ids_with_chunking_and_preemption \
          tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py::test_prompt_logprobs_with_chunking_and_preemption
# -> 2 passed in 79.69s   (1 failed against the pre-fix code, as above)

pytest -q tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py
# -> 3 passed in 1.12s    (adds the DELTA pop test)

pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k "logprob_token_ids"
# -> 6 passed in 5.22s    (adds the max_logprobs ceiling test, which also
#    pins that the message names the value to raise the setting to)

cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client
# -> 102 passed, including python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding, which
#    round-trips fixtures generated from the current Python definitions
cargo fmt --check   # clean

pre-commit run   # ruff, ruff-format, mypy-3.10, SPDX, forbidden-imports: all pass
```

AI assistance was used for this change. The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and reran the tests above.

## Update 2026-09-17: re-verification after merging main, Rust e2e, audit fixes

Re-run on the merge commit with the `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` container of 2026-09-15 (`0.29.1rc1.dev47+gdc36fcce9`), this branch's Python overlaid, GB200.

- `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k prompt_logprob_token_ids`: 3 passed. The chunked-prefill/preemption test now also compares its scores against an unchunked, unpreempted run of the same requests (`rtol=0.1`: batch composition moves bf16 tail logprobs by ~2%, a misaligned row differs by nats). `tests/v1/engine/test_logprobs_processor.py`: passes.
- Correctness script: 10/10 (chunked vs unchunked `0.00e+00`, vs `prompt_logprobs=-1` `0.00e+00`, row-offset scan picks 0).
- Perf (same setup as above, baseline 77.2 ms): 1000×64 +0.9, 1000×242 +1.6, 1000×1024 +3.9, 4000×64 +4.4, 4000×242 +5.6, 4000×1024 +11.3 ms; `prompt_logprobs=0` all rows +73 ms.
- **Cost with the feature off**: every per-step touchpoint mirrors the existing `prompt_logprobs_dict` one beside it (an unconditional worker call that returns on an empty dict, one dict comprehension over an empty dict, one `dict.get` per request in the scheduler, a trailing `None` field that `omit_defaults` drops from the wire). Measured A/B on one GB200, Qwen3-0.6B, 256 requests × 256 greedy decode steps, no scoring params, merge base vs this branch, two alternating rounds: 4.059 / 4.121 ms per step (base) vs 4.138 / 4.094 ms per step (branch); the round-to-round drift (1.5%) is larger than the A/B difference in either direction.
- **Rust frontend e2e** (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`, `vllm-rs` built from this branch, Qwen3-0.6B, chunked prefill at 64 tokens): the same `vllm serve` config brought up with the Python and the Rust frontend agrees on greedy completions, `echo` logprobs (the lm_eval/CI path) and `prompt_logprobs`, and a 32-request concurrent burst matches sequential greedy; 17/17. `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client`: 113 passed. The binary has to come from this branch: the Rust client decodes `EngineCoreOutput` positionally with a fixed length, so a `vllm-rs` built before this PR rejects the appended field (`array had incorrect length, expected 17`).

**Audit fixes** (Codex, read-only, on the diff). Two configurations let a prefill skip prompt rows that must be scored, which would have emitted uninitialized rows; one is rejected here, the other is fixed for `prompt_logprobs` too. An explicit `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False` is left to the caller, as it is for `prompt_logprobs`:

1. A KV connector prefix hit: `skip_reading_prefix_cache` gated only the local prefix cache, so a remote hit (NIXL, LMCache, Mooncake, MoRIIO) skipped rows for `prompt_logprobs` as much as for this feature. Split out as #57269, which makes the scheduler discard the hit for such requests; this PR depends on it and no longer carries that change itself.
2. `--kv-sharing-fast-prefill` (Gemma3n) leaves non-sampled rows without the cross-decoder; rejected, as `prompt_logprobs` already is in `AsyncLLM`, but in `InputProcessor` so both engines agree.

Not changed: with `n > 1` every child scores the prompt and, in DELTA mode, each child's first output carries the matrix, exactly as `prompt_logprobs` behaves today.

## Update 2026-09-20: partially scored prefills

A second review found that a prefill can begin past `prompt_logprob_start`, leaving the leading rows of the score buffer unwritten while the buffer is still emitted at its full shape. Two ways in: a caller passing `skip_reading_prefix_cache=False` explicitly (the force-set in `__post_init__` only applies when the flag is left `None`), and a streaming-input session, which extends its prompt in place and keeps its computed tokens, so the next prefill starts mid-prompt with `prefill_len == prompt_len`.

`prompt_logprobs` degrades on the same paths by returning fewer entries. This path was worse: the shape stayed correct and the leading rows carried uninitialized device memory. With the guard removed, the new regression test shows what a caller would have received:

```
array([[ 1.84094184e-40,  0.00000000e+00,  1.85467457e-40],
       [ 0.00000000e+00,  1.87048122e-40,  0.00000000e+00], ...
       [-2.19386425e+01, -2.27218456e+01, -2.54796581e+01]], dtype=float32)
```

The leading rows are denormals rather than log probabilities, and `exp` maps them to ~1.0 — the worst direction for a distillation target.

The worker now drops a request whose first scoring chunk starts past its first scored row (`chunk_start > req.start`), so the caller gets no scores rather than fabricated ones. This covers both entry points without an admission gate, and the condition is exact: a chunk starting before the first scored row still writes every scored row and is emitted as before.

Also in this update: `trace_decode_token_ids` rejects `prompt_logprob_token_ids` as it already rejects `prompt_logprobs`, and the row convention (row i predicts prompt token i+1, last prompt row excluded, result shape) is stated on the parameter and the result instead of only in the tests.

Verification: `tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py -k prompt_logprob_token_ids` 4 passed, correctness 10/10 on the same GB200 setup. The new test is a real regression test: with the guard removed it fails with the array above.

## Update 2026-09-21: `/inference/v1/generate`, Python and Rust

Before this update the endpoint accepted the parameters, scored the prompt, and dropped the result: `GenerateResponse` had no field for it, and the Rust frontend silently discarded the parameters. Both frontends now return it (see "Token-in/token-out HTTP and the Rust frontend" above).

Verification (GB200, nightly container with this branch overlaid, Qwen3-0.6B, `vllm-rs` built from this branch):

- New `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py::test_generate_prompt_token_id_logprobs`: posts to `/inference/v1/generate` with `prompt_logprob_token_ids`, `prompt_logprob_start=1` and `prompt_logprobs=0`, decodes the `.npy`, checks the shape and that each target token's score matches `prompt_logprobs` from the same response. Passes with the Python frontend and with the Rust frontend; fails with a `vllm-rs` built from the previous head of this branch (same container, same engine), so the Rust change is what makes it pass.
- Whole file, Python frontend: 12 passed, 1 error (`test_generate_with_lora_adapter`: the offline container cannot download the adapter). Rust frontend: the new test passes; `test_generate_logprobs[1]`, `test_generate_logprobs[5]` and `test_stop_string_workflow` fail identically with the previous-head binary, so they predate this change.
- `cargo test -p vllm-engine-core-client -p vllm-text -p vllm-llm -p vllm-server`: all pass (new: lowering validation, streaming rejection, `.npy` bytes equal to `numpy2base64`). `cargo clippy` clean; `pre-commit` passes.

title: [Bugfix][V1] Restore hybrid GDN prefix-cache hits under MTP spec decoding
body:
## Purpose

On **Qwen3.5-122B-A10B** with MTP speculative decoding, a replay of a cached prompt never reaches the depth the prefix cache could give it, and prompts whose length is a multiple of the hash unit get **no hit at all**. Measured live before this change, with a 1072-token GDN page and `--prefix-match-unit 67`:

| prompt | cached tokens on replay | ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| 1072 | **0** | 938 |
| 2000 | **0** | 1876 |
| 2144 | **0** | 2010 |
| 3000 | 1072 | 2881 |
| 3500 | 2144 | 3417 |

### Root cause

Three rules compose badly. A lookup caps at `prompt_len - 1`, because the last token must be recomputed for logits. The MTP/EAGLE drafter then rewinds the hit one hash unit (67) further. But the producer publishes the GDN state at the prompt's own tail boundary, `prompt_len // 67 * 67`, which is at or above the cap — so the recurrent group cannot resume where the rewind lands, and the coordinator intersects the two groups down to the previous full page (or to zero).

The same cap breaks the full-attention side whenever `prompt_len` is a multiple of 67 — and every page multiple is, since `1072 = 16 × 67`. Its partial-tail entry is registered at `prompt_len // 67 * 67 == prompt_len`, which the `- 1` cap excludes, so full attention itself matches nothing below the page boundary and the hybrid hit collapses to 0. That is the `1072 → 0`, `2144 → 0` row above.

### Fix

Write-side only, all of it gated on MTP/EAGLE plus fine-grained hashing being active:

- `mamba_state_cache_position(num_tokens, block_size, hash_block_size)` in `kv_cache_utils.py`: `unit = min(hash_block_size, block_size)`, returns `(num_tokens - 1 - unit) // unit * unit` — the position a replay actually lands on.
- `Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split` stops a prefill chunk there, so that state exists to be published. It is an **extra** stop; the existing block-aligned stops stay. Replacing them lets intermediate chunks end off-grid and re-triggers the state poisoning of #43559 (14 tests in `test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py` fail that way).
- `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` publishes the GDN state there instead of at the prompt tail.
- `FullAttentionManager._cache_partial_tail_block` additionally publishes `(prompt_len - 1) // 67 * 67`, the deepest tail a replay can reach. The unshifted tail is kept, because requests that *extend* this prompt have a higher cap and can still match it.
- `MambaManager` reports a block-aligned prompt end as unreachable through a new `reachable_block_mask()` argument, so that state is not cached in any retention mode: no lookup can land at or past a prompt's own end, and the rewound state below it is where consumers land. Guarded on the latter being cached. The rewound position is read from one `MambaManager` helper rather than recomputed per caller, and keys off whether the engine runs a drafter rather than the per-group `use_eagle` bit, which is only set on groups that take the drop.

Without the last item the page multiples stay at 0 no matter where the GDN state sits: the producer had the state at 938 / 2010 / 3082, but full attention offered nothing below 1072 / 2144 / 3216 for the intersection to meet.

## Test Plan

```bash
# unit
pytest tests/v1/core -q

# e2e: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B, 4x B200, MTP 3 tokens, sub-page hashing
vllm serve $QWEN35_122B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --enable-chunked-prefill \
    --spec-method mtp --spec-tokens 3 --prefix-match-unit 67 --port 8110
```

Hit depth is read from the `vllm:prefix_cache_hits_total` delta of a replay: a token-id prompt of an exact length is sent three times and the second and third deltas are the cached length. 132 lengths from 1 to 15k were swept — every page multiple with its `+1`, `+unit-1`, `+unit`, `+unit+1` neighbours, plus scattered lengths. Two further passes cover the configurations where the patch must do nothing, and quality was checked on top of real hits.

## Test Result

(1) Hit Length Boundary

All 132 lengths land exactly on the replay ceiling `(P - 1 - 67) // 67 * 67`. Page-boundary neighbourhoods, where the old code either missed entirely or fell back a full page:

| prompt | position | before | after | replay ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1072 | k*1072 | 0 | 938 | 938 |
| 1073 | k*1072 + 1 | 0 | 1005 | 1005 |
| 1138 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 0 | 1005 | 1005 |
| 1139 | k*1072 + unit | 0 | 1005 | 1005 |
| 1140 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 0 | 1072 | 1072 |
| 2144 | k*1072 | 0 | 2010 | 2010 |
| 2145 | k*1072 + 1 | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 |
| 2210 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 |
| 2211 | k*1072 + unit | 1072 | 2077 | 2077 |
| 2212 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 1072 | 2144 | 2144 |
| 3216 | k*1072 | 0 | 3082 | 3082 |
| 3217 | k*1072 + 1 | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 |
| 3282 | k*1072 + unit - 1 | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 |
| 3283 | k*1072 + unit | 2144 | 3149 | 3149 |
| 3284 | k*1072 + unit + 1 | 2144 | 3216 | 3216 |

title: [mooncake] support CUSTOM_MEM_POOL in vllm
body:
### Purpose
Add support for Mooncake custom memory pools (NVLINK / BAREX) when allocating KV cache in vLLM. This enables KV cache to use NVLink or BAR-exposed device memory instead of the default CUDA allocator, which is required by some MooncakeStoreConnector deployments for RDMA-based KV-cache transfer.When custom_mem_pool is configured in kv_connector_extra_config, MooncakeStoreConnector creates a torch.cuda.MemPool using the corresponding Mooncake allocator (NVLinkAllocator / BarexAllocator). When unset, the existing CuMem/default allocator behavior remains unchanged.Custom pools are incompatible with CuMem allocation and sleep mode. These conflicting configurations are rejected during connector initialization.In some scenarios, a specific allocator is required due to hardware limitations.
### Changes:
-mooncake/store/worker.py: Validate custom_mem_pool, create and retain the Mooncake memory pool, detect CuMem/sleep-mode conflicts, and provide actionable errors for unsupported Mooncake versions.
-mooncake/store/connector.py: Expose the custom memory-pool context to the GPU worker.
-multi_connector.py: Forward a custom pool from child connectors and reject configurations where multiple children provide pools.
-vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py: Use a connector-provided pool during KV-cache allocation, while preserving the existing fallback behavior.
-test_multi_connector.py: Add coverage for no pool, single-pool forwarding, and multiple-pool conflicts.

title: [ROCm] Enable fused QK-norm+RoPE+gate Triton kernel for Qwen3-Next/Qwen3.5
body:
## Purpose

`Qwen3NextAttention` fuses the gated QKV split + QK-RMSNorm + (partial) NeoX RoPE + gate copy into a single Triton kernel (`fused_qk_rmsnorm_rope_gate`, added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44176). The kernel is pure Triton and backend-agnostic, but it is gated behind `current_platform.is_cuda()`, so ROCm falls back to the slow multi-op eager path, even though the kernel runs correctly and fast on AMD GPUs.

This PR relaxes that one-line guard to `is_cuda_alike()` so ROCm gets the same fusion. It affects the whole `Qwen3NextAttention` family: Qwen3-Next, Qwen3.5, Qwen3.5-MoE

Measured on MI325X (gfx942), bf16, against the model's real eager branch
(`GemmaRMSNorm` + the `rotary_emb` custom op), 300 timed iters after 50 warmup:

| 64 | 281.7 | 33.9 | 8.32× |
| 512 | 277.4 | 33.7 | 8.22× |

Note: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47719 is an opt-in AITER path that additionally fuses the KV-cache write.

title: [Bugfix] MiniMax-M3: recover decode_query_len during CUDA graph capture
body:
## Purpose

MiniMax-M3 fails to start whenever CUDA graph capture is enabled, on an
assertion in its attention metadata builders:

```
File "vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/indexer.py", line 304, in build
    assert decode_query_len > 0
AssertionError
```

### Root cause

The indexer and sparse-attention builders derive the uniform decode query
length by differencing `query_start_loc_cpu`:

```python
query_lens_cpu = qsl_cpu[1 : num_decodes + 1] - qsl_cpu[:num_decodes]
decode_query_len = int(query_lens_cpu[0].item())
assert decode_query_len > 0
```

CUDA graph capture builds `CommonAttentionMetadata` from the persistent
`self.query_start_loc` buffer without staging real cumulative offsets into it
-- capture only needs shapes and addresses, not values. Every per-request
difference taken from it is therefore zero, and the assertion fires before the
server finishes starting.

The batch descriptor itself is well-formed: `num_decodes` and
`num_decode_tokens` *are* staged, and capture uses a uniform decode batch. The
information the builder needs is present; it is just not in the offsets.

## Fix

When the offsets are all zero and the token count divides evenly, derive the
length from the counts and fill `query_lens_cpu` to match, so the invariants
below still run and still hold rather than being skipped:

```python
if decode_query_len == 0 and num_decode_tokens % num_decodes == 0:
    decode_query_len = num_decode_tokens // num_decodes
    query_lens_cpu = torch.full_like(query_lens_cpu, decode_query_len)
assert decode_query_len > 0
```

Normal decode is untouched: with real offsets the first difference is non-zero,
so the branch is never taken.

The same derivation appears in four builders, so all four are fixed:
`common/indexer.py`, `common/sparse_attention.py`, `amd/indexer_aiter.py` and
`nvidia/indexer_msa.py`.

## Test Plan

Exercise the metadata derivation for the three batch shapes it has to serve --
capture, uniform decode, and speculative decode -- before and after the change.

## Test Result

| batch | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| capture (zeroed offsets, 8 reqs / 8 tokens) | `AssertionError` | `decode_query_len=1` |
| uniform decode (8 reqs / 8 tokens) | `decode_query_len=1` | `decode_query_len=1` |
| speculative decode (4 reqs / 8 tokens) | `decode_query_len=2` | `decode_query_len=2` |

Both real-traffic shapes are unchanged, and all three invariants
(`decode_query_len > 0`, uniform per-request lengths, and
`num_decode_tokens == num_decodes * decode_query_len`) pass in every case.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on `vllm/models/minimax_m3/` with
the repo's pinned v0.14.0.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Use AITER tuned GEMM for the MoE router gate
body: ## Purpose The MoE gate linear layer was set to use a bf16×bf16→fp32 GEMM on tier 5 for faster performance, but it is conditioned on Hopper and Blackwell. This enables it for AITER when the underlying tuned GEMM shapes exist. ### Trace comparison On the CPU side, the gate previously performed two operations: a conversion of its input to fp32, followed by the multiply. AITER was already invoked, but with fp32 operands it found no tuned kernel and fell through to `aten::linear` → `aten::matmul` → `aten::mm`. title: [Bugfix][Model] Make Glm5NextMoE.forward rank-agnostic
body:
## Purpose

`Glm5NextMoE.forward` starts with:

```python
num_tokens, hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape
...
return final_hidden_states.view(num_tokens, hidden_dim)
```

which only works for the rank-2 `[tokens, hidden]` layout. Model runners that pass bucketed rank-3 `[1, T, hidden]` activations — the Intel Gaudi backend does — raise `ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)` in every MoE layer.

The fix flattens on the way in and restores the caller's leading dims on the way out. It deliberately does not broadcast: `sequence_parallel_chunk`, `tensor_model_parallel_all_gather` and the `[:num_tokens]` slice inside the block all require tokens to live on dim 0.

No-op for rank-2 input.

Found while bringing up GLM-5.3-Flash on Intel Gaudi 2.

## Test Plan

`tests/models/glm5next/test_moe_input_rank.py`, CPU-only, no model weights needed. Exercises the block's shape contract for rank-2 and rank-3 input: the experts must see a rank-2 `[tokens, hidden]` view, and the caller must get its original shape back.

The test reads `Glm5NextMoE.forward` via `inspect.getsource` and asserts the flattening is present, so it tracks the implementation instead of silently drifting from a copy.

```bash
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_moe_input_rank.py
```

## Test Result

With the fix:

```
3 passed
```

Against the unpatched code the same tests fail.

End-to-end, this was one of the changes needed to get GLM-5.3-Flash serving on Intel Gaudi 2 (TP=4); with it and the related mHC fixes the model produces correct output.

---

*AI disclosure: this change was developed with assistance from Claude (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line, reproduced the failure and validated the fix on real hardware, and ran the tests myself.*

title: [Model][Spec Decode] Enable EAGLE3/DSpark pipeline parallelism for Sarvam MLA
body:
## Purpose

Enable EAGLE3 auxiliary hidden-state transport across pipeline stages for `SarvamMLAForCausalLM`, including DSpark drafts whose target taps span multiple stages.

The change reuses `EagleModelMixin` to transport stage-local captures and assemble them in layer order on the final stage. Stage-entry capture runs only on the first stage to avoid duplicate boundary taps. The final stage also loads the target embedding when speculative decoding requires it.

This extends #53052's stage-local Sarvam support using #50514's generic transport; #53577 provides the separate DSpark runtime/model support. Only `sarvam.py` changes. No test files are added.

## Validation status

- **September 17:** rebased onto main `fdcd42350b`; current head `d9e3224dda`. Resolved one docstring-formatting conflict; the patch otherwise remains unchanged. All **94 focused CPU tests and pre-commit passed**, using the existing September 16 runtime/native extensions.
- **September 16 GPU results below:** tested head `00006af451` against main/native extensions `903285fbcc`. **GPU tests have not been rerun after the September 17 rebase.**

CPU coverage includes Sarvam forward with lightweight blocks, numerical equality across PP partitions, boundary and remote/local auxiliary captures, embedding placement, full-graph tracing, and existing worker tests.

## End-to-end results

Sarvam 105B MLA target with a five-layer GQA DSpark draft, taps `[2, 9, 16, 23, 30]`, eight speculative tokens, BF16, TP=2, B200 GPUs. Real-checkpoint coverage is DSpark; a separate EAGLE3 checkpoint was not tested.

GSM8K: all 1,319 questions per row, five-shot, greedy, 512 output-token cap, prefix caching off. Both compilation modes use full decode CUDA graphs; mode 3 additionally enables vLLM/Inductor compilation.

| Configuration | GPUs | Compile mode | Accuracy | Mean acceptance length | Eval seconds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Target only, PP=1 | 2 | 0 | 85.97% | — | 151.6 |
| DSpark, PP=1 | 2 | 0 | 85.90% | 4.13 | 121.3 |
| DSpark, PP=2 | 4 | 0 | 85.06% | 4.15 | 114.7 |
| DSpark, PP=4 | 8 | 0 | 86.20% | 4.13 | 154.8 |
| DSpark, PP=2 | 4 | 3 | 87.26% | 4.14 | 117.5 |

Acceptance is `1 + accepted/drafts`, including short warmup/smoke. These runs do not establish exact token parity or a general accuracy improvement. Evaluation times include residual inference JIT and use different GPU counts, so they are not a controlled efficiency comparison.

- **Eager PP=2:** eight requests ×128 output tokens passed; mean acceptance length 2.65.
- **Compiled PP=2 HTTP:** 28/28 requests passed, covering long-prefix reuse, concurrent streaming/non-streaming completions and chat. Recorded 9,856 prefix-cache hit tokens and 140 FULL CUDA-graph replays; mean acceptance length 2.83.

## PP=1 latency and CUDA-graph coverage

Compared unpatched main against the patch with identical dependencies, TP=2/PP=1, compilation mode 3 and prefix caching off. Each batch had two warmups and 12 measured calls in shuffled order, generating 128 tokens per request. Times include prefill, decode and host overhead; startup/warmup are excluded.

| Configuration | Batch | Base median seconds | PR median seconds | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Target only | 1 | 0.5779 | 0.5812 | +0.57% |
| Target only | 8 | 1.1677 | 1.1432 | −2.10% |
| Target only | 32 | 1.6532 | 1.6183 | −2.11% |
| DSpark, capture cap 288 | 1 | 0.3993 | 0.3960 | −0.84% |
| DSpark, capture cap 288 | 8 | 0.9348 | 0.9309 | −0.41% |
| DSpark, capture cap 288 | 32 | 1.4699 | 1.4512 | −1.27% |

No consistent PP=1 regression was observed. The patch adds no GPU operations or communication at PP=1. Larger-batch outputs varied within runs, affecting speculative acceptance; these measurements do not guarantee zero overhead for every workload.

Eight draft tokens require nine target verification tokens per request, so 32 requests need a **288-token capture**. The original custom cap of 256 left larger batches without graph coverage. With cap 288, the baseline and patched PP=1 runs recorded **238 and 240 FULL replays at exactly 288 tokens**, respectively. This expanded cap was **not retested at PP=2**; the earlier PP=2 replay count covers smaller batches. Prefill/non-uniform steps can still use NONE under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`.

## Runtime and test commands

title: [Feature] Triton kernel dispatcher
body:
## Purpose

Currently, some default triton kernel implementations do not perform correct or well on different platforms, and there is no way to override the default Triton kernel implementation on different platforms.

This PR introduces a new mechanism to dispatch Triton kernel calls to platform-specific implementations.

outdated
> The usage is quite simple. For the target triton kernel, we decorate it with `@pluggable_kernel`, Then in the out-of-tree or non-default platform, we register a platform-specific implementation using `@register_kernel`. The dispatcher will then dispatch the kernel call to the platform-specific implementation if available, otherwise to the default implementation.

This PR also take `expand_kernel` as an example to show that how the dispatcher works in in-tree and out-of-tree platform.
- In-tree: see the change in cpu model runner
- out-of-tree: see https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/9265 in vllm-ascend

title: [Don't merge][Experiment] Move MediaIO decode to MM preprocessing
body:
## Purpose

Move media **decoding** (image/video/audio) out of the chat parsing layer and
into the mm processor, behind the processor cache. Downloads stay where they
are (async, concurrent, in the renderer); what crosses the boundary is now a
`LazyMedia` handle (encoded bytes + decode callable) instead of a decoded
object.

- `LazyMedia` (`vllm/multimodal/media/base.py`) decodes on first access,
  thread-safe, with `map()` for stacked transforms and `release_bytes()` for
  early memory release. Hashing uses the encoded bytes (images keep their
  exact eager-path hashes via an eager header-open that preserves EXIF
  ImageID / `io_config` semantics), so a **processor-cache hit skips decoding
  entirely** and the raw bytes are freed right after hashing.
- `apply()` is split into two phases: phase 1 (hash, cache lookup, submit
  miss-item decode futures) runs on the single-worker `_mm_executor`; the
  decode await happens on the event loop; phase 2 (HF processing, cache
  writes) runs back on the worker and re-derives the cache state. The worker
  never blocks on a decode join, so multi-second video decodes overlap across
  requests while the P0/P1 cache ordering protocol is preserved. Processors
  overriding `apply()` / `_cached_apply_hf_processor` (EncDec, ASR, several VL
  models) automatically keep the previous blocking path via
  `supports_two_phase_apply`.
- Memory: cache-hit items cost zero pixel memory; original bytes are released
  after hashing (hit) or after HF processing (miss).

Design doc: `docs/design/lazy-media-decode.md`.

Intentional behavior changes:

- Corrupt-media decode errors now surface as HTTP 422
  (`VLLMUnprocessableEntityError`) from the processor instead of 400 at fetch
  time.
- Audio/video cache keys are derived from the encoded bytes instead of the
  decoded waveform/frames (in-process cache; keys change, no persistence
  concerns). Image keys are unchanged.
- Byte-consuming model processors (e.g. Dots3 NOTE) keep access to
  `original_bytes` through HF processing on the cached path; miss-item bytes
  are released only afterwards (`try/finally`).

### Related / duplicate-work check

## Test Plan

Unit / component (from the worktree):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/ -q

    tests/renderers/test_process_multi_modal_uuids.py -q
```

Microbenchmark:


`Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct` from a local HF cache:

```bash

export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0

# Server (one per side under test). --mm-processor-cache-gb 24 keeps all 175
# MMVU videos cached between the back-to-back video runs; --allowed-local-
# media-path is bench-only (pools and the MMVU snapshot are local files).

  --max-model-len 32768 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --enforce-eager \

# Warmup (also primes the mm processor cache for the image-pool runs):
```

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Stop double-encoding tool call arguments
body:
## Purpose

Granite 4 models emit tool call `arguments` already serialized as a JSON string rather than as an object:

```text
<tool_call>{"name": "get_db_config", "arguments": "{\n  \"param\": \"max_connections\"\n}"}</tool_call>
```

The hermes tool parser serializes that value again, so the client receives a JSON string that decodes to another JSON string instead of an object. `_postprocess_messages` in `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py` then decodes it once, finds a `str` rather than a `dict`, and coerces it to `{}` (the guard added in #48922, commit `161ffd37`). The arguments are silently dropped from the replayed conversation history, so multi-turn tool calling loses the previous turn's arguments. The rendered turn 2 prompt, before and after that guard landed:

```text
before: {"name": "get_db_config", "arguments": {"param": "buffer_pool_size"}}
after:  {"name": "get_db_config", "arguments": {}}
```

Server log fingerprint: `Tool call 'X' arguments decoded to str, not a JSON object; coercing to an empty object.`

Two changes, one per commit:

1. **Tool parsers stop double-encoding.** `granite4_tool_parser.dump_args()` already had exactly this guard, so the quirk was already known upstream; the guard just never made it into hermes. Rather than add a second near-duplicate, this hoists one shared `dump_tool_arguments()` into `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` and calls it from both parsers. Both hermes paths are fixed. The streaming path double-encoded by a different mechanism: `_extract_tool_args` regex slices the raw text after `"arguments":`, which for a string-valued argument is the escaped string literal.

   Only a string that holds a JSON object or array is unwrapped, so an `arguments` string that is not itself JSON is still serialized and reaches the client as valid JSON. Both paths route that decision through the one `dump_tool_arguments`, so they agree byte for byte. Since JSON validity cannot be judged from a prefix and an unwrap already streamed cannot be retracted, the streaming path returns nothing for a string-valued `arguments` until the literal closes, then applies the same rule; such arguments therefore arrive in a single chunk, while object-valued `arguments`, the normal case, still stream incrementally. Unwrapping only real JSON is a small behavior change for `granite4`, which previously forwarded any string untouched; its own test suite passes unchanged.

2. **`_postprocess_messages` unwraps one more level.** This also repairs histories that already carry double-encoded arguments, whether from an older server, another parser with the same flaw, or a client that stored them, so it is worth having in addition to the parser fix.

#48922's intent is preserved: a JSON-encoded string that does not itself hold JSON, such as `'"hello"'`, still coerces to `{}`, because decoding `hello` raises and falls through to the existing coercion. All 12 tests that PR added pass unchanged.

Related but distinct: #46924 (tool parsers returning nested object arguments as JSON strings).

### Why the existing tests missed this

`tests/entrypoints/tool_parsers/test_hermes_tool_parser.py` serves `ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny` only with `--tool-call-parser granite4`, and `docs/features/tool_calling.md` recommends that pairing, so hermes with a Granite 4 model is off-doc and untested. `tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py` does deliberately exercise string-valued arguments via `create_complex_input(create_string_args=True)`, so the model quirk was covered, but only for the one parser that already handled it. Separately, no test replays a parser's own output back as assistant history, which is the path that actually breaks; the server-level tests assert on the first response only.

Adding an "arguments arrive already serialized" case to `tests/tool_parsers/common_tests.py` would codify this for every parser, but it is left as a follow-up: `test_hermes_tool_parser.py` does not use that mixin, so it would not have caught this bug, and the shared config would need a new required field in all 7 files that do. The new non-streaming tests here do run against both the hermes and granite4 parsers, through the parametrized fixture that file already has.

## Test Plan

Unit tests, model-free:

```bash
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_hermes_tool_parser.py
pytest tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_utils.py -k tool
pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py   # guards the shared helper
```

New cases: a string-valued `arguments` returns single-encoded JSON, non-streaming and streaming at stream intervals 1, 2, 3 and 5; a bare non-JSON string argument still arrives as valid JSON; streaming output equals non-streaming output for string-valued arguments, including strings that only look structured (`{hello world}`, `[oops`, `{"a": 1} tail text`); `_postprocess_messages` recovers a double-encoded object; and `test_tool_call_arguments_valid_json_non_object` is extended with the double-encoded non-objects `'"[]"'`, `'"42"'` and `'"true"'`, to confirm the extra unwrap does not let a non-object through.

End to end: `granite-4.0-h-small` in bf16 on one Intel Gaudi 3 card, served with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`, running a 3-turn scenario in which turns 2 and 3 are elliptical follow-ups on the same tool, so the model has to read the previous call's arguments out of the conversation history.

## Test Result

Unit tests:

| suite | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/tool_parsers/test_hermes_tool_parser.py` | 30 passed, 1 skipped | 50 passed, 1 skipped |
| `tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_chat_utils.py -k tool` | 12 passed | 16 passed |
| `tests/tool_parsers/test_granite4_tool_parser.py` | 4 passed | 4 passed |

End to end, 3-turn scenario:

| config | turns correct | double-encoded | coercion warnings |
|---|---|---|---|
| `hermes`, before | 1/3 | yes | 2 |
| `hermes`, after | 3/3 | no | 0 |
| `hermes`, after, double-encoded arguments injected into history | 3/3 | yes, injected | 0 |
| `granite4`, before | 3/3 | no | 0 |

The third row exercises the `chat_utils.py` change on its own, by injecting double-encoded arguments into the history that the parser fix would otherwise have prevented.

`arguments` on the wire for turn 1:

```text
before: '"{\n  \"param\": \"max_connections\"\n}"'   decodes to a str
after:  '{\n  "param": "max_connections"\n}'         decodes to an object
```

Streaming, with `stream=True` against the same server, was double-encoded before this change and is single-encoded after, byte-identical to the non-streaming result. It arrives in one argument chunk, which is the cost of waiting for the string literal to close; object-valued arguments are unaffected.

The streaming extractor was additionally checked character by character over 7 payload shapes (serialized object, serialized object with escapes, unicode escapes, serialized array, bare string, plain object, empty serialized object) to confirm it never returns a value that retracts text it has already sent, which is the invariant the streaming diff in `_compute_args_diff` relies on. All 7 are correct and monotonic after the change; 5 of the 7 were double-encoded before it.

Streaming and non-streaming output were then compared directly on 5 string-valued `arguments` payloads at 2 stream intervals, including three that only look structured. All 10 agree and are valid JSON; on the first version of this PR, 6 of the 10 disagreed and delivered invalid JSON, which is what the third commit fixes.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes, including `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `mypy`, `typos` and the SPDX header check.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Swap the unified-attention 2D grid order on gfx1151
body:
## Important Reviewer Notice

Depends on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56232, but cannot stack them since branches are coming from outside the repository. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56232 needs merging first and then rebase this one over main.

Only last commit is meaningful, the rest are coming from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56232

## Summary

On gfx1151 the 2D unified-attention kernel schedules better when the KV head is the fastest varying grid axis rather than the query block. This launches the 2D grid as `(kv_heads, q_blocks)` there, worth **up to 31% of attention kernel time on long prefill**.

The kernel gains a `USE_SWAPPED_GRID` constexpr defaulting to `False`, so every other platform compiles and launches exactly what it does today. The whole change is **2 lines of existing code** plus the new gating helper.

## Base

This is stacked on `rocm-2d-launch-config`, so the diff here shows only the swap. It is textually independent of that series — they share no hunks — but the swap is only meaningful on top of it: without the 2D launch tuning gfx11 does not route to `TRITON_ATTN` at all, and the `head_size >= 80` boundary is the one that series already established.

## Output is unchanged, bit for bit

The swap only relabels which grid axis carries which index. Every program still computes the same `(q_block, kv_head)` pair and accumulates over KV in the same order, so there is no reassociation and no change in results — unlike the tile/block-size tuning in the base series, which does alter reduction blocking.

Verified rather than asserted: a 3968-token Qwen3-8B-shaped prefill run with the swap on and off produces outputs that are `torch.equal` over the full `[3968, 32, 128]` tensor (max abs diff 0.0, zero differing elements).

## Results

**These are kernel microbenchmarks.** `benchmarks/attention_benchmarks` operates on synthetic tensors; the configs carry only head geometry (`num_q_heads`, `num_kv_heads`, `head_dim`, `block_size`) and load no weights. The model names are shorthand for that geometry — quantization labels in particular have no effect here.

| geometry | head_dim | shape | base | swapped | run 1 | run 2 |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-1.7B | 128 | `q8k` | 14.80 ms | 11.28 ms | +31.1%** | +40.9% |
| Llama-2-7B | 128 | `q8k` | 107.54 ms | 93.59 ms | +14.9%** | +15.4% |

title: [Bugfix] Disable prefix caching for encoder-only before model config hooks
body:
## Summary

An `--mm-encoder-only` instance runs no language model and holds no KV cache, so `VllmConfig.__post_init__` forcibly disables prefix caching for it. That override ran **after** `try_verify_and_update_config()`, where any `is_hybrid` (attention+mamba) model sets `mamba_cache_mode="align"` / `mamba_block_size=block_size` based on the stale "prefix caching on" value (`HybridAttentionMambaModelConfig` → `MambaModelConfig`). The later `validate_mamba_block_size()` then rejects the derived state:

```
Value error, --mamba-block-size can only be set with --enable-prefix-caching
```

So every hybrid VLM crashes on startup under `--mm-encoder-only` with default flags; the only workaround is explicitly passing `--no-enable-prefix-caching`.

**Fix:** move the encoder-only prefix-caching disable to right after `_resolve_mm_encoder_only()`, before any model config hook runs. One block moved, no logic change.

Reproduced with `--mm-encoder-only` + default flags:
- Kimi-K3-pruned75: `ValueError` at startup
- Qwen3.5-VL (Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration): `ValueError` at startup

After the fix, both start cleanly with default flags; `mamba_cache_mode` resolves to `none` and `mamba_block_size` to `max_model_len`, matching the intended "prefix caching off" state.

## Test Plan

- `VllmConfig` construction with a hybrid model + `mm_encoder_only=True` + default prefix caching: previously `ValueError`, now passes (`enable_prefix_caching=False`, `mamba_cache_mode='none'`).
- End-to-end `vllm serve --mm-encoder-only` on Qwen3.5-VL and Kimi-K3 with default flags: previously crashed at config validation, now reaches "Application startup complete".

## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI coding assistance; a human author reviewed every changed line and ran the verification above.

title: [KVConnector] Share KV cache spec-type classification across connectors
body:
## Purpose

Cross-engine KV transfer has to classify each cache group's spec type (attention / SSM / other) before it can plan anything. In tree there are three implementations of that step: NIXL keeps `_is_attention_spec` / `_is_ssm_spec` private in `nixl/tp_mapping.py` and `get_representative_spec_type` in `nixl/utils.py`, MooncakeConnector calls `isinstance(...)` inline at three sites, and MoRIIO unwraps the group spec on its own. The same classification therefore gets fixed per connector.

This PR moves those three helpers to the connector framework layer as `v1/transfer_planning.py`: `is_attention_spec`, `is_ssm_spec`, `get_representative_spec_type`. NIXL and MooncakeConnector import them, and `nixl/tp_mapping.py` no longer defines a private copy.

The shared surface is deliberately only the classification vocabulary. `TPMapping`, `compute_tp_mapping` and `ReadSpec` stay in the `nixl` package, because `rank_to_attention_slot`, `rank_offset_factor` and `local_consumers` encode NIXL's read path and its completion-notification accounting. Extracting the peer shard relation and the transfer plan comes later, once the primitive list in #57373 is settled.

The three converted Mooncake sites are the cache-group classification calls. The `FullAttentionSpec` checks in the same connector ask a narrower question, and the layer-level checks in its validation path are left for the later adoption stage.

No behavior change: the three helpers are moved verbatim (`get_representative_spec_type` gains a one-line docstring), `isinstance(inst, Cls)` becomes `is_*(type(inst))`, which is the same predicate, and the NIXL transfer paths and the wire formats are untouched.

## Related work

- RFC #57373 — the primitive list and the staged plan this PR is the first step of.
- Continues the merged framework work of #53779 / #53780 (externally transferable KV cache groups, per-region transfer geometry).
- Duplicate check: `gh pr list --state open --search "tp_mapping"`, `"transfer planning"` and `"spec classification"` return nothing that promotes this module. The closest hits are #57662 (NIXL region dedup) and #55523 (Mooncake mixed-TP); neither touches the classification vocabulary.

## Test plan

Verified on an 8xH20 host with the branch checked out and on `PYTHONPATH`, using the 0.29 virtualenv. The Hugging Face cache was warmed through `hf-mirror.com` (the host cannot reach `huggingface.co`) and the suites then ran with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. Every suite was also run on the PR's base commit (`71fc70d3a`) in an identical tree on the same host, and the two runs agree test for test:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_transfer_planning.py` — **8 passed** (new file; the base does not carry it).
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_tp_mapping.py` — **26 passed** on both.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_push_connector.py` — **78 passed** on both.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector_hma.py` — **91 passed, 1 failed** on both. The failure is `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]`: `google/gemma-3-1b-it` is a gated repository and returns `403 Forbidden` without a token that has gated access.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_desc_geometry.py` — **210 passed** on both.
- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py` — **75 passed** on both. Its async tests need `pytest-asyncio`, which `requirements/test` declares and that environment lacked; with the plugin installed the file is green on both trees.

Also run:

- Import smoke over every changed module (`transfer_planning`, `nixl.tp_mapping`, `nixl.base_worker`, `nixl.push_worker`, `nixl.pull_worker`, `mooncake.mooncake_connector`): all import; `nixl.tp_mapping.is_ssm_spec is transfer_planning.is_ssm_spec` is True, so NIXL keeps no private copy; `TPMapping`, `compute_tp_mapping` and `ReadSpec` still resolve from `nixl.tp_mapping`; the classification still answers correctly for `MambaSpec` and `FullAttentionSpec`.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` (0.14.0, the pinned version) on the changed files: clean.
- No model evaluation: no behavior change.

## Status

Open for review. The shared surface stays at the classification vocabulary while the primitive list in #57373 is settled; the peer shard relation and the transfer plan are later stages.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to prepare the change and run the verification; the human submitter has reviewed every changed line and defends the change end-to-end.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] AMD-Quark mixed-precision DeepSeek-V4.1 support
body:
## Purpose

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` does not load today. It is a **mixed-precision** AMD-Quark export — MXFP4 experts, but 226 per-layer attention specs in MXFP8:

| | scheme |
|---|---|
| `global_quant_config` | `fp4` / `per_group` / `group_size=32` / `e8m0` |
| `layer_quant_config` (226 entries) | `fp8_e4m3` / `per_block` / `block_size=[32,32]` / `float8_e8m0fnu` |

Four independent bugs block it. Each one assumes DeepSeek **V4**'s `128x128` block geometry, or the DeepSeek-native scale naming.

| # | Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | All 226 per-layer specs silently discarded | Decline mixed-precision Quark exports, let `QuarkConfig` take them |
| 2 | `NotImplementedError: No quark compatible scheme was found.` | New `QuarkW8A8Mxfp8` scheme |
| 3 | Attention shards silently fall back to global MXFP4 | Expose the VL wrapper's mappings as class attributes |
| 4 | Engram scale tensor never routed | Add a `weight_scale$` mapper rule |

### 1. The V4.1 config claims the checkpoint, then throws the specs away

`DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method` accepts any Quark export whose *global* scheme is MXFP4 — this one qualifies. But `from_config` then rewrites the config into a single global FP8 scheme with `weight_block_size = [128, 128]`, discarding all 226 per-layer specs. `get_quant_method` then gates its MXFP8 path on `weight_block_size == [32, 32]`,
which that rewrite has just made unreachable.

**Fix:** a Quark export carrying `layer_quant_config` is mixed precision by definition, so decline it and let `QuarkConfig` handle it.

### 2. QuarkConfig has no scheme for 32×32 per-block FP8

`_is_fp8_w8a8` only accepts per-block FP8 at `[128, 128]` (V4 geometry), and the OCP-MX matchers only accept 1-D `per_group` weights. A 32×32 per-block e8m0 weight matches neither, so dispatch raises.

**Fix:** extend `QuarkOCP_MX` to handle MXFP8 as a first-class OCP-MX dtype. `mxfp8_e4m3` is added to `_WEIGHT_QUANT_KEY_MAP` / `_ACTIVATION_QUANT_KEY_MAP`, a normalizer (`ocp_mx_weight_dtype_and_rows()`) accepts both config dialects, and `QuarkOCP_MX` gains an unpacked MXFP8 branch with 3-way `packed_factor` (`1` for mxfp8, `2` for mxfp4, `8/6` for mxfp6).

The only difference from canonical 1-D MXFP8 is scale layout. MXFP8 carries one e8m0 value per weight *row* per 32-element group; Quark's `block_size=[R, 32]` carries one per *R* rows. The loader expands each scale row:

```python
loaded_weight.view(torch.uint8).repeat_interleave(rows, dim=0)
```

At `R == 1` the two layouts coincide and expansion is a no-op. The kernel is the shared `init_mxfp8_linear_kernel()` — the same one compressed-tensors and INC MXFP8 schemes use. Existing 128×128 per-block FP8 keeps
`QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock`, asserted in the new tests.

This also fixes a latent dispatch inconsistency: `get_quant_method()` and `get_quant_method_target()` now agree on MXFP8 layers, since both walk the same `QuarkOCP_MX` matcher chain.

Both MXFP8 config dialects are accepted:

| | Shape A (canonical MX) | Shape B (DeepSeek-V4.1) |
|---|---|---|
| `dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| shape | `qscheme=per_group`, `group_size=32` | `qscheme=per_block`, `block_size=[32,32]` |
| scale | `scale_format="e8m0"` | `scale_type="float8_e8m0fnu"` |
| `scale_block_rows` (R) | 1 | 32 |

### 3. The VL wrapper hides its module mappings from the quant config

`configure_quant_config` reads `hf_to_vllm_mapper` and `packed_modules_mapping` off the **class**, before `__init__` runs.
`DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` (vision variant) defined neither at class level, only as instance attributes. So per-layer keys naming `layers.N.attn.wq_a` never matched the runtime `language_model.model.layers.N.attn.wq_a`, and every
attention shard silently fell back to the global MXFP4 spec.

**Fix:** expose both as class attributes, with the prefix rules shared via one module-level constant so they cannot drift.

### 4. The engram scale name

Quark spells it `engram.embed.weight_scale`. The mapper's rules match `\.scale$` — a literal `.scale` suffix — so the rule never fires.

**Fix:** add an explicit `weight_scale$` rule alongside the existing one.

## Scope

ROCm/AMD path only (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/`). The `nvidia/` twins have the same shape for items 3 and 4, but this PR deliberately leaves them alone — only the AMD path has been validated on hardware.

## Test Plan

**Quark dispatch tests (`test_quark.py`):**

- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_2d_block` — a 32×32 per-block e8m0 linear dispatches to `QuarkOCP_MX` with `scale_block_rows == 32`; experts still fall through to the global MXFP4 spec; 128×128 per-block FP8 still gets
  `QuarkW8A8Fp8PerBlock`.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_canonical` — canonical 1-D per-group MXFP8 (Shape A) dispatches to `QuarkOCP_MX` with `scale_block_rows == 1`; `get_quant_method` / `get_quant_method_target` agree.
- `test_quant_method_dispatch_mxfp8_moe_raises` — MXFP8 experts raise `NotImplementedError`.
- `test_quark_override_delegates_to_quark_config` — all `quant_method=="quark"` configs (MXFP4, MXFP8, mixed, etc.) return `None` from  `DeepseekV4FP8Config.override_quantization_method`, confirming delegation to `QuarkConfig`. Parametrized over V4 and V4.1 model types (10 cases).

**FP8 / DeepSeek-V4.1 tests (`test_fp8.py`):**

- `test_deepseek_v41_declines_mixed_precision_quark_config`
- `test_deepseek_v41_vl_exposes_quant_mappings_on_class`
- `test_deepseek_v41_engram_scale_accepts_quark_name`

## Test Result

**0 new code failures.** 

### End-to-end

`DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-MXFP4` (48 shards, 475 GB) on 4x MI355X at TP=4: all shards load in 74.5 s, MXFP8 attention resolves to `QuarkOCP_MX` via the `RocmDotScaledMxfp8LinearKernel`, and the model is coherent.

GSM8K accuracy (1319 problems, greedy, seed=42, 8-shot)
| Config | flexible-extract | strict-match |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| MXFP4 | 92.34% ± 0.73 | 92.42% ± 0.73 |
| Base FP8 | 92.87% ± 0.71 | 92.95% ± 0.71 |

Hardware: 4x MI355X (gfx950/CDNA4), TP=4.

title: [Core] Pick hybrid KV cache group size by worst-case padding bytes; add --min-kv-cache-group-layers
body:
## Purpose

`_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` splits each KV cache bucket into groups of `group_size` layers and pads the last group of each bucket. The current heuristic uses the smallest bucket as `group_size` (or the largest, if it is within 1.5x). A single-layer bucket, typically a speculative drafter layer whose spec cannot merge with the target's, drives this to `group_size = 1`, which means one KV cache group per layer, each rebuilding attention metadata every step. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash ends up with 46 groups.

This PR replaces the min / 1.5x-max heuristic:

- **Search** group sizes from `max(smallest bucket, --min-kv-cache-group-layers)` up to the largest bucket. The floor is capped at the largest bucket.
- **Pick** the group size that wastes the fewest worst-case bytes per request on padding layers. Each padding layer costs its spec's `max_memory_usage_bytes` at `max_model_len`, so full attention padding scales with context length, while sliding window / mamba padding stays bounded. Ties prefer fewer groups.
- **New option `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` (default 3)** trades metadata overhead (more groups) against KV capacity (more padding).

This subsumes the 1.5x rule (gpt-oss + eagle still pads sw 12 → 13 instead of full 13 → 24).

Grouping at `max_model_len=256k`, default `--min-kv-cache-group-layers 3`:

| Layer buckets (target + *drafter*) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B + DFlash `[30 mamba, 10 full, *5 sw, 1 full*]` | gs=1, 46 groups | gs=3, 17 groups; 2 target full + 2 drafter full + 1 drafter sw padding layers |
| Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + Eagle3 `[30 mamba, 10 full, *1 full*]` ¹ | gs=1, 41 groups | gs=5, 9 groups; 4 drafter full padding layers |
| MiMo + MTP `[9 full, 39 sw, *5 sw*]` ¹ | gs=5, 11 groups; 1 full + 1 sw padding | gs=9, 7 groups; 10 sw padding |
| gpt-oss-20b + eagle `[12 sw, 13 full]` | gs=13, 2 groups | unchanged |
| Gemma3-1B/4B/12B/27B, Llama4-Scout, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B | — | unchanged |

¹ Computed assuming the drafter's KV bytes per token equal the target's (Eagle3) and a 128-token MTP window (MiMo); not measured.

Behavior change: with the default floor of 3, a model whose smallest bucket has exactly 2 layers can get a larger group size than before (no model in the table above is affected).

### Comparison with #58175

#58175 targets MiMo. On DFlash / Eagle3 it keeps main's per-layer grouping (gcd of `[10, 1]` = 1); on the other models above both PRs leave grouping unchanged.

| MiMo-V2-Flash + MTP `[9 full, 39 sw, *5 sw*]` ² | group size | groups | padding layers | padding per request (256k context) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 5 | 11 | 1 full + 1 sw | ~640 MiB + `S` |
| #58175 | 3 | 18 | 1 draft sw | `S` (~40 MiB) |
| this PR (default) | 9 | 7 | 6 sw + 4 draft sw | 10 `S` (~400 MiB) |

`S` = one sliding window padding layer's bounded worst case, (window + in-flight tokens) × 5 KiB/token, ~40 MiB at 8k batched tokens. Neither PR pads full attention. This PR pads more (bounded) sliding window memory than #58175 in exchange for 7 instead of 18 groups; it does not consider gs=3 because its search starts at the smallest bucket (5).

² MiMo-V2-Flash: 9 full attention (4 KV heads, 2.5 KiB/token) and 39 SWA (8 KV heads, 128-token window, 5 KiB/token) per its config; the 5 MTP layers are assumed to be sliding window with the same shape. Not measured.

Relation to other PRs:
- #51742 ignores single-layer buckets when taking the min (gs=5 for DFlash) without bounding the resulting full attention padding.
- #49472 minimizes `padding + num_groups` in layer counts, without distinguishing full attention from bounded-memory padding (e.g. pads 3 full attention layers on Gemma3-27B).

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hidden_states_connector.py -q
```

## Test Result

All pass. `test_hybrid_group_size_selection` covers the drafter (floor 2 and 3), gpt-oss + eagle, Gemma3-27B and MiMo layouts. One sub-case of `test_get_kv_cache_config_one_worker` changed expectation: at its `max_model_len=16`, a sliding window layer's worst case (2 blocks) exceeds full attention's (1 block), so padding full attention is now cheaper.

### Benchmarks

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash, 1× B300, BF16 mamba states, GSM8K, single runs, acceptance length 5.1–5.2 in all runs.

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --max-num-seqs 32 --no-enable-prefix-caching --block-size 128 \
  --mamba-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16 --min-kv-cache-group-layers $M \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"z-lab/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-DFlash","method":"dflash","num_speculative_tokens":7}'
vllm bench serve --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 --dataset-name hf --dataset-path openai/gsm8k --hf-split test \
  --num-prompts max(32, 8*C) --max-concurrency C --num-warmups 2*C
```

(`--block-size 128` is needed on main too: the DFlash drafter's FLASH_ATTN backend only supports 128-token kernel blocks on B300, but the hybrid block size is aligned only to the target backend, giving 592 → `No common block size for 592`. Separate issue.)

Left: this PR. Right: this PR + #52297 (GDN metadata, orthogonal). `--min-kv-cache-group-layers 1` reproduces main's grouping (46 groups).

![min-kv-cache-group-layers sweep](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucasWilkinson/vllm/af4013a3827d250b266c6e48b1fc124880523780/pareto_min_layers.png)

Grouping and padding cost per request vs. context length. Target full attention is 2 KiB/token/layer (2 KV heads × 256); drafter layers are 4 KiB/token/layer (8 KV heads × 128). For reference, the unpadded full attention KV is 24 KiB/token (10 target + 1 drafter layer).

| `--min-kv-cache-group-layers` | gs | groups | KV cache capacity | padding layers | full-context padding | 8k | 32k | 128k | 256k |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (= main) | 1 | 46 | 7.42M tokens | none | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 2 | 24 | 6.42M tokens | 1 drafter full, 1 drafter sw | 4 KiB/token (+17%) | 48 MiB | 144 MiB | 528 MiB | 1.02 GiB |
| 3 (default) | 3 | 17 | 5.19M tokens | 2 target full, 2 drafter full, 1 drafter sw | 12 KiB/token (+50%) | 112 MiB | 400 MiB | 1.52 GiB | 3.02 GiB |
| 4 | 5 | 10 | 4.80M tokens | 4 drafter full | 16 KiB/token (+67%) | 128 MiB | 512 MiB | 2 GiB | 4 GiB |

The sliding window padding layer adds a bounded ~16 MiB (4096-token window × 4 KiB), included above. The measured KV cache capacity drops (−13.5% / −30% / −35%) track the full-context overhead.

title: [Perf][Frontend] Serialize completion responses without an intermediate dict
body:
## Purpose

Long non-streaming completions build a nested Python dictionary and then encode it as JSON, concentrating duplicate work when many requests finish or abort together. Render ordinary completion models directly with Pydantic's existing `model_dump_json()`. Reuse `JSONResponse` so headers and background load accounting keep their lifecycle. Runtime change: one file, +46/-2 lines.

Fall back to the original renderer for non-finite logprobs, arbitrary extras, transfer metadata, prompt logprobs, metrics, or fast-path serialization errors. Preserve existing errors; successful JSON number formatting can differ while parsed values match. Error responses and streaming are unchanged.

Part of #57479, independently reviewable from #58278. Open-PR searches for the RFC, completion/native JSON and serialization found no duplicate: #52875 optimizes streaming frames, #54050 caches token decoding, and #48585 changes non-finite-logprob handling; this PR preserves that handling.

## Validation
