Server serialization-tail median **4.974 → 3.740 s (24.8% lower)**; client last-body-read median **6.312 → 5.692 s (9.8% lower)**. Both balanced blocks are token-matched within 5%; mean B/A token ratios 1.0051 / 0.9988. A's observed tail range is 0.613 s; median tail saving is 1.234 s. Predeclared strong-live gate: PASS.

All **8,000 requests** returned HTTP 200 / `abort`; raw per-engine Prometheus gauges confirmed 250 active and zero waiting requests on each engine, with 1,000 render/send events per run. Each B run recorded **1,000 successful native encodes and zero legacy renders**. Thirteen rank-pinned greedy API cases (including top-k logprobs, echo, prompt logprobs, token IDs and streaming) matched across all eight starts. No model weights, kernels or sampling changes.

Both arms include the identical listener fix on pinned serving base `0fd2e8d503`; B ports this PR's runtime code from main base `955bd6abef`, changing only two relocated imports. Source/harness hashes and four frontend source manifests were checked per run. The earlier one-A-run attempt was stopped for a type-annotation correction and excluded; the full eight-run sequence was restarted.

Four repeats/arm, no significance or full-model/DP8 claim. Server serialization excludes ASGI send/network/client parsing. Client body-read is application-observed and can be delayed by other responses' parsing; `/pause` return is separate, with no pause-HTTP speedup claim. These results do not use the historical 100s+ baseline or earlier unguarded-JSON measurements.

Twenty supplementary serialization checks on the exact PR base cover sampled logprobs, top-k=20, no logprobs, and prompt/metrics fallback, with parsed-value parity and actual native/fallback counts. Their shared-host timings are exploratory and not used for performance acceptance.

title: [Perf][SM120][MLA] Use compact FP8 KV rows for NoPE models
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to merged #55277: use compact 528-byte `fp8_ds_mla` rows for native NoPE on the FlashInfer SM120 backend. Rebased onto upstream main `c843f0cab78b413f2b0a5c2282cb71e3a3937b11`, which includes the squash merge of #55277. The two commits in this PR are now `1dc1ae03837` and `bea90f7efee` (head); range-diff confirms both are unchanged by the rebase.

The row contains 512 FP8 latent bytes and four FP32 group scales. There is no RoPE payload. A single backend-owned row-size method supplies both the KV spec and early HiSparse registration. On SM120, compact selection depends solely on `kv_lora_rank=512` and `qk_rope_head_dim=0`, independent of model name, connector, or offloading configuration. Other backend layouts are unchanged; real RoPE64 `fp8_ds_mla` retains 656-byte rows. No new dtype or CLI option is added.

The writer accepts NoPE 528/656, preserves legacy zero-tail behavior for 656, and rejects RoPE64 with 528. It distinguishes logical row width from physical stride. The fixed 576-dimensional gather rejects compact input. HiSparse uses actual row widths for byte movement and rejects incompatible shared-staging layouts.

No connector changes, layout negotiation, or old-cache migration are added. Local prefix caching remains supported. External connectors were not tested end to end.

Duplicate-work check: #53969/#55778/#55543 use padded compatibility layouts; #55219/#57169 address broader paging/stride plumbing, not this compact writer/spec change. The community B12X GLM_NEXT path already uses the same 528-byte encoding; that is a useful precedent, not the FlashInfer backend wiring implemented here. Reference: local-inference-lab/vllm `cff8aebfeb73de96c97b4c5a0550c5a49f27451c`, `b12x_mla_sparse.py`. FlashInfer compact-row support was merged in flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5075.

## Test Plan

Validation used 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell for official NVIDIA GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4, TP4, BF16, no speculation, text-only, context 65536, max sequences 32, batched tokens 4096, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs. FlashInfer source: `dc04f50c9aa3eabcdaa5feb0934edb3d85e9529a`.

Commands below are shown without local environment wrappers, not as verbatim execution transcripts. Paths are relative to the vLLM checkout unless noted. The following checks were rerun after the rebase onto main:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py \
  -k concat_and_cache_ds_mla -q -rs
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_cp_gather_fp8.py -q
python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_mla_backends.py::test_mla_kv_cache_spec_uses_layer_cache_dtype \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_index_group_preserves_row_width \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_shared_staging_requires_uniform_row_width \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_swap_in_preserves_rows_across_eviction \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py::test_hisparse_gather_prefill_cache_prefers_resident_rows
prek run --from-ref c843f0cab78b413f2b0a5c2282cb71e3a3937b11 --to-ref bea90f7efee
```

Earlier validation from the FlashInfer checkout, not rerun after the rebase:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/attention/test_sparse_mla_sm120.py \
  -k glm53_nope_compact_rows -q
```

Model validation preceded gate removal and was not rerun after the rebase. It used GSM8K and random-8k1k workloads with `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` explicitly selected. As in #55277, successful runs used the disclosed distributed-autotune workaround:

```text
VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS=fp4_gemm,trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1,trtllm::fused_moe::gemm2
```

This PR does not fix that separate autotune issue or the noncanonical-layout calibration restriction. FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, pinned in upstream vLLM, is not the dependency used for this validation.

## Test Result

Rerun after the rebase, at head `bea90f7efee`:

- Selected spec and HiSparse width/guard/data-path tests: **31 passed, no skips**. Includes uint8 528/656 host miss, hit, eviction/reload, and prefill byte gather. No claim of a complete model-level HiSparse deployment or external-connector end-to-end test.
- CUDA writer: **9 passed, 3 existing unsupported-geometry/input-size skips**. Includes compact/padded rows, row/page gaps, invalid slots, and legacy payload parity.
- Fixed-layout gather regression: **18 passed**.
- All applicable `prek` hooks passed across **all 10 changed files**, including Ruff, formatting, and mypy.

Earlier validation, not rerun after the rebase:

- FlashInfer compact/padded/sliced cache attention parity and CUDA graph replay: 3 passed (before gate removal).
- Broader `test_mla_backends.py` attempt stopped after 53 passes at an SM100 CUTLASS-only operator unavailable in this SM90/SM120 build. The complete cross-architecture suite was not qualified.
- GSM8K strict match, #55277 parent → compact: **1223/1319 (92.72%) → 1228/1319 (93.10%)**, concurrency 32, max output 2048. The compact evaluation gate passed; +5 samples is not evidence of a meaningful accuracy gain. Its recipe initially failed the immediate cleanup check; a subsequent managed stop verified all allocated devices freed.
- Random 8K/1K: **both runs completed 252/252 requests with zero failures**, with 4 × concurrency requests per level. Matrix server cleanup verified.

### KV-cache capacity

Compared with #55277 on the same hardware and serving configuration:

| Metric | #55277 | Compact |
|---|---:|---:|
| Encoded bytes per KV row | 656 | 528 (**−19.51%**) |
| Engine-reported KV token capacity | 4,301,231 | 5,282,546 (**+22.81%**) |
| Available KV-cache memory | 40.57 GiB | 40.57 GiB |

The benefit is more KV capacity within the same memory budget, not a throughput claim or a 19.51% reduction in total GPU allocation. Capacity is engine-reported, not saturation-tested; the validation runs used dirty source trees with differing build metadata.

Developed with AI assistance. Opened as a draft pending human line-by-line review; automated validation is not represented as human review. No changes were pushed to #55277.

title: [Perf][KV Connector][Mooncake] Pack hybrid/MLA KV into coalesced transfer regions
body:
## Purpose

Mooncake PD currently emits one RDMA descriptor per layer-view × block. Hybrid/MLA caches (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Flash) expand into many views of the same packed allocation, so descriptor counts are ~10× NIXL on the same workload.

This matches NIXL's packed-page path: one transfer region per block-major storage row, then coalesce consecutive blocks. There is **no extra_config flag** (NIXL has none either). Packed is used when the cache is block-major **and** MLA or not HNC-contiguous. Mamba / KpoolTail stay unpacked. HNC-contiguous FA (LBHNC) stays one region per layer.

Handshake still requires matching region metadata on P and D. Empty `registered_source_groups` (older peer) is treated as 1:1 group mapping.

Production delta is ~136 LOC (under the 500-LOC RFC bar). No docs change: no new user-facing extra_config.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py

pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hybrid_mamba.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector_hma.py
```

CPU unit tests cover:

- shared-backing MLA/HMA views collapse to one packed region (`source_groups` spans groups)
- `_paired_blocks_for_region` dedup + one coalesced copy
- packed vs unpacked `kv_block_len` / region-count handshake failure
- empty `source_groups` defaults to 1:1
- FA LBHNC/LHBNC and hybrid GDN region counts stay unpacked; BHLNC packs like NIXL

Cross-node PD (RoCE): Mooncake old vs packed vs NIXL, DeepSeek-V4-Flash 4P4D / 8P4D and DeepSeek-V2-Lite TP1. Prefill `KV Transfer metrics` for xfer / MB / GB/s / descriptors; client TTFT from first SSE token.

## Test Result

Unit: packed-related **17 passed**; full Mooncake connector files **104 passed** locally (one hetero-TP case only failed when swapping `facebook/opt-125m` for a local Qwen checkpoint).

DSV4-Flash 4P4D cross-node (xfer is not the TTFT bottleneck; packed 166 extra views → 1 region):

| tokens | path | TTFT | xfer | GB/s | desc |
|--------|------|------|------|------|------|
| 512 | MC old | 260 ms | 1.87 ms | 11.2 | 781 |
| 512 | MC packed | 251 ms | 1.52 ms | 18.2 | 22 |
| 512 | NIXL | 256 ms | 2.27 ms | 12.2 | 22 |
| 3072 | MC old | 613 ms | 3.03 ms | 10.2 | 1401 |
| 3072 | MC packed | 600 ms | 2.00 ms | 18.7 | 33 |
| 3072 | NIXL | 608 ms | 2.03 ms | 18.4 | 33 |

V2-Lite TP1 24k (large KV; user-visible xfer):

| path | TTFT P50 | xfer | GB/s | desc |
|------|----------|------|------|------|
| MC old | 1737 ms | 62.3 ms | 12.0 | 6354 |
| MC packed | 1702 ms | 23.7 ms | 30.1 | 6354 |
| NIXL | 1756 ms | 39.4 ms | 18.1 | 6354 |

DSV4 8P4D: desc 1649 → 34 at 4k, GB/s ~12 → ~19; TTFT still prefill-bound (xfer 2–5 ms). NIXL 8P4D was not a fair baseline (HTTP 200, KV transfer metrics 0).

## Documentation

No `docs/` update: behavior is layout-driven, no new extra_config.

title: [Rust Frontend] Accept custom chat roles for HF templates
body:
## Purpose

The Python Chat Completions API accepts roles outside the OpenAI set and passes them through to chat templates (`CustomChatCompletionMessageParam`, since #4758). The Rust frontend's HTTP `ChatMessage` is a closed enum tagged by `role`, so the same request fails with HTTP 400 before rendering.

Some public templates depend on this. The `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` chat template maps a leading `root` message to its high-priority system prompt, replacing the default model identity text, while `system` / `developer` go to the lower-priority developer prompt. Under the Rust frontend, callers that override the identity with `root` are rejected.

Changes:

- **HTTP DTO:** add `ChatMessage::Custom { role, content }`. The serde derive now uses `remote = "Self"` and covers only the standard roles; hand-written `Serialize` / `Deserialize` impls dispatch on the role tag. Standard roles go through the derived impl unchanged, and any other string role becomes `Custom`. A `#[serde(untagged)]` fallback variant was rejected: serde falls back to it whenever the tagged variant fails, so a malformed standard message (e.g. a `tool` message without `tool_call_id`) would be silently accepted as a custom role, and field errors would be replaced by the generic untagged-enum error.
- **`vllm-chat`:** add `ChatMessage::Custom`, `ChatRole::Custom(String)`, and `ChatMessage::custom()`. The HF renderer passes the role string to templates unchanged (`TemplateMessage` now borrows its role). Media in custom-role content is collected like other content-bearing roles.
- **Native renderers** (DeepSeek V3.2 / V4 / V4.1, Harmony, Inkling, Kimi K3) reject custom roles with a new `Error::UnsupportedChatRole`, classified as a request validation error (HTTP 400) rather than an internal template error.
- `name` on custom-role messages is dropped, consistent with how the Rust frontend treats `name` on the other roles (Python forwards it to the template).

Duplicate check: searched open PRs for custom / `root` chat roles in the Rust frontend; none found.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change and description.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-chat
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all --check
```

New tests:

- `prepare_chat_request_accepts_custom_role_messages`: a `root` message in the request JSON lowers to `ChatMessage::custom("root", ..)`.
- `chat_http_message_keeps_standard_role_errors`: a `tool` message without `tool_call_id` still fails with `missing field \`tool_call_id\``.
- `chat_template_passes_custom_roles_unchanged`: the HF template sees `root` / `system` / `user` roles as sent.
- `custom_roles_are_rejected_as_request_errors`: the DeepSeek V4 renderer rejects a custom role with a request validation error.

Manual parity check against the public `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3` template (revision `f0e1c1e04d`, metadata files only): start `vllm-rs render` on the snapshot, send `[root, system, user]` with `chat_template_kwargs={"thinking_mode": "disabled"}` to `/v1/chat/completions/render`, and compare the token IDs with `transformers` `apply_chat_template(..., add_generation_prompt=True)` followed by `encode(..., add_special_tokens=False)`.

## Test Result

- `cargo nextest run -p vllm-server -p vllm-chat`: 801 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- Parity check: Rust and `transformers` 5.17.0 produce identical token IDs (126 tokens). The `root` content replaces the default identity in the system prompt, and the `system` message renders in the developer prompt.
- Error behavior on the render server: `{"role":"tool","content":"x"}` returns 400 `messages[0]: missing field \`tool_call_id\``; `{"role":"root"}` returns 400 `messages[0]: missing field \`content\``.

No model evaluation: the change affects prompt rendering only for requests that were previously rejected; standard-role deserialization and rendering are unchanged.

title: [ROCm][RDNA3] Fix W4A16 split-K accuracy and determinism
body:
## Problem

The RDNA3 (gfx11) W4A16 GPTQ kernels accumulate split-K partials in
bf16/fp16 via CAS atomics. The narrowing happens **before** accumulation,
and low-precision addition is not associative — so whichever split block
wins the CAS first changes the result. That numerical error is present on
**every affected forward pass**, in every decoding configuration.

Greedy decoding is merely where it becomes visible: at temperature 0 the
rounded logit wobble can flip `argmax` between repeated identical
generations (the trail in #50603). Under sampling (e.g. T=0.6) the same
error hides under the sampler's own noise while still sitting under every
reported metric.

## Root cause

```
FP32 per-block partial
  -> bf16/fp16 narrowing (8 / 11 mantissa bits)
  -> CAS-atomic accumulation in execution-dependent order
```

gfx11 has no packed bf16/fp16 atomic, so the epilogue emulated one with a
CAS retry loop — which also made the accumulation order scheduler- and
contention-dependent.

## Fix

Keep the compute kernels and dispatch unchanged; replace only the epilogue
on both paths:

```
FP32 per-split partials
  -> fixed ascending-z FP32 reduction
  -> one final bf16/fp16 cast
```

* Every path writes each output element exactly once; `k_split == 1`
  (WMMA) and `z_count == 1` (scalar) keep/store directly — no scratch, no
  reduce, no atomics.
* The FP32 partials scratch is `at::empty`: coverage is total by
  construction (every reducer-visible `(z, m, n)` slot has exactly one
  writer in all seven WMMA variants and the scalar kernel; the invariant
  is documented at `alloc_wmma_partials`), so there is no zero-fill pass.
* Scratch is per-call via the caching allocator, row-tiled so the bound is
  independent of the caller's M.

## Accuracy (W7900/gfx1100, FP32 dequantized reference)

Max abs error, synthetic uint4b8/group-128 weights, K=4096:

| path | dtype | legacy CAS | this PR | factor |
|------|-------|-----------:|--------:|-------:|
| scalar | bf16 | 0.24–0.37 | 0.0625 | 4–6x |
| WMMA | bf16 | 0.15–0.23 | 0.09–0.11 | ~2x |
| WMMA | fp16 | 0.024–0.038 | 0.011–0.018 | ~2x |
| scalar | fp16 | ~0.95 | ~0.95 | 1x* |

bf16 is the headline; fp16 carries 11 mantissa bits so the removed CAS
rounding costs it ~8x less (as expected). *scalar fp16's remaining error
is the classic exllama dequant bit-trick (per-group offset constant
rounded to fp16) — pre-existing, unchanged by this PR.

The earlier "0.028 → 0.0061" measurement is the same bf16 improvement
factor on real Muse weights. bf16 residual error now sits at the final
output cast (1 ulp); WMMA at the B-tile narrowing.

## Determinism

Fixed inputs now produce bit-identical outputs on every call: 20/20
benchmark shapes repeatable; real Muse q_proj at M=1 gives 1 distinct
result / 100 calls (previously up to 200/200 distinct). Repeatability
alone is not correctness, so the tests also check values against the FP32
reference — a stale `at::empty` scratch slot would be bitwise-repeatable
and wrong, and is caught by the tolerance analysis in the test module.

## Performance (W7900/gfx1100, median of 100 CUDA-event timings)

Rows are **bf16**; fp16 differs in dispatch (bf16 reaches WMMA at
M ≥ 16, fp16 not until M ≥ 64 — at M=16 fp16 is still on the scalar path):

| M | N | K | path | k_split | scratch MB | before µs | after µs | Δ |
|--:|---:|---:|------|--------:|-----------:|----------:|---------:|---:|
| 1 | 4096 | 4096 | scalar | 16 | 0.25 | 44.5 | 39.7 | -10.8% |
| 8 | 4096 | 4096 | scalar | 16 | 2.0 | 61.8 | 57.2 | -7.5% |
| 16 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 16x16_1w | 4 | 1.0 | 58.8 | 53.7 | **-8.7%** |
| 64 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 64x64_4w | 4 | 4.0 | 120.5 | 112.0 | **-7.0%** |
| 128 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 8.0 | 123.5 | 114.7 | **-7.2%** |
| 512 | 4096 | 4096 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 32.0 | 378.4 | 350.8 | **-7.3%** |
| 512 | 4096 | 6656 | wmma 128x64_k32 | 4 | 32.0 | 554.7 | 527.4 | -4.9% |
| 512 | 25600 | 6656 | wmma 128x64_k32 | **1** | **0** | 3070.7 | 2894.2 | -5.8% |

fp16 WMMA rows move the same way (M=64: 104.7→97.8, M=128: 116.1→107.9,
M=512: 353.1→327.6). Full tables for both dtypes incl. N/K/k_split/scratch
per row: `05-benchmark.md` in the evidence package:
https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/evidence/pr-54706-jartx-w7900/validation-54706-jartx-w7900
(immutable: same tree at commit
https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/9bc79045c157dd12a2728cad4e52fd9b21b0ccc3/validation-54706-jartx-w7900)

Notes:
- "before" = this branch's original HEAD (zero-filled WMMA scratch);
  "after" = with the dead zero-fill removed (`at::zeros` → `at::empty`
  once total coverage was proven). Same-M/different-N matters: at M=512,
  N=4096 → k_split=4 (32 MB scratch) while N=25600 → k_split=1 (none).
- Versus a locally restored legacy-CAS control build, the deterministic
  epilogue is now at parity or **faster** for prefill shapes (bf16 M=16:
  53.7 vs 55.3 µs); only M=1 decode pays a residual ~4–10% (scratch
  round-trip at tiny output) — the price of bit-reproducibility.
- Numerics are bit-identical before/after the memset removal on all 20
  shapes (zero-init was dead traffic).
- A follow-up fix (CodeRabbit finding) gave the V7/V8 k_split==1 path
  the same direct-store branch the 64x64 path had: no scratch, no
  reduce, partials == nullptr. N=25600 row: bf16 3020.1 -> 2894.2 µs
  (-4.2%), fp16 2858.3 -> 2668.6 µs (-6.6%); split-K shapes unchanged
  within noise; numerics bit-identical.

## Why not FP32 atomics?

gfx11 does have `global_atomic_add_f32`; an FP32 scratch accumulated with
native atomics plus one cast pass would remove nearly all the rounding
error with no reduce kernel. We still chose the fixed-order reduce:
FP32 addition is also non-associative, so atomic accumulation remains
order-dependent — vastly better numerically, but not bit-reproducible.
Since bit-exact reproducibility is an explicit goal of this PR, the
fixed ascending-z reduction is the design that guarantees it.

## Tests

`tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna3_w4a16_determinism.py` — 24 tests:

* bit-repeatability through the public op (scalar/WMMA × bf16/fp16),
  with the scalar regression at K=4096 (16 concurrent writers — well
  inside the old failure regime, whose onset was 2–4 writers);
* FP32-reference correctness for scalar and WMMA, split-K and
  direct-store (k_split == 1 / z_count == 1) paths, both dtypes, with
  tolerances derived from each path's rounding structure;
* explicit V7/V8 (128x64) no-split coverage at M=512, N=25600, K=6656
  (repeatability + FP32 reference, both dtypes; routing asserted via a
  replica of the k_split heuristic);
* test hygiene: repo-standard `dist_init` fixture (no `__enter__` leak,
  no hardcoded MASTER_PORT).

On a locally restored legacy-CAS build, 8 tests fail (7 repeatability +
the scalar-bf16 reference check at max_abs 0.30 vs 0.10 tolerance,
measured on the then-20-test suite); on this PR, 24/24 pass.

## Validation

- W7900D / gfx1100, ROCm 7.14 runtime, torch 2.14; upstream base
  `40b2f62061575905aaac8bc360eaea62a4baeb67`
- targeted tests 24/24 PASS (bf16 + fp16, scalar + WMMA, incl. V7/V8
  no-split)
- FP32-reference correctness + A/B legacy control: see above
- benchmark matrix: dtype × M{1,8,16,64,128,512} × N{4096,25600} ×
  K{4096,6656} with path/k_split/scratch per row (full evidence package
  below)
- independent RX 7900 XT evidence from @cadamcat (A/B table in #50603)
- full W7900/gfx1100 reproducibility package (environment, correctness
  and A/B-control evidence, complete benchmark tables):
  https://github.com/AIwork4me/vllm/tree/evidence/pr-54706-jartx-w7900/validation-54706-jartx-w7900
- Muse eager ctx512: 1 unique / 8 greedy generations; 0
  same-input/different-output events across 16,640 intercepted W4A16
  GEMM calls

## Scope

gfx11 / RDNA3 W4A16 only; no attention-routing changes. The residual
Muse eager/8192 divergence after this fix was traced to ROCm paged
attention V-cache tail consumption and is fixed by #53856. Investigation
trail: #50603; full earlier evidence in the
`validation-50603/rdna3-w4a16-upstream-cleanup` tree linked there.

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used for code iteration, validation orchestration, and
drafting. I reviewed the final diff, kernel behavior, test results,
performance data, and evidence and can explain the change end to end.




---

## Rebase validation (2026-09-09, post-#54809)

title: [Perf][MRV2] Keep padded prompt-tail verification on FULL CUDA graphs
body:
## Purpose

Keep eligible padded prompt-tail verification batches on FULL CUDA graphs in Model Runner V2, including the first autoregressive draft pass.

After a decode worker obtains cached prompt KV, a request can have exactly one prompt token left. With K speculative tokens, the scheduler pads that tail to `1 + K` positions with reject-only `-1` drafts. `has_prefill` remains true, so the current uniform-decode classifier rejects this batch even though it has the full verifier layout. This also takes co-batched running requests off the FULL graph path.

This change recognizes that case without changing `has_prefill` or prompt input preparation:

- Infer the complete, uniform verifier layout directly from `SchedulerOutput`: each row must schedule `decode_query_len > 1` tokens with exactly `num_scheduled_tokens - 1` draft slots. Together with the existing `has_prefill`, this identifies scheduler-padded prompt tails without reconstructing prompt/computed lengths or scanning draft token values. Async running decodes can also use `-1` placeholders, so sentinel values alone are not a padding signal. This also admits a one-token uncached prompt when the scheduler pads it alongside running decode.
- Derive the width from the speculative configuration; there is no Hy4/model-name, K=3, cache-dtype, attention-backend or TP1 whitelist.
- Require explicit drafter support. Preserve the existing behavior for recurrent/attention-free models, Q-only draft paths, multimodal/encoder-decoder targets, PCP, PP>1, adaptive verification and multiple bonus tokens.
- Extend `get_uniform_decode_token_count` with the keyword-only `is_padded_prompt_tail` flag. Target and drafter use this same classifier; it still requires uniform shape, even when the validated flag is true.
- Carry only the validated boolean on `InputBatch` to the first autoregressive draft pass, rather than duplicating the padded query length or overriding the classifier result. It reuses the target's DP synchronization, so reclassifying it independently as prefill would trigger `reusing a DP sync taken over a different batch`. Existing graph availability and cross-rank agreement remain authoritative.

### Relationship to existing work

Open-PR searches covered `prompt tail`, `has_prefill graph`, `padded cudagraph`, and `54102 in:body`.

- #54102 addresses related residual-padding/sentinel correctness and adds a verifier-topology **rejection** guard. It does not remove the `has_prefill` veto or change autoregressive draft dispatch. Executing its added guard on the reproduced complete tail layout leaves `uniform_tok_count=None` unchanged. This PR does not incorporate or claim to fix its scheduler/sentinel issues.
- #55126 already supplies padding for an idle decode worker with cached context; the runner-side fallback remains.
- #54810 is an opt-in cached DP execution-contract/scheduling-policy change. This PR neither caches DP agreements nor defers prompt work.

## Test Plan

Base: upstream `1ea7c63f4af7bb4fd6f025c8db44434ab274cb51`.

The three affected existing pytest suites cover fixed draft widths 1/2/3/5/8, isolated and mixed prompt tails, incomplete/nonuniform verifier layouts, genuine short prefills, unsupported drafter capabilities, and the actual autoregressive `propose()` -> DP-dispatch assertion/reuse behavior.

The padding regressions call the real `GPUModelRunner.execute_model()`, request-state gathering, and CUDA graph dispatch. They assert FULL selection for idle-to-tail and tail-with-running-decode batches across K=1/2/3/5/8, async decode placeholders and scheduler-padded one-token uncached prompts. They require fallback for same-shaped real prefills (including those mixed with async `-1` placeholders), incomplete drafts, nonuniform verifier widths, recurrent targets and K=0, and check unchanged prefill state and propagation of the padding flag to the drafter's input batch. GPU input/attention preparation is stubbed so the regression needs no model weights or graph capture.

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --import-mode=importlib \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1 -v \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dynamic_sd_cug.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_autoregressive_speculator.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_ordering.py
```

For pytest, the complete upstream Python source tree with this PR was overlaid on the installed local nightly in a disposable container, retaining its compiled extensions and using a uv virtualenv with system site packages. This includes the new upstream modules required to import the actual runner. `--import-mode=importlib` prevents the unbuilt source checkout from hiding the image's compiled extensions. This is not a clean rebuild of all current-main binaries.

## Test Result

Pre-commit passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX and test-tethering checks. All three pytest files passed, including the runner-level cases and shared-classifier shape/padding checks: **68 passed, 14 warnings in 31.83s**.

### Hy4-preview GPU experiment

These serving measurements precede the shared-helper refactor and scheduler-output simplification. The current implementation is covered by the runner/drafter and shared-classifier regression tests above; the full serving experiment has not been rerun for these follow-ups. The simplified classifier relies on the scheduler's complete verifier-layout contract and additionally admits scheduler-padded one-token uncached prompts alongside running decode.

Tested on September 22, 2026 with real **Hy4-preview-FP8** weights on **8 GB300 GPUs across two nodes**. Runtime: local ARM64 nightly `0.29.1rc1.dev452+g3df4ae153`; image manifest digest `sha256:a17c15e30254f83adadcf1d9b85db18c59ea1e76a1aca1db8db20c3a12b48ba2`.

Configuration: MRV2, TP1/DP8/EP8, DeepEP v2, MTP3, `FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, FP8 KV (backend-normalized to `fp8_ds_mla`), prefix caching disabled, max 4 requests/rank, 2048 batched tokens, max model length 300032. `FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, capture token sizes `[4,8,12,16]`.

Both arms ran in the same model processes with the same captures and weights. A diagnostic switch enabled/disabled this admission exception; target dispatch was traced per rank. Both arms also included an independent Sparse-MLA capture prerequisite in `v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py`: during stream capture, run top-k index conversion on the compute stream and bypass the side-stream readiness events. This prerequisite is not part of this PR; **the baseline is stock prompt-tail classification, not an otherwise pristine image**.

KV was supplied by `DecodeBenchConnector` with constant synthetic fill (`fill_mean=0.015`, `fill_std=0.0`). These are decode-only execution/output comparisons, **not real-KV model accuracy or NIXL transfer evaluation**.

Representative first-step trace:

```text
Both: has_prefill=true, prompt_len=4096, computed_prefill=4095,
      query_lens=[4], scheduled_drafts=[[-1,-1,-1]]
Baseline: uniform_token_count=None, graph=NONE
Patched:  uniform_token_count=4,    graph=FULL
```

| Check | Baseline | Patched |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sequential requests, six context lengths, 64 output tokens | 6/6 completed | 6/6 completed |
| Eligible prompt-tail batch executions, sequential | 6 NONE | 6 FULL |
| Mixed load, 32 requests, 64 output tokens | 32/32 completed | 32/32 completed |
| Eligible prompt-tail batch executions, mixed load | 30 NONE | 32 FULL |
| Tail batches also containing running decode requests | 18 NONE | 24 FULL |
| All per-rank target executions, mixed load | 103 NONE / 946 FULL | 0 NONE / 1191 FULL |
| Client median TPOT, mixed load | 65.20 ms | 38.43 ms |
| Client median TTFT, mixed load | 1320.32 ms | 179.14 ms |

Batch counts differ because execution latency changes request coalescing. The latency figures are **single-run observations**, not a controlled production performance claim; TTFT includes queueing and synthetic KV preparation. No inference errors or DP-reuse assertions occurred in these completed probes.

Workload: repeated synthetic prompt token ID `1000 + request_index % 32`, temperature 0, seed 123, ignore EOS, 64 generated tokens, streamed token IDs and logprobs. Sequential lengths: `[127,128,4096,4097,32768,290000]`. Mixed load: `[4096,32768,120000,290000] * 8`, concurrency 16, 0.12-second submission interval. Both modes were warmed with eight 4096-token requests before measurement.

**Output comparison and remaining work:** the first five sequential lengths matched every token and logprob (320 generated tokens). At 290K, the outputs first differed at output index 17. A preceding fixed-rank experiment also showed baseline-vs-baseline divergence at 290K; its cause is unresolved, so this is not a long-context equivalence pass. Real-KV model evaluation, long-context investigation and runtime coverage for other models/backends/distributed configurations remain outstanding. The PR remains draft.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, duplicate-work checks, regression tests, GPU experiments and this description. The commit includes attribution. Human line-by-line review and the outstanding validation are required before requesting merge; no completed human review or model-accuracy qualification is claimed here.

title: [CI][Test] Use file:// rendezvous in MoE parallel_launch to fix EADDRINUSE flakes
body:
## Summary

`tests/kernels/moe/parallel_utils.py::parallel_launch` builds its NCCL rendezvous as `tcp://localhost:<get_open_port()>`. `get_open_port()` closes its probe socket before the spawned workers' `TCPStore` binds it, so on busy CI hosts another process can claim the port in between — producing intermittent `torch.distributed.DistNetworkError: ... EADDRINUSE` failures that pass on retry.

Example: B200 FusedMoE Layer Kernels, build 90548 — `test_deepep_v2_moe` failed with `EADDRINUSE` on port 41137; main's latest run of the lane is green.

## Fix

Use a `file://` rendezvous in a `TemporaryDirectory` — no ports, no race. Same pattern the deepep-v2 config sweep already uses in `test_deepep_v2_moe.py`.

Affects all `parallel_launch` callers: `test_deepep_moe.py`, `test_deepep_v2_moe.py`, `test_deepep_deepgemm_moe.py`, `test_moonep_bf16_poc.py`.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Implement get_top_tokens() on the generic MTP drafter
body:
## Purpose

`speculative_config.use_local_argmax_reduction` is unusable with the generic MTP
drafter: enabling it does not fall back to a slower path, it fails engine startup.

```
ValueError: use_local_argmax_reduction is enabled but draft model DeepSeekMTP
does not implement get_top_tokens().
```

The reduction itself already lives in core as `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` — each
TP rank argmaxes its own vocab shard and only `(value, index)` pairs are gathered. Both
opt-in sites probe the draft model for the method and raise without it:

- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py` (V2 model runner)
- `vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py`

`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_mtp.py` has `compute_logits` but no
`get_top_tokens`, so every checkpoint that resolves to it raises. On current `main` that
is the `deepseek_v3` family — DeepSeek-V3 and R1 — on every platform:

| checkpoint `model_type` | architecture | resolved draft class | platform |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek_v3` | `DeepSeekMTPModel` | `deepseek_mtp.DeepSeekMTP` | all |
| `deepseek_v32`, `glm_moe_dsa` | `DeepseekV32MTPModel` | `deepseek_mtp.DeepSeekMTP` | XPU, CPU only |

`DeepSeekMTPModel` maps to `deepseek_mtp` in `registry.py` with no platform dispatch, so a
DeepSeek-V3 / R1 MTP drafter is this class on CUDA and ROCm alike. `deepseek_v32` and
`glm_moe_dsa` are dispatched in `vllm/models/deepseek_v32/__init__.py`: CUDA uses
`nvidia/mtp.py`, which already implements the method, and since #51915 ROCm uses
`amd/mtp.py`. So for the DSA family only XPU and CPU still fall back here. `amd/mtp.py`'s
own `DeepseekV32MTP` has the same gap, but it is a different file with its own pre-head
path and is out of scope for this PR.

This PR adds the two forwarding methods, mirroring the `compute_logits` pair already in
the file. The capability has been rolled out per model since the flag landed in #34049,
and `deepseek_v3` was never covered on any platform.

### Which checkpoints this actually reaches

Resolving real `config.json`s through `hf_config_override` and the registry on
`main@94f4170df3` (ROCm), then asking the speculator's own question
(`hasattr(cls, "get_top_tokens")`). Of the current flagship checkpoints that ship MTP
layers at all:

| verdict | checkpoints |
|---|---|
| **reached by this PR** | DeepSeek-R1-0528 (fp8 and MXFP4) |
| already had the method | GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next` → `Glm5NextMTP`) |
| still blocked, different class | DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3 (ROCm: `amd/mtp.py`); DeepSeek-V4-Flash / -Pro, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, MiniMax-M3 |

What it does not reach matters as much. On ROCm the DSA family now has its own drafter
class, as do the DeepSeek-V4 line and MiniMax-M3; on CUDA the DSA family already works
through `nvidia/mtp.py`. Kimi-K3, Qwen3.5-397B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Qwen3-Next-80B ship
no MTP layers in the checkpoints checked.

### Scope

Resolving every entry of `_SPECULATIVE_DECODING_MODELS` on `main@94f4170df3` and asking
`hasattr`, 27 of the 62 speculative architectures satisfy the guard and 34 do not, so this
flag is broadly unavailable rather than uniquely broken here. 24 of the 27 get it from
`LocalArgmaxMixin` (the EAGLE, DFlash and DSpark families, plus Qwen3.5 MTP); only
`Gemma4MTP`, `InklingMTP` and `Glm5NextMTP` write the method themselves (plus
`DeepseekV32MTP` in the CUDA-only `nvidia/mtp.py`).

This PR fixes one of the 34 rather than sweeping them, because the correct call differs
per family and getting it wrong is silent:

- `deepseek_mtp.py`'s draft layer returns `(pre-final-norm, post-final-norm)` and the
  proposer consumes the first element, so `compute_logits` — and therefore
  `get_top_tokens` — must apply `shared_head` (the final RMSNorm).
- `deepseek_v32/nvidia/mtp.py`'s layer returns the post-norm hidden in both tuple
  positions, so its `get_top_tokens` correctly applies the LM head only.

Reusing the second form in the first file does not raise; it just returns a different
draft token. The added test is built to fail in that case (see Test Result). Extending
this to the remaining families needs the same per-family check, which is better done in
separate PRs by people who can run those models.

A second commit amends the flag's own docstring. It currently says only "reduces
communication from O(vocab_size) to O(2 * tp_size)", which reads as unconditional; the
measurements below show it is a break-even-dependent trade, and low-concurrency serving
at high TP is the case where the current wording would mislead someone into enabling it.

`LocalArgmaxMixin` in `models/interfaces.py` is the right tool where it fits, and
`Qwen3_5MTP` shows it fits some MTP models: it owns a flat `self.lm_head` and its
`compute_logits` is just `self.logits_processor(self.lm_head, hidden_states)`. This class
is not like that. It has no `self.lm_head` at all — the head is
`self.layers[str(mtp_start + spec_step_idx)].shared_head.head`, chosen per draft step,
and the hidden state has to pass through `shared_head`'s norm first. The mixin reads
`self.lm_head` and applies no norm, so it cannot serve this class.

### What this cannot affect

`use_local_argmax_reduction` defaults to `False`, and every call site of
`get_top_tokens` is behind it — no site probes for the method to auto-enable anything.
With the flag off, this PR adds two unreachable methods and changes nothing.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_local_argmax.py
pytest tests/v1/sample/test_head_dtype.py   # existing coverage of get_top_tokens
```

New `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_local_argmax.py` builds a real `SharedHead`
(RMSNorm + `ParallelLMHead`) and `LogitsProcessor` on a single vocab shard and asserts
`get_top_tokens()` picks the same token as `compute_logits().argmax(-1)`, including with
a padded vocab. The norm's weight is given a non-uniform gain on purpose: the argmax is
invariant to the norm's per-row rescale, so a default all-ones weight would let a
skipped `shared_head` pass unnoticed.

End to end, on a `deepseek_v3` checkpoint (DeepSeek-R1-0528, official fp8 weights) at TP=4,
with a fresh server per run:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528 -tp 4 --max-model-len 4096 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1,
                         "use_local_argmax_reduction":true}'
vllm bench serve --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-0528 --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 288 \
  --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos --seed 1234 \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el
```

The base arm is upstream `main` with the flag off; with it on, `main` raises at engine
init.

## Test Result

Hardware for every number below: MI355X (gfx950), ROCm. Correctness and micro numbers
are at real model shapes in bf16 at TP=2 and TP=4; GSM8K and end to end are
DeepSeek-R1-0528 (official fp8 weights) at TP=4 against `main@94f4170df3`.

### Correctness

`tests/v1/spec_decode/test_mtp_local_argmax.py`: 3 passed. Mutating the patch to drop
`shared_head` from `get_top_tokens` turns 2 of the 3 into failures, so the equivalence
assertion is load-bearing rather than decorative.

`tests/v1/sample/test_head_dtype.py`: identical results with and without this PR
(7 passed, 1 pre-existing failure in the `core_model` e2e test, which downloads
`facebook/opt-125m`).

Token-for-token equivalence over a sweep at real model shapes, **TP=2**, batch sizes 1 to
1024: **agreement 1.0000 in all 20 cases**. Cross-rank tie-breaking is the part a
single-shard test cannot reach, and it agrees too. The same sweep run against a variant
that skips `shared_head` agrees on as little as **0 %** of tokens.

Before this PR, the `vllm serve` / `vllm bench` invocation above raises the `ValueError`
at engine init. After it, both workers log

```
Using local argmax reduction for draft token generation
(communication: O(2*tp_size) vs O(vocab_size)).
```

and generation completes.

### Accuracy (GSM8K)

A vocab-parallel argmax is a reduction-order change, so "the unit tests pass" does not
cover it. On DeepSeek-R1-0528, all 1319 items, 5-shot greedy: **no measurable accuracy
change on GSM8K, within the base-repeat noise floor.** Patched scores 0.9568 against
0.9530 / 0.9560 for two runs of `main` — a base-vs-base drift of 0.0030, which the
patched-vs-second-base difference (+0.0008) sits well inside. Per-sample agreement is
inside the same control range. Full table in the comment below.

### Micro benchmark

The two providers on a real vLLM process group with a real `SharedHead` and
`LogitsProcessor`, driven through the patched predictor so the only difference between
arms is the collective:

- baseline — `compute_logits(h).argmax(-1)`, what the drafter does today
- patched — `get_top_tokens(h)`

Five interleaved pairs per point, arm order alternated per pair, 300 iterations after
100 warmup, no other tenant on the box. The `delta` column is what actually matters:
both arms pay the same per-call launch overhead (~200 µs in this harness, which times
the sampling step in isolation), so the *percentage* exaggerates the cost at small batch
and the absolute difference does not.

**TP=2**, GLM-5.2 shapes (`hidden_size` 6144, `vocab_size` 154880) / DeepSeek-V3 shapes
(7168, 129280):

| batch | GLM base | GLM patch | GLM delta | DSV3 base | DSV3 patch | DSV3 delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1    |  204.2 µs | 228.4 µs |    +24 µs |  222.4 µs | 219.2 µs |     -3 µs |
| 8    |  252.4 µs | 270.7 µs |    +18 µs |  251.7 µs | 271.1 µs |    +19 µs |
| 16   |  287.4 µs | 269.1 µs |    -18 µs |  273.0 µs | 273.4 µs |     +0 µs |
| 32   |  354.1 µs | 271.7 µs |    -82 µs |  317.0 µs | 270.4 µs |    -47 µs |
| 64   |  473.8 µs | 287.0 µs |   -187 µs |  398.8 µs | 271.7 µs |   -127 µs |
| 128  |  713.5 µs | 318.1 µs |   -395 µs |  598.6 µs | 299.1 µs |   -300 µs |
| 256  | 1202.4 µs | 364.8 µs |   -838 µs |  922.6 µs | 298.7 µs |   -624 µs |
| 512  | 2166.8 µs | 535.2 µs |  -1632 µs | 1778.0 µs | 494.3 µs |  -1284 µs |
| 1024 | 4124.6 µs | 848.3 µs |  -3276 µs | 3289.3 µs | 811.0 µs |  -2478 µs |

Within-arm spread over the five pairs is ≤ 1 % for 34 of the 40 arms and ≤ 4.7 %
everywhere, and the per-pair deltas are tight (e.g. GLM bs=128: +55.2, +55.4, +55.4,
+55.3, +55.4 %).

**TP=4**, same shapes, same protocol:

| batch | GLM base | GLM patch | GLM delta | DSV3 base | DSV3 patch | DSV3 delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1    |  218.5 µs | 308.2 µs |    +90 µs |  224.5 µs | 314.0 µs |    +90 µs |
| 32   |  286.3 µs | 382.3 µs |    +96 µs |  294.7 µs | 395.2 µs |   +100 µs |
| 64   |  317.6 µs | 384.5 µs |    +67 µs |  295.2 µs | 393.3 µs |    +98 µs |
| 128  |  443.9 µs | 392.2 µs |    -52 µs |  379.6 µs | 385.2 µs |     +6 µs |
| 256  |  710.0 µs | 387.6 µs |   -322 µs |  573.1 µs | 391.7 µs |   -181 µs |
| 512  | 1322.0 µs | 385.9 µs |   -936 µs | 1003.5 µs | 386.8 µs |   -617 µs |
| 1024 | 2583.3 µs | 579.0 µs |  -2004 µs | 1854.6 µs | 488.9 µs |  -1366 µs |

So the trade is a **fixed per-step overhead — one extra small collective, ~20 µs at TP=2
and ~95 µs at TP=4 — against a gather that grows with `batch × vocab_size`.** The patched
arm is nearly batch-independent (382–392 µs across bs=1..512 at TP=4); the baseline is
not. Break-even draft batch is **≈ 16–32 at TP=2 and ≈ 128–256 at TP=4**, and it moves
right as `tp` grows because the reduction's own collective is latency-bound while the
gather it replaces is bandwidth-bound.

Being explicit about the cost: **below break-even this is a regression**, up to -41 % of
the sampling step at TP=4 bs=1 (which is +90 µs in absolute terms). A batch-size median
is a bad summary here since it just reflects which batch sizes one tabulates; the
crossover and the absolute delta are the honest statement. The flag is opt-in, so the
decision can be made per deployment, and the numbers above are what it should be made on.

Token agreement was asserted at every point before timing: **1.0000 in all 40 cases
across TP=2 and TP=4.** Cross-rank tie-breaking is what a single-shard test cannot
reach, and it agrees at both rank counts.

Communication per draft step, derived from `logits_processor.py` rather than measured:
the default path materializes a `[batch, vocab_size]` logits tensor on every rank, the
reduction gathers `[batch, 2 * tp_size]` fp32 instead.

| model | `vocab_size` | tp | batch | default | reduction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V3 | 129280 | 2 | 512 | 126.2 MiB | 8.0 KiB |
| GLM-5.2 | 154880 | 2 | 512 | 151.2 MiB | 8.0 KiB |
| GLM-5.2 | 154880 | 8 | 1024 | 302.5 MiB | 64.0 KiB |

### End to end

DeepSeek-R1-0528 at TP=4, the invocation in the Test Plan, median of three runs per arm
after one warm-up:

| metric | `main` | this PR, flag on | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s | 5764.9 | 5812.4 | +0.8 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 29.49 | 29.49 | 0.0 % |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 332.0 | 328.7 | −1.0 % |

**Flat, which is what the micro numbers predict for this point.** Concurrency 64 puts the
draft batch at 64, below the TP=4 break-even, where the reduction costs ~+70–100 µs per
step — about 0.3 % of a 29.5 ms TPOT, under the ~5 % within-arm spread of throughput.
So at this operating point the flag costs nothing measurable. The gain needs a draft batch
above break-even, i.e. higher concurrency at TP=4, or TP=2. Per-run numbers, including
mean TPOT and TTFT, are in the comment below.

title: [Bugfix][SM120][MLA] Support NoPE sparse MLA (GLM-5.3-Flash) on the FlashInfer SM120 backend
body:
## Purpose

Enable native NoPE (`qk_rope_head_dim=0`) cache writes for GLM-5.3-Flash on `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, without padding the query or allocating a synthetic RoPE tensor.

Rebased onto `a6131b0e656e18eeb3797b8856aa3dbc69efd8e5`. The former physical top-k capacity patch has been dropped: #53781 already implements it in the shared `_run_mqa_kernel`, including HiSparse paths. This PR now contains the cache-writer fix and regression tests only.

## Changes

- Accept `pe_dim` 0 or 64 for `fp8_ds_mla`.
- Preserve the existing 656-byte cache row: 512 bytes of FP8 latent, 16 bytes of FP32 tile scales, and 128 bytes of RoPE/reserved storage.
- For NoPE, do not read the empty `k_pe` tensor; zero the reserved tail. The 64-dimensional RoPE path is unchanged.
- Compare BF16 NoPE writes byte-for-byte with the existing zero-RoPE path at block sizes 64/256. Fixed slots cover a block boundary and an invalid token; explicit assertions check zero tails and untouched sentinel rows. Existing tests retain responsibility for quantization correctness.

## Dependencies and related work

FlashInfer native GLM53_NOPE support (#4802) and backend-scoped length validation (#4947) have merged. Later #5075/#5197 implementations accept the existing 656-byte padded pool through runtime row stride; this PR deliberately does not change vLLM cache allocation to compact 528-byte rows.

The validation below uses FlashInfer source revision `dc04f50c9aa3eabcdaa5feb0934edb3d85e9529a`, which includes those later changes. vLLM's default `flashinfer-python==0.6.18.post1` pin does not provide native GLM53_NOPE support: this writer change alone does not make the default pinned stack sufficient. No dependency bump is bundled here.

This is the existing native-kernel alternative to the padding approaches in #53969 and #55778, not a new duplicate PR. Native NoPE avoids manufacturing a 64-dimensional query/RoPE lane. Credit to @hamiltongaianimd for originally surfacing the kpool width issue; that part is now handled upstream. The independent warmup changes in #55264 are not included.

## Fresh validation

Hardware/model: 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, TP4, NVIDIA `GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4`, BF16 activations, no speculation, text-only, max context 65536, max sequences 32, batched tokens 4096, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA graphs. Logs confirm `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120` and `fp8_ds_mla`, not the community B12X attention backend.

- `pixi install --locked --all`: passed, rebuilding the CUDA extensions.
- `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 inferlab run -- python -m pytest vllm/tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py vllm/tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py -k 'concat_and_cache_ds_mla or sm120' -q -rs`: **8 passed, 3 skipped** after test simplification (existing unsupported-rank/input-size cases).
- Repository pre-commit hooks: passed, including Ruff, clang-format, mypy, SPDX, and test tethering.
- The final cleanup changes only comments and tests; runtime code is unchanged from the serving validations below. Those full serving runs were not repeated for the cleanup.
- Managed smoke completion: HTTP 200 with coherent output; CUDA graph capture succeeded. The smoke recipe initially reported cleanup verification too early; a subsequent managed stop verified all GPUs freed.
- Full GSM8K, 1319 samples, strict exact match, concurrency 32, max output 2048: **0.9272175891 (1223/1319)**. Recipe and cleanup succeeded. This is fresh evidence, not a reuse of the old 0.9325 result.
- Random 8000-input/1000-output-token matrix, cold prefix cache at each level, 4 requests per concurrency unit: **252/252 requests completed, zero failed**, all six cases succeeded.

| Concurrency | Requests | Output tokens/s | Mean TTFT ms | Mean TPOT ms |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 4 | 99.09 | 1299.26 | 8.80 |
| 2 | 8 | 174.15 | 1257.75 | 10.23 |
| 4 | 16 | 281.54 | 1655.10 | 12.55 |
| 8 | 32 | 414.32 | 2140.93 | 17.15 |
| 16 | 64 | 559.25 | 2949.53 | 25.61 |
| 32 | 128 | 706.52 | 4500.77 | 40.64 |

### Validation limitation: distributed autotune

The unmodified all-operator autotune configuration did **not** pass startup. Leader-only sparse warmup populated rank-local tuning entries; the later distributed pass showed asymmetric cache hits and follower Gloo all-reduce timeouts. Skipping only dense `fp4_gemm` exposed the same pattern in CUTLASS MoE GEMM1, whose cache keys include `tp_rank`.

Successful serving/evaluation/benchmark runs explicitly used:

```text
VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_SKIP_OPS=fp4_gemm,trtllm::fused_moe::gemm1,trtllm::fused_moe::gemm2
```

FlashInfer autotune otherwise remained enabled. This is a disclosed validation workaround, not an autotune fix or a claim that the original configuration passes. These performance numbers are specific to this configuration. No warmup workaround code is included in this PR. FP16 was not qualified; a separate scale-conversion issue also reproduces with the existing 64-dimensional RoPE writer.

title: [Attention][Spec Decode] Multi-query Triton split-K for spec-decode verify, with empty-segment/padding hardening
body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

**Same admission mechanism as #45450 (earlier; needs rebase) and #52879 (draft):** uniform spec-decode verify batches (1+K = 2–5 tokens/request) run on the Triton 3D split-K kernel instead of 2D, with scratch indexed per query token. This PR adds split-K hardening for empty tiles/segments and CUDA-graph padding.

At width ≤ 5 on global layers (except SM100 head-256) #45450 and this PR launch the same 3D config (A5000: 698.0 vs 700.6 µs), and #52879 as published matches this PR on MiniMax below: the speedups come from the shared admission. Verified differences: correctness hardening (claims 2–4; GPU repro vs #45450's path) and broad SM120/H100 E2E evidence. We are happy to consolidate into whichever PR maintainers prefer; comparison and proposal in #52049. #57409 edits the same scratch/`use_3d` hunks.

## Claims

1. **Speed (shared mechanism):** Llama-3.1-8B EAGLE3 16k c1 +91.5% tok/s (SM120), +145% (H100) (random prompts, AL ~1.0: verify-cost cut; spec still ~0.9× non-spec); Gemma-4-26B-A4B MTP c1 +22.1%; MiniMax-M3 EAGLE3 c12 1.84× tok/s/GPU vs admission reverted. Non-spec: -1.3 to +1.9%.
2. **Empty-tile/segment fix:** main's `softmax_step` clamps a fully masked tile's -inf running max to 0, so later tiles underflow when all valid logits are very negative; now 0 is only the `exp` shift. `reduce_segments` excludes empty/unvisited segments from the max and rescale. A5000 repro (width 5, seq_len 242, GQA 8, valid logits ~-200): #45450's 3D path returns 0 for a query row (ref 0.1465); this PR matches. The masked-tile test gives NaN with main's/#52879's helper. Latent (not seen E2E); non-spec rows change only after a fully masked tile (rounding-level unless underflowing).
3. **Padding/capture:** the reducer returns early for CUDA-graph padding rows and `seq_len <= 0`; uniform verify graphs capture with `seq_len` = width (main: 1, i.e. negative context). Without them, capture-warmup rows are NaN (discarded; no replay failure shown).
4. **Narrower admission, launch checks:** 3D only for CPU-verified uniform decode (same width 2–5, not prefilling, causal, no per-seq causal/mm_prefix, adaptive verification off); scratch checked at launch (rows, dims, fp32, device, contiguity) with 2D fallback. #45450/#52879 admit any max query len ≤ 1+K (no failure shown).

## Validation

Predeclared rules: accuracy |Δ| ≤ max(2 pt, 2 SE) (4 pt floor at n ≤ 200); perf: every cell tok/s ≥ -3% and TPOT p50 ≤ +3% (mean of 2 GPU-swapped reps); 0 request errors, no NaN/IMA. Arms: main 8c87c333 vs + this PR's 3 files (tested bytes also had the removed width-6 branch, inactive at K=3).

**Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct + `yuhuili/EAGLE3-LLaMA3.1-Instruct-8B` K3**, TP1, `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN` (drafter too), `--max-model-len 20480`, prefix caching on, default T=0.6; `vllm bench serve` random 1024|16384 in/256 out, `--ignore-eos --seed 0`, c1/4/16/64; RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) and H100:
- GSM8K-1319 (`tests/evals/gsm8k`, 5-shot, T=0): 5 A/B pairs incl. H100 V1 runner, |Δ| ≤ 0.53 pt (tol ~3.3).
- 31/32 cells pass. Spec c1/c4: SM120 1k +11.3/+6.6%, 16k +91.5/+71.2%; H100 1k +17.8/+12.3%, 16k +145/+113%. Non-spec -1.0 to +0.3%.
- **FAILED: SM120 spec 16k c64, -5.3% tok/s, TPOT +12.6% (reps +9.1/+16.1%).** Diagnosis (verdict stands): reused seed-0 prompts; PR arm had lower prefix-cache hit rates (0.39/0.34 vs 0.42/0.44). Caching off, 4 GPU-swapped reps: +0.2% tok/s, TPOT +1.1%.

**Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it MTP K3** (mixed head dims, SWA), SM120, both arms `--moe-backend triton`:
- 1k/256 c1/c8: spec +22.1/+2.1% tok/s; non-spec -0.1/-1.3% (TPOT +2.4%). GSM8K-200, NIAH-8K (100/100) equivalent.
- Long context, caching off, random 8k|16k in, c4/8/16: 11/12 cells pass; other spec cells +5.3 to +14.1% tok/s; non-spec -0.1 to +1.9%; GSM8K-200 chat 98.5 vs 98.0.
- **FAILED: spec 8192/c16, TPOT p50 +15.3% (23.49 → 27.08 ms; reps +17.2/+13.3%), tok/s -0.8%.** Post-hoc diagnosis (not a gate): server-default T=1.0 sampling; PR-arm acceptance length lower there (1.96 → 1.75), median ITL lower for the PR in every predeclared spec cell. 2 more pairs: default sampling TPOT -1.3%/+4.0%, greedy -4.9%/-8.9%.

**gpt-oss-120b EAGLE3 K3** (sinks, SWA), SM120: c1/c8 +3.6/+1.3%. **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 MTP K3** (hybrid), H100: +7.7/+0.4%. Accuracy equivalent. Not bit-identical to 2D (Gemma T=0: 20–24/200 identical across arms, 82–90 within).

**MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 + EAGLE3 K3, TP4×PP2, 8× RTX PRO 6000**, c12 agentic-trace replay (not public), synthetic acceptance 2.83, on main 213c379 + #57197 + FP8 Triton indexer (as #47665) + #56151/#56147 (no measured effect). tok/s/GPU, 1 run unless noted: this PR 5203.7 (afffcfc6 5122–5213, 3 runs); admission/scratch reverted 2833.2; all stack speed paths off 2775–3190 (2 runs); #52879 as published 5152.6, + this PR's softmax/reducer fixes 5239.6.

**Tests** (+398 lines; CI: L4 kernels/attention, H100/B200 v1/attention). This tree, SM120, `pytest` on both test files: 1636 pass incl. all 48 PR-added; 290 `use_td*` fail identically on base. pre-commit incl. mypy passes. No upstream CI yet.

## Details

**Since afffcfc6** (production +12/-25; vs 8c87c333: +104/-16, tests +398/-7):
- Removed the SM120 single-request width-6 special case; width ≥ 6 uses 2D.
- Scratch last-dim check `>=` (afffcfc6's `==` disabled main's q=1 split-K on Gemma-4's smaller-head layers, by inspection).
- SM100-family head-256 multi-query keeps its tuned 2D path.

**Tradeoffs**
- SM120 c64 (2D in both arms), caching off: TPOT ~+1% (1k: +0.5 to +1.7% in 4/4 paired reps; 16k +1.1%); 1k cache on +2.9% (equal hit rates). H100 1k c64 caching off -0.9%.
- q=1 operator latency (older revision): +0.17–5.53% (16/16, 2.12% geomean), not attributed.
- No window-relative segmentation (#45450 has it). A5000 SWA layer, width 5, 27k ctx, window 1024: 1 seq 83.4 µs vs 2D 85.5 (#45450 44.1); 8 seqs 309.6 µs vs 2D 210.0 (#45450 276.5). Predicted Gemma-4 per-step (ITL) slowdown not observed (above).
- V1 full graphs (replayed by token count) may run a 1+K-token prefill chunk on 3D (same causal kernel).

**Not validated:** ROCm/XPU; E2E on SM80/89/100 or at widths 2/3/5; R-SWA, kv_sharing_fast_prefill, DFlash, DiffKV, INT4/TurboQuant, mm_prefix/VLMs; #52049's 31B model; current main.

title: [Bugfix] Unify device-pointer tensor storage to uint64 for Mamba spec-decode
body:
## Why

Per the convention proposed in #50834, device pointers stored in tensors (`data_ptr()` values) are semantically unsigned 64-bit and should use `torch.uint64` instead of `int64`, which silently overflows/wraps for
addresses `>= 2**63` (observed on XPU USM pointers).

This PR only covers `MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.state_base_addrs` /`block_table_ptrs` in  `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py`: switch them to `torch.uint64` and drop the `_reinterpret_u64_as_i64` int64 bit-pattern workaround, assigning `data_ptr()` directly.

## ⚠️ Do not merge until CUDA's pinned torch reaches 2.14

torch's element-wise tensor `__setitem__` overflow-checks the assigned Python int as a signed `long long`, even when the target tensor is `torch.uint64` (pytorch/pytorch#191458), so `state_base_addrs[idx] = state.data_ptr()` will raise `
OverflowError:  Python int too large to convert to C long` for real device pointers
`>= 2**63` 

torch version that doesn't include the upstream fix (pytorch/pytorch#191604, not yet released). XPU has already moved to torch 2.14, which includes the fix, so this works there today; CUDA is still on torch 2.13 and does not have it. Merging now would break Mamba spec-decode on CUDA whenever a state tensor's device pointer happens to
have its top bit set.


## Tests

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py` ->
  8 passed, 35 skipped (run on XPU + torch 2.14; **not yet validated on
  CUDA**, blocked on the torch upgrade above)
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on changed files: passed

title: [Feature][Core] Warn when estimated decode coverage exceeds CUDA graph capture size
body:
## Purpose

Add an early warning when estimated decode-token coverage exceeds the CUDA graph capture limit. This is a usability and observability improvement, not a kernel bugfix.

CUDA graphs can be enabled while a decode batch is too large for the captured graphs. In that case, execution can fall back to eager kernel launches without a clear explanation of the performance cost. With speculative decoding, each resident request contributes multiple verification tokens, making it easy to overlook the mismatch between request capacity and graph-token coverage.

Diagnosing such a slowdown can require checking configuration, investigating cache behavior, comparing speculative and ordinary decoding, and profiling graph dispatch. A startup warning could point users directly to the capture limit and save substantial debugging time. This PR makes that risk visible without changing execution behavior.

## Change

After cache initialization and warmup, estimate short-request residency using the resolved cache pool and supported cache-group requirements:

```text
q = uniform_decode_query_len
blocks/request = Σ Mamba(1 + num_speculative_blocks)
               + Σ full-attention ceil(q / block_size)
residents = min((num_blocks - 1) // blocks_per_request,
                max_num_seqs, max_num_batched_tokens // q)
decode_coverage = residents × q
```

Warn once if this estimate exceeds the resolved capture cap. The message includes the estimated residency, query width, block accounting and capture limit, and recommends checking observed batch sizes and available memory before increasing `--max-cudagraph-capture-size`.

As a purely hypothetical example, 200 resident requests with five speculative tokens each need 1,200 verification tokens. A 1,024-token capture limit would not cover that batch. All numeric examples and regression fixtures in this PR are synthetic; no deployment measurements are included.

The warning and its limitations are documented in `docs/configuration/optimization.md`.

## Scope and related work

This is a short, unshared-request estimate, not a guaranteed peak. Prompt length, prefix sharing, dynamic speculation and alignment can change actual occupancy. Unsupported layouts are skipped. The warning does not change scheduling, allocation, capture sizes or model outputs, and does not detect every compatibility gap below the scalar cap.

Related upstream draft: vllm-project/vllm#51509 inspects graph-compatible shapes against configured scheduler limits and dynamic speculative widths. This PR estimates residency from the resolved physical cache pool rather than assuming every configured request slot can be resident. That avoids recommending capture coverage for request counts the cache cannot support under the stated assumptions. It deliberately does not replace the existing proposal's compatibility or dynamic-width checks; the two approaches could be combined. This is submitted as a cache-accounting alternative for maintainer review, with the overlap explicitly acknowledged.

## Test Plan

Run the focused warning regression tests and repository pre-commit checks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  -k 'cache_resident_decode_graph_warning or decode_graph_warning_skips' -q
pre-commit run --files tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py \
  vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py vllm/v1/engine/core.py \
  docs/configuration/optimization.md
```

## Test Result

- 20 isolated regression cases passed using the exact helper and test functions with lightweight configuration/cache containers. The synthetic cases cover speculative widths, cache group counts, scheduler limits, equality, reserved-block accounting, disabled graphs and unsupported layouts.
- Applicable repository pre-commit checks passed, including formatting, lint, documentation checks and the configured type-check hook.
- Native upstream pytest collection remains blocked locally by missing dependencies. The isolated checks do not validate engine integration.
- No model evaluation was performed for this logging-only change. Full integration testing remains pending.

## AI assistance and review status

OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, validation and PR preparation. The submitting author confirmed reviewing every changed line and running relevant tests. The automated validation and its integration limitations are reported above. Commits include AI attribution and the author's DCO sign-off.

title: fix(parser): keep fenced code examples out of qwen3 tool calls
body:
keep fenced code examples out of qwen3 tool calls

Fixes #57541

## what happens

qwen3 models document the tool call format inside markdown fences. the parser has no fence state at all, so it reads the example XML as a real call header and emits a phantom bash tool call while swallowing most of the answer text

the reporter measured it at chunk sizes 1, 7 and 10000, all agree. on v0.29.0 and on the #56661 backport the content comes back as 59 of 149 chars and the parser reports a tool call named Bash that the model never made. i reproduced it verbatim on master at 4c6c1a4 with their CPU-only snippet, same output, no gpu needed

## the fix

a FENCE terminal on the qwen3 config plus a FENCED engine state. a fenced span runs from the first ``` to the next ``` and everything in between is emitted as plain text, streaming and non streaming

- (CONTENT, FENCE) enters FENCED and re-emits the fence itself as text
- (FENCED, FENCE) returns to CONTENT the same way
- FENCED has no tool transitions, so XML inside it can never promote
- an unterminated fence settles back to CONTENT in finish(), it never turns into a call

```xml
<tool_call>
<function=Bash>
<parameter=command>ls -la</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

stays exactly the text you see there. a real call right after a fenced example still parses, and backticks inside a parameter value never open a fence (TOOL_ARGS content is untouched)

## why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- search for PRs referencing #57541: 0 hits
- #56658 and #56661 fix a different case, a bare <tool_call> in prose with no fence. the reporter measured their case still broken with #56661 applied
- no open PR touches fenced example handling (157 open qwen3 and parser PRs scanned by title and by fence keyword searches)

## why engine/ changed

the vllm/parser AGENTS.md says keep model fixes in the model file and change engine/ only when the behavior is wrong for every parser. the fence semantics live in the shared state machine: FENCED is a new ParserState with a default content_events row, and finish() normalizes it like the other non-final states. without the state in engine/, the FENCE transitions cannot exist in a declarative config

## tests

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/test_qwen3_fenced_examples.py -q
# 8 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/parser/engine/ tests/parser/test_parse.py tests/parser/test_streaming.py tests/parser/test_include_reasoning.py tests/parser/test_harmony.py -q
# 4447 passed
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/ -q -k qwen
# 88 passed, 2 skipped
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/reasoning/ -q
# 432 passed
.venv/bin/ruff check <changed files>      # clean
.venv/bin/ruff format --check <changed files>   # clean
.venv/bin/mypy <changed source files> --ignore-missing-imports   # Success
```

the new tests cover the reported case non streaming and streaming at chunk sizes 1 and 7, full text equality, the unfenced promotion staying intact, a real call after a fenced example, backticks inside a parameter value, and a fenced example right after </think>

no model evaluation was run. the change is parser level, the serving-level effect is that text the model meant as documentation stays in content instead of becoming a tool call. the reporter's serving validation showed the same defect through the full serving stack

title: [Profiler] Add per-session profiling controls to Python and Rust frontends
body:
## Purpose

Implement the Part D frontend/API split from #56542 on top of #57460.

`POST /start_profile` now accepts three optional per-session controls in both Python and Rust frontends:

- `profile_prefix`
- `delay_iterations`
- `max_iterations`

The same options are available through the Python `LLM` and `AsyncLLM` APIs. Worker profiler wrappers remain reusable across sessions while each session can select its own output name and iteration bounds.

For reviewer, main behavioral/logic changes are in
- `wrapper.py`: per-session overrides, output names, duplicate start handling
- `async_llm.py`: frontend CPU-profiler handling
- `api_router.py`: request parsing/validation and backwards compatible dispatch
- `gpu_worker.py`: validation + applying overrides
- `routes/profiles.rs, state.rs`: rust side equivalent of API/session handling

## Reviewed behavior and compatibility

- Unknown request fields are ignored so `vllm bench serve --profile` completion-shaped payloads remain compatible.
- A second start before an explicit stop returns HTTP 409 instead of silently discarding the new options. Notably this is different from previous behavior (allows duplicate start, 2nd start is ignored if profiler is running). I think once we introduce per-session overrides, this convention makes more sense.
- Iteration bounds apply to worker profiling. The frontend CPU profiler runs until `/stop_profile`, which remains required after worker auto-stop.
- New worker RPC arguments are keyword-only and sent only when supplied, preserving ordinary calls to out-of-tree workers.
- `ProfilerConfig.should_profile_frontend` centralizes frontend eligibility for Torch CPU activity.
- Profile prefixes are validated consistently by the Python and Rust frontends.
- the summary table `profiler_out_{i}.txt` also uses the prefix so output from later sessions doesn't override previous ones.

## Duplicate-work assessment

- This is the followup (Part D, frontend + api server changes) of #56542 after #57460 merged.
- It supersedes the Python-only iteration-control work in #35340 by adding Rust parity, prefix validation, compatibility tests, and overlapping-session handling.
- It differs from #51974, which proposes arbitrary backend profiler kwargs; this PR exposes only the typed prefix and iteration controls requested in #55207 and supports both frontends.

title: [Bugfix][Engram] Reject offloaded tables larger than host memory
body:
## Purpose

With `cpu_offload=True` (the default), each rank pins its shard of the Engram tables in host memory (`torch.empty(..., device="cpu", pin_memory=True)`). Nothing checks that the node can hold them before allocating. The per-rank view is also misleading: all TP ranks of an engine pin their shards inside the same container, so the node needs the **whole** table.

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`engram_num_embeddings=[384006168, 384016682]`, `head_dim=256`) the tables come to 188.8 GiB. At TP8 each rank asks for only 23.6 GiB, which looks fine against, say, a 55 GiB pod limit. Once all eight ranks allocate, the container is OOM-killed during worker init with no hint about the cause or the fix.

This adds `EngramConfig.verify_host_memory()`, next to the existing `verify_*` methods, and calls it from `DeepseekV4Model` right after the `/dev/shm` sharing decision (a fallback from `/dev/shm` is exactly what puts the tables on the per-rank pinned path). The check:

- computes what **this node** pins: a full table per local DP replica, or the local share when `embedding_across_dp` shards one table over DP;
- raises only when that exceeds a hard limit (the cgroup limit, or physical RAM when that is lower or there is no cgroup). Pinned memory cannot be reclaimed or swapped, so such a request can never succeed. The error gives the size and suggests `--engram-config '{"cpu_offload": false}'`;
- otherwise hands off to the existing `check_cgroup_memory_available`, which only warns, because current usage may be reclaimable.

It skips GPU-resident tables and `dp_shared_memory`, since `can_share_engram_tables` already checks `/dev/shm` for the latter. It also moves the table-size formula into `engram_table_bytes()` so the `/dev/shm` check and this one share it.

It assumes an engine's TP ranks share one node, which is how Engram is deployed today.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/config/test_engram_host_memory.py
ruff check / ruff format --check on the changed files
```

The tests fake cgroup and physical limits. They cover: the whole table is rejected even though one TP8 shard fits; physical RAM is used without a cgroup; the tighter of the two limits applies; a table that fits goes to the soft check; each local DP replica pins a full table; `embedding_across_dp` pins only the local share; nothing is checked for GPU-resident or `/dev/shm`-backed tables.

## Test Result

- `8 passed` on `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` with the changed config module overlaid.
- As a control, a mutant that checks only one rank's shard (the per-rank view) fails 5 of 8.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`: clean.
- Context: we hit this on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120) serving DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP8 under a 55 GiB pod limit, and currently run with `cpu_offload: false`.

AI assistance was used to write this patch and its tests. The tests above were run as described.

title: [Bugfix] Capture prefill kernels for mixed FULL graphs
body:
- Give mixed FULL graph capture a query-length bound covering the entire token batch so prefill kernels are captured with sufficient coverage.
- Preserve explicit variable-length and uniform decode bounds in both the target-model and autoregressive speculator capture paths.
- Add regression coverage for mixed, piecewise, and decode-only capture metadata, including speculative warmup and capture.
- Pass the selected attention backend to both test engines, use matching partition settings, and avoid mutating shared backend configuration.
- Filter unsupported platform/backend combinations, pair the existing FlashInferMLA case with an MLA model, and give each configuration a descriptive test ID.

The MI250 fullgraph mirror in PR #56679 exposed 44 failures and 40 setup errors in [Buildkite build 90563](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90563/list?jid=01a0cc36-f74d-4555-8660-a33c414768ac&tab=output). The fixture ignored backend selection and admitted NVIDIA configurations on AMD, while shared V2 capture inferred query lengths from one-token dummy requests and omitted prefill work needed during mixed FULL replay.

title: [KV-Offloading][TP] : Expand replicated_layout detection to multi-group MLA
body:
## Purpose
KV offloading for MLA models + TP need only offload KV values from one TP rank. 
This is controlled by replicated_layout determination in `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`

Building on top of @almogtavor 's work https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50667 (which was eventually closed) , this PR expand the replicated_layout check to include, 
 - SlidingWindowMLASpec
 - Multi-group MLASpec / SlidingWindowMLASpec
 models. 
 
Notably, 
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash
- deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp and 
- zai-org/GLM-5.3
fall in this category. 

### Changes:
 - in the replicated_layout check, 
   * Unwrap `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` and check that the internal layer specs are MLA
   * Check if all the layer_spec in all the Attention groups are in [MLAAttentionSpec, SlidingWindowMLASpec]
   * Additionally, check that the advertises `num_kv_heads = 1`, indicating TP sharding of KV heads is not possible. 
   * Remove the existing size check 
   ```
        and worker_kv_bytes_per_block
        == single_group_spec.page_size_bytes
        * len(kv_cache_config.kv_cache_groups[0].layer_names)
   ```
    this is critical and loosens the existing conditions on `main` . This is because the KV cache groups are flattened in the Scheduler process here https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/038cb14bd7874030e98bb6edc4b6f4efe649fff7/vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py#L2376 . 
    Specifically, the realization of the comment, 
    ```
            # All layers in the UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs have the same type,
            # so use an arbitrary one to initialize the scheduler.
    ```
    makes it impossible to compute the correct size from the KVCache groups to correctly effect this "size" sanity check. Groups such as 
```
(Worker_TP2 pid=3815418) group[2]  wrapper=UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs  (62 layer specs)
(Worker_TP2 pid=3815418)   layer=model.layers.2.attn.indexer.k_cache  spec=MLAAttentionSpec  num_kv_heads=1
(Worker_TP2 pid=3815418)   layer=model.layers.2.attn  spec=MLAAttentionSpec  num_kv_heads=1
```
    from DSV4-Flash suffer from this flattening.
