title: [MM][1/n] Paged shared memory storage for mm tensor ipc.
body:
## Usage Add the following arguments when starting vLLM: ```bash vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct \ --mm-processor-cache-type paged_shm \ --mm-processor-cache-gb 4 ``` | Argument | Description | |---------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------| | `--mm-processor-cache-type paged_shm` | Enables Paged Shared Memory caching for multi‑modal inputs. | | `--mm-processor-cache-gb 4` | Allocates a 4GB SHM pool (adjust as needed). | ## milestone - infrastructure - **mm tensor ipc** <- this pr - **mm processor cache using pshm** <- this pr - entrypoints - **improve mm processor cache** - **Multimodal RL inputs #51472** - **async mm Processor（execute in a separate group of Python processes to bypass the Python GIL.）** - **streaming video processing** - core - **enable low‑latency H2D path from SHM to GPU** - **mm encoder cache using pshm** - **async mm encoder(vit)** ## Purpose Paged shared memory storage for mm tensor ipc. 0. This compares two approaches for IPC of mm tensors: - **Paged shared memory (pshm):** mm tensor → shm → swap_blocks_batch → GPU - **ZMQ RPC:** mm tensor → ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory → GPU 1. CPU‑to‑GPU (H2D) bandwidth saturates when transferring 1 MiB blocks, so a page size of 1 MiB is a reasonable choice for shared memory storage. 2. A typical multimodal data payload is around 10 MiB, which is larger than page size of 1 MiB. Therefore, using paged shared memory for storing and transferring mm tensors is practically meaningful. 3. For payloads smaller than one page (e.g., 0.5 MiB), shared memory space is wasted, and the performance is nearly identical to that of ZMQ RPC. Hence, such small payloads offer no practical advantage. 4. Every copy operation along the mm data path introduces overhead, with dynamic memory allocation and pin memory being particularly expensive. Thus, removing the ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory steps in the ZMQ RPC path would bring significant performance gains. 5. For server memory, multi-threaded copying is needed to achieve maximum server memory throughput. We use a Numba multi-threaded copy to accelerate it. Supplement↓
### 1. CPU‑to‑GPU (H2D) bandwidth saturates when transferring 1 MiB blocks PTAL: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48936 ### 2. A typical multimodal data payload is around 10 MiB Qwen2VL outputs 10,764 patches when the input is a 1920×1080 image. Stored in bf16, this takes about 24 MiB; stored in uint8 (see #50411), it uses about 12 MiB. ### 3. For payloads smaller than one page (e.g., 0.5 MiB), the performance is nearly identical to that of ZMQ RPC. Hence, such small payloads offer no practical advantage. https://github.com/noooop/snippet/tree/main/benchmarks/pshm/h2d | Scenario | Data Path | ZMQ Usage | |----------|-----------|-----------| | **zmq** | CPU Source → ZMQ Send → ZMQ IPC → ZMQ Receive → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory → GPU | **Transfers full data payload** | | **zmq+shm (copy)** | Shared Memory → CPU Read → Clone → Pin Memory → GPU | **Control only** | | **zmq+shm (no-copy)** | Shared Memory → Zero-copy CPU Read → GPU | **Control only** | ### 4. Removing the ZMQ IPC → CPU Buffer → Pin Memory steps in the ZMQ RPC path would bring significant performance gains. https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/5ac2684976ee22c04fe0d2f968c6cf6096b383f2/vllm/v1/serial_utils.py#L416-L425 ### numba multi-thread copy ``` python benchmarks/paged_shm/benchmark_memcpy_utils.py INFO 09-23 07:23:38 [memcpy_utils.py:187] paged_shm memcpy: cores=144 numa=2 mem=2016GiB -> multithread (8 threads, subchunk=8 KiB) Buffer: 4.00 GiB Block: 1.00 MiB (4096 blocks) Iters: 512 blocks per run (512.00 MiB copied per run) Runs: 10 (best taken) Threads: 8 (MT run) Host: cores=144 numa=2 mem=2015.51 GiB numba: yes Heuristic: use_multithread()=True get_copy_threads()=8 Sub-chunk: 8.00 KiB Allocating 4.00 GiB paged buffer + 512.00 MiB staging... JIT compiling numba kernel... done. === ST vs MT (512.00 MiB per run) === Dir | Threads | Bandwidth (GiB/s) | Time (ms) | Speedup --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- scatter | 1 | 7.12 | 70.18 | 1.00x scatter | 8 | 40.01 | 12.50 | 5.62x gather | 1 | 7.20 | 69.48 | 1.00x gather | 8 | 39.26 | 12.73 | 5.46x === Summary === scatter: ST= 7.12 GiB/s MT(8T)= 40.01 GiB/s speedup=5.62x gather: ST= 7.20 GiB/s MT(8T)= 39.26 GiB/s speedup=5.46x ```
## Design Recommended review order: cache.py -> serial_utils.py -> client.py -> storage.py -> manager.py -> server.py.
Currently, a very simple transport protocol is used: - **Sender (P0) cache** (`PagedShmSenderCache`) 1. Call `open_write(item)` to allocate blocks for a given mm item. 2. async copy tensor data into the allocated SHM blocks (e.g., via `storage.write()`). 3. Call `close_write(uuid)` to finalize the write, making the item readable. - **Receiver (P1) cache** (`PagedShmReceiverCache`) 1. Call `open_read(uuid_or_token)` to acquire a read lock and obtain the block list. If the item is still being written, the call may wait (with a configurable timeout). 2. Read the data from SHM into CPU. 3. After reading, the read lock is **released immediately** by calling `close_read(token)`. This is safe because the data has been copied to the target device; any asynchronous H2D transfers should be synchronized upfront if needed. The immediate release simplifies the lifecycle and avoids extra reference counting. ### Shortcomings 1. Currently, multiple mm items for the same request are allocated separately, which can lead to [the dining philosophers problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dining_philosophers_problem). This can be resolved by a single atomic operation `open_write(items)` for multiple requests. Furthermore, `open_write_or_read` could atomically allocate new blocks for cache misses and open existing ones for cache hits in a single call. 2. When `close_write(uuid)` is called, the corresponding `uuid` is briefly set to `IDLE`, which may cause the data to be evicted before P1 can read it. To address this, `open_write` supports `generate_read_token`, which creates a read token to temporarily pin the data and prevent eviction. When P0 calls `close_write(uuid)`, it will notify any waiting P1 that `open_read(token)` can now proceed. Of course, the read token must be transferred from P0 to P1. 3. A read token can be used by multiple `open_read` calls to support tensor parallelism. When `close_read(token)` is called, the token becomes invalid and can no longer be used for `open_read`. 4. This raises a timing issue for `close_read(token)`. Due to the inherently asynchronous nature of CUDA, an H2D transfer may not have completed when the launch returns, so `close_read(token)` cannot be called immediately unless a CUDA stream synchronization is performed. Another feasible timing for `close_read(token)` is when the request is fully completed. Regardless, we must ensure that close_read(token) is called for every opened token to avoid token leaks and to keep all items pinned. 5. Currently, batching of multiple requests is performed on the CPU, which prevents the low‑latency H2D path from SHM to GPU from being utilized.
#### Performance Now you can use 100G+ of SHM as cache, and it uses the LRU eviction algorithm and is thread-safe. Currently, aside from being able to use paged shared memory storage for the MM processor cache, paged_shm cache is slightly slower compared to LRU cache and SHM cache, because it does not yet use the fastest data flow channel. Currently, batching of multiple requests is performed on the CPU, which prevents the [low‑latency H2D path from SHM to GPU](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51349/changes#r3922552107) from being utilized. Based on a copy speed of 5 GB/s, every 10 MB takes 2 ms, which would block ZMQ IPC, whereas asynchronous writes to SHM do not block ZMQ IPC. > frankly, hitting the mm processor cache only saves 4ms in this test, so we should focus on the mm encoder cache instead. ``` with paged_shm cache Mean TTFT (ms): 71.28 Median TTFT (ms): 66.09 P99 TTFT (ms): 154.55 Mean TTFT (ms): 67.92 Median TTFT (ms): 62.42 P99 TTFT (ms): 146.89 with lru cache Mean TTFT (ms): 70.57 Median TTFT (ms): 64.88 P99 TTFT (ms): 152.84 Mean TTFT (ms): 66.56 Median TTFT (ms): 61.06 P99 TTFT (ms): 145.25 with shm cache Mean TTFT (ms): 70.61 Median TTFT (ms): 65.32 P99 TTFT (ms): 151.93 Mean TTFT (ms): 66.71 Median TTFT (ms): 61.22 P99 TTFT (ms): 146.38 without cache Mean TTFT (ms): 70.13 Median TTFT (ms): 64.84 P99 TTFT (ms): 152.58 ``` 9800x3d + 4090

title: [Feature] Disk-backed PLE n-gram tables (`VLLM_PLE_DISK_OFFLOAD_DIR`)
body:
> Stacked on #53899: this branch includes its commits, so the diff shows both. The disk-offload change itself is the final commit (151 insertions, worker.py + envs.py).

**Depends on #53899** (PLE CPU offload); addresses the disk/aux-placement request in #53908.

## Motivation

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 51B-parameter n-gram table needs ~95 GB (BF16) of host RAM in the PLE offload
worker. That locks single-GPU serving to hosts with ~100+ GB of free RAM. The table is a pure
gather — each decoded token touches ~100–200 KB of rows — so its working set is tiny relative to
its size, which makes it the textbook candidate for file-backed paging. SGLang has an NVMe path
for the same table (sgl-project/sglang#36567); this is the vLLM equivalent, deliberately minimal:
no new I/O machinery, just a file-backed mapping and the kernel page cache.

## Design

`VLLM_PLE_DISK_OFFLOAD_DIR=<dir>` (with `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1`):

- At weight discovery, each `PleOffloadLayer`'s largest parameter (≥1 GiB) is swapped for a
  file-backed memory map at `<dir>/<layer>.<param>.bin`.
- **First boot**: the mapping is shared read-write; the existing shard-copy load path writes
  through it unchanged. Dirty pages flush under memory pressure, so the load completes on hosts
  with far less RAM than the table (peak incremental cost ≈ one checkpoint shard, ~750 MB).
  A completion sidecar is written after `process_weights_after_loading`.
- **Later boots**: the finished file maps copy-on-write instantly and the table's checkpoint
  shard reads are skipped — startup no longer pays the 95 GB read.
- `MADV_RANDOM` on the mapping keeps readahead from inflating RSS.
- The gather/IPC path is untouched: the parameter is an ordinary CPU tensor to the layer.

## Measurements

Single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB), NVFP4-expert checkpoint
(`primitive-ai/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-mixed-NVFP4-FP8`), BF16 table (95.4 GB), local NVMe,
kernel 6.1.0-52-cloud-amd64, 176 GB host. vllm bench serve, random dataset, 8192 in / 512 out,
`--random-prefix-len 0`, two seeds per cell (both shown as a/b).

| config | host RAM for the table | boot | tok/s @c1 | tok/s @c32 | median TTFT @c1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RAM offload (baseline) | ~95 GB anonymous | 302 s | 84.5 / 84.4 | 516.8 / 523.6 | 569 / 573 ms |
| disk, container capped 48 GB | ≤48 GB cap | 263 s | 79.4 / 76.8 | 427.0 / 435.8 | 571 / 573 ms |
| disk, uncapped 176 GB host | page cache | 303–344 s | 50.4–62.1 | 196.7–396.7 | 1807–2853 ms |
| disk, cold page cache | page cache | 404 s | 40.8 / 37.0 | 134.2 / 290.3 | 4611 / 5198 ms |
| disk, first boot (writes the file) | page cache | 504 s | — | — | — |

- Net cost of the disk path, run capped: **−8% @c1, −17% @c32, TTFT parity** against RAM offload.
- The capped configuration is the target use case (host RAM below table size) and also the
  fastest disk configuration — that inversion is real and reproduces (two boots, four seeds).
  Uncapped, the boot's own 172 GB checkpoint streaming passes through the global page cache and
  evicts the table it is about to serve, so early gathers fault back to NVMe. A container memory
  cap makes reclaim cgroup-local: checkpoint reads can only evict the container's own cache and
  the table stays resident. Deployment guidance in the docs should say to cap the serving
  container when using this flag.
- Inside the 48 GB cap, a 200-item tool-calling suite scored 78.5 with 0 request errors and
  0 truncations — within the checkpoint's published run-to-run spread (78.0–80.5). A
  generation-sanity gate passed on the first-boot and capped configurations.
- Cold-cache is the floor, not the steady state: the two c32 seeds ran back to back and the
  second recovered from 134 to 290 tok/s as gathers repopulated the cache.
- First boot writes the 95.4 GB file through the mapping while loading; later boots map it
  instantly and skip the table's checkpoint shard reads. All boot times above had the checkpoint
  at least partially page-cache-resident; a fully cold weight read adds its own time to any row.

## Notes

- `ps` RSS on the offload process counts resident file-backed pages (observed up to ~65 GB on an
  uncapped host after sustained load); these are clean, reclaimable pages, and the cgroup-enforced
  48 GB cap held for the full capped run with no OOM kill and no throughput penalty. Anonymous
  memory stays ~4 GB.
- The same mechanism generalizes to any future `PleOffloadLayer` (the swap is size-gated, not
  name-gated).

## Contribution notes (per AGENTS.md)

- **AI assistance**: this change was developed with Claude Code (AI-assisted); the submitting
  human is reviewing every changed line and owns the contribution.
- **Not a duplicate**: #53908 is an open request for exactly this placement option with no
  attached PR; #53899 (which this stacks on) provides the host-RAM offload path and does not
  touch placement. `gh pr list --search` for PLE/offload turns up only #53896 (model support),
  #53899, and this PR.
- **Tests run**: a mechanics test on the target hardware exercising first boot (write-through +
  finalize + gather), reboot (instant map + gather), and gather equivalence against the BF16
  path — all passing; plus the full serving matrix above (5 configurations, two seeds per cell)
  and a generation-sanity gate on the first-boot and capped configurations. No existing pytest
  suite covers `v1/ple_offload` yet (it lands in #53899); happy to add one there or here as
  reviewers prefer.
- **Model evaluation**: included above — a 200-item tool-calling suite inside the 48 GB cap
  scored 78.5, within the checkpoint's published 78.0-80.5 run-to-run spread, 0 errors.
- Commit is DCO signed-off.

title: [Model] Fix DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash SM120/GB10 geometry mismatch for SWA …
body:
Fixes #56461.

## Summary

On SM120 and SM121 architectures (such as GB10), DeepGEMM kernels enforce a strict hardware invariant: the number of kernel states (`num_states`) must equal 64. 

For DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, this created a geometry mismatch because the SWA cache layer block size was hardcoded to 32, and the indexer backend attempted unsupported virtual block splitting between ratio-1 and ratio-2 layers. This PR aligns the block size geometry across SWA and indexer backends on SM120/SM121 to satisfy the DeepGEMM requirement without altering the behavior on older architectures.

## Hardware and Kernel Context

- DeepGEMM SM120 kernel constraint: `num_states == 64`.
- For ratio-1 layers (`tokens_per_state == 1`): requires `kernel_block_size == 64` to yield 64 states.
- For ratio-2 layers (`tokens_per_state == 2`): requires `kernel_block_size == 128` to yield 64 states (`128 // 2 == 64`).
- SWA sliding-window cache: aligned to block size 64 on SM120/121 so paged attention allocations match the indexer's kernel state geometry.

## Changes

- SWA block size resolution (`vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py`):
  Checks platform capability family and selects block size 64 for SM120 and SM121, falling back to 32 when the platform is unavailable or on other architectures. Uses `kv_cache_spec.get_num_kernel_states` to guard against zero compression ratios.

- Indexer backend (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):
  Exposes `[64, 128]` on SM120/SM121 instead of forcing `[128, 64]`, allowing both ratio-1 and ratio-2 layers to take their required spec size directly without virtual block splitting. Added explicit layout guards naming packed and strided layouts.

- Backend capability declarations:
  Updated `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/sparse_mla.py` and `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py` to declare block size 64 support on SM120/SM121.

- Regression tests (`tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v41_block_size.py`):
  Added comprehensive tests covering block size selection across SM90, SM120, and SM121, verifying ratio-1, ratio-2, and common-size resolution paths.

## Validation

- ruff check: All checks passed with 0 errors.
- ruff format: Compliant with the 88-character limit across all touched files.
- pytest: Verified test suite passes cleanly.

title: [CPU][Perf] Add vectorized Sampler Kernel
body:
## Purpose
Add fused CPU sampling kernels (Gumbel-max + greedy argmax) to replace the expensive default random sampling pipeline (softmax → exponential → div → argmax) on CPU backends.

Profiling on s390x showed `aten::exponential_()` alone consuming **93% of sampling wall time** (~62ms out of 67ms per step at batch=16, vocab=128K). The fused Gumbel-max kernel eliminates this entirely using a precomputed noise table and single-pass vectorised argmax, achieving up to 58x speedup.

Both kernels use vLLM's portable `vec_op::FP32Vec8` abstraction, so they compile on all CPU backends (x86, arm64, power, risc-v, s390x). However,I have only benchmarked on s390x so far.

@bigPYJ1151 @fadara01 @Akashcodes732  could you run the benchmark on your  x86/arm/power and share results? If the fused kernel doesn't help I can gate it for s390x only or close this PR.

title: [EPD][Model Loader] Skip language-model checkpoint shards for `--mm-encoder-only`
body:
## Summary

`--mm-encoder-only` already skips building the language model (#30242), but the default loader still iterates every safetensors shard. This PR filters **pure LM shards** out of `hf_weights_files` using the HF weight index before any weights iterator runs: under `--mm-encoder-only`, shards are classified via `_language_model_names` plus the model’s existing `hf_to_vllm_mapper`, pure-LM shards are dropped, and resolve fail-closes (full file list) when an LM module prefix is also an HF ancestor of non-LM mapper entries. Encoder-only EPD cold start therefore avoids reading the full VLM checkpoint on prefix-match families (e.g. Kimi top-level `language_model.` / MiniCPM `llm.`, Qwen nested/flat via the mapper).

**When this helps:** Encoder-only cold start under `--mm-encoder-only` — e.g. EPD Encoder scale-out / restart, or single-Encoder bring-up & testing — by skipping LM-only safetensors I/O when the Encoder never builds the LM.

## Motivation

1. **Finding:** On **[Kimi-K3 pruned75](https://huggingface.co/mgoin/Kimi-K3-pruned75)**, even the Encoder node under `--mm-encoder-only` still had to walk/load the **full** safetensors shard set — very slow and wasteful for cold start / Encoder restart.
2. **Fix:** Index-based **LM-shard skipping** on the default loader (filter pure LM shards before iterators). Confirmed on that finding: pruned75 **96→2** shards, `Loading weights took` **683.36s → 0.31s**.
3. **Broader check:** Same mechanism validated on **original Kimi-K3**, same-series **Kimi-K2.6**, and **Qwen** (Qwen3 nested + Qwen2.5 flat, classified via `hf_to_vllm_mapper`), including `safetensors` / `instanttensor` / `fastsafetensors` where measured.
4. **Out of scope this PR (extendable):** Families whose LM module prefix is a shared HF root with non-LM weights (e.g. Molmo / Phi-4-MM / Muse with bare `model.`) are **not covered** by whole-shard skip here — fail-closed, full file list (safe). They can use the **same** mechanism later with finer non-overlapping HF prefixes or key-level filtering.

Steady GPU memory was already small under Encoder-only; the waste is **startup I/O**, not steady VRAM.

## Test Plan

Intent:

- [x] Unit: fake index filter + Qwen nested/flat + shared-root fail-closed → resolve `None` (`test_mm_encoder_only_weight_filter.py`).
- [x] Gate: filter only under `--mm-encoder-only`.
- [x] Prefix-match serve: Kimi-K3 full + pruned75 / Kimi-K2.6 → shard drop + faster load.
- [x] Qwen3-VL / Qwen2.5-VL → real shard skip via `hf_to_vllm_mapper` classification (not empty/dummy).
- [x] Load-format matrix: Kimi-K3 full + Kimi-K2.6 + Qwen3-VL × `safetensors` / `instanttensor` / `fastsafetensors`.
- [x] Out-of-scope guard: shared HF root (Molmo-shaped `WeightsMapper`) → `resolve(..., weights_mapper=...)` is `None` (full file list this PR).
- [x] Tier-2: Kimi-K3 full single-Encoder image chat → HTTP 200 + non-zero prompt tokens / no weight crash.

## Test Result

**Environment:** `--mm-encoder-only` · 1xH200 · warm NFS · vLLM **0.29.0** (patched ≡ this PR).

**Gate:** filter only when `mm_encoder_only=True`. Shared-root LM prefixes (e.g. bare `model.` with vision under the same HF root) fail-closed — full file list this PR.

| Model | Outcome | Shards | Load time | 
|-------|---------|--------|-----------|
| Kimi-K3 pruned75 | Prefix match → skipped | 96→**2** | 683.36s→**0.31s** | 
| Kimi-K3 | Prefix match → skipped | 96→**2** | **0.51s** | 
| Kimi-K2.6 | Prefix match → skipped | 64→**2** | **1.24s** | 
| Qwen3-VL-30B | Mapper classify → skipped | 13→**1** | 92.49s→**0.21s** | 
| Qwen2.5-VL-32B | Mapper classify → skipped | 18→**1** | 45.66s→**0.42s** | 

**Load format matrix** (shared `hf_weights_files` filter before each iterator — Kimi top-level `language_model.*` and Qwen nested/flat via mapper):

| Model | `--load-format` | Skip | Loaded | `Load time` | `/health` | Result |
|-------|-----------------|------|--------------------|------------|-----------|--------|
| Kimi-K3 | `safetensors` | 94/96 | **853 MiB(2/2)** | **0.73 s** | **200** | **PASS** |
| Kimi-K3 | `instanttensor` | 94/96 | **853 MiB(2/2)** | **2.52 s** | **200** | **PASS** |
| Kimi-K3 | `fastsafetensors` | 94/96 | **853 MiB(2/2)** | **0.35 s** | **200** | **PASS** |
| Kimi-K2.6 | `safetensors` | 62/64 | **899 MiB(2/2)** | **1.24 s** | **200** | **PASS** |
| Kimi-K2.6 | `instanttensor` | 62/64 | **899 MiB(2/2)** | **3.09 s** | **200** | **PASS** |
| Kimi-K2.6 | `fastsafetensors` | 62/64 | **899 MiB(2/2)** | **0.42 s** | **200** | **PASS** |
| Qwen3-VL-30B | `safetensors` | 12/13 | **2.71 GiB(1/1)** | **0.19 s** | **200** | **PASS** |
| Qwen3-VL-30B | `instanttensor` | 12/13 | **2.71 GiB(1/1)** | **8.59 s** | **200** | **PASS** |
| Qwen3-VL-30B | `fastsafetensors` | 12/13 | **2.71 GiB(1/1)** | **0.69 s** | **200** | **PASS** |

**Tier-2 functional smoke (single-Encoder):** `/health` ≠ functional proof. On **Kimi-K3** with the skip patch (`94/96` shards skipped, load **0.71s**), `POST /v1/chat/completions` with `tiny_smoke.png` (agent-generated local 64×64 solid RGB PNG via PIL) returned **HTTP 200** in **~0.79s**, `prompt_tokens=113` (text-only control **95**), `finish_reason=stop`, empty assistant content (**expected** — encoder-only does not sample LM tokens), no missing-weight / EngineDead. Serve used `--no-async-scheduling` (default async path hit a `step_with_batch_queue` EngineDead on this stack; unrelated to shard skip).



## Addressing review: hard-coded HF prefixes

Review asked to avoid a model-specific hard-coded HF nest list and a magic bare-`model.` deny set in the loader.

**Current design (this PR):**

1. **Prefix source:** `_language_model_names` only → vLLM *module* prefixes (fallback `language_model.`). No per-model override attr.
2. **HF key classification:** map each index key through the model’s existing `hf_to_vllm_mapper`, then test the *vLLM* name against those module prefixes — Qwen nested (`model.language_model.*`) and flat (`model.layers.*` via the catch-all `model.`→`language_model.model.` mapping) need no nest list in `weight_utils`.
3. **Shared-root guard:** if a module prefix (e.g. `model.`) is also an HF ancestor of non-LM mapper entries (vision under `model.vision_*`), resolve returns `None` and the file list is left unchanged (Molmo / Phi-4-MM / Muse). Detected from `WeightsMapper.orig_to_new_prefix`, not a name allow/deny set.

No global HF-prefix tuple; no magic `{"model."}` set; no `mm_encoder_only_lm_prefixes` escape hatch.

**Regression pointers:** unit 9/9 PASS; K3 safetensors 94/96 + Tier-2 HTTP 200 (pt 113 vs 95); Qwen3-VL 12/13; K3 instanttensor / fastsafetensors PASS (load Δ within noise). Live log prefixes=`('language_model.',)` confirms the mapper path.

## Approach

- Applies on `DefaultModelLoader` safetensors-file+index path (also `fastsafetensors` / `instanttensor` / `mistral` via the shared file list); other loaders untouched.
- Under `--mm-encoder-only`, derive LM *module* prefixes from `_language_model_names` (fallback `language_model.`) and capture the model’s existing `hf_to_vllm_mapper`.
- `resolve_mm_encoder_only_lm_prefixes()` returns those module prefixes, or `None` (fail-closed → full file list) when a prefix is a shared HF root with non-LM `WeightsMapper` entries (Molmo / Phi-4-MM / Muse).
- `filter_mm_encoder_only_safetensors_files()` reads the index `weight_map`, maps each HF key through the optional mapper, and drops shards whose keys are all LM-module-prefix.
- In `DefaultModelLoader.load_weights`, when multimodal `mm_encoder_only` is set, resolve prefixes + capture mapper, then apply the filter in `_get_weights_iterator` **after** `_prepare_weights` and **before** choosing `safetensors` / `fastsafetensors` / `instanttensor` iterators.
- Missing index / shared-root fail-closed / no key match → unchanged file list (safe).

## Related

- Relates to / reopens intent of #30231 (Skip LM weight load).
- Completes **I/O** side of #30242 (module skip already merged).
- Useful for EPD tracker #52409 (no prior loader/shard-filter item).

**Why this is not a duplicate:** Before opening, searched open PRs on `vllm-project/vllm` for `mm-encoder-only`, skip LM/checkpoint shard I/O, and #30231-in-body. Open hits are unrelated (encoder CUDA graph, encoder cache, lm_head quantization, etc.). No open PR applies safetensors **shard-level** filtering under `--mm-encoder-only` before weight iterators.


## AI assistance

This change was developed with AI coding assistance. A human author (grYe99) reviewed every changed line, ran the pod verification above, and is responsible for defending the design end-to-end.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Keep zero MiniMax MXFP8 activation blocks finite
body:
- Compute the finite reciprocal block scale in the fused MiniMax-M3 SwiGLU/MXFP8 kernel.
- Multiply by that reciprocal to avoid `0/0` when the byte-zero E8M0 divisor flushes to zero on CDNA, while preserving the encoded scale bytes.
- Reuse the existing mixed-magnitude/zero-block regression and the full AMD MiniMax kernel suite.

The MI355 parity run exposed NaNs in an all-zero activation block. Merged #53674 corrected the fused kernel’s scale formula but retained division by the decoded scale. The generic quantizer already uses reciprocal multiplication from merged #53110, and this change applies the same arithmetic to the fused path. Fresh searches and the related PR review found no open change covering this remaining fused-kernel defect.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted with diagnosis, implementation and validation.

title: [Kernel][GDN] Use flashinfer bf16 mm for the GDN gate projection
body:
## Purpose

The Gated DeltaNet gate projection (`in_proj_ba`) costs 112 ms of a 1494 ms decode (7.5%) on an RTX 5090 at batch size 1 with MTP speculative decoding — to produce 96 numbers per token. cuBLAS selects a degenerate kernel for its shape. Routing it to FlashInfer's `mm_bf16` drops it to 14 ms, cutting decode by 6.5%.

## Root cause

`in_proj_ba` is `[tokens, 5120] x [5120, 96]` in bf16. It stays unquantized on NVFP4/FP8 checkpoints because it matches neither quant group. At 2–4 tokens cuBLAS picks `cutlass_80_wmma_tensorop_bf16_s161616gemm_bf16_16x16_128x2_tn_align8`:

- 16x16 tiling over N=96 gives 6 tiles (grid rounded to 8 by `GemmIdentityThreadblockSwizzle<8>`), and M=4 gives one tile-row
- 8 CTAs of one warp each, on 170 SMs, each walking all of K=5120 serially
- 35.8 GB/s achieved against 1790 GB/s available — latency bound, not bandwidth bound

This is a heuristic gap, not a general small-M problem. cuBLAS is fine at 1 token (GEMV path) and at 8+ (tiled with split-K). Batch size 1 with 3 speculative tokens lands exactly in between. Confirmed with `CUBLASLT_LOG_LEVEL=5`, which shows `numSplitsK=16` chosen at 24 tokens but a plain tiled kernel at 4.

## Where the win exists

Swept over the b/a shape of **every shipped Qwen GDN model**, as `cuBLAS_us / flashinfer_us` with the `cudnn` backend this change selects (>1 means FlashInfer wins). `N = 2 * linear_num_value_heads`, `K = hidden_size`:

**RTX 5090 (sm_120, 170 SMs)**

```
model                     N      K      M=1      M=2      M=4      M=8
Qwen3.5-0.8B             32   1024     0.48     1.48     1.48     1.48
Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B       64   2048     0.64     3.52     2.50     2.92
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B          64   2048     0.56     2.65     2.53     2.56
Qwen3.5-4B               64   2560     0.88     3.46     3.51     3.80
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next       96   2560     0.84     3.04     3.14     3.51
Qwen3.8-27B              96   5120     1.59     5.96     6.15     0.80
```

**GB10 (sm_121, 48 SMs)**

```
model                     N      K      M=1      M=2      M=4      M=8
Qwen3.5-0.8B             32   1024     0.53     1.60     1.63     1.60
Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B       64   2048     0.60     2.79     2.79     2.79
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B          64   2048     0.57     2.79     2.79     2.79
Qwen3.5-4B               64   2560     0.67     2.82     3.00     3.04
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next       96   2560     0.84     3.55     3.51     3.51
Qwen3.8-27B              96   5120     1.10     6.16     6.05     1.31
```

**GB300 (sm_103, 152 SMs)**

```
model                     N      K      M=1      M=2      M=4      M=8
Qwen3.5-0.8B             32   1024     1.00     1.00     1.00     1.00
Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B       64   2048     0.99     1.05     0.95     1.00
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B          64   2048     0.90     1.05     0.95     1.00
Qwen3.5-4B               64   2560     0.95     1.09     0.93     1.06
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next       96   2560     0.95     1.13     0.93     0.96
Qwen3.8-27B              96   5120     0.95     1.04     1.00     0.95
```

**GB200 (sm_100, 152 SMs)**

```
model                     N      K      M=1      M=2      M=4      M=8
Qwen3.5-0.8B             32   1024     1.00     1.00     1.00     1.00
Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B       64   2048     0.96     1.03     1.00     0.97
Qwen3.5-35B-A3B          64   2048     0.96     1.03     1.00     1.00
Qwen3.5-4B               64   2560     0.97     1.06     1.00     0.92
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next       96   2560     0.94     1.00     1.04     1.00
Qwen3.8-27B              96   5120     0.93     1.00     1.03     0.97
```

Three conclusions:

- **Every shape wins at 2 and 4 tokens on sm_120 and sm_121** (1.48x-6.16x). Smaller K narrows the win but never reverses it.
- **All but one shape *loses* at 1 token**, by up to 2.1x. cuBLAS has a dedicated GEMV path there that FlashInfer does not beat. The routing is therefore bounded below as well as above (`_BA_PROJ_MIN_TOKENS = 2`) — without that, plain non-speculative decode would regress on five of six models.
- **Neither sm_100 nor sm_103 shows a gap** (0.90–1.13 across both). cuBLAS already selects a good kernel on datacentre Blackwell, so there is nothing to win and a little to lose. The routing is gated to the sm_12x family; **B200 and B300 are unaffected**, verified on both rather than inferred.

`2 * num_v_heads` is 96 or less for every model above, so `_BA_PROJ_MAX_N = 96` is a guard against a future wider model rather than a tuning knob, and no shipped model is near it.

## End to end

`nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`, RTX 5090, bs=1, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, 86 decode steps:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `in_proj_ba` per call | 27.2 us | 3.40 us |
| `in_proj_ba` total | 112.4 ms | 14.0 ms |
| decode | 1494.3 ms | 1397.7 ms (−6.5%) |

After the change the layer runs as `cudnn_generated_..._matMul` (2.74 us) + `splitk_reduce_contiguous_kernel` (0.66 us) — FlashInfer doing the split-K decomposition cuBLAS declines to. On GB10 the same projection goes 34.0 us -> 6.2 us per call.

## Changes

Dispatches `in_proj_ba` to `flashinfer_bf16_mm` when the token count and shape qualify, falling back to the layer otherwise. **Off by default**, gated by `VLLM_GDN_BA_GEMV_MAX_TOKENS` (default 0); 4 is the measured crossover, clamped to 32 (FlashInfer's `mm_bf16` limit). Routing additionally requires the sm_12x family, 2+ tokens and `N <= 96`, all hardcoded from the sweep above — no user override.

The size check lives in a registered custom op rather than a plain Python branch: the model is compiled via `TorchCompileWithNoGuardsWrapper`, so a shape comparison in the traced region is frozen at whatever shape the single tracing pass saw (prefill), permanently selecting one side.

Routing away from the layer skips whatever the layer would have applied, so the gate declines whenever the layer might be doing more than a plain bf16 matmul:

- a quantized `quant_method`, or a bias
- **LoRA** — adapters wrap the module *after* construction, and the fast path would compute only the base projection
- **batch-invariant mode** — it has its own unquantized kernel and a bitwise contract that routing only below a token threshold would break
- backend support is resolved through `is_flashinfer_bf16_gemm_supported`, which also keeps ROCm out (`forward_hip` can fall back to `forward_cuda`)

The concrete backend is named rather than left to `"auto"`, so this layer does not silently diverge from the configured linear backend.

The per-call shape guard reuses `bf16_mm_shape_supported` rather than restating it. Extracting that from `_can_use_flashinfer_cutedsl_bf16` leaves the cute-dsl entry behaviourally identical (it keeps its sm_10x gate) and avoids a second copy drifting — in particular the shared guard enforces FlashInfer's `1 <= m <= 32` bound.

## Why this is not a duplicate

Two open PRs touch this layer; I checked both against their branches rather than their descriptions.

**#53645 (FlashInfer fused decode for Qwen GDN)** does fold the b/a GEMV in, but only on plain non-spec decode. Its own docstring: *"Everything else — prefill, spec/MTP decode, the gated RMSNorm, the output projection — stays with vLLM."* The regime measured here is MTP spec decode at M=2–4, which that PR explicitly leaves on `self.in_proj_ba(...)`. The two compose rather than collide: this change lands in the `if not use_fi_fused_decode:` branch that PR introduces. It is additionally gated on `VLLM_GDN_DECODE_KERNEL=cuda` and on FlashInfer exposing `gdn_fused_decode_step`.

**#55260 (concat tiny GEMMs, C6)** folds `in_proj_ba` into the `in_proj_qkvz` GEMM, but two independent gates exclude this configuration:

```python
if not (current_platform.is_cuda() and self.gqa_interleaved_layout):
    return                          # Qwen3-Next layout only
if qkvz_w.dtype not in (torch.bfloat16, torch.float16, torch.float32):
    return                          # quantized qkvz (NVFP4) skipped
```

Note those two PRs require *opposite* layouts — #53645 needs non-interleaved, #55260 needs interleaved. This change is layout-agnostic and works with a quantized `qkvz`.

## Risk

- Opt-in; default behaviour is unchanged.
- Numerics shift slightly — FlashInfer accumulates split-K partials in a different order than cuBLAS. α and β feed a sigmoid, so the effect should be small.
- Benefit is batch-size dependent: at 8+ tokens the gate declines and cuBLAS is used. This helps low-batch latency and does nothing under serving load.
- The win is SM-count dependent; measured on sm_120 (RTX 5090) and sm_121 (GB10).

## Test plan

`tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_ba_proj_dispatch.py` has one case per guard. Routing bypasses `in_proj_ba`, so the tests assert that everything the layer might otherwise apply declines it — a quantized projection (parametrized over the flag both set and unset, since such a layer registers `qweight` and has no `weight` at all), LoRA, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT`, a bias, a non-2D weight, and FlashInfer present without a bf16 backend for the device. Plus the three measured bounds: sm_12x only, 2+ tokens, and `N <= 96`.

Two of them matter most:

- `test_routed_path_matches_linear` — the routed call must equal the layer it bypasses, parametrized over all five model shapes at 2 and 4 tokens. `mm_bf16` takes `b` pre-transposed, so a layout mistake would otherwise pass every eligibility test and silently corrupt output.
- `test_op_dispatches_on_token_count` — exercises the op itself with a stubbed forward context, checking 2 and 4 route while 8 defers to the layer.

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_ba_proj_dispatch.py
platform linux -- Python 3.12.3, pytest-8.1.1, pluggy-1.6.0
collected 27 items

test_gdn_ba_proj_dispatch.py ...........................            [100%]
```

Run on an RTX 5090;

Lint is clean on the changed files:

```
pre-commit run --files vllm/envs.py vllm/model_executor/layers/utils.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/gdn/qwen_gdn_linear_attn.py \
  tests/kernels/mamba/test_gdn_ba_proj_dispatch.py
```

`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos`, `mypy`, SPDX headers, forbidden imports, root lazy imports, the `torch.cuda` API check and the config-docstring validator all pass; the remaining hooks have no matching files.

Also:

- Microbenchmark and M×N sweep above, timed inside a CUDA graph (eager timing is dominated by ~5 us of per-launch CPU cost).
- End-to-end decode timings from Nsight Systems traces, above.


## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this change and this description. The analysis, profiling, measurements and review were done by me; the code has been reviewed line by line, and an earlier revision went through internal review whose findings (LoRA, batch invariance, backend capability checks, quantized-checkpoint construction, the duplicated shape guard) are incorporated here.

title: [ROCm][Model][MiniMax-M3] Context-parallel sparse lightning indexer (Triton, opt-in)
body:
## Summary

Adds context-parallel decode scoring for MiniMax-M3's sparse lightning indexer on ROCm (TP>1, opt-in).

### Problem
With TP>1, every rank independently scores the entire KV cache for the sparse indexer — redundant work scaling linearly with world_size.

### Solution
- Each rank scores only its 1/world_size shard of global KV blocks (round-robin: block = local * world + rank)
- Scores scattered into a global-shape `[heads, tokens, max_block]` tensor pre-filled with `-inf`
- MAX allreduce across TP group fills all positions from their owning rank
- `minimax_m3_index_decode(precomputed_score=...)` skips internal re-scoring and runs top-k directly

**Activation:** `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP=1` — off by default. ROCm + TP>1 only.

## Changes

| File | Type |
|---|---|
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/indexer_context_parallel.py` | New — `MiniMaxM3IndexerTritonCPImpl` |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/amd/ops/indexer_context_parallel.py` | New — Triton `_context_score` kernel |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/indexer.py` | Modified — CP dispatch in `select_indexer_impl_cls` |
| `vllm/models/minimax_m3/common/ops/index_topk.py` | Modified — `precomputed_score` param in `minimax_m3_index_decode` |
| `vllm/envs.py` | Modified — `VLLM_ROCM_MINIMAX_INDEXER_CP: bool = False` |

## Benchmark A — AgentX QoS

**Setup:** MiniMax-M3 BF16, 8xMI350X (gfx950), vLLM 0.28.1.dev0, TP=8, prefix-caching enabled
**Dataset:** semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126_256k, 300s

| Concurrency | Config | TTFT p50 | TTFT p90 | ITL p90 | tput/user |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | Baseline | 519ms | 16,087ms | 116ms | 33.3 tok/s |
| **20** | **CP Indexer** | **478ms** | 16,815ms | 146ms | 29.7 tok/s |
| 32 | Baseline | 2,956ms | 15,280ms | 132ms | 23.8 tok/s |
| **32** | **CP Indexer** | **2,626ms** | **11,964ms** | **114ms** | **24.8 tok/s** |

At concurrency 32: **−22% TTFT p90** (15.3s → 12.0s), **−14% ITL p90** (132ms → 114ms), +4% throughput/user.
At concurrency 20: TTFT p50 improves (−8%); p90 slightly worse — CP overhead vs savings near break-even at lower load.

## Benchmark B — Throughput at AgentX-representative ISL



| ISL | Baseline (tok/s) | CP Indexer (tok/s) | Delta | TTFT p99 delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|

title: [Bugfix][ToolParser] Guard against IndexError for single closed tool in required streaming
body:
## Purpose

`extract_required_tool_call_streaming` steps back to `obj[-2]` when a tool call finishes without a `"parameters"` key, assuming a newer incomplete tool call already exists in the list. That assumption breaks for a single tool call.

With `tool_choice="required"`, a lone parameter-less tool call that closes within one chunk (e.g. `'[{"name": "f"}]'`) yields `obj` of length 1. `filter_delta_text` reports `finishes_previous_tool=True`, the `"parameters" not in current_tool_call` branch is taken, and `obj[-2]` raises `IndexError: list index out of range`, aborting the stream.

## Fix

Only fall back to the previous tool call when one actually exists:

```python
if (
    finishes_previous_tool
    and "parameters" not in current_tool_call
    and len(obj) >= 2
):
    current_tool_call = obj[-2]
```

For the single-tool case, `current_tool_call` correctly stays at `obj[-1]`, and the name is emitted as expected.

## Test

Added `test_required_streaming_single_closed_tool_no_indexerror` in `tests/tool_use/test_tool_choice_required.py`, which drives the streaming extractor with `'[{"name": "f"}]'` and asserts the name `f` is returned without raising. The test fails on `main` (IndexError) and passes with this change.

title: [Bugfix][EPLB] Use group-local ranks for torch P2P transfers
body:
## Purpose

With pipeline parallelism, EPLB passes EP-group-local peer ranks to its
communicators, but the torch NCCL and Gloo backends pass them as `P2POp.peer`,
which is a global rank. For an EP group containing global ranks `[2, 3]`,
local peer `1` is therefore interpreted as global rank `1`, outside the group,
and expert-weight transfer fails.

Use `group=...` and `group_peer=...` for both send and receive in the two
torch.distributed communicators. Add a transfer regression covering PP=1 and
PP=2 with two ranks per EP group and both backends.

Duplicate-work checks on 2026-09-08 found no matching open PR in searches for
`EPLB`, `EPLB P2POp`, and `group_peer`. The related explicit EP topology PR
#52099 does not modify this communicator file.

AI assistance was used to prepare the implementation, regression, and local
validation. Backend and model validation were performed by the PR author.

## Test Plan

On a configured vLLM environment with four GPUs:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py \
  -k test_eplb_communicator_pipeline_parallel -q
```

The regression exchanges rank-tagged tensors within each two-rank EP group
and checks the received values against the global rank of the expected peer.
The four-rank case covers the nonzero-rank group `[2, 3]`.

## Test Result

The author validated EPLB with pipeline parallelism using both `torch_gloo`
and `torch_nccl`:

- Before the fix, both backends raised the following error:

  ```text
  ValueError: Global rank {global_rank} is not part of group {group}
  ```

- After the fix, tests completed successfully with both backends.
- Model evaluation after the fix: **Qwen3.6-35B-A3B**, using the **Gloo**
  backend, achieved **96.51% GSM8K accuracy**.

Additional local checks:

- Supplemental local CPU validation with PyTorch 2.14.0: both communicator
  classes were loaded from the production source and exercised with real Gloo
  process groups and real `P2POp`/`batch_isend_irecv`. Only CUDA stream contexts
  and synchronization were replaced with CPU no-ops; the NCCL class also used
  Gloo transport, so this is not NCCL device-transport validation.
- Before the fix, both classes fail in group `[2, 3]` with
  `Global rank 0/1 is not part of group`; the two-rank PP=1 controls pass.
  After the fix, all four combinations of communicator and world size (2, 4)
  transfer the expected tensor values successfully.
- Ruff 0.14.0 lint and format checks, Python compilation, and
  `git diff --check`: passed.
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/distributed/eplb/eplb_communicator.py
  tests/distributed/test_eplb_execute.py`: all applicable hooks passed with
  the Python 3.12 virtual environment on `PATH`.
- Native pytest command above: blocked during collection by missing `tblib`
  in the local macOS environment. The backend and GSM8K results above come
  from the author's separate test environment.

title: [XPU][CI] Make `test_mamba_prefix_cache` block-size agnostic
body:
## Purpose
The test requests `block_size=560`, but Qwen3-Next's linear-attention layers use the GDN backend, and on XPU those kernels only support block sizes divisible by 64, so `XPUPlatform.update_block_size_for_backend` rounds the request up to `cdiv(560, 64) * 64 = 576`:

```bash
INFO [kv_cache_utils.py:763] kv lcm block sizes 576
```
The step-action tables in the test are written as absolute token counts around a 560-token boundary (554, 557, 560*2, ...), so every case that depends on where a block boundary falls breaks. 

Since `BLOCK_SIZE` is an arbitrary hard-coded value here and the test is about where block boundaries fall relative to the in-flight speculative tokens, not about any particular block size. This PR sets it to a multiple of 64 and expresses the step-action tables relative to it.

In addition, this PR also fixes a small logging error, since `cache_config.mamba_page_size_padded` and `original_mamba_page_size_padded` can be None rather than integer. 

## Test Plan
```bash
pytest -sv tests/v1/e2e/general/test_mamba_prefix_cache.py
```

## Test Result
```bash
========== 4 passed, 17 warnings in 318.44s (0:05:18) =====
```
The tests pass both on XPU and CUDA. 

## AI Assistance 
This PR was prepared with AI assistance. I have reviewed every changed line, understand the rounding behaviour it works around, and ran the tests above myself.

title: [Perf][ROCm][Attention] Narrow the Triton prefill-attention KV tile on RDNA3/RDNA4
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #58060. On RDNA3/RDNA4, `context_attention_fwd` in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_prefill_attention.py` launches `_fwd_kernel` with a 128x128 tile for bf16/fp16, which is slow on these GPUs. This PR narrows only the KV tile (`BLOCK_N`) to 32 when `on_gfx1x()` is true. `BLOCK_M`, `num_warps` and `num_stages` are unchanged, float32 is untouched (its tile is already 32), and CDNA, gfx1250 and NVIDIA keep the existing configuration. No other open PR addresses #58060.

This kernel serves encoder / non-causal pooling, so embedding and reranking models benefit. Generation prefill and decode use different kernels and are unaffected.

## Test Plan

W7900 (gfx1100) and R9700 (gfx1201), ROCm 10.0, bf16, TP=1, stock clocks.

- `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_prefill_attention.py`, including 5 new cases that check the launch configuration with the platform predicates mocked, so CI covers the RDNA branch without an RDNA GPU.
- Kernel A/B over all 9 supported head sizes x 4 mask modes, checked against an fp32 reference.
- End-to-end A/B on gte-Qwen2-1.5B, bge-base-en and gemma-3-1b (non-causal): 24 interleaved ABBA pairs each.
- `vllm bench serve` on gte-Qwen2-1.5B embeddings at concurrency 1/4/16/64.
- SciFact retrieval accuracy, with a batching-only control run for comparison.

## Test Result

- Tests: 25/25 pass on both GPUs.
- Kernel: every cell is faster on both GPUs; median 2.56-2.67x (gfx1100) and 2.25-2.30x (gfx1201).

| | gfx1100 | gfx1201 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| End to end, embedding models | 1.10-1.23x | 1.08-1.12x |
| Serving throughput | 1.17-1.19x | 1.03-1.05x |

- Accuracy: nDCG@10 moves by -0.0001 (gfx1100) and -0.0005 (gfx1201). Changing only `max_num_seqs`, with no kernel change, moves it by +0.0011 and +0.0005. Recall@10 is identical.
- Limitations: measured on bf16, TP=1 and gfx1100/gfx1201 only. Other RDNA3/RDNA4 parts are covered by `on_gfx1x()` without being measured; the gate can be narrowed if preferred.

Developed with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot CLI) for the benchmarking, analysis and this description. I reviewed every changed line and ran all measurements myself.

- Automatically enable model SP with the existing sequence-parallel MoE configuration (`TP>1`, `DP>1`, EP enabled, and a supported all-to-all backend).

SP currently requires PP=1 and MoE layers. External LoRA adapters on SP-sharded GR/PLE projections are not supported.
