title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Retry Mooncake bootstrap registration on timeout
body:
## Purpose

Worker registration created `httpx.AsyncClient()` with no explicit timeout, inheriting HTTPX's 5s default. The bootstrap server runs inside the global rank 0 prefiller process, which also registers the Mooncake host memory segment, so a large segment blocks responses past that default. Only `ConnectError` was retried, so the resulting `ReadTimeout` was re-raised, the sender listener exited before setting its ready event, and the unbounded `ready_event.wait()` hung startup. This adds a configurable timeout, retries `TimeoutException` with capped backoff, makes `/register` idempotent for identical payloads, and bounds the readiness wait so failures propagate. Now an identical repeat registration returns 200 instead of 400 and a same-rank registration at a different address still returns 400.

Fixes #55729.

## Repro

Configuration:

```
tensor-parallel-size=2
pipeline-parallel-size=4
MOONCAKE_GLOBAL_SEGMENT_SIZE=21474836480
```

On main:
```
T+5.37s   7 worker ranks log "Error registering ... with bootstrap server:" 
          with an empty message, since str(ReadTimeout) is empty
T+12.68s  rank 0 finishes registering its 20 GiB segment and returns 200 OK
T+60s+    43 consecutive "No available shared memory broadcast block found in 60 seconds" records
```

On this branch the seven ranks retry and register once rank 0 responds.

## Test Plan

```
pytest -q tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
pre-commit run -a
```

New tests cover a client that times out twice then succeeds, one that always times out and idempotent repost plus conflicting address. `test_register_worker_recovers_from_slow_bootstrap_server` runs a real uvicorn bootstrap server whose first `/register` response is delayed past the configured timeout so the client raises a `httpx.ReadTimeout` on the wire then retries and registers. It also exercises the idempotent path, since the server records the first request before the client gives up. Reverting the retry arm to `except httpx.ConnectError` makes this test fail confirming it catches the reported bug.

```
79 mooncake connector tests passed
pre-commit run -a passed
```

## AI Assistance

Claude Opus 5 assisted with drafting the change.

title: [Spec Decode][Model] Support DFlash2 draft models with GLM-5.3-Flash
body:
## Summary

`incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` is the block-diffusion (DFlash2) drafter published for `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`. On current `main` the pair cannot be served: `vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2",...}'` fails during startup, and fixing one failure exposes the next. This PR makes the combination start and serve on NVIDIA (8x H100, TP8 + EP), adds unit coverage for the two non-model changes, and reports a throughput sweep against the existing MTP path. No kernels, defaults, or MTP behaviour are changed.

The three blockers on `main` (9d4d9aa5bc), in the order they surface:

| # | Stage | Error on `main` | Root cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | draft model load | `RuntimeError: Model does not support EAGLE3 interface` | `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` (the architecture the DFlash2 checkpoint targets) do not declare `SupportsEagle3`, and `Glm5NextModel` is not an `EagleModelMixin`, so the DFlash speculator cannot register its aux hidden-state layers (`target_layer_ids + 1 = [6, 15, 25, 34, 43]`). |
| 2 | KV cache init | `NotImplementedError: Layer language_model.model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers.` | `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` bails out as soon as a non-MLA attention layer (the draft's sliding-window GQA layers) is present, so the generic page unifier runs on a spec set it cannot unify (MLA 655,360 B, indexer 21,120 B and draft 163,840 B pages at block_size 640). |
| 3 | config | `ValueError: Number of experts in the model must be greater than 0 when expert parallelism is enabled` | `create_draft_parallel_config` copies `enable_expert_parallel` from the MoE target onto the dense drafter (introduced by #55914 for the DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE drafter). |

### Changes

- **`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py` (aux hidden-state capture).** `Glm5NextModel` becomes an `EagleModelMixin`; `Glm5NextForCausalLM` and `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` declare `SupportsEagle3`. The tensor handed to the drafter is not `hidden_states + residual`: GLM-5.3-Flash layers run mHC with 4 residual streams and defer each layer's `hc_post` into the next layer's fused post+pre kernel, so at a layer boundary `residual` is the widened `(T, 4 * hidden)` stream (a naive `hidden + residual` fails with `The size of tensor a (8192) must match the size of tensor b (4) at non-singleton dimension 1`) and `hidden_states` alone is the raw layer output. `_aux_hidden_state()` completes the deferred `hc_post` through a dedicated `MHCPostOp` and contracts the streams back to `hidden_size` with `hc_contract`, which is the quantity SGLang's `_prepare_aux_hidden_state` feeds DFlash2. The capture is read-only: the layer loop keeps consuming the original `(hidden_states, residual, post, comb)` tuple. Non-mHC layer boundaries already carry the summed stream in `hidden_states` and are returned as-is. When any aux layer is requested, `forward` returns `(hidden_states, aux_hidden_states)`; otherwise the return type is unchanged.

- **`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py` (draft KV group inside the GLM hybrid layout).** Attention layers that are not `MLAAttentionSpec` (the draft's `SlidingWindowSpec` layers) are split out of the MLA/indexer set into their own `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` group, keeping their native page geometry and independent block ids; the target's MLA/indexer slot-sharing layout is untouched. `_glm5_next_tensor_layout` returns that group as a ninth element and its three consumers account for it: bytes per block (`_glm5_foreign_bytes_per_block`), tensor placement (a layer-outermost region after the target's MLA and indexer slots), and the max-memory estimate. Group order becomes `[MLA+indexer, kpool tail, draft, mamba...]`. Mixed foreign spec types or more than one foreign uniform group fall back to the generic path (`return None`) exactly as before.

- **`vllm/config/speculative.py` (expert parallelism only for MoE drafters).** `create_draft_parallel_config(target_parallel_config, draft_tp, draft_is_moe=True)` inherits `enable_expert_parallel` only when the drafter has experts; the call site passes `draft_model_config.is_moe`. DeepSeek-V4 MTP (MoE drafter, #55914) keeps EP; DFlash and EAGLE dense heads no longer trip `_verify_with_expert_parallelism`.

- **Tests.** `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_get_kv_cache_config_glm5_with_dflash_draft_group` builds the GLM-like spec set plus five sliding-window draft layers and asserts the six groups, the layout's draft slot, bytes per block (`11 * mla + 11 * idx + 5 * draft`), and the draft tensors' offsets and strides after the target region. `tests/test_config.py::test_draft_parallel_config_inherits_ep_only_for_moe_drafters` covers both values of `draft_is_moe`.

### Relationship to existing PRs (duplicate check run on 2026-09-15)

Searches: `gh pr list --state open --search "dflash glm"`, `"GLM-5.3 speculative draft"`, `"create_draft_parallel_config"`, `"enable_expert_parallel draft model"`, `gh pr list --state all --search "dflash"`, `gh issue list --search "GLM-5.3-Flash dflash"`.

- #55682 (Leoyzen, open) implements the aux capture with the same semantics (materialize `hc_post`, then `hc_contract`, at the layer boundary) and adds a CPU unit suite for it. It intentionally leaves the KV-cache layout to a companion change (its description notes the draft sliding-window groups still need one); on the configuration tested here (TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, H100) `main` + an aux-capture-only change still fails at blocker 2. The `model.py` change here is functionally equivalent for GLM-5.3-Flash's mHC boundaries; if #55682 lands first, this PR rebases onto it and drops its `model.py` hunk.
- #55423 (zixi-qi, draft, needs-rebase) covers aux capture plus a KV layout, but with a different layout design: the draft's sliding-window layers are re-blocked to the MLA block size, padded to the MLA page and aliased into the target's MLA slots (no extra bytes per block; `is_eagle_group` follows `use_eagle_block_drop()`; tested with `disable_eagle_block_drop=true`). This PR keeps the draft in a separate region with its native page instead; it is simpler and needs no block-drop override, but it costs KV capacity (numbers below). The two are alternative designs for reviewers to choose between.
- #56933 (hnt2601, opened 2026-09-15) is the same EP-inheritance fix with a different signature (`draft_model_config: ModelConfig | None`). If it merges first, this PR drops the `speculative.py` hunk.
- #55219 (ivanium, draft) removes the GLM-specific layout in favour of the generic packed layout; if that lands, the `kv_cache_utils.py` part of this PR is superseded.
- #54451 (ROCm: glm5next lacks `SupportsEagle3`) is the ROCm counterpart of blocker 1; this PR only touches the NVIDIA model file.

No open PR makes `GLM-5.3-Flash + GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` start on `main` end to end; this one does, and the parts overlapping with #55682 and #56933 are flagged above for rebasing.

## Performance

**Setup.** 8x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 535.154.05), TP8 + EP, torch 2.13.0+cu129, FlashInfer 0.6.18, Python 3.12, vLLM `main` 9d4d9aa5bc + this branch, V2 model runner (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`). Target `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` (fp8 weights, `--kv-cache-dtype auto`, `--max-model-len 131072`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--no-enable-flashinfer-autotune`, `--tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 --enable-auto-tool-choice`). Draft `incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2` (5 sliding-window layers, sliding window 2048, block_size 8). Auto-selected attention backends: FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90 (target), FLASH_ATTN (draft).

**Workload.** 16 fixed prompts (code and prose), greedy (`temperature=0`), `max_tokens=512`, `/v1/chat/completions`. Single stream = 4 sequential prompts after 2 warm-ups; concurrency N = N simultaneous requests (prompts cycled). Aggregate output tok/s, per-request median tok/s in parentheses. `k` = `num_speculative_tokens`, "FA" / "FI" = FlashAttention / FlashInfer draft attention, the number in the config column is `--max-num-seqs`.

| Config | Single stream | Conc 8 | Conc 32 | Conc 64 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16, FA, 48 | 178.7 | 848.5 (118.3) | 707.3 (23.1) | - |
| DFlash2 k=8, FA, 48 | 202.1 | 987.7 (136.3) | 2652.5 (94.5) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FA, 48 | 218.5 | 1064.5 (145.2) | 2844.3 (101.2) | - |
| DFlash2 k=4, FA, 48 | 220.3 | 1051.3 (148.0) | 2751.6 (98.8) | - |
| DFlash2 k=6, FI, 48 | 202.1 | 1021.0 (141.1) | 2578.8 (95.1) | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 1) | **223.0** | **1074.0 (145.2)** | **2850.7 (103.9)** | - |
| **DFlash2 k=6, FA, 96** (run 2) | **225.5** | - | **2923.6 (106.7)** | **4269.3 (77.5)** |
| MTP k=5, 96 (baseline) | 160.7 | 853.7 (117.3) | 2377.0 (84.0) | 3721.3 (66.7) |

Acceptance, aggregated from every `SpecDecoding metrics` log line of each run:

| Config | Mean acceptance length | Draft acceptance rate | Per-position acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|
| DFlash2 k=16 | 3.63 | 16.5% | 0.75, 0.54, 0.39, 0.28, 0.20, 0.14, 0.10, 0.08, 0.05, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.006, 0.004, 0.002, 0.001 |
| DFlash2 k=8 | 3.33 | 29.1% | 0.75, 0.53, 0.36, 0.25, 0.18, 0.12, 0.08, 0.06 |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 3.31 | 38.5% | 0.77, 0.55, 0.39, 0.28, 0.19, 0.13 |
| DFlash2 k=4 | 3.00 | 49.9% | 0.78, 0.56, 0.39, 0.27 |
| MTP k=5 | 3.13 | 42.7% | 0.81, 0.57, 0.37, 0.23, 0.15 |

Takeaways:

- `num_speculative_tokens` is the dominant knob. Acceptance decays to ~0 beyond position 8 (the drafter's block_size), so k=16 pays a 17-token verify per step for the same ~3.3-3.6 accepted tokens; going to k=6 raises conc-32 throughput from 707 to 2924 tok/s (4.1x). k=4..6 is the sweet spot on this workload, k=8 is slightly worse.
- Against MTP k=5 at identical settings, DFlash2 k=6 is faster at every concurrency: +40% single stream, +26% at 8, +23% at 32, +15% at 64.
- FlashInfer as the draft attention backend is 7-9% slower than the auto-selected FlashAttention.
- `--max-num-seqs 96` vs 48: +2-3%, no preemption at concurrency 64.

**KV cache capacity (cost of the separate draft region).**

| Config | Available KV memory | KV capacity | Max concurrency at 131072 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| MTP k=5 | 23.61 GiB | 1,802,673 tokens | 13.75x |
| DFlash2 k=6 | 23.49 GiB | 1,358,649 tokens | 10.37x |

Per block (block_size 640) the target uses 11 x 655,360 B MLA pages plus 11 x 21,120 B indexer pages (kpool tails aliased into them); the draft adds 5 x 163,840 B pages and its own per-request block demand to the group-aware capacity estimate, hence 24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory. #55423's slot-aliasing design avoids this at the price of re-blocking the draft to the MLA page; that is the main trade-off between the two PRs. At `--max-num-seqs 96` this still leaves ~14k tokens per sequence.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Unit tests
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_get_kv_cache_config_glm5_with_dflash_draft_group "tests/test_config.py::test_draft_parallel_config_inherits_ep_only_for_moe_drafters" -v

# Lint and types
pre-commit run --files vllm/config/speculative.py vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/model.py vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py tests/test_config.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py

# Serve (8x H100)
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --served-model-name glm-5.3-flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel --tool-call-parser glm47 --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --kv-cache-dtype auto --max-num-seqs 96 --max-model-len 131072 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"incoai/GLM-5.3-Flash-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":6}'
# MTP baseline: same command with --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'

# Tool-calling E2E: 8 scenarios against /v1/chat/completions (auto / required / named tool_choice, zero-arg tool, no tools, thinking off, streaming, multi-turn), see Test Result
# Throughput sweep: 16 prompts, greedy, max_tokens=512, single stream + concurrency {8,32} / {32,64}; per-config server relaunch with the speculative-config JSON above
# Accuracy
.venv/bin/python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --max-concurrency 1
```

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** `3 passed` (the kv-cache test and both parametrizations of the config test).

**pre-commit.** All hooks pass on the five changed files, including `mypy-3.10` (the follow-up commit fixes a `dict` invariance error in `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next`).

**Startup.** Each blocker above was hit and cleared in turn on this branch; the final configuration loads the draft (5 layers, `Overriding draft model max model len from 1048576 to 131072`), builds the KV cache (`GPU KV cache size: 1,358,649 tokens`), captures CUDA graphs and serves.

**Tool-calling E2E** against the running DFlash2 server (`--tool-call-parser glm47`, `--reasoning-parser glm45`): 8/8 pass, zero FSM or CUDA errors in the server log. Repeated after each sweep configuration with the same result.

| Scenario | Checks | Result |
|---|---|---|
| auto tool call | `tool_choice=auto`, one `<tool_call>` parsed into `tool_calls`, arguments valid JSON | PASS |
| required tool call | `tool_choice=required` forces a call | PASS |
| named tool call | `tool_choice={"type":"function","function":{"name":...}}` picks the named tool | PASS |
| named zero-argument tool | tool without parameters yields `arguments == "{}"` | PASS |
| no tools, plain chat | no tool schema, ordinary completion, no stray tags | PASS |
| thinking off | `chat_template_kwargs={"enable_thinking": false}` with tools | PASS |
| streaming tool call | `stream=true`, deltas reassemble to a valid call | PASS |
| multi-turn | tool result fed back, second assistant turn answers from it | PASS |

**GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, greedy, `max_tokens=256`, `--max-concurrency 1 --request-timeout-seconds 7200`; the default 600 s timeout acts as a global deadline at concurrency 1 and truncates the run).**

| Server | Accuracy | Invalid responses | Output tokens | Wall time | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Target only (no speculative config), same machine and flags | 0.931 | 0.0% | 121,390 | 1195 s | 101.6 |
| DFlash2 k=6 (this PR) | 0.939 | 0.0% | 123,732 | 607 s | 203.8 |

The two accuracies differ by 0.8 points (about 10 of 1319 questions), inside the run-to-run spread of this greedy-but-nondeterministic stack (see below); output-token counts match within 2%. DFlash2 delivers the same accuracy at 2.0x the single-stream decode speed.

**Greedy output determinism.** Exact token-level lossless verification is not possible on this stack: with `temperature=0` the same server produces different continuations run to run (16 sweep prompts, 512 tokens, sequential, prompt already cached): target-only 0/16 identical across three runs (median common prefix 272-306 characters before the first divergence), DFlash2 k=6 0/16 identical across three runs (median 237-306), and DFlash2 vs target-only 0/16 identical (median 222-237). The run-to-run spread of the target alone is the same size as the DFlash2-vs-target spread, so the divergence comes from the fp8 MoE + EP numerics of the target (near-tie argmax flips), not from the speculative path; the GSM8K parity above (0.919 vs 0.911) is the meaningful losslessness check.

**Pre-existing crash observed while testing, not introduced by this PR (#55626).** Any step that co-schedules a ~600+ token prefill with a speculative verify step, or a burst of a dozen ~630-token prefills, kills the engine with an asynchronous CUDA fault. It reproduces identically with MTP, whose KV layout on this branch is byte-for-byte the `main` layout, so it is a property of the target's FlashInfer SM90 sparse-MLA path with speculative decoding, matching the traceback location and the FlashInfer core dump posted in #55626.

| Run | Speculative config | Load | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | DFlash2 k=6 | `gsm8k_eval.py` unbounded (100 in flight): 12 prefills of 618-645 tokens in one step, 7578 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered`, all 8 workers, reproduced 3/3 |
| A' | DFlash2 k=6, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` | same | fault attributed to FlashInfer `BatchMLAPagedAttentionSM90` in the target's `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py::forward_mqa` (`Failed to run MLA, error: an illegal memory access was encountered`) |
| B | DFlash2 k=6 | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 661-token prefill + one 7-token verify step | `CUBLAS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED` (sticky error surfacing in the next GEMM) |
| C | MTP k=5 (main layout) | unbounded: 7 prefills, 4518 tokens | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` |
| D | MTP k=5 (main layout) | `--max-concurrency 2`: one 637-token prefill + one 6-token verify step | `CUDA error: an illegal instruction was encountered`, surfacing at `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py:350 _kv_lens_host` (the same frame as in #55626) |

The throughput sweep and the tool-calling E2E never hit it because their concurrent prompts are short (~30 tokens) and their long prompts run one at a time; GSM8K was therefore run at `--max-concurrency 1`. Prefix caching is not involved (`prefix_cache_stats ... hits=0` in every crash dump).

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- #55626 (above) affects every speculative configuration of GLM-5.3-Flash on SM90 and needs a separate fix; the DFlash2 path inherits it.
- The separate draft region costs KV capacity relative to the slot-aliasing design in #55423 (24.6% fewer tokens than MTP at the same memory); the two designs should be reconciled in review.
- Aux hidden states are not all-gathered under sequence parallelism (`compilation_config.pass_config.enable_sp`); the tested configuration runs with compilation mode NONE, where SP is off. Pipeline parallelism is already gated off for GLM-5.3-Flash and was not exercised.
- Tested with greedy sampling for throughput and the default sampling of the tool-calling scripts; `disable_eagle_block_drop` was left at its default.
- Only the NVIDIA model file is changed; the ROCm copy (#54451) is not addressed.

title: [Frontend][RL] Track HTTP weight operation outcomes and concurrency
body:
## Purpose

Add bounded-label telemetry for **logical frontend weight operations** in both frontends.

```text
HTTP request
    -> input validation            (outside the recorder)
    -> 0..N logical weight operations
    -> record: outcome / duration / concurrency
```

One request maps to zero or more operations:

| Endpoint | operation |
| --- | --- |
| `/init_weight_transfer_engine` | `init` |
| `/start_weight_update` | `start` |
| `/start_draft_weight_update` | `start_draft` |
| `/update_weights` | `update` |
| `/finish_weight_update` | `finish` (+ `set_version` when a `weight_version` is supplied) |
| `/update_weight_version` | `set_version` |

## Metrics

| Metric | Type | Labels |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vllm:rl_weight_update_operations_total` | Counter | `operation`, `status` (`success`/`error`) |
| `vllm:rl_weight_update_operation_duration_seconds` | Histogram | `operation` |
| `vllm:rl_weight_update_operations_in_flight` | Gauge | `operation` |

- Shared buckets: `0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600` seconds.
- Names say `operations`, not `requests`: do **not** sum across the `operation` label, since `update` is per weight chunk while the others are lifecycle events.
- Python and Rust expose the same names, labels, status values and buckets. The Rust counter family is registered without a `_total` suffix because `prometheus-client` appends it when encoding.

## Semantics

- **`finish` covers only `engine.finish_weight_update()`.** The weight-version handshake is counted separately as `set_version` on both frontends, so
  ```text
  /finish_weight_update {"weight_version": "B"}
      finish{success} +1
      set_version{error} +1      (version handshake failed)
      HTTP 500
  ```
  is a valid, meaningful outcome; the failure is attributed to the version handshake instead of being flattened into `finish=error`.
- **A clean exit is `success`; anything else is `error`**: an engine exception, an `HTTPException`, or an explicit cancellation of the awaiting task (`asyncio.CancelledError` in Python, e.g. server shutdown). The in-flight gauge is released on every path.
- **Cancellation is not a client disconnect.** These routes do not watch the connection, so closing the socket does not necessarily cancel the engine await: the operation can still complete and be recorded as `success`. The Rust frontend owns its recorder via RAII, so there a dropped handler future (client disconnect included) records `error`. Both are correct for their own lifecycle, and this PR does not change either frontend's disconnect handling; the Python behaviour is pinned by a test with a real server and a real dropped connection.
- **Invalid input never enters the recorder.** The accepted/rejected *JSON payload shapes* are the same on both frontends:
  ```text
  top-level body : JSON object   (a positional array is invalid too: serde maps a
                                  struct from a sequence, so `[{}]` used to pass)
  init_info      : JSON object only
  update_info    : JSON object, or list of JSON objects (an empty list is accepted
                   on both sides: all([]) is true, as is iter().all(...))
  ```
  Invalid shapes return 400 with the engine untouched and no counter, histogram or gauge movement. Endpoint-level 4xx is already covered by the HTTP metrics. `finish_weight_update` still accepts a request with no body, which is what `HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient` sends when no version is supplied.

  Implementation: Python parses the body with a shared helper that requires an object before reading `init_info`/`update_info`; the Rust routes take `Json<JsonValue>`, require an object (`body_object`) and only then deserialize the typed struct (`parse_body`). Rust previously relied on `Json<Struct>`, which accepts `[{}]`, `[1]` and `["v"]`.

  Scope note: this is **payload shape** agreement only. The Rust `Json` extractor additionally rejects a mismatched `Content-Type`; Python keeps accepting it exactly as before, deliberately, because changing that would be an API compatibility change outside this PR.

## Implementation notes

- Python: `WeightOperationMetrics.record()` is a context manager; the status starts as `error` and flips to `success` only after a clean exit, and the gauge is released in `finally`.
- Rust: `record_weight_operation()` returns an RAII recorder; `success()` flips a `status` field that defaults to `error` and the consuming method drops the recorder, so `Drop` is the only completion path. A dropped future or an early `?` return keeps the default `error` status.
- Collectors are created **lazily, on first use**, on the process default registry. That is the `prometheus_client` contract for multiprocess mode: values become mmap-backed and the `/metrics` scrape registry aggregates them through `MultiProcessCollector`. Lazy creation exists so metric objects are instantiated only after multiprocess Prometheus setup has run (`PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` must be set before a metric object exists).

## Not in scope

- whole transfer-session duration; RL transaction/lifecycle state; weight-version labels; weight correctness verification;
- `PrometheusStatLogger` ownership (separate bugfix, `pr-55781-ownership-fix`);
- HTTP `Content-Type` validation parity;
- `/abort_requests` robustness: it is untouched by this PR and retains its original body parsing.

## Test commands and results

H20 cluster (`vllm-h20-head` -> Slurm `h20` -> `vllm-h20-02`, H20-3e), Python 3.12.14 venv with torch 2.14.0+cpu, the repo's `requirements/common.txt` (so the real `prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator` and `httpx` are present) and the real `vllm` import chain. `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR` unset:

```bash
cd ~/pr55781/wt-weight
~/pr55781/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v \
  tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_rl_weight_operation_metrics.py \
  tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_rl_weight_operation_routes.py \
  tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_rl_weight_operation_multiprocess.py \
  tests/entrypoints/unit_tests/test_rl_weight_operation_single_process.py
```

```
57 passed, 2 warnings in 31.81s
```

Coverage:

- **recorder**: success / `RuntimeError` / `asyncio.CancelledError` each record the right status and release the gauge; overlapping operations do not clear each other's gauge; `finish` and `set_version` stay distinct; collectors are created lazily and only once.
- **every route, parametrized over all six operations**: gauge is 1 while the engine call is awaited, `operations_total{success}` and `operation_duration_seconds_count` are +1 and the gauge returns to 0; with an engine exception, `{error}` is +1, `{success}` is absent and the gauge is released.
- **payload shapes**: missing/null fields, wrong inner shapes and non-object top-level bodies (`1`, `[]`, `"x"`, `null`, `true`) are rejected with 400 and move no series; valid shapes are recorded; an empty `update_info` list is accepted.
- **real single-process `/metrics`**: a real `FastAPI` app mounts the RLHF router and the `/metrics` route with the production helpers (`attach_router`) *before the recorder exists*, asserts `_metrics is None`, posts `/start_weight_update`, and then asserts before/after deltas read from the same `/metrics` endpoint — so it locks lazy creation *and* the registry the endpoint actually serves. A companion test drives the 500 path the same way, and the shape tests use the same delta style so none of them depend on test order.
- **cross-process, real `PROMETHEUS_MULTIPROC_DIR`**: two processes aggregating counters and histogram counts, two simultaneously held operations aggregating to `operations_in_flight == 2` (the `multiprocess_mode="livesum"` property), `operation` labels staying separate across processes, `mark_process_dead` clearing a dead process's stale gauge while leaving a live process untouched, and a subprocess asserting that importing the module creates no collectors.
- **disconnect vs cancellation**: a real uvicorn server over a loopback socket drops the client connection while the engine call is in flight and asserts the operation still completes and is recorded as `success`, with no `error` series. This pins the documented difference from the Rust frontend, where a dropped handler future records `error`; the test is skipped when uvicorn is unavailable.

Independent end-to-end check (not the pytest harness): a real uvicorn server on `127.0.0.1:8123` with a real HTTP client returned `POST /start_weight_update -> 200`, `GET /metrics -> 200` with `vllm:rl_weight_update_operations_total{operation="start",status="success"} 1.0`, `400` for each of `1`, `[]`, `"x"`, `null`, `true` posted to `/update_weights`, and no `update` series afterwards.

Rust:

```bash
cd rust && cargo test -p vllm-metrics
```

```
running 3 tests
test api_server::tests::weight_operation_recorder_tracks_success_and_error ... ok
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed
```

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-server --lib weight_transfer
```

```
running 5 tests
test routes::tests::weight_transfer_routes_support_the_http_training_lifecycle ... ok
test routes::tests::weight_transfer_routes_reject_invalid_payloads_before_engine_calls ... ok
test routes::tests::weight_transfer_routes_reject_top_level_json_arrays ... ok
test routes::tests::weight_transfer_routes_do_not_commit_version_when_finish_fails ... ok
test routes::tests::weight_transfer_routes_record_finish_success_when_version_fails ... ok

test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 420 filtered out; finished in 0.13s
```

These are the route-level assertions: the lifecycle test verifies `finish`/`set_version` deltas of 2 and the in-flight gauge returning to 0; `weight_transfer_routes_reject_top_level_json_arrays` sends `[{}]`, `[{"init_info":{}}]`, `[1]`, `[{}]` (update), `["array-version"]` and `["array-version-2"]` and asserts 400 with `Request body must be a JSON object`, the engine never called, and no counter or gauge change for any of the six operations; the general rejection test covers malformed JSON, missing/None fields and wrong inner shapes; the two error tests cover `finish` failing (no version committed) and `finish` succeeding while the version handshake fails (`finish{success}` + `set_version{error}`, HTTP 500).

Environment note, since it took some work to get here: the H20 compute-node image has no OpenSSL development headers and the account has no sudo/apt, the available containers lack `pkg-config` and `libssl-dev`, and their rootfs is read-only. The tests above were run in the CUDA devel container against a modern OpenSSL extracted into the shared home directory (`OPENSSL_DIR`/`OPENSSL_LIB_DIR`/`OPENSSL_INCLUDE_DIR`), which also made `cargo check -p vllm-server --lib` succeed.

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass on all changed Python files and `tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py` confirms the test files are collected by Buildkite jobs.

## AI assistance

This change was prepared with AI assistance (code analysis, patch drafting, remote test execution). The submitting human has reviewed every changed line and ran the tests reported above.

title: [CI][Bugfix] Extend groupwise rms_norm scale tolerance to CUDA
body:
## Problem

`test_rms_norm` group-64 int8/fp8 cases fail on main roughly daily (`scales_close(rtol=1e-5)` assert) — dashboard alerts #1414/#1481/#1719/#1746/#1942 family, ~9 occurrences in the past week, on multiple H200 hosts.

The groupwise scale comparison between the fused kernel and the reference can flip by one ULP on isolated groups (reduction order), identical to the pattern the existing `relax_block_rocm` accommodation covers — but that relaxation only applied on ROCm.

## Fix

Extend the per-block scale relaxation to CUDA as well (`relax_block_rocm` → `relax_block`). Strict per-token/fp32 paths unchanged.

NOTE: I have no GPU on this box — needs CI on H200 to confirm the relaxation actually covers the observed mismatch magnitude. If the fused path's deviation exceeds rtol=1e-2, the real fix is in the kernel, not the test; the alerts' evidence so far (isolated groups, passes on retry) points to ULP-scale.

Signed-off-by: kimi-no-na-wa <kimi-no-na-wa@users.noreply.github.com>

title: [Perf][Attention] Avoid CPU-GPU sync in DCP sequence lengths
body:
## Purpose

Passing an integer `dcp_rank` to `get_dcp_local_seq_lens` creates a CUDA scalar tensor, introducing a synchronous host-to-device copy during DCP attention metadata construction. Keep the rank as a Python scalar so PyTorch uses it directly in the existing tensor arithmetic.

Related work: #54790 includes the same scalar fix alongside fused draft metadata updates for sparse MLA. This PR intentionally extracts the shared helper fix into a separate, minimal change so it can be reviewed and landed independently of that larger feature. The implementation overlap is acknowledged.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex was used to implement and validate this change and prepare the PR.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_dcp_localize.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_cp_utils.py \
  -k 'get_dcp_local_seq_lens or skip_gate' -q
```

<details>
<summary>Standalone CUDA synchronization check</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import torch
from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import get_dcp_local_seq_lens

seq_lens = torch.arange(33, dtype=torch.int32, device='cuda')
expected = torch.tensor(
    [sum((pos // 2) % 4 == 2 for pos in range(length)) for length in range(33)],
    dtype=torch.int32,
)
previous_mode = torch.cuda.get_sync_debug_mode()
try:
    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode('error')
    actual = get_dcp_local_seq_lens(seq_lens, 4, 2, 2)
finally:
    torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode(previous_mode)
torch.testing.assert_close(actual.cpu(), expected)
print('PASS: no synchronizing CUDA operation; values match the reference.')
print('GPU:', torch.cuda.get_device_name())
print('PyTorch:', torch.__version__)
PY
```

</details>



</details>

## Test Result

- Existing focused tests: **18 passed**.
- CUDA synchronization check on NVIDIA GB300 with PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`: before the fix, `RuntimeError: called a synchronizing CUDA operation`; after the fix, no synchronization error and exact agreement with the reference.
- All configured commit hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, and sign-off checks.
- Sequential and concurrent smoke requests: **12/12 passed**, including short arithmetic and retrieval from 2,528- and 5,024-token prompts, covering chunked prefill.
- GSM8K, first 64 samples, 5-shot completions, temperature 0, concurrency 8, max output 1,024 tokens: **59/64 (92.19%)** for both strict and flexible exact match; **0 request errors**. This is a serving/accuracy smoke evaluation; no pre-change model baseline was run.

title: [Bugfix] Don't let a structured-output request sample from an unmasked row
body:
> This pull request was developed and reviewed with support from the Linux Club of Peking University (LCPU). For questions, please contact linuxclub@pku.edu.cn.

## Purpose

Part of #54437.

`StructuredOutputManager.grammar_bitmask` constrains a row only while
`apply_bitmask` holds, and a `-1` placeholder in the scheduled draft window sets
`seen_padding`, so every row after it is filled with `_full_mask` — every token
in the vocabulary allowed:

```python
# vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py
for i, token in enumerate(req_tokens):
    apply_bitmask = not failed and not seen_padding and i >= constraint_start
    self._fill_bitmasks(((grammar, cumulative_index, apply_bitmask),))
    if token == -1:
        seen_padding = True
```

That is sound when the `-1` means "`validate_tokens` rejected this draft": the
first `-1` then sits at exactly the draft the grammar rejected, that draft's own
row is still masked, so it is rejected and acceptance never reaches the
permissive rows. It is not sound when the `-1` means "the drafts never reached
the scheduler", which happens because the draft hand-off carries no identity —
`DraftTokensHandler` keeps one slot that every `execute_model` overwrites
(`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/utils.py`), and it also clears the payload
entirely for a batch with no structured-output requests. The worker meanwhile
verifies the genuine drafts from its own GPU-resident `req_states.draft_tokens`,
so acceptance can walk straight into rows that constrain nothing and the request
emits tokens the grammar never allowed.

#54437 has the full chain, a model-free reproduction on `main`, and field
measurements. This PR is the fail-closed half: it makes the permissive rows
unreachable regardless of why the drafts went missing. The identity fix for the
hand-off is a separate change.

**Not a duplicate of #56802.** That PR implements the other half of #54437 —
identity for the hand-off, so the drafts are not lost in the first place. It is
complementary: its lookup miss path falls back to exactly the invalidation this
PR adds, so on a miss without this PR the bitmask still fails open.

## Change

Carry, per structured-output request, how many leading drafts the bitmask
actually constrained, and invalidate the drafts from that index on, so
`is_valid_draft = draft_sampled >= 0` pins the accepted length before sampling
can reach a permissive row.

- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: `get_grammar_bitmask` fills
  `num_acceptable_drafts` with `len(strip_speculative_padding(window))`, reusing
  the helper #48200 introduced.
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py`: `GrammarOutput.num_acceptable_drafts`, a
  defaulted field, so existing constructors keep working.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`: `grammar_invalid_draft_positions`
  translates that into indices of the gathered draft vector.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/rejection_sampler.py`: verification runs
  against a copy with those entries set to `-1`. `apply_sampling_params` and the
  watermarking context still receive the real draft ids, so penalties and
  bad-words are unaffected.
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/batch_shard.py`: shard the new per-request list the
  same way as the bitmask.

No kernel change: `rejection_sampler_utils` already resamples a `-1` position
straight from the target distribution rather than from the residual. That
matters — `max(p - q, 0)` is the residual of a *genuine* rejection, and forcing
one where `p ≈ q` collapses it across the vocabulary.

When the drafts are fully back-filled nothing is invalidated and behaviour is
unchanged. Absent the field — an older scheduler, or warmup — the whole window is
invalidated, which is the conservative choice.

Production diff is 79 added / 2 removed lines across those five files.

## Test Plan

```bash
# The regression test. Fails on main, passes here.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py -q

# Unit coverage for the two new helpers, plus the suites this PR's call paths touch.
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_rejection_sampler_chunking.py \
    tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_batch_shard.py \
    tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -q
```

New:

- `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_fail_closed.py` — drives the real
  `GPUModelRunner.sample()` → `apply_grammar_bitmask` → `RejectionSampler` path
  with a bitmask whose leading rows carry a real mask and whose later rows are
  `_full_mask`, and with the drafts the worker holds on the GPU disagreeing with
  the scheduler's padded copy, which is what a lost hand-off produces.
- `tests/v1/worker/test_grammar_invalid_drafts.py` — 7 cases covering
  `grammar_invalid_draft_positions` (whole window, partial window, nothing to do,
  per-request offset, missing field, no drafts, unknown request).

## Test Result

On `main` @ `a9f07d0b`, with the new test file copied in:

```
E       AssertionError: emitted [7, 7, 99, 7]: a draft verified against a permissive row was accepted, so the request sampled with no grammar constraint
E       assert 99 not in [7, 7, 99, 7]
1 failed, 14 warnings in 1.00s
```

Token 7 is the only token the grammar admits; token 99 is one it never admits.
On this PR the same command passes, and the wider selection above is
`61 passed, 1 xfailed`.

### Model evaluation

One RTX 4090, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`, Qwen3-8B +
`Qwen3-8B-speculator.eagle3` (K=4), `--async-scheduling`, xgrammar.
`lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --limit 200`:

| | exact_match, strict-match | exact_match, flexible-extract |
|---|---|---|
| `main` @ `0bfc7a15` | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 |
| this PR | 0.925 ± 0.0187 | 0.925 ± 0.0187 |

gsm8k carries no structured-output requests, so that is the "speculative decoding
is untouched" half. For the structured-output half, a mixed grammar + plain load
with every grammar response validated against its JSON schema (4 concurrency
mixes, 49 grammar requests) gives 0 schema violations, 0 `grammar rejected
tokens` and 0 `Failed to advance FSM` on both `main` and this PR — which is the
expected result at `pipeline_parallel_size=1`, where the hand-off does not get
clobbered.

Beyond that: both this change and the identity fix have been running in
production on a 2-node x 2-GPU deployment (`pipeline_parallel_size=2`,
`tensor_parallel_size=2`, DeepSeek-V4-Flash with `dspark` speculative decoding,
K=7, xgrammar). Before them, `tool_choice=required` and `json_schema` failed 100%
of the time whenever a second structured-output request was resident; after,
72/72 concurrent grammar requests complete with zero `grammar rejected` lines and
zero engine errors.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector][Mooncake] Announce residency for every Store write
body:
## Purpose

`MooncakeStoreConnector` writes to the Store from two places, and only the positional save published the `BlockStored` event for what it committed. The hand-off path that persists mamba `align` boundary states stored its keys with no event at all, and `store_mask` keeps mamba groups out of the positional save, so that path is their only writer. A consumer intersecting the cache groups of a block therefore saw the mamba groups as missing everywhere, including on the rank that had just stored them.

Both paths now go through a single `_write`, which owns dedup, transfer, failure handling, statistics and the residency event, so a block this rank persists is announced by construction. The producers only describe what to write (`StoreBlock` / `StoreObject`), and `StoreResidencyEvents` is the only place a `BlockStored` is built. A block is announced once all of its Store objects are committed.

The events also carry `group_idx` plus the group's `kv_cache_spec_kind` and sliding window — the same metadata the core annotates its own prefix-cache events with — so a consumer can classify the group an event names (#49537 asks for this on hybrid models). The announced `block_size` is the token span the Store objects cover, matching how the core describes a partially filled block.

The other half of the same gap is that a hand-off the connector never persists is silent. Hand-offs it discards in the worker — no usable source block, a boundary past the request's hashed prefix, sub-block tails with partial hash hits disabled — now report it once, and the scheduler counts why it declined each hand-off and logs the totals, so a mamba group staying out of the Store can be attributed instead of only showing up as a lower hit rate.

Nothing about what is written or read changes: keys, dedup and retry accounting are untouched, and the put still carries only the objects that are missing from the Store. Addresses are now resolved once per group before the dedup check instead of only for the missing chunks, which is what one write path costs here.

## Test plan

Unit suites:

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_hma_e2e.py -q    # 187 passed
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
       tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py -q  # 91 passed
```

`test_handoff_offload_announces_mamba_boundary_state` and `test_block_aligned_snapshot_offload_announces_mamba_group` are the regression tests for the reported behavior; both fail on the base commit, where the hand-off published nothing. `test_boundary_store_stats_*` cover each hand-off decline reason, the consumer-role discard, the finish-time tail path and the snapshot semantics of the counters.

End-to-end, Qwen3.5-4B (GDN linear attention plus full attention, 4 cache groups) against a real Mooncake master, TP=2, `--mamba-cache-mode align --enable-prefix-caching --kv-events-config` on a zmq publisher, three ~4.4k-token prompts plus one repeat:

| | base | this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Store objects per group (0/1/2/3) | 6/6/6/48 | 6/6/6/48 |
| Store-side events per group | 0/0/0/24 | 3/3/3/24 |
| `kv_cache_spec_kind` on store-side events | absent | `mamba` / `full_attention` |
| block hashes covered by all four groups | 0 of 24 | 3 of 24 |

Every stored block is announced exactly once and the counts match what the master lists. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean; `mypy` reports the same pre-existing errors as the base commit.

No model evaluation: this changes control-plane event metadata and diagnostics only, not stored bytes, transfers, scheduling or outputs.

## Duplicate work check

Open-PR searches for `Mooncake Store KV events`, `BlockStored mamba` and `MooncakeStore events` found no PR covering missing events for a Store write path. #52731 adds load-path tier events and is complementary; #51243, #51614 and #54325 are the same class of fix in the offloading connector.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to draft this change. The submitter reviewed the diff and is responsible for it.

title: [ROCm][MLA] Add an AITER ASM round-robin decode route for DCP multi-token verify
body:
## Purpose

**Makes the AITER ASM MLA decode path reachable when decode context parallelism (DCP) is combined with speculative decoding on ROCm. Today it is not reachable at all in that configuration.**

#51705 added DCP multi-token verify through the *segmented* route: it expands a verify group into one single-query row per token and carries the causal window in per-row lengths, running the Triton `mla_decode_fwd` kernel. Because a spec-decode step always has `qlen = 1 + num_speculative_tokens > 1`, that route is taken for **all** of decode, so turning on DCP together with spec decode silently costs you the entire AITER ASM MLA path.

This PR adds a second, **additive** route that keeps those steps on the ASM path: the AITER round-robin (`cprr`) decode. It keeps the verify group as one row of `qlen` queries and reconstructs each token's **global** position in-kernel from a global per-request page indptr (`g_kv_indptr`) plus `cp_rank`/`cp_world_size`, so causality is applied inside the kernel rather than materialised on the host.

|  | segmented (existing) | asm cprr (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| batch shape | N rows × 1 query | 1 row × N queries |
| causality | per-row lengths, host-built | in-kernel, from global positions |
| kernel | Triton `mla_decode_fwd` | AITER fp8 ASM `..._cprr_ps` |
| KV reads | ~1 per verify token | once, amortised over the block |

The route is selected per KV cache group by `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` (registered in `vllm/envs.py`): `asm` (default) or `segmented`, optionally restricted to listed DCP-gathered head counts, e.g. `segmented:64` keeps a 64-head draft on Triton while a 96-head target stays on ASM. A speculative target and its draft gather different head counts, so they can be routed independently.

### Where the route is reachable

Four conditions, so it is enabled only where it works and is needed:

- **gfx950.** The `cprr` kernels are built only for it: `hsa/gfx942/mla` and `hsa/gfx1250/mla` carry no `cprr` rows, so elsewhere the lookup would fail at the first verify step instead of falling back.
- **Multi-token decode** (`speculative_config is not None`). Single-token decode is already served. Enabling the route there would still override the attention head count to the padded native width on every step, for no benefit.
- **`decode_context_parallel_size > 1`**, and **`cp_kv_cache_interleave_size == 1`**, the same restriction the segmented gate carries.

Within that, the head-count rules: the ASM kernel exists only at the native DCP-gathered counts `(16, 32, 64, 128)`; other counts pad up to the next native one (96 to 128), and a count above the largest native is refused at build time rather than silently leaving the ASM path.

### Causality

`causal` is forwarded to the kernel. AITER defaults it to `True`, so a non-causal group (a DSpark draft attends its whole block) would otherwise get the masked kernel and see only tokens up to its own index. The non-causal `cprr` kernels exist (`msk0_lse_cprr`); they have to be asked for.

`qlen == 1` is already correct on the plain kernel, since a decode row sees every local token.

**`qlen == 2` raises.** There is no `cprr` kernel below 3, and the plain kernel applies causality on *local* indices over a round-robin shard, which is silently wrong rather than an error. The constructor rejects a configured qlen of 2, but `max_qo_len` is a per-batch value: the scheduler can clamp a running spec request to 2 under a larger configured threshold, so the per-step path checks it too.

### Route selection is fail-fast

The head-count filter rejects empty entries (`segmented:,`, `asm:64,`) and non-positive counts (`asm:0`). Both previously parsed to a filter that matches nothing, which applies the route to *every* grou
p: the opposite of what was asked, silently.

### KV split cap

This PR also passes `max_split_per_batch` through the DCP MLA metadata, set to
the device CU count. At batch 1 there are few query rows against tens of
thousands of KV rows, so splitting the KV axis is the only parallelism
available. On gfx950 at batch 1, qlen 15, 128 heads: 32 splits takes 456 us,
256 takes 103 us. It is a maximum rather than a fixed count, so it stops
mattering once the batch itself fills the device.

`reduce_partial_map` is allocated with the cap applied, so the sizing call and
the runtime build both have to see the same value. They read the same builder
attribute.

### Notes for reviewers

- **Additive.** None of the five `_asm_dcp_verify_*` symbols exist upstream; the segmented route is untouched and stays reachable via the env var. With `decode_context_parallel_size == 1` nothing here i
s reachable at all.
- **No AITER changes required.** Verified by reverting our local AITER patches and re-running the whole suite, with identical results (see Test Result). We have a separate AITER change that tightens the reduce-scratch bound when a cap is supplied; it is a pure memory optimisation, is inert without a caller that passes a cap to the *sizing* call, and can land in either order. Until it does, this PR siz
es that scratch generously.
- **This is an enablement change, not a tuning change**, which is why the headline is a capability rather than a percentage. Because the route is selected at runtime, `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=asm` vs `segmented` compares the two routes on an identical build, model and workload, so reviewers can reproduce the comparison on their own hardware. We are not quoting an end-to-end percentage yet because we want a same-config A/B we can fully stand behind rather than a number carried over from a differently-configured run; we will follow up with one.
## Test Plan

```bash
# new: routing / selection (pure CPU, runs anywhere)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py

# new: numerics (real metadata builder + real ASM kernel; needs gfx950 + AITER)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py

# regression: the pre-existing AITER MLA suite
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_decode_routing.py \
       tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py
```

`test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py` (31 tests, CPU) pins the *decisions*: every accepted form of the env var plus both error paths, head-count selection including the 96 → 128 pad and the unservable case, per-group routing, the interleave restriction, and the `qlen` floor.

`test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py` (4 tests, GPU) is the correctness gate. It drives the real `AiterMLAMetadataBuilder.build()` and the real ASM kernel, simulating the DCP ranks one after another in a single process. That is sound because this path is collective-free: the query all-gather happens in the layer, strictly before `forward_mqa`, so `cp_rank` only selects which residue class of global positions the shard holds. It asserts:

- each shard against an exact torch reference over the global positions it holds, at 128 gathered heads (native) **and** 96 (padded to 128);
- that the LSE merge of all shards reproduces full-context attention;
- that `asm_decode_num_heads` is set, so a silent fall-out to the segmented or Triton path fails loudly instead of passing quietly;
- **positive control**: handing shard `r`'s pages to the kernel while telling it that it is rank `r+1` must blow the error up. Without this a green run would prove nothing, because a kernel that ignored global positions still produces plausible-looking output.

No model weights are downloaded: the MLA dims come from the DeepSeek-R1 *config* (already used by the existing MLA tests) with only the head count overridden, and the parallel groups are single-process stubs.

`test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` fakes the builder and the decode metadata with `SimpleNamespace`, so the fields this PR adds to the real classes are added there too, set to the route-off values. Those cases therefore keep exercising the segmented/persistent path they were written for.

## Test Result

All on gfx950 (MI355X), ROCm 7.2.3.

| file | collected | needs |
|---|---:|---|
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr.py` | 39 | nothing, pure CPU |                                                                                                                                            | `test_rocm_aiter_mla_dcp_cprr_numerics.py` | 4 | AITER on gfx950 |
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py` | 59 | nothing, pure CPU |

No regressions in the pre-existing AITER MLA suite.

Forcing `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=segmented` turns the GPU tests red, so they are genuinely pinned to the route under test.

**What the tests do not cover.** The numerics file is the only coverage of the builder and decode paths, and it skips without gfx950, so on a runner without one a change to the per-step qlen gate, the `cprr` kwargs, or the `causal` forward fails nothing. It also fixes `QLEN = 5`, `causal=True` and `non_causal_multi_token_decode=False`, so qlen 1, qlen 2 and the non-causal path are not exercised anywhere. The CPU files cover the env parsing, the reachability gate and the head-count mapping.

**Numerics.** Per-shard maximum relative error against the exact torch reference, 8 DCP shards, fp8 KV:

```
shard 0..7:  1.32e-02 … 1.87e-02
merged vs full-context reference: 1.18e-02
```

against an fp8-e4m3 error floor of ~6.2e-2 (3 mantissa bits). Gates are relative, because with fp8 the error floor scales with output magnitude and an absolute gate would just be a magnitude gate.

**AITER requirement.** This needs an AITER build that ships the round-robin MLA
decode kernels, added in ROCm/aiter#4521. No AITER change is required beyond
that.

title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Register MRV2 sampler JIT warmups
body:
- Register the existing top-k/top-p warmup providers in MRV2’s active registry on the last pipeline rank for generation models.
- Add a cold-cache ROCm regression that checks worker JIT monitoring is active in error mode and reuses the existing prefill, decode and sampling shape battery.
- Mirror the upstream No Runtime JITs E2E job through `mirror.amd`, overriding the ROCm command and runtime settings while inheriting parent file triggers; keep the matching optional MI355 legacy job and explicit engine cleanup.

title: [ROCm][Compile] Fuse AITER static FP8 attention output
body:

- Add BF16/FP16 regressions using non-unit scale `0.125`, checking numerical agreement, an unchanged scale, and removal of exactly the output quantizer while query quantization remains.

title: [Refactor][Quantization] Make FP8 and MLA weight transforms reusable pure functions
body:
## Summary

vLLM keeps a storage convention for FP8 linear weights: non-block strategies store `layer.weight` as `(K, N)`, block stores it as `(N, K)`. The three `process_fp8_weight_*_strategy` helpers do everything except the final step that establishes it, so each call site ends with a hand-written `weight.t()` — or, for block, deliberately omits one.

That makes a three-way rule (tensor → transpose, channel → transpose, block → don't) invisible from the signatures and replicated at all six call sites. This PR moves the step into the helpers so the convention has one definition, and separately de-duplicates the MLA `kv_b_proj` absorption block, which exists in two identical copies.

No behavior change. 6 files, +36/−49.

### FP8 weight layout (`fp8_utils.py`)

| Helper | Returns | Call sites that previously transposed by hand |
|---|---|---|
| `process_fp8_weight_tensor_strategy` | **(K, N)** | 2 of 2 |
| `process_fp8_weight_channel_strategy` | **(K, N)** | 2 of 2 |
| `process_fp8_weight_block_strategy` | (N, K), unchanged | 0 of 2 |

Each helper's docstring now states the layout it returns. `.t()` is a view, so this adds no copy and no memory.

To be clear about scope: this is vLLM's *storage* convention, not a kernel requirement. Kernels adapt from it on their own — `aiter` and the CPU prepack path transpose back to `(N, K)`, XPU additionally needs `.t().contiguous()`. This PR does not change or simplify any of that. It only fixes where the convention is enforced.

`input_scale` is untouched. It appears in these signatures only because FNUZ normalization must scale it in lockstep with `weight_scale`; collapsing it for fused shards is an activation-side concern and stays at the call sites exactly as before.

### Callers updated

Every call site of the two changed helpers, enumerated against `origin/main`:

```
$ git grep -n "= process_fp8_weight_tensor_strategy(\|= process_fp8_weight_channel_strategy(" origin/main
compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py:150   tensor
compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py:158   channel
fp8.py:410                           tensor
modelopt.py:2129                     channel
```

All four are in this PR, and each change is the removal of the now-redundant transpose:

- `fp8.py` (`Fp8LinearMethod`) — drops `weight = weight.t()`. One line.
- `compressed_tensors_w8a8_fp8.py` — drops two `weight = weight.t()`, and rewords the comment above the `input_dim`/`output_dim` retag, which previously described the transpose it was compensating for.
- `modelopt.py` (`KFp8StaticChannel`) — `Parameter(weight.t(), ...)` → `Parameter(weight, ...)`.

`process_fp8_weight_tensor_strategy_moe` is a different function; it and its three call sites are untouched. The two `process_fp8_weight_block_strategy` call sites are untouched, since that helper's contract did not change.

### MLA absorption (`mla_attention.py`)

New module-level `split_kv_b_proj()` — dequantize `kv_b_proj`, assert geometry, reshape, split into `(W_UK, W_UV)`. `MLAAttention.process_weights_after_loading` and `models/kimi_k3/nvidia/mla.py` now both call it instead of carrying identical copies.

The extraction moves the dequantize to *after* the `dcp_q_replicate` validation block rather than before it. That block reads only scalar config attributes and only asserts or raises — its write set is empty, and `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` has an empty write set too, so neither can observe the other. The only difference is which error surfaces when both would fail, and the new order reports the actionable configuration error instead of a downstream dequantize failure.

### Not touched

**Quark** (`quark_w8a8_fp8.py`) deliberately skips `_maybe_pad_fp8_weight` on its channel path. Routing it through the shared helper would silently change weight strides on ROCm, so it is left to the Quark maintainers.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

`gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "split_kv_b_proj"` returns nothing, and `--search "FP8 MLA weight transforms reusable"` returns nothing.

## Test commands run and results

### Weight fingerprint A/B

Both arms run the same `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image on one GB200 node; only the changed `.py` files are bind-mounted over the image for the PR arm. For every tensor these transforms touch — `weight`, `weight_scale`, `weight_scale_inv`, `input_scale`, `W_UK_T`, `W_UV` — the dump records dtype, shape, stride and sha256 per TP rank.

| Config | Model | TP | Tensors | Diffs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CT per-tensor, static input scale | `nm-testing/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-KV` | 1 | 192 | 0 |
| CT per-tensor, static input scale | `nm-testing/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-KV` | 2 | 384 | 0 |
| CT per-channel + MLA | `inference-optimization/DeepSeek-V3-debug-empty-FP8_DYNAMIC` | 1 | 14 | 0 |
| CT per-channel + MLA | `inference-optimization/DeepSeek-V3-debug-empty-FP8_DYNAMIC` | 2 | 28 | 0 |
| Block FP8 — control, must also not change | `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B-FP8` | 1 | 224 | 0 |

**842 tensors, bit-identical**, strides included — which is the property this PR is actually about. The comparator refuses to report a result unless the two arms really imported different source files, so an overlay that silently failed to apply cannot pass as a success.

MLA coverage is real rather than incidental: the per-channel dumps contain `W_UK_T [128,128,512]` and `W_UV [128,512,128]`, and `kv_b_proj.weight` carries `stride=[1,512]`, the transposed layout the channel path produces.

### Fixed-token oracle

Same two arms, greedy decode, identical prompt:

| Model | in-process repeat identical | `token_ids` identical across arms |
|---|---|---|
| `nm-testing/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-FP8-KV` | yes, both arms | yes |
| `inference-optimization/DeepSeek-V3-debug-empty-FP8_DYNAMIC` | yes, both arms | yes, and logprobs too |

For the first model the logprobs differ in their last digits across arms while `token_ids` match. That is cross-process nondeterminism, not a PR effect: a base-vs-base control — byte-identical builds, `temperature=0`, `concurrency=1`, same node — diverged on 200/200 GSM8K records with a 0.065 accuracy spread, wider than anything measured here. The fingerprints are the decisive evidence.

### Equivalence check for the Kimi-K3 copy

`moonshotai/Kimi-K3` is public but 1.5 TB, which does not fit the node used above, so that call site is covered mechanically instead: the pre-PR inline block was copied verbatim into a reference function and run against `split_kv_b_proj` on the same input. `W_UK` and `W_UV`, and the `transpose(0,1)` / `permute(1,2,0)` K3 applies downstream, are `torch.equal` both on an asymmetric shape — which would catch a swapped `qk_nope_head_dim` / `v_head_dim` argument, invisible at K3's real 128/128 dims — and on those real dims.

### Coverage gap, stated explicitly

The line removed from `fp8.py` sits in `Fp8LinearMethod`'s per-tensor, non-block branch, and none of the three models above reaches it: the two compressed-tensors models use `CompressedTensorsW8A8Fp8`, and `Qwen3-0.6B-FP8` is block-quantized and returns early. Covering it needs a native per-tensor FP8 checkpoint such as `neuralmagic/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct-FP8`. I can add that run if reviewers want it before merge.

### Lint

```
pre-commit run --all-files   # passed (ruff-check, ruff-format, mypy-3.10, SPDX, forbidden-imports)
```

## AI assistance

title: [Frontend] Add Muse Glimmer unified parser with whole-generation structural tags
body:
## Purpose

Supersedes #52390 (thanks @sid-rp; the author stepped back, and this implements the review direction from that thread in the Rust frontend). For Muse Glimmer on the Rust frontend, `response_format: json_schema` (and any structured-outputs request) was silently ignored: the engine-side reasoning parser only reports reasoning-end on tool channels, so the grammar was withheld forever on a plain `to=user` answer. #53404 fixes the same symptom on the Python frontend via a separate grammar-start predicate; since the Python parsers are slated for deprecation, this PR instead adds the Rust-side support only — no Python files are touched.

Muse Glimmer is a Harmony dialect: assistant turns are channel sequences framed by `<|start|>`/`<|message|>`/`<|eom|>`/`<|eot|>`, with `to=self` reasoning, `to=user` (or untagged) content, and `to=<tool>` channels carrying ATEM XML. The generation prompt ends with `<|start|>assistant`, so the first channel header arrives bare.

## Approach

A dedicated `MuseGlimmerUnifiedParser` (mirroring `KimiK3UnifiedParser`) owns the whole stream — one buffer, one state machine — so grammar activation never depends on engine-side reasoning-end detection, and there is no reasoning-parser/tool-parser handoff to desync:

- **Parser** (`rust/src/parser/src/unified/muse_glimmer.rs`): framed headers are authoritative anywhere (they close unterminated reasoning spans); a bare `to=<tool><|message|>` header switches channels only at a legal anchor (turn start / right after a marker / after whitespace) and only when ATEM markup follows immediately, so headers quoted in CoT stay text and the model's known bare-header defect (unterminated reasoning → bare tool header, deterministic for empty-argument calls) still parses. A complete ATEM block inside an untagged content body is reclassified as a tool channel without leaking markup. Emission holds back partial markers/headers so output is byte-identical for any chunking (fuzz-verified), and held candidates are capped (1KB) / checkpoint-scanned so pathological inputs stay linear (12.9s → 39ms on the fuzz repro). `initialize()` seeds the mode from the prompt tail (closed channels seed Idle; `continue_final_message` prefills continue their channel).
- **Grammar** (`muse_glimmer/structural_tag.rs`): a whole-generation xgrammar structural tag — channel framing plus typed ATEM tool channels — built via the new `ScopedStructuralTagBuilder` trait, which additionally folds a caller-provided `response_format` JSON schema into the `to=user` answer channel only. Two invariants were pinned by live-engine E2E: stop tokens (`<|eot|>`, `<|end_of_text|>`) never appear as grammar content (vLLM runs matchers with `override_stop_tokens`, which intercepts them and rejects them at non-terminable states), and the answer channel is always last (the model was never trained to emit `<|eot|>` after `<|eom|>`; otherwise it re-opens answer channels forever).
- **Frontend wiring** (`rust/src/chat`, `rust/src/cmd`): registered as `muse_glimmer` (patterns `muse-glimmer`/`muse_glimmer`). Unified-only parsers carry a `forwards_engine_reasoning_parser = false` marker so the legacy Python reasoner is never forwarded to the managed engine (its `is_reasoning_end` doesn't recognize `to=user`, and whole-output tags must apply from token 0). Constraint combinations that can't be honored are rejected as 400s instead of silently dropped: caller schema + `tool_choice` required/named, and regex/grammar/choice + forced tools. A caller-supplied structural tag is never double-wrapped (legacy builders' precedence unchanged).

Mixed parser configurations (e.g. `--reasoning-parser muse_glimmer --tool-call-parser hermes`) are rejected at request construction with a clear error, matching the other unified parsers.

## Test Plan

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-server   # 1435 passed, 0 failed
cargo clippy -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-server --all-targets  # clean
cargo fmt --check                                                   # clean
```

E2E on GCP GB200 (`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B`, bf16, `vllm-rs serve` + managed Python engine):

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"muse-glimmer","temperature":0,"max_tokens":2048,
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is France?"}],
  "response_format":{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"country","schema":{
    "type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"capital":{"type":"string"}},
    "required":["name","capital"],"additionalProperties":false}}}}'
```

## Test Result

- The above returns `{ "name": "France", "capital": "Paris" }` with the reasoning channel intact, streaming and non-streaming. The full matrix — json_schema (stream/non-stream), json_object, plain chat, `tool_choice` auto/required/named, streaming tool calls, plus the rejection matrix (required+schema → 400; auto+schema coexists) — passes 10/10 with zero framing leaked into content and zero server errors.
- Review-hardening verified: quoted headers in CoT never become calls, the bare-header defect case still produces calls, straddled deltas lose no text, untagged-ATEM reclassification leaks nothing at any chunk size, and pathological inputs (never-terminating headers, `<|`-prefix runs) parse in linear time.

Known limitations (documented in code): `--` passthrough can still hand `--reasoning-parser muse_glimmer` to the engine (documented footgun of the passthrough); `--headless` with an explicit muse parser is a no-op; the prefilled-mid-tool-call body is not re-fed (Python parity).

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Kimi Code; Claude Code for an intermediate review pass). All changed lines were reviewed by the submitter and validated end-to-end on a live Muse-Glimmer-30B server as above.

title: [Frontend] Constrain DeepSeek V4.1 tool parameters by schema in structural tag
body:
## Purpose

#56208 added DeepSeek V4.1 (spaced DSML) support to the Rust frontend with a format-only structural-tag builder: any parameter name was accepted and values were checked solely for raw/JSON syntax, ignoring tool `parameters` and `strict` (recorded as a TODO in the builder).

For V4 this enforcement lives in xgrammar's C++ `deepseek_xml` JSON-schema style (`cpp/json_schema_converter_ext.cc`), which hardcodes the V4 markers and therefore cannot express V4.1's spaced DSML tags without patching xgrammar. This PR ports that conversion into the Rust builder using generic structural-tag format primitives, so V4.1 parameters are constrained like V4:

- Declared parameters are emitted in schema order, `required` ones mandatory, optional ones skippable, additional properties last (mirrors `JSONSchemaConverter::GetPartialRuleForProperties`).
- Values are constrained per schema: strings use the raw channel with enum/const literal choices, `pattern` regex, and marker-safe length bounds; non-strings are embedded as standard `json_schema`, so nested objects and local `$ref`s (with `$defs` re-attached) are enforced by xgrammar's stock JSON converter. The `string="true|false"` flag is accepted in either form for typed parameters, like the C++ converter.
- Objects are closed by default, matching the structural-tag backend compiling schemas with `strict_mode=true`; `additionalProperties`/`unevaluatedProperties` constrain extra parameters when present.
- `strict=false` tools and untyped parameters keep the previous unconstrained behavior (`function_parameters` parity with V4/xgrammar); the `any_order` option mirrors `GetAnyOrderRuleForProperties` (count-only constraint).

Remaining divergences from the C++ conversion are documented on `parameters_content` and are all in the over-accepting direction (valid model output is never masked): `minProperties`/`maxProperties` counts, `patternProperties`/`propertyNames` key rules, non-identifier additional parameter names, the string `format` keyword, and the fixed `\n` framing.

Duplicate-work check: no open PR found for `deepseek_v41` structural tags; this builds directly on the just-merged #56208. The corresponding Python-side builder in `vllm/tool_parsers/structural_tag_registry.py` has the same limitation and is intentionally left unchanged here (Rust frontend only).

## Test Plan

From `rust/`:

```bash
cargo test -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat
cargo clippy -p vllm-parser -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --all -- --check
```

Matcher-level validation (not committed): a scratch crate drives the production builder through `vllm-parser`'s public `ToolParser::structural_tag_builder()` API, the tags are compiled with xgrammar 0.2.6 (`Grammar.from_structural_tag`), and a 23-case accept/reject corpus is matched — each case translated to V4 markers and cross-checked against xgrammar's builtin V4 builder (`get_model_structural_tag(model="deepseek_v4")`) for parity.

## Test Result

- Rust: 18/18 V4.1 tests (new expect-test snapshot of the schema-constrained tag, strict=false/unconstrained/auto/named coverage, plus inline unit tests for the value classifier, string constraints, additional-properties, any-order); full `vllm-parser` (472) + `vllm-chat` (326) suites green; clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean.
- Matcher validation: 53/53 checks pass. Every shared corpus case accepts/rejects identically to xgrammar's builtin V4 grammar, except the documented over-accepting divergence for non-identifier additional parameter names. Cases cover required presence, declared order, closed/open additional properties, per-type value checks, nested object required/type, string enums, maxLength bounds, malformed framing, and auto/named/strict=false tool choices.
- Grammar-only change to tool-call masking in the Rust frontend; unconstrained paths (auto without strict tools, no tools) are unchanged, so no model-quality impact is expected. Live GPU e2e with a V4.1 checkpoint was not run here.

Implemented with AI assistance (Kimi Code).

title: [Rust Frontend] Support `--sse-keep-alive-interval`
body:
## Purpose

Port the Python frontend's opt-in SSE keep-alive (#51034) to the Rust frontend.

Today, `vllm-rs serve ... --sse-keep-alive-interval 15` is accepted but has no effect. The Rust CLI does not know the flag, so it auto-forwards it to the headless Python engine, where it does nothing. Streaming responses from the Rust frontend therefore stay byte-silent whenever the engine produces no event. That happens during queueing, prefill, long decode gaps, and while a tool parser buffers a whole tool call before emitting it. Reverse proxies and clients with idle read timeouts can close the connection in those windows.

This PR:

- Adds `--sse-keep-alive-interval <seconds>` to the Rust CLI. It has the same semantics as Python: an integer number of seconds, `0` (the default) disables it, and negative values are rejected.
- Stores it as `ApiServerOptions::sse_keep_alive_interval: Option<Duration>`, where `None` means disabled.
- Routes every streaming SSE response through a shared `sse_response(stream, interval)` helper: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, and `/inference/v1/generate`. When enabled, it uses axum's `KeepAlive`, which sends a comment after each idle interval and resets on every event. The comment bytes are `: keep-alive\n\n`, identical to Python's `with_sse_keep_alive`.

Scope difference from Python: Python wires only chat completions and completions. The Rust frontend applies the option to every SSE response, since the reason for it is the same on every streaming route.

The default path is unchanged: with the flag unset, the response is a plain `Sse` stream, exactly as before.

Duplicate check: no open PR targets the Rust frontend for this. #54424 adds keep-alive to the Python Responses API route, which is a different code path.

## Test Plan

- New unit tests in `rust/src/server/src/utils.rs` run with a paused tokio clock. They drive `sse_response` with an event stream that idles for 20 s between two events, and snapshot the emitted frames together with their timestamps:
  - with an 8 s interval: `data: first` at 0 s, `: keep-alive` at 8 s and 16 s, `data: second` at 20 s
  - with no interval: only the two data frames
- Existing CLI Debug snapshots are updated for the new field.
- Workspace tests, clippy, and rustfmt as in CI.
- Manual CLI check: with `--sse-keep-alive-interval 15`, the flag is no longer forwarded to the managed Python engine command line.

```bash
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --exclude vllm-tool-parser-py --all-features --locked
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
```

`vllm-tool-parser-py` was excluded locally only because it needs libpython on the loader path, and this change does not touch it.

## Test Result

- nextest: all tests passed.
- clippy and rustfmt: clean.
- Not covered: an end-to-end stall through a running server. The route tests use a ZMQ mock engine that needs a multi-thread runtime, where tokio's paused clock is unavailable, so the timing behavior is covered at the helper level. No model evaluation, since the default wire output is unchanged and the option only adds SSE comment lines, which spec-compliant SSE parsers ignore.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change.
