title: [Bugfix] YaRN RoPE: honor explicit attention_factor from the rope config
body:
> This replaces #46280, which was closed when its source fork was deleted. The original context remains there.

## Purpose

`get_rope()` builds the YaRN branch's keyword arguments from a whitelist that includes `attn_factor` but not `attention_factor` (`vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/__init__.py`). HF stores the final YaRN magnitude scaling under `attention_factor` and applies it to cos/sin (`transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py::_compute_yarn_parameters`), while vLLM expresses the same quantity as `mscale = yarn_get_mscale(factor) * attn_factor` (`yarn_scaling_rope.py`). A config that sets `attention_factor` has the key silently dropped, vLLM falls back to `0.1 * ln(factor) + 1`, and the two stacks apply different magnitude scaling whenever the configured value differs from that fallback.

This PR lets `YaRNScalingRotaryEmbedding` accept `attention_factor` and use it as the mscale when present, matching transformers, and `get_rope` forwards it on the YaRN path. Configs without the key are unchanged; only the values baked into the cos/sin cache change. Scope is intentionally the explicit `attention_factor` on the plain YaRN path: the `mscale`/`mscale_all_dim` fallback and MRoPE-yarn are not covered here.

## Affected configs

When #46280 was opened (2026-06-21), the then-current `poolside/Laguna-XS.2` config ([revision f5f4885](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-XS.2/blob/f5f48854b62bd9bbe208dcaae6cd4b92ce4aa5da/config.json), committed 2026-06-18) set `factor=64, attention_factor=1.0`, so transformers applied 1.0 while vLLM applied 1.4158883. On 2026-07-14 poolside corrected the configs across their repos ([commit](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-XS.2/commit/69e3f4046616e40fb55ac54e0e2e6accbe5cadfe): "fix(rope): YaRN attention_factor is (0.1\*ln(factor)+1)\*attn_factor, not the bare multiplier"). The corrected values equal vLLM's fallback exactly, so for the canonical poolside repos this change is now numerically a no-op.

The divergence is still live in third-party requantizations that snapshotted an older config (`factor=32`, from before the 256K context bump): [RedHatAI/Laguna-XS.2-FP8](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Laguna-XS.2-FP8/blob/main/config.json), [RedHatAI/Laguna-XS.2-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/Laguna-XS.2-NVFP4/blob/main/config.json) and [cyankiwi/Laguna-XS.2-AWQ-INT4](https://huggingface.co/cyankiwi/Laguna-XS.2-AWQ-INT4/blob/main/config.json) still carry `attention_factor=1.0`, where transformers applies 1.0 and vLLM main applies 1.3465736. More generally, transformers reads the documented key first and vLLM silently drops it, so any config that sets it away from the fallback gets divergent numerics between the two stacks.

## Related work

#48623 and #48629 address the broader #48621 `mscale`/`mscale_all_dim` and nested Llama 4 gaps. This PR is limited to honoring an explicit `attention_factor`; #48629 is stacked on it, while #48623 is independent and does not currently cover that explicit override.

## Test Plan

The earlier standalone `tests/model_executor/test_yarn_attention_factor.py` asserted the internal `.mscale` field. It is replaced by two tests in the existing `tests/kernels/core/test_pos_encoding.py` suite, asserting the output of `forward_native` on a `get_rope`-constructed module instead of internal fields. At position 0 all rotation angles are zero, so the output is exactly `query * mscale`, which makes the applied scaling observable:

- `test_yarn_explicit_attention_factor[1.0 / 0.5]`: an explicit `attention_factor` is the applied mscale.
- `test_yarn_default_mscale`: without the key, the applied mscale stays `0.1 * ln(factor) + 1`.

```
pytest tests/kernels/core/test_pos_encoding.py -k yarn
```

## Test Result

Local run on macOS CPU (torch 2.11.0, transformers 5.14.1):

```
3 passed, 385 deselected, 16 warnings in 0.60s
```

With the two source files reverted to `main` and the tests kept, `test_yarn_explicit_attention_factor[1.0]` and `[0.5]` fail while `test_yarn_default_mscale` passes. The tests exercise `forward_native` on CPU; I have no CUDA device locally, so the kernel paths were not run. The diff does not modify kernel code, only the mscale written into the cos/sin cache.

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Implement get_top_tokens() on the DeepSeek V4 MTP drafter
body:
## Purpose

Enabling `speculative_config.use_local_argmax_reduction` with a `deepseek_v4` draft model **fails
engine startup** rather than falling back to the full-vocab path:

```
ValueError: use_local_argmax_reduction is enabled but draft model DeepSeekV4MTP
does not implement get_top_tokens().
```

Both opt-in sites probe the draft model with `hasattr(model, "get_top_tokens")` and raise when it
is missing (`vllm/v1/spec_decode/llm_base_proposer.py:1609`,
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/speculator.py:389`), and `DeepSeekV4MultiTokenPredictor` implements
only `compute_logits`. So the flag is a trap for every `deepseek_v4` checkpoint: it does not run
slower, it does not start.

`model_type: deepseek_v4` is rewritten to `DeepSeekV4MTPModel` by its own branch in
`SpeculativeConfig.hf_config_override`, which the registry resolves to the per-platform
`DeepSeekV4MTP`, so the generic MTP drafter fix in #56995 does not reach it.

**Fix.** Forward to `LogitsProcessor.get_top_tokens()` from both the predictor and the wrapper on
`amd`, `nvidia` and `xpu`, mirroring the `compute_logits` pair already in each file. `cpu/mtp.py`
is left alone because its constructor raises `NotImplementedError` unconditionally, so no instance
exists to probe.

V4 reaches its LM head through `hc_head` over the `(T, hc_mult, D)` residual and then the shared
head's RMSNorm, unlike V3 (`shared_head` alone) and V3.2 (an already-normed hidden state). Running
a different transform returns a *different draft token* instead of failing, so that transform is
factored into `_pre_head()` and shared by `compute_logits` and `get_top_tokens` rather than written
twice.

`use_local_argmax_reduction` defaults to `False` and gates every call site, so the default path is
unchanged.

## Test Plan

Hardware: MI355X (`gfx950`), HIP 7.2.53211, torch 2.11.0. Measurements ran against a substrate
built from upstream `releases/v0.27.1` (the sha the host's build names) plus that build's compiled
extensions; in the region this PR touches, v0.27.1 and `main` differ only in how the shared-head
RMSNorm kernel is re-exported, so the arms transfer. The two arms are one tree differing in exactly
one file (`diff -r`).

1. **Unit tests** (added): `pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dsv4_mtp_local_argmax.py`, asserting
   that the token `get_top_tokens` selects carries the row maximum of the full-vocab logits.
2. **Falsifiability**: the same tests run against the merge base, and against two deliberately
   wrong implementations — the shared-head RMSNorm dropped, and `hc_head` dropped.
3. **Micro, TP=2**: both arms as methods on the same predictor over a real TP process group with
   the real `hc_head` op, RMSNorm kernel, `ParallelLMHead` and `LogitsProcessor`, swept over draft
   batch. Four pairs per point, pair 0 discarded, arm order alternated.
4. **e2e, TP=2**: `vllm bench serve` on `DSV4-base-tpl`, fp8 KV cache, 1024 in / 512 out, 300
   prompts, `--max-concurrency 68`. Four interleaved pairs, pair 0 discarded.
5. **GSM8K A/B**: `lm_eval --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, greedy, all 1319 items,
   `enable_prefix_caching=False`, per-sample logging, **with a base-repeat control** (`base2`, a
   second run of the same build) so the noise floor is measured rather than assumed.

## Test Result

**Unit tests.** 3 passed. All 3 fail on the merge base. Dropping the shared-head RMSNorm fails 2 of
3; dropping `hc_head` fails 2 of 3. The norm gain is `normal_(1.0, 0.5)` and the `hc_head`
scale/base are non-trivial on purpose: an argmax is invariant to RMSNorm's per-row rescale, so a
default all-ones weight could not detect a skipped norm at all.

**Micro (TP=2).** This is a trade-off with a crossover, not a uniform win, so the crossover and the
absolute per-step cost matter more than any median over the sweep:

| shape | crossover (draft batch) | worst cost below | best saving above |
|---|---|---|---|
| hidden 4096, vocab 129280 | 36 → 44 | bs=6: +80.8 µs/step (−42.7 %) | bs=1028: −2496.6 µs/step (+80.1 %) |
| hidden 7168, vocab 129280 | 12 → 20 | bs=6: +29.6 µs/step (−12.4 %) | bs=1028: −2511.1 µs/step (+71.9 %) |

**Token agreement is 1.0000 at all 32 swept points**, on both the selected index and the selected
logit value. The crossover had to be recomputed for V4 rather than carried over from #56995's V3
numbers, and it differs between the two V4 shapes.

**e2e (TP=2, concurrency 68, above the crossover).** No change in either direction:

| metric | base | patched | pairwise median | pairwise range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total tok/s | 1935.13 | 1929.16 | −0.17 % | −0.92 … +1.26 % |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 31.25 | 31.22 | +0.55 % | −0.73 … +0.62 % |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 30.37 | 30.48 | −0.07 % | −1.72 … +0.89 % |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 584.73 | 588.33 | −1.11 % | −1.59 … −0.33 % |
| Acceptance length | 1.31 | 1.31 | −0.11 % | −1.08 … +0.67 % |

That is the expected result, and it is worth stating why rather than leaving it to be read as a
disappointment: the micro saving at the batch this run reached is 84.7 µs, while the measured
engine step is 40.83 ms (mean TPOT 31.25 ms × acceptance length 1.31), so the predicted e2e effect
is **+0.21 %** — an order of magnitude below the pair-to-pair spread. The e2e arm can show that
nothing regressed; it cannot resolve the win. Pair 0, had it been kept, would have read +8.41 %,
because the base arm alone rose from 1775.6 to 1935.1 tok/s between pair 0 and pair 1 on AITER JIT
warmup. Unchanged acceptance length is the e2e-level statement that the draft tokens did not
change.

**GSM8K (1319 items, 5-shot, greedy).**

| arm | strict | flexible |
|---|---|---|
| base | 0.9515 ± 0.0059 | 0.9507 ± 0.0060 |
| base2 (same build, control) | 0.9522 ± 0.0059 | 0.9530 ± 0.0058 |
| patched | 0.9500 ± 0.0060 | 0.9492 ± 0.0060 |

Effect (base → patched) is −0.0015 strict against a noise floor (base → base2) of +0.0008; both are
well inside the ±0.0059 stderr. Per-sample agreement is the sharper test and needs the same
control: base vs base2 produce identical text on **36.5 %** of items, base vs patched on **36.0 %**
— indistinguishable. Same-verdict rates are 98.1 % and 98.2 %. Two runs of one build already
disagree on most generations because vLLM's batching makes bf16 reductions batch-shape dependent,
so without the control column the 64 % of differing prompts would read as a regression. Claim: no
measurable accuracy change on GSM8K within the base-repeat noise floor — not bit-exactness.

**Not covered.** The `nvidia` and `xpu` files carry the identical change but were not executed:
this host is gfx950. They are argued from source — each file's extracted `_pre_head` is
line-identical to the transform its own `compute_logits` ran before, each keeping its own hc_head
kernel (`hc_head_fused_kernel_tilelang` on nvidia, `mtp_layer.hc_head_op` on amd/xpu). GSM8K
exercises one shape of one path and says nothing about long context, sampling or multi-turn.

---

AI assistance: the patch, its tests and the measurements above were produced with Claude via
Cursor, and reviewed by the submitter. Found by
[Hyperloom](https://github.com/AMD-AGI/Hyperloom).

title: [Structured Output] Add optional persistent disk cache for compiled xgrammar grammars
body:
## Summary

xgrammar's compiled grammars are cached only in the in-process `GrammarCompiler`
LRU (`VLLM_XGRAMMAR_CACHE_MB`), which dies on every restart — so any autoscaled
deployment that scales to zero (e.g. Cloud Run `min-instances=0`) **recompiles
every guided-decoding grammar on every cold start**.

This PR adds an **optional, env-gated, default-off** persistent on-disk cache for
compiled grammars, wiring xgrammar's existing `CompiledGrammar.serialize_json()`
/ `deserialize_json()` into `backend_xgrammar.py`. A cold start then
**deserializes grammars from disk instead of recompiling them**, and the cache
survives process restarts.

**When disabled (the default), `get_xgrammar_disk_cache()` returns `None`, the
backend takes the original compile path unchanged, and there is zero added
overhead and no behavior change.**

It mirrors the existing **Outlines** disk cache (`get_outlines_cache`, #6203,
hardened default-off in #14837) and improves on it by being **bounded**
(`size_limit` + LRU eviction, vs Outlines' unbounded `eviction_policy="none"`)
and **pickle-free** (stores xgrammar's `serialize_json()` string, not a pickled
object — complies with `check_forbidden_imports.py` and `SECURITY.md`).

## Design

- **`vllm/envs.py`** — two vars, both added to `compile_factors()`
  `ignored_factors` so a cache-only toggle never perturbs the `torch.compile`
  key (mirrors `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` / `VLLM_MEDIA_CACHE_*`):
  - `VLLM_XGRAMMAR_DISK_CACHE` (bool, default `0`/off) — enable the cache.
  - `VLLM_XGRAMMAR_DISK_CACHE_MB` (int, default `512`) — size bound.
- **`vllm/v1/structured_output/utils.py::get_xgrammar_disk_cache`** — bounded,
  LRU-evicting `diskcache.Cache` under `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/xgrammar_cache`,
  version-keyed by `xgr.get_serialization_version()` (clear-on-mismatch). A
  `hasattr` guard disables the cache rather than crashing if a build lacks the
  serialization API, and a one-time warning carries the "trusted clients /
  non-shared cache directory" caveat.
- **`vllm/v1/structured_output/backend_xgrammar.py`** — cache-aware
  `compile_grammar` (deserialize on hit; compile + serialize on miss). The key
  is `sha256(tokenizer_fingerprint, request_type, disable_any_whitespace,
  grammar_spec)`. `max_rollback_tokens` is excluded on purpose: it parameterizes
  the `GrammarMatcher` (rebuilt fresh every call), not the cached
  `CompiledGrammar`. **The compile dispatch and matcher construction are
  unchanged.** The entire read path (`.get()` + `deserialize_json`) and the
  write are guarded: any cache error — corrupt SQLite, lock contention,
  format/version skew — falls back to a fresh compile, so a cache problem never
  fails a request.

## Security

Structured-output deserialization is the sensitive surface, so the design is
built around it:

- **JSON-only, no pickle** — only a `str` is ever stored.
- **Re-validated on load** — `deserialize_json` checks the embedded
  serialization version + tokenizer metadata; a mismatch raises and we
  recompile, so a stale/wrong-tokenizer entry can never produce a wrong grammar.
- **Default-off + bounded** — same hardening posture as the Outlines cache after
  #14837, plus a real size bound.

## Test plan & results

- New CPU-only `tests/v1/structured_output/test_xgrammar_disk_cache.py`
  (`pytest.mark.cpu_test`): persistence + functional identity (token-mask
  equality, not just file presence), non-JSON GRAMMAR round-trip, hit/miss key
  partitioning, deserialize-failure fallback, raising-read fallback,
  serialization-version wipe, tokenizer-dependent key, and the default-off
  zero-overhead path. Each test is wrapped in `fork_new_process_for_each_test`
  and uses a single backend per process (a second `compile_grammar` call for
  the same grammar already takes the deserialize-from-disk path).
- `tests/test_envs.py` covers the two new env getters via its existing
  iteration over `environment_variables`.

**Results on a GCP `g2-standard-8` (8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM) + 1× NVIDIA L4 (24 GB),
torch 2.11.0+cu130, xgrammar 0.2.2:**

- `tests/v1/structured_output/test_xgrammar_disk_cache.py` — **8 passed** in
  ~11 s; `ruff` clean.
- `tests/test_envs.py` — **52 passed**.

> Note on test structure: building a *second* cache-enabled `XgrammarBackend`
> in one process triggers a native SIGSEGV (a `diskcache` × `xgrammar`
> interaction, reproducible on a coherent CUDA build, and reduced to a
> vLLM-free repro filed upstream as
> [mlc-ai/xgrammar#664](https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/664)).
> Production is unaffected — vLLM constructs the backend once per process — but
> to keep the tests CI-safe they fork a fresh process per test and never build
> a second backend in-process.

The benchmark below was run on the same instance type.

Cold (recompile) vs warm (deserialize-from-disk) microbenchmark — alternation
grammars:

| grammar   | compile (cold) | deserialize (warm) | speedup |
|-----------|---------------:|-------------------:|--------:|
| alt-500   |        4.4 ms  |            1.1 ms  |   3.9×  |
| alt-1000  |        7.2 ms  |            2.0 ms  |   3.7×  |
| alt-2000  |       15.4 ms  |            3.8 ms  |   4.0×  |
| alt-4000  |       31.2 ms  |            7.6 ms  |   4.1×  |
| alt-8000  |       63.2 ms  |           15.3 ms  |   4.1×  |
| alt-16000 |      147.1 ms  |           30.8 ms  |   4.8×  |
| **total** |   **268.5 ms** |        **60.6 ms** | **4.4×**|

## Not a duplicate

Duplicate-work checks found no open PR addressing a persistent xgrammar grammar
cache:

```
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "xgrammar disk cache"
# -> only this PR (#45948)
```

The Outlines disk cache (#6203 / #14837) is a different backend; this PR mirrors
its hardening posture but does not overlap it.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude). I have reviewed every changed
line, run `tests/test_envs.py` and the benchmark locally, and am able to defend
the change end-to-end.

## Notes

- **Env naming** is deliberate (`VLLM_XGRAMMAR_DISK_CACHE*` groups with
  `VLLM_XGRAMMAR_CACHE_MB`); happy to rename the bool to
  `VLLM_V1_USE_XGRAMMAR_DISK_CACHE` to match the `VLLM_V1_USE_OUTLINES_CACHE`
  spelling if maintainers prefer.
- No new dependencies (`diskcache` is already pinned; `xgrammar >= 0.2.1`
  already provides the serialization API).
- The env-var docs (`docs/configuration/env_vars.md`) regenerate automatically
  from the `envs.py` snippet markers — no manual doc edit.

title: [CI][ROCm] Report why VRAM is still held when the memory wait times out
body:
**Do not merge.** This is a debugging PR. The point is to get the diagnostic
 output from an AMD CI run so we can tell what holds the memory, not to land
 this instrumentation as it is.

## Motivation

`Distributed Torchrun + Shutdown Tests (2 GPUs)` on MI300 has been failing for
the past few days in `tests/v1/shutdown/test_delete.py::test_llm_delete`, with
roughly 179 GiB of 192 GiB still allocated on both devices after `del llm`. One
of the failures: https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/11651/list

We could not reproduce it locally. Sixty runs of the full `v1/shutdown` suite on
MI300, including runs under heavy CPU load, all passed. So the practical way
forward is to make the failure describe itself the next time it happens in CI.

## Purpose

`wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear` only reports that the memory did not drop, never
why. There are three causes behind it and each needs a different fix:

1. an engine-owning object outlived the `del` that was supposed to release it, so
   teardown never started;
2. the object was released, but an engine subprocess never finished tearing down;
3. both are gone and the memory is held below the runtime, in the driver.

This prints which one it was. For (1) it also names what still holds the
reference, giving the variable name for a dict holder, or the function, file and
line for a frame holder.

The report is emitted after the memory has failed to drop for 30 s, and again on
the way out with the error. The early one matters because an outer watchdog such
as pytest-timeout usually kills the process before this loop reaches its own
timeout, and it does so without unwinding, so a report placed only next to the
`raise` would never run. 30 s is safe because teardown that succeeds finishes in
a couple of seconds, so nothing is printed on passing tests.

This also covers more than the one test above: on ROCm nearly every VRAM wait in
the suite reaches this function via `wait_for_rocm_memory_to_settle`, which
`VllmRunner` calls both before constructing an engine and on exit.

@music-dino 
One known second instance is
`models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py::test_voxtral_realtime_forward`,
which runs with `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, so the engine is not in a
separate process. Something from the engine stays alive and keeps the memory, and
the test that pays for it is `test_voxtral_realtime_generator`, which runs next
and waits for VRAM in its fixture before building its own engine. Since the wait
happens before construction, the report there describes what the *previous* test
left behind.

That in-process case needed two things. Engine startup calls `gc.freeze()`, and
frozen objects are invisible to `gc.get_objects()`, so with the engine in the test
process the scan found nothing at all; the diagnostic calls `gc.unfreeze()` first.
And `EngineCore` and `GPUModelRunner` are included among the objects looked for,
because with no subprocess they are the ones holding VRAM, and they can outlive
the `LLM` on their own: in validation `EngineCore` was held both by `InprocClient`
and, independently, by a bound method.

## Test Plan

The diagnostic only runs on the failure path, so it was tested by forcing each
shape on purpose with a temporary test: a leaked reference kept in a dict, a
clean teardown against an impossible threshold, and a leak where a thread calls
`os._exit` mid-wait to emulate how pytest-timeout kills the process. Plus
`tests/v1/shutdown/test_delete.py` on 2 GPUs to confirm the happy path.

## Test Result

MI300 (gfx942), ROCm.

Leaked reference with the process killed mid-wait. The report lands 15 s before
the process dies:

```
gpu memory used/total (GiB): 0=178.18/191.98;
Memory still held after dur_s=30.01, reporting early:
[mem-diag] 4 engine-owning object(s) still alive:
[mem-diag]   vllm.entrypoints.llm.LLM
[mem-diag]     held by dict, keys=['leaked_llm']
[mem-diag]   vllm.v1.engine.llm_engine.LLMEngine
[mem-diag]     held by LLM: LlamaForCausalLM()(
[mem-diag]   vllm.v1.engine.core_client.SyncMPClient
[mem-diag]     held by LLMEngine: <vllm.v1.engine.llm_engine.LLMEngine object at 0x7f53d3247f50>
[mem-diag]   vllm.v1.engine.utils.CoreEngineProcManager
[mem-diag]     held by BackgroundResources: BackgroundResources(ctx=<zmq.Context(3 sockets) ...
[mem-diag] gc.collect() freed 94 object(s)
[mem-diag] 1 child process(es) still alive:
[mem-diag]   pid=278521 status=sleeping name=python cmd=python -m pytest ...
```

`keys=['leaked_llm']` is exactly the reference the test planted. Clean teardown
against an impossible threshold says so instead of blaming an object:

```
[mem-diag] no engine-owning objects alive; teardown did start
[mem-diag] no child processes left; VRAM is held below the runtime
```

Happy path unchanged: `tests/v1/shutdown/test_delete.py` on 2 GPUs, `10 passed in
314.74s`, zero `[mem-diag]` lines.

---
<details>
<summary> Essential Elements of an Effective PR Description Checklist </summary>

- [ ] The purpose of the PR, such as "Fix some issue (link existing issues this PR will resolve)".
- [ ] The test plan, such as providing test command.
- [ ] The test results, such as pasting the results comparison before and after, or e2e results
- [ ] (Optional) The necessary documentation update, such as updating `supported_models.md` and `examples` for a new model.
</details>

title: [V2] Offload CUDA process state during sleep without graph recapture
body:
Level-1 cuMem sleep releases weights and KV cache, but leaves graph executables and native CUDA graph pools resident. This adds opt-in CUDA process checkpointing to the existing sleep/wake path so that the live EngineCore can give up its GPU state and resume the same captured graphs.

### Implementation

Set `VLLM_SLEEP_OFFLOAD_CUDA_CONTEXT=1` and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` with `--enable-sleep-mode`. Ordinary cuMem sleep first copies weights to CPU and discards KV cache. A short-lived external Python helper then calls the CUDA driver checkpoint API to offload the remaining process GPU state, including GraphExec and native PyTorch graph pools. Wake restores and unlocks the CUDA process before waking the requested cuMem allocations. Any partial wake restores the whole CUDA context first.

Capture and replay code are unchanged. There is no graph destruction, re-instantiation, or recapture, no custom graph allocator, and no C++ wrapper: the helper uses `cuda.bindings.driver`. The CPU EngineCore stays alive. The driver provides the host backup described in its [checkpoint API documentation](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__CHECKPOINT.html).

Five core Python files implement this path. Configuration validation is centralized in the executor; failed operations keep scheduling paused and allow a state-aware retry. Helpers have bounded waits. A sleeping engine exits its dedicated process without CUDA finalizers or reallocation, including when checkpointing failed after cuMem sleep. Both the allocator and capture implementation are unchanged.

Sleeping-engine exit bypasses Python finalizers, so pending optional profiler, telemetry, or KV-event buffers may not flush.

Initial scope: Linux, CUDA driver API 13.2+, installed `cuda.bindings`, standard V2 worker, local multiprocess EngineCore, `uni` executor, one GPU, cuMem backend, and level-1 sleep. Level 0 remains scheduler-only. V1, distributed execution, Ray actors, and level-2 offload are rejected. Quantization, multimodal models, speculative decoding, and live RL weight replacement have not been validated.

### Validation

GPU tests used the pinned ARM64 `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` image at `sha256:b0501f99fec5136f248f78d5850977a2ec32d55cd9a665f4a9ffef24cbdf7fe5`: vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, one GB200 GPU per run. The host driver was `580.173.02`, with isolated `595.71.05` CUDA compatibility libraries. Only this PR's core patch was applied to the image; no replacement vLLM wheel or earlier graph-pool patch was installed.

- `pre-commit run`: all applicable staged-file hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, and CUDA API checks.
- 31 focused state-recovery, worker-ordering, scheduler, and configuration tests passed. A native graph/RNG probe passed five cycles, repeated transitions, and recovery after a refused restore, retaining the same GraphExec handle and exact RNG results.
- The real 30B HTTP lifecycle test passed two cycles of repeated sleep, partial wake/re-sleep, and complete wake with exact output and **0 MiB** reported for the sleeping EngineCore. Exit succeeded while another process held **183.6 GiB**. Injecting a checkpoint failure after cuMem sleep but before driver lock also allowed exit while another process held **181.7 GiB**; the holder continued using its memory in both cases. Shutdown still emits frontend/resource-tracker warnings; this verifies termination without GPU restoration, not warning-free shutdown.
- Full GSM8K validation of published revision `a5df54f0ef` passed:

| Arm | Correct / total | Accuracy | Generated tokens |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Stock nightly | 1084 / 1319 | 82.18347% | 605,759 |
| Patched, awake | 1084 / 1319 | 82.18347% | 605,759 |
| Patched, across 10 sleep/wake cycles | 1084 / 1319 | 82.18347% | 605,759 |

All three complete result files are byte-identical: zero differences in question IDs, predictions, correctness, text, token IDs, selected-token logprobs, and finish/stop reasons. All ten checkpoints reported **0 MiB** for the target process; capture count stayed **300**. Median sleep/wake times were **0.993/1.206 s** (sleep range 0.983–4.121 s, wake 1.156–1.208 s). These timings include ordinary weight offload/restore and the driver operation.

GSM8K used all 1,319 questions, the local Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 BF16 model, five raw-completion demonstrations, the repository last-number scorer, greedy decoding, seed 42, and a 1,024-token cap. Each arm had 373 length-limited completions and one invalid answer. Configuration: V2 Breakable `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, capture sizes `[1,2,4,8,16,32]`, gated batch admission of 32, max model length/batched tokens 4,096, 16 GiB KV cache, Triton MoE, no prefix caching or async scheduling. This is a controlled regression recipe, not the model's official chat benchmark or a claim of batch invariance.

Tests extend three existing suites; probes, evaluation scripts, traces, and data are not committed. Focused pytest ran against the patched image using copies of the worker/executor suites and the relevant test definitions extracted verbatim from the engine suite to avoid unrelated tokenizer downloads:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest /tmp/test_sleep_mode_backend.py /tmp/test_executor.py /tmp/test_engine_focused.py -k 'checkpoint or pause_synchronizes or worker_drives' -v
```

### Related work and review

Open-PR and issue checks found related checkpoint work. #37921/#37925 introduce a C-extension checkpointer and new suspend/resume interfaces; #52132 uses CRIU snapshots to terminate and recreate the EngineCore subtree; #51360 targets reusable startup snapshots. This PR instead composes driver GPU-state checkpointing with the existing cuMem sleep/wake contract while retaining the same live CPU process. #47700 addresses graph-pool allocation rather than GraphExec residency. These integration and scope differences are intentional; this does not claim to resolve every configuration in #47654.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and this description. Claude Code identified the asleep-free remap OOM risk, which this revision removes by simplifying dedicated-process exit. Its focused follow-up audit found no blocking issue with that rule and confirmed the Ray-actor exclusion is necessary. Human line-by-line review and end-to-end ownership remain required before merge.

title: [Quantization] Select per-token NVFP4 MoE backends explicitly
body:
## Purpose

Online `nvfp4_per_token` previously advertised the ordinary NVFP4 activation scheme even though execution uses per-token scales. This could select an incompatible backend. One-sided dispatch also sized its buffer for packed FP4 although the per-token path sends unpacked activations and quantizes inside the expert kernel.

- Add `kNvfp4DynamicToken` and use it for online NVFP4 MoE selection.
- Declare TRTLLM support and size modular expert workspaces for unpacked inputs.
- Size one-sided communication buffers with an optional `input_dtype` override. An explicit BF16/FP16 dtype reserves `hidden_dim * input_dtype.itemsize` activation bytes and zero scale bytes; `None` preserves quant-config-based sizing. Per-token NVFP4 supplies `moe_config.in_dtype`. This supports deferred quantization without relying on another BF16 layer enlarging the shared buffer.
- Cover both packed/deferred dispatch sizing, including BF16/FP16 dtype overrides and early rejection of FP32, FP8 E4M3, FP8 E5M2, and INT8 overrides. FlashInfer’s per-token NVFP4 quantizer accepts only BF16/FP16 activations; its FP32 per-token scales do not imply FP32 activation support.

Depends on #57091 and must merge after it. All Marlin capability changes belong to that PR's generic activation contract; there is no Marlin diff here. CuTe-DSL per-token support remains in #50030. The per-token backend-contract tests were removed from this PR because they need #57091; they should return with it.

## Validation

Latest sizing and dtype-validation changes:

- `uv run --no-sync --project /home/matej/prime-rl-stack-clean python /home/matej/prime-rl/outputs/glm53-rl-startup/20260922/nvfp4-one-sided/run_pr_tests.py` — **8 passed, 50 deselected**. The wrapper runs `pytest tests/quantization/test_online.py -k nvfp4_one_sided -q --tb=short` against this checkout, with existing compiled CUDA extensions and isolated test dependencies. Both per-token modes with BF16/FP16 input dtypes and rejection of four unsupported override dtypes are covered. FP16 acceptance is checked at the configuration/quantizer-contract level; the GPU communication check below uses BF16.
- `uv run --no-sync --project /home/matej/prime-rl-stack-clean pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/all2all_utils.py vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py tests/quantization/test_online.py` — passed, including Ruff and mypy. Commit hooks also passed.
- Isolated two-B300-GPU check: `uv run --no-sync --project /home/matej/prime-rl-stack-clean torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=2 /home/matej/prime-rl/outputs/glm53-rl-startup/20260922/nvfp4-one-sided/gpu_dispatch_check.py` — FlashInfer one-sided BF16 dispatch/combine using this checkout's dtype override, hidden size 6144, capacity 320, batches of 1/96/320 tokens per rank, three repetitions each. **All 9 round trips matched the original input exactly**; no BF16 model layer or manager growth was used to provision the buffer. The initial harness incorrectly assumed token order is preserved during dispatch; the corrected check compares dispatched value multisets per source rank and requires exact original token order/values after combine.

These checks validate configuration and GPU communication, not full-model numerical accuracy. No full-model evaluation was rerun for this update, and the live GLM-5.3 RL deployment remains on its previous wheel.

Prior validation, before the sizing update: 30 configuration tests passed with prerequisite #57091 applied. Historical single-GPU and DP2/EP2 TRTLLM comparisons were reported for the original implementation; those were not rerun here.

## Non-duplicate and assistance

This updates the existing backend-selection fix split from #50030 at maintainers' request, rather than opening a competing implementation. #57091 owns the prerequisite Marlin activation-contract changes.

AI assistance (OpenAI Codex) was used. The submitting human must review every changed line, run the relevant tests, and defend the change.

title: [KV Offload] Expose OffloadingManager.lock()/unlock() and service the tiering control plane off the scheduler thread
body:
## Purpose

Two things, in priority order.

**1. Expose exclusive access to an `OffloadingManager` as a public API.** `lock()` / `unlock()`, plus a `locked()` helper, guard a manager's whole state subtree: the manager, the tiers it composes, and any front-end state those tiers own. Manager methods never acquire it themselves, so a caller holds it across as many operations as its own invariants need. That property is the point — several manager operations only make sense in sequence. `prepare_load()` documents that its keys are offloaded, a fact `lookup()` established one hook earlier, so a caller has to be able to span both. Internal per-method locking cannot offer that.

**2. Use it for the first case that needs it** (#55179). The `p2p` secondary tier answers a remote peer, which the engine does not drive, so its control plane only advanced from `on_schedule_end`. A peer's lookup or fetch therefore waited for a model-step boundary — seconds on a saturated rank, gating a transfer of well under one. Tiers now opt in with `needs_control_plane_thread`, and `TieringOffloadingManager` runs one thread that polls them and lets them serve between steps.

## Not a duplicate of the open PRs on #55179

This overlaps open work and I want that on the record rather than buried.

| PR | Author | Driver | Locking |
|---|---|---|---|
| **this** | me | thread owned by `TieringOffloadingManager` | **public `lock()`/`unlock()` on `OffloadingManager`, held by callers** |
| #58113 | me | same thread, same sweep | private `_enter_step`/`_exit_step`/`_observation_lock` + `*_unlocked` variants |
| #57165 | @nilig | `EngineCore` poller thread | new `KVConnectorBase_V1.poll_pending_work` |
| #55962 | @Etelis | `EngineCore` + connector base API + executor changes | new base-API hook |
| #57139 | me | — | the separate async peer-registration half, not this |

**This supersedes my own #58113, which I will close.** The difference is not cosmetic:

- **#58113 does not expose an API.** It takes the lock inside the manager's public methods, which forces a `*_unlocked` variant of every method `_SecondaryTierFacingParent` can re-enter (`lookup`, `on_new_request`, `create_store_job`, `on_request_finished`, `reset_cache`) because the parent handle's caller already holds it. That duplication is most of its `+393` lines in `manager.py`, and it is precisely what prevents an outside caller from saying "hold this across several operations." Moving the lock to the caller removes every one of those variants.
- **#58113 releases at `on_schedule_end`, which is not the end of the step.** `build_connector_meta` called `on_schedule_end` ~40 lines early, before `_build_store_jobs` → `prepare_store` (which evicts) and before `on_request_finished`. So its `prepare_store` re-acquired via `_enter_step()` and nothing released it: on every step that builds store jobs — the common case under load — the lock was held across `future.result()`, starving the control thread in exactly the window the change exists to exploit. That plausibly explains #58113's own "parity-within-noise" result, which was measured through the bug, and that conclusion should be re-tested.

Relative to #57165 / #55962: same goal, but no new `KVConnectorBase_V1` hook and no `EngineCore` or executor changes. In #55179 @nilig asked for a read on "a thread touching the connector from inside `EngineCore`, even phase-exclusive, versus a control thread owned by the tier" — this is a working implementation of the second option, offered as input to that question. If maintainers prefer either existing PR, close this one.

## Changes

Commit 1, **`on_schedule_end` runs last** — independent of all locking, reviewable on its own. Its docstring already claimed "called once at the end of each scheduler step"; it was called ~40 lines early. Moving it makes the contract true and gives callers a sound release point. Two ordering consequences, both handled: `prepare_store`'s poll becomes unconditional (the per-step gate was previously reset mid-`build_connector_meta`, which is where its fresh completion data came from — without this, eviction decisions would run on data up to a step stale), and `_flush_pending_cascades` now re-parks keys this step parked, which is safe because `_maybe_finalize_request` holds off while `pending_cascade_keys` is non-empty.

Commit 2, **the API and its consumer**.

`OffloadingConnectorScheduler` holds one region per engine step, opened by the first manager-touching hook and closed at the end of `build_connector_meta`, so the manager is free while the engine runs the model. Hooks outside `schedule()` take a short region.

Two placements are load-bearing and easy to get wrong:

- **`has_pending_push_work` must use the short region.** `EngineCore.step()` returns early at `core.py:597` when `has_requests()` is false, so a step-scoped acquire there would never reach the release and would hold the manager for good — the state an idle engine settles into. It does still need the lock: `has_pending_work()` iterates `_req_state` while the control thread may insert or delete via `parent.on_new_request` / `on_request_finished`.
- **`take_events` drains inside the region.** `manager.take_events()` is a generator whose backing list is cleared once exhausted, so iterating it lazily both pinned the manager for the consumer's duration and discarded events a concurrent `complete_write` appended, unpublished. It stays a generator so the caller's truthiness check at `sched/scheduler.py` is unchanged.

The thread yields unconditionally *after* `unlock()`, which is what bounds the scheduler's wait to one round — Python locks are not fair, so a release-then-reacquire loop could starve it. A failed round is logged, not fatal, and `on_schedule_end` still serves every tier, so the fallback is per-step servicing. `_process_finished_jobs` takes a tier filter so a round does not drag tiers that expect the scheduler thread. `shutdown()` stops and joins the thread before any tier teardown, since closing a transport under a live round can end the process rather than raise.

Config: `control_plane_interval_s` in `kv_connector_extra_config`, default 1 ms, `0` disables the thread and restores per-step servicing.

Docstrings that claimed single-threaded tier access are corrected, including the eviction-race argument in `_pin_and_register_hits` — which still holds, now because `serve_external_requests` runs inside one hold of the lock. `async_lookup.py`'s "owned exclusively by the scheduler thread" claim was outright false once `parent.lookup` can fan out to `fs.lookup` from the control thread.

## Test results

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/ tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/ -q
  901 passed, 12 skipped in 295s      (baseline on this tree: 889 passed, 12 skipped)

pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/ -q
  217 passed in 66s                   (subset of the above; re-run on its own)

pre-commit: all hooks pass, including ruff, ruff-format, mypy, and check-test-tethering.
```

Note for reviewers: a whole-directory run of `tests/v1/kv_offload/` produces a large number of CUDA IMA errors that are **pre-existing and unrelated** (`tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/` poisons the rest of the session). Run the subdirectories separately.

12 new tests. The two that matter most were both verified to fail without the change, not just to pass with it:

- `test_on_schedule_end_is_the_last_manager_call_of_a_step` — without the reorder it observes `['on_schedule_end', 'prepare_store']`. This is the check #58113's suite lacks, because its `_step()` helper drives `on_schedule_end` with no following `prepare_store`.
- `test_control_thread_and_scheduler_never_overlap` — with `lock()`/`unlock()` stubbed to no-ops it detects 86 overlaps. It also asserts both threads made progress, so neither a thread that never runs nor one that starves the scheduler passes it.

I wrote and then **deleted** a third test ("no eviction between a served lookup and its pin") after finding it still passed with the lock neutered: LRU keeps evicting the fresh keys rather than the constantly-looked-up hit keys, so it could never fail. The overlap test is the real guard for that property, and a test that cannot fail is worse than no test.

## Model evaluation — the 4-case matrix from #55179

Run on two H200 pods, Llama-3.2-1B, `--enforce-eager`, `--block-size 16`, 96 GiB CPU
primary tier, `secondary_tiers: [{"type": "p2p"}]`, `max-model-len 32768`.

**Topology.** Source = the pod holding the KV in its CPU offload tier. Consumer = the
other pod, which probes the source over P2P (`remote_kv_source`) and fetches. Every
measured fetch uses a freshly generated ~27k-token prompt that is populated on the source
first, so nothing hits a GPU prefix cache and the fetch is real work: each one moved
**~1720 chunks** (`kv_offload_tiering_chunk_hits` delta), i.e. the full prefix.

**Busy** = source saturated with 8 concurrent ~27k-token prefills. That took its
request latency from **0.018 s idle to 1.40 s**, so the control plane really is gated
behind ~1.4 s of model work — the same regime as the issue's report.

**Cold** = no P2P session yet. A session lives as long as the engine, so only the first
fetch after a restart is genuinely cold; both pods were restarted between every phase and
the cold fetch measured first.

**Signal** = the consumer's `vllm:kv_offload_lookup_async_delay_seconds` delta for the
measured request (one observation per fetch). Warm figures are the mean of 3 reps.

| case | A: baseline (`7b077f36a8`) | B: #58113 | C: this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| idle, cold | 0.177 s | — | **0.133 s** |
| idle, warm | 0.0455 s | — | **0.0457 s** |
| busy, cold | 0.440 s | 0.289 s | **0.155 s** |
| busy, warm | 0.220 s | 0.129 s | **0.0534 s** |

**The per-step gating penalty, which is what this PR removes:**

| arm | idle-warm | busy-warm | penalty |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: baseline | 0.0455 s | 0.2196 s | **4.83x** |
| C: this PR | 0.0457 s | 0.0534 s | **1.17x** |

Saturating the source costs baseline 4.8x on the consumer's lookup delay. With the control
thread it costs 1.17x — the stall is essentially gone, and a busy source now behaves like
an idle one.

Supporting numbers on busy-warm: per-chunk tiering delay
(`kv_offload_tiering_lookup_async_delay_seconds`) 0.100 s → 0.0174 s (5.8x), and end-to-end
TTFT for the fetch 0.310 s → 0.144 s (2.2x). Idle is parity within noise in every metric,
as expected — there is no model step to hide behind.

Per-rep spread, busy-warm: baseline `0.1929 / 0.2532 / 0.2127`, this PR
`0.0388 / 0.0427 / 0.0786`. The distributions do not overlap — the worst rep here is still
better than the best baseline rep.

**No source-side slowdown.** The concern that holding the manager lock slows the scheduler
does not show up: on the busy source, request latency was 1.4174 s (baseline) vs 1.4039 s
(this PR), and the populate-request mean 1.7056 s vs 1.7100 s. The background load
generator completed 158 vs 153 requests over comparable windows, a ~3% difference that is
within single-run noise and not corroborated by either latency measure. A dedicated
`vllm bench serve` throughput comparison is still worth running before merge; I did not
run one.

### On #58113

Arm B is #58113 at `b8ea135c71`, measured on the same pods in the same session. It lands
**between** baseline and this PR: busy-warm 0.129 s vs baseline 0.220 s vs 0.0534 s here.

That is what the release-point bug predicts. #58113's thread is not dead — on steps that
build no store jobs the lock is released normally, so it recovers some of the win (1.7x
over baseline). But on any step that does build store jobs, `prepare_store` re-acquires
after `on_schedule_end` released and nothing releases it again, so the lock is held across
`future.result()` and the thread is shut out for exactly that step. Under load most steps
build store jobs, which is why it recovers only about a third of what is available (4.1x
over baseline here, 2.4x over #58113).

I am reporting this as *consistent with* the bug rather than as direct proof of the
mechanism; the mechanism itself is demonstrated by the unit test, which observes the call
order `['on_schedule_end', 'prepare_store']` without the reorder in commit 1.

### Caveat on absolute magnitudes

These numbers are much smaller than the issue's 13.6 s, and deliberately so: this is
Llama-3.2-1B on a single H200 per side, not GLM-5.2-FP8 on DP8. What reproduces here is the
**mechanism and its scaling** — the consumer's lookup delay is proportional to the source's
step time under baseline, and roughly independent of it with the control thread. The issue's
13.6 s came from a far slower source; the ratio, not the absolute, is what transfers.

Raw per-rep JSON for all six runs is available on request.

## NIXL thread-safety: checked, and it holds

Checked against the **NIXL 1.4.1** sources (`ai-dynamo/nixl` at tag `v1.4.1`), which is the
deployed version. **This corrects an earlier version of this description**, which said
`NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_RW` does not exist and that the config offers no way to request a sync
mode. Both statements were true of 0.6.0, which is what I had installed; neither is true of
1.4.1.

**Serialized use from a second thread is supported.** `makeMtType`
(`src/plugins/ucx/ucx_utils.cpp:383-392`) returns only `WORKER` or `SINGLE`, never
`CONTEXT` -- and `mt_mode_t::CONTEXT` is the only value that maps to
`UCS_THREAD_MODE_SINGLE` (`ucx_utils.cpp:476-492`), the one UCX mode with creator-thread
affinity. Grepping confirms `CONTEXT` never appears as a produced value, only in switch
arms. So the weakest mode NIXL ever requests is `UCS_THREAD_MODE_SERIALIZED`, which UCX
documents as *"Multiple threads can access, but only one at a time"* -- precisely this
design. And because `enable_prog_thread` defaults on for this transport, it actually gets
`UCS_THREAD_MODE_MULTI`, with a hard library-support check that throws if unavailable.

**The manager lock is load-bearing, not redundant.** With `syncMode = NONE` -- which is what
this transport gets, since it sets neither `enable_listen` nor `sync_mode` -- NIXL's internal
agent lock compiles to no-ops (`src/core/sync.h:36-39`), leaving ~23 agent entry points
unguarded over shared, non-atomic containers. The external mutex is therefore the only
protection, and it must cover every entry point plus the lifetime of handles passed between
calls. It does.

Two caveats worth recording:

- NIXL binds a shared UCX worker per calling thread (`tlsSharedWorkerMap`,
  `ucx_backend.cpp:821-825`). That is harmless only while there is exactly one shared
  worker, which holds for this configuration (`num_workers` unset ⇒ `numSharedWorkers_ == 1`,
  so every thread maps to worker 0) but would not if a `num_workers` UCX backend param were
  ever set. The chosen worker also travels on the request handle rather than being
  re-derived per call, so a transfer prepped on one thread and polled on another still uses
  the same worker.
- 1.4.1 *does* accept an explicit `sync_mode` (including `NIXL_THREAD_SYNC_RW`, value 2),
  which would make NIXL's own locking real as belt-and-braces, and is what every upstream
  multi-threaded test uses. I have not added it, because the parameter does not exist on
  0.6.0 and passing it unconditionally would break older environments; it needs the same
  kind of version gate `capture_telemetry` already needs. Worth a follow-up.

Honest limit: `~/nixl` is a 1.4.1 source checkout, not a build, and only 0.6.0 is installed
locally, so every 1.4.1 claim above is static source reading rather than runtime
introspection. A runtime confirmation (log the thread mode `ucp_worker_query` actually
grants, or run the two-thread pattern under TSan) would close the remaining gap. The
end-to-end matrix above ran on the deployed 1.4.1 across ~14k P2P chunk fetches with no
transfer failures, which is evidence but not a substitute.

pyzmq is fine under strict serialization: libzmq permits migrating a socket between threads
given a full memory barrier, which lock acquire/release provides, and nothing is bound
thread-locally at socket creation. The one hazard is `zmq_ctx_destroy` racing a socket call,
which the shutdown ordering handles.

The two items that were blocking this leaving draft are now done: the 4-case matrix has been run on H200 hardware (results above) and the NIXL question has been checked against 1.4.1. What remains before undraft is a dedicated throughput comparison and a human pass over the diff.

title: [DSpark] Support pipeline-parallel targets in aggregated serving
body:
## What

DSpark on a pipeline-parallel target in aggregated (non-PD) serving. The drafter runs wholly on the last PP stage; this PR makes that work correctly:

- **Draft broadcast across stages**: the last stage's speculator proposes drafts, but earlier stages need them for the next verification step. The last rank now broadcasts the fresh drafts on the PP group (`PPHandler.broadcast_drafts`), and the broadcast is gated out of the no-op second call site when a speculator ran (double-posting misaligned the recv FIFO and hung the pipeline).
- **Warmup**: the deferred PP post-update triton kernel never runs during warmup steps on non-last ranks; its first mid-serving compile would deadlock against the in-flight NCCL broadcast. `warmup_pp_decode_update` compiles it during capture, and the sampled-token broadcast is disabled for the warmup window.
- **Draft embedding under PP**: the drafter aliases the target's embedding table, which #50514 retains on the last PP stage when speculative decoding is active. (An earlier revision of this PR loaded a separate drafter copy; dropped per review.)
- **Padded graph batch safety**: the DFlash prepare-inputs kernel clears `input_ids`/`positions` and sets `is_padding` on CUDA-graph padding rows, and the DSv4 top-k router zeroes padded-row selections instead of reading uninitialized state.

## Not a duplicate

Split from #53577 (reviewer request): this PR is the aggregated-serving half; the PD prefill + KV-transfer half follows separately.

## Tests

- New/extended: `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py`, `tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py`.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_prepare_inputs.py tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py -q` → 1686 passed, 6 skipped.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_warmup_blocks.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py -q` → 34 passed.

## Model evaluation

DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0731) DSpark K=5, IFB PP2×TP2, GSM8K strict-match: **0.9484** (1319 samples; an earlier revision measured 0.9545 — both within noise of the target-only arm). Spec decode mean acceptance length 4.38.

Kimi-K3 DSpark IFB PP relies on the TritonMLA causal multi-token fix from #51065 (merged; included in this branch's base). Smoke-verified on SM120 (PP2×TP4): coherent outputs with healthy per-position draft acceptance (144/96/55/31/22/17/12/6 over K=8).

title: [Bugfix] GLM-5.3-Flash: fp8 plan dtype on SM90 sparse MLA, and right-size the indexer prefill workspace
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55221.

Two independent fixes for GLM-5.3-Flash, both live on `main` after #53906 landed.

**1. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` cannot start on the SM90 sparse MLA backend.** An fp8 KV
cache is allocated as `uint8` storage and `run()` views it as `float8_e4m3fn`, but
`plan()` was handed the storage dtype, which the FlashInfer wrapper rejects:
`ValueError: MLA kv_data_type torch.uint8 is not supported`. One-line dtype fix in
`FlashInferMLASparseSM90Builder`.

**2. The indexer prefill workspace is sized in the wrong unit.**
`get_max_prefill_buffer_size()` returns a token count (`max_model_len * 40` entries of
132 bytes), but this indexer's KV is pool-granular: the spec carries
`compress_ratio == index_kpool`, and `split_indexer_prefill_chunks()` is fed compressed
sequence lengths. `deepseek_v4/attention.py` already divides at the same call site.
At `--max-model-len 1048576` with `index_kpool = 4` this locks ~5.16 GiB per GPU during
the memory profile, straight out of the KV budget. Reported by @nood-co1 in #53906.

## Not a duplicate

- #51252 divides the *builder's* chunk budget by `compress_ratio` for DeepSeek; this is
  the model-side `max_total_seq_len` for GLM-5.3. Per @nood-co1 the two compose.
- #54743 scopes offload group configs to prefix-cacheable groups; different file,
  different failure.
- Searched open PRs for `get_max_prefill_buffer_size`, `max_total_seq_len` and the SM90
  sparse backend; nothing else touches these call sites.

## Testing

No unit test covers either path (both need a GLM-5.3 checkpoint and FlashInfer on
Hopper), so this was validated by serving. 2x H200 NVL, TP2, LibertAI NVFP4 weights,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, MTP k=3, CUDA graphs on, CPU offload
with a 256 GiB region. Both fixes have been running in production here since 2026-08-29
and 2026-09-01 respectively.

- fp8 fix: without it the server does not start; with it `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` is
  selected and the KV pool holds 4,503,445 tokens against 2,532,577 in bf16.
- workspace fix: available KV memory 29.44 -> 32.06 GiB, GPU KV cache size
  4,503,445 -> 4,904,494 tokens (+8.9%). Note that run also raised `--max-num-seqs`
  16 -> 32, so part of the freed memory went back into per-sequence buffers.
- Regression battery after the workspace change: needle retrieval on 1M-token prompts
  4/4 at depths 0.05/0.35/0.65/0.95; 32 concurrent 118k-token prompts, 32/32 with 0
  failures and 0 preemptions; an eviction cycle of eleven 500k-token prompts against a
  4.9M-token KV pool, where the return visit is served from CPU offload (61.0s cold,
  3.5s on return, `external_prefix_cache_hits_total` +492,800).

## Model evaluation

fp8 KV against bf16 on the same checkpoint: GSM8K 0.888 vs 0.880, MATH exact 0.9050 vs
0.9071 (symbolic 0.9671 vs 0.9664), MBPP 0.910 vs 0.920, IFEval prompt strict 0.880 /
instruction strict 0.925. All within noise. The workspace change moves no math: same
kernels, same inputs, only a smaller scratch allocation, and the needle battery above is
identical before and after.

title: [Bugfix][MoE] Handle missing DP metadata in the two-sided NVLink all2all
body:
## Purpose

#54016 fixed this in `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided.py`: with expert parallelism but no data parallelism — it was hit with `TP=1, PCP=4, EP` — `ForwardContext.dp_metadata` is None, and `get_local_sizes()` asserted that it is not.

`flashinfer_nvlink_two_sided.py` still carries the unfixed copy of the same function:

```python
def get_local_sizes():
    dp_metadata = get_forward_context().dp_metadata
    assert dp_metadata is not None
    return dp_metadata.get_chunk_sizes_across_dp_rank()
```

The consumer in the same file is already written for the None case:

```python
# flashinfer_alltoall_dispatch
max_num_token = (
    max(global_num_tokens_cpu) if global_num_tokens_cpu is not None else x.shape[0]
)
```

so that fallback branch is unreachable today — the assert fires first. `flashinfer_nvlink_two_sided` is a currently selectable `all2all_backend`; only the older `flashinfer_all2allv` spelling of it is deprecated (`cuda_communicator.py:231`).

Reproduced without a GPU:

```python
>>> with patch.object(two_sided, "get_forward_context",
...                   lambda: SimpleNamespace(dp_metadata=None)):
...     two_sided.get_local_sizes()
AssertionError
>>> # same call on one_sided, after #54016
None
```

## Changes

- `get_local_sizes()` returns `None` when there is no DP metadata, exactly as #54016 did for the one-sided module.
- Widen `flashinfer_alltoall_dispatch`'s `global_num_tokens_cpu` annotation to `list[int] | None`, matching what its body already accepts.

I checked the other prepare/finalize backends that read `dp_metadata` — `deepep_v2.py:201`, `moonep.py:360`, `experts/batched_deep_gemm_moe.py:393` — and they all already guard for None. This was the last one that did not.

## Test

`tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_nvlink_local_sizes.py`, CPU-only (`cpu_test`), pins **both** modules to the same contract with and without DP metadata, so the two copies cannot drift apart again.

On current `main`:

```
FAILED tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_nvlink_local_sizes.py::test_get_local_sizes_without_dp_metadata[two_sided]
1 failed, 3 passed
```

With this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_flashinfer_nvlink_local_sizes.py
4 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files. I do not have an NVLink/MNNVL machine, so the end-to-end EP path is not exercised here; the change is the same three lines that were already reviewed and merged for the sibling module.

---

Found by taking a merged fix (#54016) and checking whether the same pattern survived in sibling implementations; the assertion failure and the new test were run on a CPU-only host, with and without the change. Commit carries `Co-authored-by: Claude`.*

title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Keep cross-node MNNVL groups off CUDA IPC all-reduce
body:
## Purpose

Addresses #52778.

**Reporter-provided multi-node GPU validation is available below; same-node GPU controls and model-output evaluation remain pending.** Local validation uses CPU tests only; this PR does not claim submitter-run GPU tests.

Cross-node MNNVL-capable groups remain enabled for custom all-gather/reduce-scatter, but cannot exchange node-local CUDA IPC handles. `should_custom_ar()` currently admits TP=2 cross-node groups; CUDA-graph teardown can subsequently exchange their IPC handles and terminate the process inside `cudaIpcOpenMemHandle`.

This patch:

- declines node-local custom all-reduce when `mnnvl_only=True`, allowing the existing caller dispatch to try another backend;
- skips IPC graph registration for those groups, whose MNNVL collectives use pre-registered symmetric memory;
- preserves same-node custom all-reduce and the existing MNNVL all-gather/reduce-scatter eligibility;
- adds regression coverage in the existing custom-all-reduce test suite.

No CUDA kernels or arithmetic implementations are changed.

## Why this is not duplicate work

Before starting, #52778 had no assignee or visible work claim. Issue/timeline checks and open-PR searches for the issue number, cross-node IPC, MNNVL custom allreduce, `mnnvl_only`, and `register_graph_buffers` found no open implementation of this specific fix. The issue-number and `mnnvl_only` searches were repeated before opening this PR.

Related changes address different mechanisms:

- Merged #53253 prevents unsupported cross-node groups from reaching MNNVL rendezvous; its description explicitly distinguishes #52778. Supported Blackwell groups still reach the paths changed here.
- Open #53377 concerns FlashInfer fusion-workspace capability checks.
- Open #46515 concerns IPC-handle lifetime rather than cross-node eligibility.
- Open #50505 changes buffer sizing for batch invariance rather than node locality.

## Test Plan

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_gather_reduce_scatter.py \
  tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py -k 'not multi_process' -v
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py
git diff --check
```

## Test Result

Executed locally on Apple Silicon macOS with Python 3.12.11 and PyTorch 2.13.0:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| New regression tests with unpatched production code | 3 failed, 13 passed, 4 GPU tests skipped |
| Patched custom-all-reduce suite | 16 passed, 4 GPU tests skipped |
| Adjacent communication suites | 19 passed, 1 GPU test skipped, 10 distributed tests deselected |
| Applicable pre-commit hooks, including Ruff and mypy | Passed |
| Diff whitespace check | Passed |

The three baseline failures cover eager/captured cross-node all-reduce dispatch and cross-node IPC graph registration. Positive controls cover same-node registration and MNNVL collective eligibility.

These tests exercise real production Python methods and CPU tensors, with CUDA operations and process-group calls mocked at the boundaries. They do not execute CUDA IPC, NCCL, or MNNVL kernels. The precompiled editable install was unavailable on this host; the Python tests ran through normal source imports after installing dependencies with `uv`.

## Outstanding validation

- [ ] Human-run relevant tests and final line-by-line review under the contribution policy.
- [x] Reporter-validated matched unpatched/patched startup, CUDA-graph capture, and serving benchmarks on two MNNVL-capable GB200 NVL72 nodes with TP=2.
- [ ] Same-node TP=2 control and GPU all-gather/reduce-scatter regression run.
- [ ] Model-output/evaluation results for the serving-backend change.

**External GPU validation: the issue reporter confirmed the fix on September 8, 2026.** See [the full validation report](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55835#issuecomment-5587236720). On two GB200 NVL72 nodes with one GPU per node, cross-node TP=2, and custom all-reduce left enabled, the unpatched control aborts with `custom_all_reduce.cuh:143`. Applying this patch as the only change allows CUDA-graph capture, server startup, and serving benchmarks at concurrency 1/16/64/128 to complete. The reporter also confirmed that MNNVL setup remains active.

The submitter still has no GPU environment. Same-node GPU controls, GPU all-gather/reduce-scatter regression runs, model-output accuracy evaluation, and the remaining human-review requirements have not been reported as complete.

## AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with issue triage, investigation, patch preparation, and execution of the local CPU tests and lint checks. The patch was approved for publication by the submitter. The outstanding checklist is intentionally incomplete. External GPU results above are attributed to the issue reporter; they do not attest to submitter-run GPU tests, model-output accuracy evaluation, or completion of the remaining human-review requirements. The commit includes AI attribution and sign-off.


## Main synchronization — September 23, 2026

Merged upstream `main` (`0f2a15c9`) without rewriting the original validated commit. Resolved the test-file insertion conflict by retaining both the PR's CPU fixture/regressions and upstream's new SM100 fused-mHC GPU regression.

- Production file is byte-for-byte unchanged from the prior PR head; all existing PR test/helper functions and both new upstream mHC functions are AST-identical to their respective originals.
- Custom-all-reduce suite: **16 passed, 5 GPU tests skipped**.
- Adjacent communication suites with `-k 'not multi_process'`: **20 passed, 1 GPU test skipped, 10 distributed tests deselected**.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks (including Ruff, mypy and test tethering), scoped whitespace checks, and independent resolution review passed.
- No GPU/model evaluation was rerun for this synchronization. Prior hardware results remain attributed to the reporter's original patch validation.

## CI status (original PR head)

The failing [`pre-run-check`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/34190799792/job/101948293711) is the repository's CI authorization gate, not a lint/test result. It requires one of `verified`, `ready`, or `ready-run-all-tests`, or at least four merged PRs from the author; the log reports one merged PR and no qualifying label. The actual `pre-commit` job was therefore skipped. GitHub's ready-for-review status is distinct from those authorization labels. Local changed-file pre-commit checks passed as reported above; upstream CI remains unexecuted behind that gate. No CI policy or authorization controls were modified.

title: [Bugfix] Make online FP8 MoE experts batch-invariant under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
body:
Fixes #57016

## Purpose

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, a MoE model served with `--quantization fp8` (online per-tensor FP8, Triton experts) still produces output that depends on which other requests share its batch: greedy tokens flip within the first ~10 positions and prefix-cached K/V differs depending on who wrote it. Dense layers are invariant; only the experts are not.

Two things were wrong:

1. `Fp8PerTensorOnlineMoEMethod` (and `Fp8MoEMethod` for FP8-serialized per-tensor checkpoints with dynamic activations) quantize the expert inputs with one dynamic scale over the whole activation tensor (`kFp8DynamicTensorSym`), i.e. the max over every token of every co-batched request. Under batch-invariant mode this PR selects `kFp8DynamicTokenSym` and passes `per_act_token_quant=True`, mirroring what `Fp8LinearMethod` already does for dense layers.
2. Switching to per-token activations exposed a latent launcher bug: `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` passed `stride_bse=0` for 1-D `[E]` weight scales (and `stride_bsn=1` for the singleton dim of `[E, 1, 1]`), so the kernel's `per_channel_quant` branch read expert 0's scale for every expert or indexed past the buffer. The combination tests already skipped "per-tensor weights + per-token activations" for the Triton experts as NYI, although `TritonExperts._supports_quant_scheme` advertises the pair. This PR passes the expert stride unconditionally and broadcasts singleton scale dims, and narrows the NYI gate to the still-unsupported "per-channel weights + per-tensor activations" case so the combination suite covers the fixed pair.

The bf16 Triton expert path is already invariant on `main` (`get_default_config`/`get_moe_configs` pin the tile config under the flag); the reporter's bf16 mismatch was on 0.27.1.

## Test Plan

- New `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::test_online_fp8_moe_logprobs_bitwise_bs1_vs_bsN` (granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct, `--quantization fp8`, greedy, BS=1 vs BS=8 bitwise tokens+logprobs). Fails on `main`, passes with this PR.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_modular_kernel_combinations.py`: the per-tensor-weight + per-token-activation FP8 config is no longer skipped for `TritonExperts` / `BatchedTritonExperts` / `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts`.
- Reporter's reproducer (co-batch and writer-suffix modes) against a running server.
- Kernel check: `fused_experts` vs `tests.kernels.utils.torch_experts`, E=32, N=1024, K=2048, M=128, topk=4, per-tensor `[E,1,1]` weight scales: max abs err 0.010 with per-tensor activations, 0.003 with per-token activations (before the launcher fix the per-token case returned values in the thousands).
- Existing suites: `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py`, `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py::test_fused_moe`, pre-commit, `mypy-3.12`.

Hardware: RTX 5090 (sm_120), WSL2, torch 2.13.0+cu130. The modular kernel combination suite itself does not run on this WSL2 machine (spawned worker fails with `CUDA error: invalid resource handle` on unmodified `main` too), so that part relies on CI and on the independent H20 run linked below.

## Test Result

- Reporter's probe, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 --quantization fp8`, before: A-alone vs A-with-B first token flip at 11 (logprob gap 0.166), warm-vs-cold flip at 11 (gap 0.347). After: every comparison identical, both rounds.
- gsm8k 5-shot, 1319 questions, granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct `--quantization fp8 --enforce-eager` (tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py): default (no flag) 34.1%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` on `main` 34.3%, `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` with this PR 32.7%. Per-token activation quantization is strictly finer than per-tensor, and the kernel-level error is lower, so the small delta is sampling noise from a 1B model.
- New e2e test: PASS with the PR, FAIL on `main` ("logprobs are not bitwise equal between BS=1 and BS=8; max abs diff 2.2e-01").
- Independent cross-architecture validation by @CarrotSwordsman on H20 (sm_90, real Linux GPU, driver 535), [comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57092#issuecomment-5730213177): the same e2e test FAILS on a clean 0.28.0+cu129 wheel (max abs diff 2.8e-01) and PASSES with this PR's files applied, reproducing and eliminating the #57016 symptom on Hopper. Their `test_modular_kernel_combinations.py` run on the patched wheel was 8 passed / 2 failed / 1 skipped, the two failures being `deep_gemm`'s `NVCC >= 12.3` assert in a container pinned to 12.1. As they note, that suite does not discriminate against a release wheel (the pre-PR NYI skip is not present there to be removed), so the e2e pair is the evidence in that setup.
- `tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py` (non-DeepGEMM): 164 passed, 20 skipped. `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe.py -k test_fused_moe`: 241 passed. pre-commit and `mypy-3.12` clean on all changed files.

Not a duplicate: no open PR references #57016 (checked with `gh pr list --search "57016 in:body"` and by searching open PRs for "batch invariant moe"); #55881 is the XPU MoE variant and does not touch the CUDA Triton path or FP8 activation quantization.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the investigation and drafting; every line was reviewed and every test run by the submitter.
