title: [Attention] Portable Triton sparse-MLA fallback for SM12x (consumer Blackwell)
body:
## Purpose

DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2) currently have **no working sparse-attention backend on
consumer Blackwell** (SM12x: RTX 5090, GB10): the native FlashMLA sparse kernels
(`vllm._flashmla_C`) only build for sm90/sm100, and the sole SM12x option,
`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, livelocks under sustained load — GPUs pin at 100 % with zero
output until the NCCL watchdog kills the server. Fixes #51921 (on SM12x).

This makes the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend work on SM12x by binding portable **Triton**
implementations of `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` / `flash_mla_with_kvcache` when the native extension
can't serve the device. The kernels are from #49026 (@marksunner, validated there on
sm_121/GB10) — this PR is that work rebased onto current main as a first-class code path
instead of that PR's runtime monkeypatch, with its model-side diffs dropped (main already has
that content). Supersedes/continues #49026 — happy to hand back or co-drive.

## Scope

This path covers **DeepSeek-geometry sparse MLA** — `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`, i.e. the
512 NoPE + 64 RoPE = **576** head layout: DeepSeek-V3.2/V4.1 and GLM-5.2. The Triton kernels
and the `fp8_ds_mla` 656-byte per-token entry are built around that 576 layout
(`get_supported_head_sizes() == [576]`).

**Not covered:** NoPE MLA models (`qk_rope_head_dim = 0`, `head_size = 512`) such as
GLM-5.3-Flash. Those are correctly rejected at the head-size gate and need the `pe_dim != 64`
work in #55277 / #53969 *in addition to* this PR. Thanks to @haqishen for confirming this
boundary on real SM120 hardware (see comments).

Changes:
- `ops/flashmla.py`: `_use_triton_sparse_mla()` (auto on SM12x; `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE`
  forces on/off) selects the Triton binding; `is_flashmla_sparse_supported()` reports True
  there; `get_mla_metadata` returns `(None, None)` (the Triton kernels self-schedule).
- New files: `sm12x_sparse_mla_attn.py`, `sparse_mla_kernels.py`, `sparse_mla_env.py`,
  `ops/deepseek_v4_ops/*` — kernels + helpers from #49026, unchanged.
- `flashmla_sparse.py`: capability 12 allowed on the Triton path; %16 fp8-decode head padding
  there (64-head models at TP=8 have 8 heads/rank — 64-padding wastes 87 % of attention
  compute); b12x fused fast path with clean fallback.
- `sparse_attn_indexer.py`: DeepGEMM not hard-required on the Triton path (fallbacks exist).
- `envs.py`: `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE*` registered.
- **Recommended runtime knob:** set `VLLM_SPARSE_MLA_SPLITK=32` on SM12x — it enables the
  split-K decode path and is a large single-stream decode win (see Test Result). The backend
  now logs a one-time hint when it is left unset.

**All changes are no-ops on sm90/sm100** unless `VLLM_TRITON_MLA_SPARSE=1` is set explicitly.

## Test Plan

End-to-end serving on 24× RTX 5090 (3 hosts, TP=8 × PP=3), GLM-5.2-NVFP4,
`--kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE`, driven by `vllm bench serve`
(1K-in/256-out latency cell @ c1, then a c16 throughput cell; repeated full passes incl.
10K-token prompts). This load reproduces the #51921 livelock on stock v0.26.0/v0.28.0 within
minutes, so it discriminates cleanly between the two paths.

## Test Result

| | stock (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`) | this PR's path (`FLASHMLA_SPARSE` + Triton) |
|---|---|---|
| latency cell (c1, n=8) | first request spins **660 s** (GPUs 100 %, zero output), engine dead before the next cell | **8/8** — TTFT 5.3 s, **TPOT 41 ms** |
| throughput cell (c16) | never reached | **64/64** in 136 s — 120 tok/s output |
| output quality | n/a | coherent, correct stop reasons, `glm47` reasoning/tool parsers intact |

Startup shows the Triton binding + backend selection on all 24 workers; KV cache
(`fp8_ds_mla`, 656 B/token layout) sizes as expected.

Note: the runtime validation above ran on this exact diff backported onto v0.28.0 (our
production pin). We are set up to re-validate a main build on the same cluster, and happy to
add unit tests in whatever shape maintainers prefer for device-gated kernels.

### Independent validation on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, GB202-class)

Separately from the 5090 gang, we ran **GLM-5.2 NVFP4** on a single 8× RTX PRO 6000 (96 GB)
node with this PR's path (`--attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla
--reasoning-parser glm47`, `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS`, `VLLM_SPARSE_MLA_SPLITK=32`), TP=8:

| cell (1K in / 256 out) | TP=8 |
|---|---|
| c1 TPOT median | 23.84 ms |
| c1 output tok/s | 36.3 |
| c16 output tok/s | 211.5 |
| KV pool | 480K tok (util 0.90) |

The 433 GB checkpoint fits one node (54.7 GiB weights/GPU at TP=8), serves coherently, and
single-stream decode (23.84 ms) approaches our 24×5090 gang's best (22.8 ms).

**On split-K:** with `VLLM_SPARSE_MLA_SPLITK` unset (the default), c1 TPOT was 44.9 ms;
setting it to 32 dropped it to 23.84 ms — the motivation for the one-time startup hint added
here.

Caveat (same as the 5090 result): this ran as this PR's files overlaid on a v0.28.0 image,
not a clean `main` build — a data point, not CI.

title: [Feature][KVConnector][DSv4.1] Encoder-only prefill with NIXL P/D
body:
## Purpose

Implement encoder-only Prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D serving with the direct `NixlConnector` pull path. This follows the full-prompt, cache-hit-replay design in RFC #57738 and builds on the asymmetric P/D direction in RFC #57383: P runs L0-L19 for the whole prompt and produces L20 Main KV/Indexer K, while D reconstructs the adopted replay tail through the full target and samples the first token.

This PR makes the NIXL handoff concrete without depending on the Mooncake implementation in #57872. Both connector paths share the same execution boundary, but their request and transfer protocols differ. P still loads the full target weights in this first change; weight omission is separate work.

I'll validate this PR on real GPU soon and check whether it is better to forward NIXL version before Mooncake.

## Implementation

- Add opt-in `KVTransferConfig.dsv41_encoder_only_prefill` for dedicated `NixlConnector` producer and consumer roles. Restrict this PR to the existing pull connector.
- On P, run L0-L19 normally, execute the L20 pre-mix and canonical compressor/Main-KV/Indexer-K writes, and skip L20 attention/FFN, L21-L39, final norm, LM head, sampling, and draft work.
- Finish a cache-only P request after its full prompt is consumed without generating a token. Each P worker synchronizes its cache writes before completion. The NIXL proxy marks the P request `cache_only=true`, then forwards the remote block/engine metadata returned in P's zero-token response to D for a normal NIXL pull.
- Select transferable groups from V4.1's Main-KV and Indexer-K owner layers. Missing, duplicate, or mixed global/local groups fail closed. Target SWA, compressor continuation, and draft groups stay D-local; D uses the existing bounded-replay path.
- For same-layout, non-DCP pulls, align producer blocks to the range D actually adopts after bounded replay. Use D's per-group local prefix counts to distinguish cached prefix blocks from a discarded partial P tail block; reject mismatched block geometry.
- Limit the initial configuration to NVIDIA, MRV2, PP=1, no PCP or microbatching, a 128-token bounded-replay window and the 40-layer/L20 source topology, text-only requests, and no prompt logprobs. P requires `--no-async-scheduling`; neither role enables speculative decoding in this first path. NIXL's compatibility hash includes drafter settings, so an asymmetric P-without-drafter/D-with-DSpark pair needs separate support.

Enable the option on both server roles:

```json
{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","dsv41_encoder_only_prefill":true}
{"kv_connector":"NixlConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","dsv41_encoder_only_prefill":true}
```

Use the NIXL toy proxy with the dedicated P and D instances. Conventional NIXL requests ignore the proxy's `cache_only` marker when the option is off.

## Validation

## Relationship to other work

RFC #57738 analyzes NIXL pull as its initial path. #57872 implements the same V4.1 execution boundary for direct Mooncake P/D and has separate H20 measurements; it does not validate NIXL. This PR does not bring Mooncake's generic empty-pull completion change into NIXL. NIXL already tracks whether D awaits KV for a real transfer. #56227 provides the bounded-replay foundation used on D.

Open PRs were checked by RFC number and by NIXL/encoder-only/V4.1 keywords. No other open PR implements this boundary on the direct NIXL pull path. The model-side execution code currently overlaps #57872; I am happy to rebase or stack the shared part if maintainers choose a common base, while keeping connector-specific handoff and tests reviewable.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, validation, and drafting. The human submitter will review every changed line, run target-GPU P/D and model evaluation, and defend the change before marking this PR Ready.

title: [RL] Add sharding-aware NCCL M2N weight transfer
body:
## Purpose

Adds a complete, sharding-aware `nccl_m2n` weight-transfer backend built on [NCCL M2N](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nccl-extensions), following [RFC #46439](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/46439).

The broadcast NCCL backend assumes both sides hold the same layout, so a trainer using FSDP or another sharded layout must materialize full parameters before sending them. `nccl_m2n` instead performs one `reshard` between two disjoint meshes in a shared communicator: trainer ranks `[0, T)` and inference-worker ranks `[T, T + N)`.

This PR now includes the full path:

- inference-side engine and wire protocol;
- trainer-side `M2NWeightSource`, `DTensorModuleSource`, and `M2NTrainerWeightTransferEngine`;
- per-parameter destination planning so each inference worker receives only its own shard when layouts permit it;
- strict layout, placement, dtype, and parameter-name validation before transfer or model mutation;
- a runnable FSDP-to-TP example, documentation, unit tests, and multi-GPU E2E coverage.

The backend is selected with `--weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "nccl_m2n"}'`. Its optional runtime is imported lazily, so default vLLM behavior is unchanged.

## Not a duplicate

Checked per `AGENTS.md`:

```bash
gh issue view 46439 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "46439 in:body"
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "NCCL M2N weight transfer"
```

No other open PR implements the RFC's NCCL M2N backend. Adjacent WPI and RDT work uses different transports and does not provide this trainer-to-inference resharding path.

## Test plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer_m2n.py -v
uvx ruff check <touched Python files>
uvx ruff format --check <touched Python files>
```

The suite covers layout and wire validation, registry dispatch, trainer planning, atomic name preflight, direct and fallback destinations, replicated E2E transfer, and a real 1-trainer + 2-worker TP=2 sharded transfer.

## Test results

- Ruff check and format check: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- **CPU or single-GPU environment:** **31 passed, 2 skipped**. The two skipped tests require the `nccl.m2n` runtime and multiple GPUs.
- **Multi-GPU environment** (H100, CUDA 12.9, NCCL 2.30.7): both M2N E2Es passed — the replicated 1-trainer + 1-worker transfer and the sharded 1-trainer + 2-worker TP=2 transfer. The 4-GPU FSDP-to-TP example also passed with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.8`.

No model-quality evaluation is required: this changes transport and placement, not model computation or generated output. The E2E tests verify exact transferred tensor values.

## Known limitations

Documented in `docs/training/weight_transfer/m2n.md`:

- requires `nccl-extensions` and NCCL >= 2.30.5;
- `VLLM_NCCL_SO_PATH` must identify the same NCCL used by `libnccl_m2n.so`;
- parameter tensors may have 1 to 3 dimensions (independent of TP world size); 4-D parameters, FP4, and `Partial` placements are unsupported;
- trainer meshes must be contiguous from rank zero and one- or two-dimensional;
- each destination shard supports at most 16 source shards (`MAX_SOURCES`, an NCCL M2N compile-time limit).

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used (Cursor and Claude Code). The submitter reviewed the resulting changes and is responsible for understanding, testing, and defending them end to end.

title: [Perf][KV Offload] Select the canonical load path by fragment size
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57342.

With `canonical_layout`, CPU→GPU copies are submitted per mapped fragment, but `_select_swap_blocks_fn` picked the load path from the page size. A page ≥ 28 KiB whose fragments are smaller ended up on `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`, in exactly the small-copy regime #42212 moved to Triton.

This makes the selector look at the sizes that are actually submitted: page sizes for the direct layout, `run.fragment_size` for the canonical layout. The 28 KiB threshold and the 8-byte alignment check (the kernel copies `size // 8` words per descriptor) use those. The kernel chunk size still follows the page: sizing it to the fragment was slower for 512-byte fragments (8 KV heads × 128, bf16, TP=8, token-major: 408 ms vs 356 ms for a 32K-token load on an A30) and within 2–4% either way for 1–2 KiB fragments, so loads that already took the Triton path keep their kernel configuration. `canonical_layout` defaults to `False` in the selector, so direct behaviour is unchanged, and stores still always use DMA.

On the default CUDA path (packed K‖V views under LBHNC) the canonical mapping is a single run per page, so nothing changes there either. It matters for mappings with more than one run per page; details and numbers are in the issue.

Not a duplicate: I searched open PRs for `swap_blocks triton offload`, `select_swap_blocks_fn`, `canonical layout triton`, `canonical fragment`, `kv offload triton threshold` and `THRESHOLD_BYTES` (2026-09-17, against `08633cb5cd`). Nothing touches the selector. Closest neighbours are #48936 (block-copy benchmark script), #53971 (attrIdxs bounds in the C++ batch path) and #53544 (skip canonical mappings for packed caches).

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py \
    tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_canonical_layout.py \
    tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_canonical_mapping.py -q \
    -k "canonical or mapping or roundtrip or topology"
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py
```

Two tests added to the existing `test_gpu_worker.py`:

- `test_canonical_load_path_follows_fragment_size`: a 32 KiB page mapped as two 16 KiB fragments resolves to DMA for direct and to the Triton path for canonical; a 4 KiB page split into 2 KiB fragments still gets a 4 KiB (page-derived) chunk.
- `test_canonical_load_path_requires_aligned_fragments`: an 8-byte-aligned page with unaligned fragments (508 B / 516 B) stays on DMA, since the kernel would drop the trailing bytes of each fragment.

## Test Result

A30, torch 2.13.0+cu126, editable install with `VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` (precompiled artifacts from nightly `cd10ed6f9f`; this change is Python-only).

- `tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py`: 42 passed, 1 skipped (the ROCm-only test).
- Both new tests fail without the source change and pass with it.
- Canonical suites, including the GPU roundtrips and `test_cross_topology_roundtrip`, whose small fragments now go through the Triton kernel: 38 passed.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `mypy-3.10`, `mypy-3.12`: passed.

Load time for the case from the issue (TP=2, 32 KiB page mapped as 2 × 16 KiB, 80 layers, A30, median of 7, byte-exact):

| prefix | direct (DMA) | canonical before (DMA) | canonical after (Triton) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1K tokens | 10.7 ms | 26.0 ms | 6.7 ms |
| 4K tokens | 30.0 ms | 103.9 ms | 26.6 ms |
| 32K tokens | 216 ms | 826 ms | 212 ms |

Host-side submit time on the model runner thread for the 32K-token load goes from 826 ms to under 1 ms. These numbers come from a standalone harness (verbatim `_swap_blocks_kernel`, single `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` call as in `swap_blocks_batch`), using the CUDA 12.8 forward-compat libcuda on a 535 kernel driver.

No model eval: the change only chooses between two byte-exact copy primitives, and the GPU roundtrip tests cover correctness.

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation, implementation and tests. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and measurements above on my own hardware.

---

title: [Bugfix][V1] Fail pending utility RPCs when the output receiver stops
body:
## Purpose

If EngineCore dies before replying to a utility call, operations such as pause, reset, or sleep can remain blocked after the output receiver has stopped. Receiver errors are forwarded to the output queue, but these callers wait on separate futures that never receive the failure. Both sync and async clients are affected.

Fail pending utility futures when the receiver exits, including shutdown and cancellation before the async receiver starts. Also clean up calls that fail or are cancelled while sending, tolerate late responses, and cancel EEP notification waiters when reconfiguration is cancelled.

## Test Plan

Add CPU regressions using real ZMQ sockets and the production client methods, covering receiver shutdown/errors, cancellation, late responses, send failure, and EEP waiter cleanup.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH="$PWD" \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_core_client_utility.py \
  -q -p no:cacheprovider

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py tests/v1/engine/test_core_client_utility.py

.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/engine/core_client.py tests/v1/engine/test_core_client_utility.py
```

## Test Result

- Before the fix: **9 failed, 1 passed** with the same test suite on `4b839c3378`.
- After the fix: **10 passed** on macOS with CPU dependencies.
- All applicable pre-commit checks and the separate mypy 3.12 check passed.

Also ran before/after EngineCore integration smoke tests on a single A10 with `Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B`. A deferred test utility confirms that the call has reached the real EngineCore without completing its response; the test then sends SIGKILL to that EngineCore.

- Before the fix, both sync and async utility calls were still pending two seconds after their receivers exited.
- After the fix, both calls raised `EngineDeadError` and the pending-call maps were empty.
- Normal generation produced identical token IDs across all four runs, and pause/resume controls passed.

Also reported in [this CodeRabbit review comment on #55274](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55274#discussion_r3930659253). Checked related open, closed, and merged PRs on September 11, 2026; no equivalent fix was found. The health-probe timeout in [#36451](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36451) addresses an engine that remains alive but unresponsive; this change propagates failure once the receiver has stopped.

AI assistance: Codex helped with the investigation, implementation, and tests.

title: [ROCm] Fuse DeepSeek V4.1 decode metadata and final norm
body:
## Summary

- let the gfx950 V4.1 sparse-decode kernel consume dense logical top-k indices directly and perform block-table translation in-kernel
- retain the ragged metadata path for other architectures, with fused length/indptr construction and small-batch packing
- fuse V4.1's final carried-pre-mix HC collapse with the final RMSNorm
- preserve the baseline sparse-attention split boundaries and reduction order
- cover invalid-token masking, non-identity request/block mappings, both ragged dispatch paths, CUDA graph replay, and empty trusted sparse metadata

The sparse metadata/direct-top-k changes are vLLM Triton changes and do not modify AITER.

The final HC collapse + RMSNorm fusion is also a vLLM Triton kernel. It is narrower than #51244, which implements broader TileLang MHC post + HC head + RMSNorm fusions; this PR keeps the measured V4.1-specific final-collapse path visible for review while it remains Draft.

## Performance

### Setup

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Hardware | MI355X (gfx950), TP8/EP8 |
| Model | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash |
| Workload | 8192 input tokens, 1024 output tokens, `--ignore-eos`, temperature 0, seed 41 |
| C1 protocol | fresh server per arm, 3 warmup requests, 16 measured serial requests |
| Pairing | baseline/final alternated three times, same window |
| Node hygiene | clean-window runs taken only after terminating an unrelated `hwq_robustness` job and confirming all eight GPUs at 0% use, 0% allocated VRAM, no KFD processes |
| Serving matrix | two directional pairs, baseline/final then final/baseline |

### C1 serving, every build measured

One row per build. `Mean TPOT` is the mean of the three per-run medians; the
delta is against the baseline collected in the same window. Only the last two
rows were collected under the clean protocol, and they are the basis for the
claim in this PR.

| Build | Artifacts | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Mean TPOT | Mean output tok/s | Saved | Delta | Window |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Baseline | `c1-a{1,2,3}` | 8.6908 ms | 8.6796 ms | 8.6697 ms | 8.6800 ms | 112.37 | — | — | contaminated |
| Ragged metadata fusion only | `c1-b{1,2,3}` | 8.5295 ms | 8.5111 ms | 8.5453 ms | 8.5286 ms | 114.23 | 151.4 us | -1.74% | contaminated |
| Full fusions, direct top-k + HC/RMSNorm | `c1-f{1,2,3}` | 8.3944 ms | 8.3716 ms | 8.3688 ms | 8.3783 ms | 116.24 | 301.7 us | -3.48% | contaminated |
| First exact build, rows 5-32 direct | `c1-x{1,2,3}` | 8.4007 ms | 8.6754 ms | 8.6633 ms | 8.5798 ms | 113.58 (115.84 / 112.34 / 112.56) | 100.2 us | -1.15% | contaminated |
| Exact zero-launch, first pass | `c1-zero{1,2,3}` | 8.6068 ms | 8.7401 ms | 8.7500 ms | 8.6990 ms | 112.03 | -19.0 us | +0.22% | contaminated |
| **Baseline, clean window** | `c1-clean-a{1,2,3}` | 8.6546 ms | 8.6497 ms | 8.6672 ms | **8.6572 ms** | 112.55 | — | — | clean |
| **This PR, clean window** | `c1-clean-b{1,2,3}` | 8.3767 ms | 8.3883 ms | 8.3829 ms | **8.3826 ms** | 116.16 | **274.6 us** | **-3.17%** | clean |

Run-by-run pairing for the three builds that were measured as alternating
pairs against their own baseline:

| Build | Pair 1 saved | Pair 2 saved | Pair 3 saved | Combined baseline | Combined build | Combined saved | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **This PR, clean window** | **277.9 us (3.21%)** | **261.4 us (3.02%)** | **284.4 us (3.28%)** | 8.6572 ms | 8.3826 ms | **274.6 us** | **3.17%** |
| Full fusions | 296.4 us (3.41%) | 307.9 us (3.55%) | 300.9 us (3.47%) | 8.6810 ms | 8.3742 ms | 301.7 us | 3.53% |
| Ragged metadata fusion only | 161.3 us (1.86%) | 168.4 us (1.94%) | 124.4 us (1.44%) | 8.6810 ms | 8.5323 ms | 151.4 us | 1.71% |

A stratified request-level bootstrap on the clean pair gives a 95% CI of
**[268.9, 281.4] us saved per output token**. The three clean baseline runs span
0.0175 ms and the three clean final runs span 0.0116 ms, an order of magnitude
below the 0.2746 ms separation. Median TTFT is unchanged across the clean pair
(233.8 / 230.8 / 234.8 ms baseline against 233.4 / 232.9 / 232.6 ms final), as
expected for a decode-path change. Per-run output throughput was
112.60 / 112.62 / 112.42 tok/s baseline against 116.25 / 116.05 / 116.19 tok/s
final, and mean ITL tracks TPOT: 8.6614 / 8.6615 / 8.6746 ms against
8.3829 / 8.3965 / 8.3879 ms.

The `c1-x` and `c1-zero` rows are why this PR was re-measured: the first exact
build lost the direct path at C1-C4, and the first zero-launch pass gave back
the entire gain. The current position-derived length formula recovers it.

### 8K/1K serving matrix, absolute

| Build | Window | C4 out tok/s | C4 TPOT | C16 out tok/s | C16 TPOT | C64 out tok/s | C64 TPOT |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline, pair 1 | clean | 383.18 | 9.3444 ms | 1197.90 | 10.9809 ms | 1908.82 | 26.0220 ms |
| This PR, pair 1 | clean | 395.54 | 9.0178 ms | 1234.70 | 10.6131 ms | 1921.08 | 25.9207 ms |
| Baseline, pair 2 | clean | 384.11 | 9.3275 ms | 1204.48 | 10.9248 ms | 1918.41 | 25.8946 ms |
| This PR, pair 2 | clean | 396.07 | 9.0076 ms | 1234.27 | 10.5943 ms | 1912.69 | 26.0202 ms |
| Ragged metadata fusion only | contaminated | 267.23 | 10.4758 ms | 1039.74 | 11.3007 ms | 1941.98 | 25.8965 ms |
| Baseline for full-fusions run | contaminated | 264.86 | — | 1042.87 | — | 1938.42 | — |
| Full fusions | contaminated | 272.28 (+2.80%) | mean TPOT -3.21% | 1064.09 (+2.03%) | mean TPOT -2.52% | 1938.72 (+0.02%) | mean TPOT +0.19% |
| First exact build | contaminated | 377.07 | 9.485 ms | 1190.83 | 11.020 ms | 1886.78 | 26.314 ms |

Baseline absolutes for the same sweep, total token throughput: 1010.63 tok/s at
C1 (112.29 output tok/s, 8.6873 ms median TPOT, 231.7 ms median TTFT),
3456.95 tok/s at C4 (1108.2 ms median TTFT), 10840.33 tok/s at C16 (2356.4 ms),
17265.70 tok/s at C64 (7360.0 ms). P99 TPOT for the first exact build was
10.320 / 12.996 / 32.782 ms at C4 / C16 / C64. All matrix runs completed with
zero failed requests.

Same-window A/B for the metadata-fusion-only build, reported as deltas because
that sweep paired its own baseline:

| Concurrency | Output tok/s delta | Mean TPOT delta |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | +2.09% | -2.09% |
| 4 | +0.90% | -1.09% |
| 16 | -0.30% | -0.09% |
| 64 | +0.18% | -0.05% |

### Serving matrix, both directions

Pair 1 ran baseline first, pair 2 ran final first, so an ordering effect would
show up as disagreement between the columns.

| Concurrency | Pair 1 output tok/s | Pair 1 median TPOT | Pair 2 output tok/s | Pair 2 median TPOT | Geometric mean |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 4 | +3.22% | -3.49% | +3.11% | -3.43% | **+3.17% / -3.46%** |
| 16 | +3.07% | -3.35% | +2.47% | -3.03% | **+2.77% / -3.19%** |
| 64 | +0.64% | -0.39% | -0.30% | +0.49% | +0.17% / +0.05% |

C4 and C16 agree in both directions. C64 disagrees in sign between the pairs
and is reported as neutral, not as a gain.

### Exactness-cost recovery

The first bitwise-exact direct implementation restored a standalone top-k
length scan in every compressed-attention consumer and restricted direct mode
to 5-32 rows. That unintentionally removed the direct path from C1/C4 and added
38 length-kernel launches per decode token at C5-C32.

The current implementation derives the exact length inside the existing sparse
partial kernel from the same graph-stable metadata used by the SWA builder:
`seq_lens`, `query_start_loc`, `token_to_req_indices`, and `is_valid_token`.
The formula is the indexer contract
`min((absolute_position + 1) // compress_ratio, index_topk)`. This preserves
the baseline split boundaries without scanning the 512-entry top-k row and
without allocating a length tensor or launching another kernel.

The exact direct path now covers C1-C64, the configured service range. A
same-process alternating full-path microbenchmark (diagnostic only because the
node is shared) showed exact direct ahead of ragged metadata by 23-50 us per
compressed-attention layer across rows 1/4/5/8/16/32/64. Production Kineto
traces confirm zero `_compute_topk_lens_kernel`,
`_build_global_topk_ragged_kernel`, and `_pack_global_topk_ragged_kernel`
launches at both C1 and C16. The sparse partial/reduce topology is unchanged.

The full ROCm attention test file passes 80 tests, including bitwise equality
between explicit-length, position-derived-length, and ragged paths at ratio 1
and ratio 2, rows 1-64, plus CUDA graph replay after in-place sequence-length
changes.

## Isolated kernel benchmarks

samples. Kernel-level only; the service-level claim is the clean C1 pair above.

title: [ROCm] Let aiter's tuned decode GEMM win over the skinny kernels
body:
Claude generated:  
  
## Purpose

On gfx950 the skinny-GEMM branch in `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` returns early for
every small-token shape, so `tgemm.mm` further down is unreachable and aiter's
tuned A16W16 config is never consulted — even for shapes where aiter has a tuned
decode kernel that is measurably faster than `wvSplitK`.

This adds a single guard: defer to aiter only when its tuned config actually
names a decode kernel for this exact shape. Nothing else changes.

Deliberately **not** a shape table in vLLM. A `flydsl_decode` row exists only
where somebody tuned that shape and the decode kernel won; every other shape,
model and architecture reports a different backend and keeps today's path. The
criterion lives in aiter's config and is updated by re-tuning, not by editing
vLLM.

The helper is a no-op unless `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER` and
`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_LINEAR` are set and the platform is gfx950, and it fails
closed if aiter is missing or raises.

Depends on ROCm/aiter#4114, which adds the decode kernel and the tuned
rows this patch keys off. Until that lands, `get_GEMM_A16W16_config`
reports a different backend for these shapes and this patch is a no-op

## Test Plan

Kimi-K3 TP8 decode shapes at M=1, bf16, on MI355X (gfx950, 256 CUs),
ROCm 7.2.4, aiter at `ROCm/aiter@main` + the tuned rows for these shapes.

1. **Which kernel actually runs** — call `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` for each
   shape and read the kernel name out of the profiler trace, with and without
   `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER`.

2. **Kernel-level comparison** — decode kernel vs `ops.wvSplitK`, both launched
   directly, ten alternating pairs in one process, medians reported. Two guards
   against the drift that made earlier attempts unreliable:
   * both kernels are checked against a torch reference first;
   * `wvSplitK` is also timed **against itself** as a null control, which
     measures the noise floor instead of assuming it.

3. **CUDA graph vs eager** — the same calls under a captured graph and eagerly,
   since vLLM captures decode by default.

## Test Result

**Dispatch is correct.** With the patch, the twelve shapes that have a tuned
decode row launch `flydsl_decode_agfx950_m1_n<N>_k<K>_...`; `shared down`
(7168x768), whose tuned row names FlyDSL HGEMM rather than decode, still runs
`wvSplitK_hf_sml_`. Without the patch all thirteen run `wvSplitK`.

**Kernel level** (10 pairs, medians in us; null control came out within ±2%,
which is the noise floor):

| shape | N | K | decode | wvSplitK | gain | decode won |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MLA gate | 1536 | 7168 | 5.52 | 7.48 | 26% | 10/10 |
| router | 896 | 7168 | 4.58 | 5.71 | 20% | 10/10 |
| MLA qb | 2304 | 1536 | 3.63 | 4.15 | 13% | 10/10 |
| MLA fused | 2112 | 7168 | 6.93 | 7.87 | 12% | 10/10 |
| latent up | 7168 | 3584 | 8.77 | 9.90 | 11% | 10/10 |
| latent down | 3584 | 7168 | 9.22 | 9.93 | 7% | 10/10 |
| attention O | 7168 | 1536 | 5.50 | 5.88 | 6% | 10/10 |
| dense down | 7168 | 4224 | 11.11 | 11.53 | 4% | 10/10 |
| KDA merged | 6288 | 7168 | 15.06 | 15.54 | 3% | 9/10 |
| vocab head | 20480 | 7168 | 43.66 | 43.86 | 0% | 9/10 |
| dense gate/up | 8448 | 7168 | 19.82 | 19.83 | 0% | 6/10 |
| KDA small-K | 1536 | 128 | 2.37 | 2.36 | -0% | 5/10 |

Sum of medians 136.2 us vs 144.0 us, **+5.5%**. Eight shapes are faster beyond
the noise floor and won every pair; four are ties; none is slower. Both kernels
agree with the torch reference to the same maximum relative error.

**Under a captured CUDA graph** the margin holds and grows on the small shapes,
which is the configuration vLLM decodes in by default:

| shape | aiter | wvSplitK | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| router | 2.67 | 3.78 | 29% |
| MLA gate | 3.94 | 5.89 | 33% |
| latent down | 7.88 | 8.09 | 3% |
| vocab head | 42.82 | 42.61 | 0% |

**Caveat for eager mode.** aiter's dispatch path costs about 11.8 us of host
time per call against 4.5 us for `ops.wvSplitK`, so with `enforce_eager` the
patched path is slower on everything except the largest shapes, where the kernel
runtime hides it. Under graph capture that cost is paid once, which is why the
graph numbers above are unaffected. Reducing it is being worked on in aiter
separately — re-parsing the tuned kernel name per launch has already been cached
away (4.4 us) — but it is host-side only and does not affect the kernel results
here.

**Shapes not covered.** These are decode shapes at M=1. `use_skinny_reduce_counting`
(10 <= n <= 128) is not reached at M=1 and is untouched.

title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Reap expired NIXL leases behind a heartbeated head
body:
## Purpose

The NIXL send-side lease reaper treated `_reqs_to_send` as expiry-ordered and stopped at the first still-live entry. Heartbeats update that map **in place**, so a request that keeps getting renewed can sit at the head forever and block reclaim of every expired entry behind it. That is the case in #58222: A is heartbeated, B and C expire, and neither is ever released.

Delete+reinsert on heartbeat is not enough either — `max(old, now + extension)` can still leave a later-inserted longer TTL in front of an already-expired entry. The reaper now scans the whole map. `_reqs_to_process.remove()` is also `discard()`, so reaping IDs the old early-exit never reached cannot KeyError.

Fixes #58222.

**Not a duplicate of [#50789](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50789):** that is a stale draft from August against an older `get_finished()` layout, and it does not target this issue. This change is against current `main`, extracts a testable helper, and pins the issue's stdlib repro as a unit test.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m ruff check vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py
```

No GPU. No model eval — reclaim path only, serving output unchanged.

## Test Result

```
tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_heartbeat.py
10 passed in 4.66s
```

Including:
- `test_reaper_reclaims_expired_leases_behind_heartbeated_head` (issue #58222 repro)
- `test_reaper_reclaims_shorter_lease_behind_later_deadline`
- existing heartbeat tests

Ruff check and format: passed on the two changed files.

AI assistance was used to locate the reaper/heartbeat code and write the regression tests. I reviewed the change.

title: [Perf][ROCm] Force Triton MXFP4 for 96-row ASM scale tiles
body:
## Purpose

On ROCm gfx950, AITER ASM MXFP4 (`gemm_a4w4`) is selected when weight-scale tiles have `rows % 32 == 0` and `cols % 8 == 0`. Qwen3.8 TP1 GDN `in_proj_ba` uses **96×160** scales, which pass that layout check, but ASM is numerically wrong for **M ≤ 64** (Arete: error ratio ~0.83–0.92; ~22–24 µs broken ASM vs ~7.6–8.9 µs Triton).

This PR forces 96-row scales onto Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4`. Other legal tiles (e.g. 128×160) stay on ASM. TP2/TP4 BA (`N=48/24`) already fail the row-%-32 check and were Triton via #55213.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `tests/kernels/quantization/test_rocm_mxfp4.py::test_asm_fp4_scale_swizzle_supported_shape_rules`
  - `(96, 160) -> False` (Triton)
  - `(128, 160) -> True` (ASM unchanged)
- gfx950 TP1 Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 serve: GDN `in_proj_ba` should log Triton, not ASM, at decode M≤64.

## Test Result

Dispatch unit cases added. Numerical mismatch for 96-row ASM at M=8/16/32/64 was measured on MI355X (Arete Qwen3.8 MXFP4 campaign). Full e2e accuracy vs Triton path still to be attached from the TP1 patched serve.

title: [Bugfix] Attach DeepSeek-V4 request tools to existing system/developer messages
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58280.

DeepSeek-V4 still put request-level `tools` on a synthetic leading system message whenever the conversation started with a **developer** prompt. That renders `## Tools` *before* the instructions, so serving diverges from the reference encoder (`{content}\n\n## Tools`) and from how the same data is packed at train time.

`#51856` already attaches tools to an existing **system** message. This extends that to **developer** as well: attach to the first `system`/`developer` message, and only insert a synthetic system message when neither is present.

Not a duplicate of `#52255` (stale, needs-rebase; would redo the already-landed system case). Smaller nits in the issue (tool-parser newlines, tool-message join) are left alone.

AI assistance was used to implement and test this change. A human reviewed the diff.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tokenizers_/test_deepseek_v4.py -v
```

## Test Result

That includes the existing system-message / golden fixture cases plus the new checks:

title: [Bugfix][XPU] store the pointer raw bit pattern instead of its numeric value
body:
Fix UT models/language/generation/test_common.py::test_models[True-False-5-32-microsoft/phi-2] meet OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C long.

Root cause: PromptEmbedsState.add_request() stores GPU data_ptr() values into a signed int64 numpy array, which only holds up to 2^63-1 CUDA pointers are low and fit; XPU device addresses have the high bit set exceeding int64's max, so numpy raises OverflowError.

title: [XPU][UT] Fix OverflowError when storing embeds.data_ptr()
body:
## Purpose

On XPU, USM device pointers returned by `embeds.data_ptr()` can exceed the positive range of a signed 64-bit integer.

`PromptEmbedsState.add_request()` stores the prompt embedding pointer in a NumPy-backed `torch.int64` buffer. Assigning a high-bit XPU pointer directly to this buffer raises the following error (similar to the issue described in #48059):

```text
OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C long
```

The error occurs when processing a request with prompt embeddings:

```text
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/prompt_embeds.py", line 58, in add_request
  self.embeds_ptrs.np[req_index] = embeds.data_ptr()
```

title: [ROCm][Perf] Enable medium-skinny dispatch in RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel
body:
## Purpose

Before this change, `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` routed a decode GEMM to the HIP `wvSplitK_int4_g` kernel only when the activation row count was at most five (`M <= 5`) and the total activation size satisfied `K * M <= 32768`.

The existing C++ operator supports up to five activation rows (`N_in <= 5`) and accepts `K_in * N_in` up to `int(max_lds_len * 1.2)`. With `max_lds_len = 32768`, the effective upper limit is `39321` elements.

Python `M` maps to C++ `N_in`. For inputs above the regular LDS capacity, the medium kernel keeps the activation prefix in LDS and reads the remaining elements from global memory.

Consequently, supported shapes with `K * M` between `32768` and `39321` (exclusive of the lower bound and inclusive of the upper bound) fell back to Triton instead of using the existing HIP kernel.

This PR aligns the Python dispatch limit with the C++ operator contract. It also adds dispatch-boundary tests and numerical correctness coverage for the newly enabled range. No C++ kernel is changed.

## Duplicate-work check

Open PR searches for medium-skinny, wvSplitK W4A16, and RDNA hybrid W4A16 found no duplicate. Related PRs #46186, #51511, and #50618 do not modify this hybrid dispatch threshold.

## Test Plan

Test environment:

All tests were run locally on the following system:

| Component | Value |
| --- | --- |
| GPU | AMD Radeon 8060S |
| GPU architecture | gfx1151 |
| Memory | 128 GB unified memory (96 GiB VRAM, 32 GiB host-visible) |
| Operating system | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS |
| ROCm | 7.2.3 |

The end-to-end comparison covered the two medium-skinny `down_proj` shapes below:

| Model | Batch | `down_proj` shape | `K * M` | Before this PR | With this PR |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| `Qwen3-8B-GPTQ-Int4` | 3 | `M=3, K=12288, N=4096` | 36864 | Triton | HIP medium |
| `Qwen3-4B-GPTQ-Int4` | 4 | `M=4, K=9728, N=2560` | 38912 | Triton | HIP medium |

The end-to-end benchmark used identical settings before and after this change:

- `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=0` with the `ROCM_ATTN` backend;

Functional validation included dispatch tests at the regular and medium boundaries, FP16 and BF16 medium-kernel comparisons against an FP32 reference, and the complete hybrid W4A16 test file. All applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` were also run on the changed files.

title: [CI] Snapshot E2E: set io_uring_disabled sysctl or skip, don't die
body:
## Problem

The Initialized Snapshot E2E lane (added in #51360) hard-fails 1.6s in on hosts where `kernel.io_uring_disabled != 2` (e.g. mithril-h200-7-1), because the script `die`s on the host precondition. The lane is `optional: true` and was block-gated on the PR's CI (#90301), so the requirement was never exercised before merge (dashboard alert #1925).

## Fix

Try `sudo -n sysctl -w kernel.io_uring_disabled=2`; if the host doesn't allow it, skip the lane with a clear message instead of dying red. The lane stays green on capable hosts and stops erroring on the rest.

title: [Attention] Allow explicit FlashInfer CuTe DSL MLA decode selection
body:
## Purpose

Allow users of `FLASHINFER_MLA` to explicitly select FlashInfer's existing CuTe DSL decode kernel:

```bash
vllm serve MODEL --attention-backend FLASHINFER_MLA \
    --attention-config.flashinfer_mla_decode_backend cute-dsl
```

The default `auto` preserves existing dispatch, including the fallback for query-head counts unsupported by TRTLLM-GEN. Native DCP still selects CuTe DSL regardless of this option. Explicit selection delegates hardware and shape validation to FlashInfer. The option participates in the attention configuration hash; prefill and MoE are unaffected.

This exposes a kernel choice for workload-specific tuning, without changing automatic selection or adding a kernel implementation.

Related work checked on September 14:

- #54507 warms up decode autotuning before graph capture. This PR adds an explicit override and does not modify autotuning.
- #54012 introduced native DCP support; its dispatch is preserved.
- #52990 migrates the FlashInfer API call. This PR retains the current entry point and can be adapted when that migration lands.

Open PRs and issues were searched for MLA decode, CuTe DSL, and `flashinfer_mla_decode_backend`; no existing PR adding this user-selectable option was found.

## Test Plan and Results

Rebased onto main `e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19`, preserving main's ragged-query metadata forwarding. Validated head `5e52843f3b74c3bba7eb215a653f3dc29431d700` on one NVIDIA B300 node.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
    tests/test_config.py \
    tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_dcp.py \
    tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py::test_flashinfer_mla_decode \
    tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_decode.py::test_flashinfer_mla_decode_workspace_supports_autotune \
    -k 'flashinfer_mla or mla_dcp' -v --tb=short
pre-commit run --from-ref e9757321527ca1ecd514c07c1418dd2c53da3d19 --to-ref HEAD
```

- Focused pytest: **89 passed, 387 deselected, 0 skipped** (133.92 seconds).
- 64 GPU numerical cases cover `auto` and `cute-dsl`, 32/128 query heads, block sizes 32/64, batch sizes 1/2/4/16, and single-token/ragged causal queries against the SDPA reference (`atol=rtol=1e-2`).
- One GPU workspace/autotuning test passed.
- 24 configuration, storage, dispatch, counter-buffer, and native-DCP cases passed. DCP dispatch uses mocks; distributed numerical DCP was not tested.
- All applicable changed-file pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, mypy, documentation checks, and test tethering. Commit-time checks also passed.
- Environment: Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, FlashInfer Python/cubin 0.6.18.post1, driver 580.159.04.
- Editable source used native binaries from nightly `355d789f0d5b29537b7adc43bd72b7c256c63fd5`; native sources/build definitions and requirements were unchanged between that commit and the pinned main.

### Main-branch model smoke test

Both `auto` and `cute-dsl` passed `vllm bench latency` with an internal 30B MLA model, BF16, TP1, batch size 8, input/output lengths 128/32, two warmup iterations, and three measured iterations. Compilation and CUDA Graph capture were enabled and completed successfully.

These runs used **`--moe-backend triton`**. The first attempt with the default FlashInfer TRTLLM MoE backend was stopped during its long initial compilation before inference; that default-MoE configuration is not validated by this smoke test. The smoke test checks execution, not accuracy or comparative performance.

### Model evaluation: equivalent v0.28.0 backport

These measurements are from the equivalent selector backport, **not this main-branch commit**. We evaluated an internal model with the same architecture as [kakaocorp/kanana-2-30b-a3b-thinking](https://huggingface.co/kakaocorp/kanana-2-30b-a3b-thinking), using BF16 weights on one B200 node with eight independent TP1 replicas, FlashInfer 0.6.16.post3, and no speculative decoding. title: [Bugfix] Pick a KV block size supported by every attention backend
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #48286.

`Platform.update_block_size_for_backend()` picks the KV cache block size from the **first** non-SSM attention backend only. Models that mix attention backends with disjoint block-size support break: GLM-DSA / DeepSeek-V3.2-style models pair a sparse-MLA main backend (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, supports `[32, 64]`, prefers 32) with `DeepseekV32IndexerBackend` (supports only `[64]`). The auto-selected 32 then fails much later in `select_common_block_size()` with the opaque

```
ValueError: No common block size for 32.
```

and the only workaround is a manual `--block-size 64` (undocumented, as #48286 notes).

This PR was split in two to keep the diff reviewable. It now carries backend collection and block-size selection only (+131/-21). Aligning phases 2 and 3 to the full backend list follows in a separate PR once this one merges.

## Changes

- `Platform._find_non_ssm_backend()` becomes `_find_non_ssm_backends()` and returns every distinct non-SSM backend in layer order rather than the first. Both call sites are updated (`interface.py`, `cpu.py`); no caller of the old name remains.
- New `Platform._preferred_block_size_for_backends()` returns the smallest block size every backend accepts:
  - a single backend keeps today's behaviour via `get_preferred_block_size()`;
  - if every backend accepts the default, the default wins;
  - otherwise candidates are the least common multiples formed by taking one supported size per backend, tried in ascending order, and **each candidate is confirmed against every backend** via `supports_block_size()`;
  - if nothing is common it raises `ValueError` naming each backend and its supported sizes.
- Candidates are validated rather than inferred. A backend may override `supports_block_size()` to accept exact sizes only, as CPU_MLA does by accepting 16 but no multiple of it, so "a multiple of a supported size" is not a safe assumption. This is the correctness point @yewentao256 raised in review.
- Phase 1 of `update_block_size_for_backend()` uses the new selection, and the log line now names all participating backends.
- Phases 2 and 3 are unchanged here and still take the first backend, exactly as before this PR.

## Test Plan

New unit tests in `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner.py`, built on a `_mock_backend` helper that can emulate an exact-size backend:

- `test_preferred_block_size_satisfies_every_backend`, parametrized:
  - a lone `MultipleOf(8)` backend keeps the default 16;
  - `[32, 64]` plus `[64]` gives 64, the #48286 shape;
  - `[32, 64]` alone still gives 32;
  - `[32]` plus `[48]` gives 96.
- `test_preferred_block_size_searches_past_an_exact_size_backend`: an exact-size backend accepting `[16, 96]` beside `MultipleOf(32)` gives 96, where a greedy lcm(16, 32) = 32 would be wrongly accepted.
- `test_preferred_block_size_rejects_backends_with_no_common_size`: an exact-size `[16]` backend beside `MultipleOf(64)` raises `ValueError`.

## Test Result

- The new unit tests and the existing `select_common_block_size` tests pass.
- End-to-end on GLM-5.2 NVFP4 (`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM`), PP=2 / TP=8 / `--enable-expert-parallel`, Ray executor, 2 nodes x 8x B200. This run was performed on the pre-split branch, whose phase 1 selection is what this PR retains. Previously it crashed at KV-cache init without `--block-size 64`; with the change it boots with no block-size flag, logging

```
Setting kv cache block size to 64 for DEEPSEEK_V32_INDEXER/FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE backend(s).
```

and serves correct output (temperature-0 smoke).

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Preserve finish_reason=length for truncated tool calls
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #58228.

When a non-streaming chat completion produced a parsed tool call but the engine stopped on `max_tokens`, the response reported `finish_reason="tool_calls"`, hiding the `"length"` stop. Clients (e.g. agent frameworks) then execute a possibly truncated tool call instead of retrying with a larger token budget.

This PR only translates an engine `"stop"` into `"tool_calls"` in the non-streaming path, matching the existing `tool_choice="required"` branch. Any other engine finish reason (e.g. `"length"`) is preserved.

The streaming path was fixed the same way in #46303, which was merged while this PR was open; this PR has been rebased on it and now covers only the remaining non-streaming path, so streaming and non-streaming behave consistently.

**Not a duplicate:** #46303 covers streaming only. #57482 addressed the non-streaming path but was closed by its author without review. No other open PR addresses this.

## Test Plan

Added `test_non_streaming_tool_call_finish_reason` in `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py` (mocked engine, no GPU or model weights needed), parametrized over engine finish reason `stop` → `tool_calls` and `length` → `length`, mirroring the streaming parametrization added in #46303.

    pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py -k "tool_call_finish_reason or n_gt1_independent" -v

title: [LoRA][Perf] Skip inactive adapters per layer in eager mode
body:
## Purpose

A batch-wide no-LoRA check cannot skip work when a request uses an adapter but
the current layer has no weights for that adapter. For example, a q_proj/v_proj
adapter still carries a valid LoRA ID through o_proj and MLP layers.

This matters for heterogeneous serving. If resident adapters target q/v,
q/k/v/o, and gate/up/down respectively, the static union covers every module,
but a request using only the q/v adapter has no useful LoRA work in most layers.

This PR:

- tracks which adapter slots are populated for each LoRA layer;
- derives active token and sampler slot sets from the existing CPU mapping;
- bypasses dense, embedding, and logits LoRA work in eager mode when the active
  and populated slot sets are disjoint;
- preserves the existing path under torch.compile and graph modes, without any
  device-to-host synchronization; and
- conservatively keeps a packed wrapper active when any packed slice is
  populated.

MoE and fully-sharded override paths are unchanged.

This does not duplicate #47951, which handles only batches with no active LoRA.
It is also materially different from #48887: that PR's host-level decision uses
the static union of all loaded adapters and explicitly cannot skip a layer when
heterogeneous resident adapters collectively cover all modules. This PR
intersects the current batch's active slots with the current layer's populated
slots.

title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Keep length finish_reason for max_tokens-truncated streaming tool calls
body:
Fixes #9053

## Purpose

When a tool call is truncated mid-JSON by `max_tokens`, the streaming `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint currently returns `finish_reason="tool_calls"` on the terminal chunk as long as any tool delta was emitted.

This causes two issues:

1. **Divergence from non-streaming**: The non-streaming endpoint already correctly returns `finish_reason="length"`.
2. **Client execution errors**: Streaming clients cannot detect truncation and may attempt to execute incomplete JSON (e.g., at `max_tokens=10`, only the function name was generated, but the terminal chunk reports `tool_calls` with `arguments="{}"`). Per the OpenAI API specification, tool calls cut off by `max_tokens` must return `finish_reason="length"`.

### Fix
Gate setting `finish_reason="tool_calls"` on the engine finishing normally (`output.finish_reason == "stop"`), aligning with the non-streaming logic. If the request was truncated (e.g., `length`), the original finish reason is preserved.

*(Note: Independent of #42213, which handles flushing buffered text when no tool delta was streamed).*

## Test Plan

1. **E2E verification**: Tested `max_tokens` values 10, 12, 16, 24, 32, and 48 on a live server (`Qwen3-0.6B`, `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes`), comparing the terminal `finish_reason` between `stream=true` and `stream=false`.
2. **Focused regression test**: Added streaming cases for both completed (`stop` → `tool_calls`) and truncated (`length` → `length`) requests to `tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py`.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=empty PYTHONPATH="$PWD" pytest -q \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py::test_streaming_n_gt1_independent_tool_parsers
```

## Test Result

### E2E Comparison (`stream` vs `non-stream`)

Across different `max_tokens` settings, streaming terminal `finish_reason` now strictly matches non-streaming:

| `max_tokens` | non-stream | stream (before) | stream (after) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | length | **tool_calls** | **length** |
| 12 | length | **tool_calls** | **length** |
| 16 | length | **tool_calls** | **length** |
| 24 | length | **tool_calls** | **length** |
| 32 | tool_calls | tool_calls | tool_calls |
| 48 | tool_calls | tool_calls | tool_calls |

The focused regression test passed both cases (`2 passed`). Without the `output.finish_reason == "stop"` check, the completed case still passes while the truncated case fails as expected.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script and environment</summary>

Hardware: 1x RTX 4090. Model: `Qwen3-0.6B`.

Server command:

```bash
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
  --model Qwen3-0.6B --served-model-name qwen \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser hermes --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --enforce-eager --max-model-len 2048
```

Client reproduction script:

```python
import json, urllib.request

TOOLS = [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
        "name": "get_weather",
        "description": "Get weather",
        "parameters": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
                "city": {"type": "string", "enum": ["Vienna"]},
                "unit": {"type": "string", "enum": ["celsius"]},
            },
            "required": ["city", "unit"],
            "additionalProperties": False,
        },
    },
}]

def post(payload):
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions",
        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
        method="POST",
    )
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120)

def read_stream(resp):
    terminal, args = None, []
    for raw in resp:
        line = raw.decode(errors="replace").strip()
        if not line.startswith("data: ") or line == "data: [DONE]":
            continue
        obj = json.loads(line[6:])
        for ch in obj.get("choices", []):
            for tc in (ch.get("delta") or {}).get("tool_calls") or []:
                fn = tc.get("function") or {}
                if "arguments" in fn:
                    args.append(fn.get("arguments") or "")
            if ch.get("finish_reason") is not None:
                terminal = ch
    return terminal, "".join(args)

for mt in [10, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48]:
    common = {
        "model": "qwen",
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Call get_weather for Vienna in celsius."}],
        "tools": TOOLS,
        "tool_choice": "required",
        "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False},
        "temperature": 0,
        "max_tokens": mt,
    }
    with post({**common, "stream": False}) as r:
        ns = json.loads(r.read())["choices"][0]["finish_reason"]
    with post({**common, "stream": True}) as r:
        term, args = read_stream(r)
    print(f"max_tokens={mt:2d} | non_stream={ns:10s} | stream={term['finish_reason']:10s} | args={args!r}")
```

</details>

title: [Bugfix][Model Loader] Keep the weight lock file name within the 255-byte limit
body:
## Purpose

`get_lock` flattens the whole model path into the lock file name:

```python
# vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py
model_name = model_name_or_path.replace("/", "-")
hash_name = hashlib.sha256(model_name.encode()).hexdigest()
# add hash to avoid conflict with old users' lock files
lock_file_name = hash_name + model_name + ".lock"
lock = filelock.FileLock(os.path.join(lock_dir, lock_file_name), mode=0o666)
```

The digest is 64 characters, so any `--model` path longer than roughly 186 characters produces a file **name** over the 255-byte cap that ext4, xfs, btrfs and APFS all put on a single path component. The full *path* may be far longer than 255 bytes, which is why this is easy to miss — the limit is per component.

It only bites on local checkpoint paths, but it bites before a single weight is read:

```
OSError: [Errno 36] File name too long
```

Reproduced on a 221-character local checkpoint path, which lands the lock name at 290 bytes:

```python
>>> path = ("/mnt/shared-storage/models/team-inference/experiments/"
...         "2026-02-long-context-run-17/checkpoints/global_step_120000/"
...         "hf_export/Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-FP8-blockwise/snapshot/"
...         "revision-2026-02-14-rc3-merged-lora-adapters/final")
>>> get_lock(path, cache_dir=tmpdir)
OSError errno=63: File name too long          # ENAMETOOLONG, macOS numbering
```

`get_lock` guards the weight download, the config download and the tokenizer download — 8 call sites in `weight_utils.py` and `tokenizers/registry.py` — so this takes out model loading entirely for anyone serving from a deep shared-storage or multi-revision export path.

## Changes

Fall back to the digest alone when the composed name is too long:

```python
if len(os.fsencode(lock_file_name)) > 255:
    lock_file_name = hash_name + ".lock"
```

The digest is already collision-resistant and is derived from the same string, so the lock stays per-model. Ordinary Hugging Face model ids keep their existing lock file name — that matters, because the file name is what makes the lock shared between processes, and changing it unconditionally would let two concurrent vLLM processes download the same model at once.

This is the same fix that already shipped in SGLang's fork of this function (`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/loader/weight_utils.py`), which is where I noticed the divergence.

## Test

`tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py::test_get_lock_handles_long_model_paths`, parametrized over a normal model id and the long path above. It asserts the basename stays within 255 bytes and that the lock can actually be acquired.

On current `main`:

```
FAILED tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py::test_get_lock_handles_long_model_paths[/mnt/shared-storage/...]
1 failed, 1 passed
```

With this PR, the whole file passes:

```
$ pytest tests/model_executor/test_weight_utils.py
34 passed in 41.07s
```

No GPU needed. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on both changed files.

---

*AI assistance disclosure, per [contributing/README.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/contributing/README.md#ai-assisted-contributions): prepared with Claude Code. Every changed line was reviewed, the failure was reproduced against current `main`, and the new test was run both with and without the fix. Commit carries `Co-authored-by: Claude`.*

title: [ROCm][Perf] Use a stacked hipBLASLt GEMM for the bf16x3 router
body:
## Motivation

Three in-tree models build their MoE router with fp32 weights: MiniMax-M3, MiniMax-M2 and HunYuan-V3. On ROCm none of the specialized `GateLinear` tiers accept an fp32 weight, so the router falls back to `F.linear`. That fallback casts the bf16 activations up to fp32 in a separate kernel, then runs the matmul on the fp32 MFMA pipe, which on gfx950 is roughly 16x slower than the bf16 one.

MiniMax-M3 has 57 MoE layers, so every forward pass pays for this 57 times.

Everything below was measured on `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4` on 4x MI350X. MiniMax-M2 and HunYuan-V3 take the same code path but were not benchmarked.

## Proposed Fix

At load time the fp32 router weight is split into three bf16 terms that add back to it exactly, since three bf16 mantissas carry the same 24 bits fp32 does.

The terms are stacked into one `(3E, K)` weight, so the router becomes a single bf16 matmul writing fp32 output, plus a small kernel that sums the three result blocks. Activations stay in bf16 and the matmul runs on the fast bf16 pipe.

Sigmoid, bias add and top-k are unchanged. Below 2048 tokens the fp32 path is faster and this tier declines. 

Scoped to gfx950 for now.

## Tests

4x MI350X (gfx950), `amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`, 
image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-1dc464d42681d22f38caf1fdc1eb632dc4421c45`.

### Router GEMM, measured on one GPU

MiniMax-M3 router shape (K=6144, E=128):

| tokens | before | after | speedup |
| ------ | ------ | ----- | ------- |
| 2048   | 46.5 us | 34.1 us | 1.36x |
| 4096   | 79.1 us | 39.9 us | 1.98x |
| 8192   | 145.4 us | 60.5 us | 2.40x |
| 32768  | 618.9 us | 201.2 us | 3.08x |

A second shape (K=3072, E=256) runs 1.44x to 2.46x over the same range.

### Accuracy, against an fp64 reference

| | relative L2 error at 8192 tokens |
| --- | --- |
| fp32 fallback (before) | 1.4e-6 |
| this PR | 4.9e-7 |

Across both router shapes at 2048, 8192, 16384 and 32768 tokens, this PR picks the same experts as the fp64 reference for every token. The fp32 fallback misses one token in one of those eight cases.


### Unit tests

`tests/kernels/test_bf16x3_router_gemm_rocm.py` and additions to `tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py`: 29 test functions, 23 of which need no GPU and run in normal CI. They cover bit exact reconstruction of the split across the full fp32 normal range, the inf/NaN contract, the eligibility predicates, and accuracy against fp64.

### End to end

Baseline is upstream without this PR. A second baseline run with identical code gives the drift column, so gains can be read against real run to run noise.

| ISL/OSL | Conc | Tput before | Tput after | Tput gain | TTFT gain | TPOT gain | drift |
| ------- | ---- | ------------ | ------------ | ---------- | ------ | ------ | ----- |
| 8k/1k   | 16   | 1132.4 tok/s | 1138.7 tok/s | +0.49%     | +2.71% | +0.20% | 0.13% |
| 8k/1k   | 64   | 2276.3 tok/s | 2301.5 tok/s | +1.18%     | +3.08% | +0.91% | 0.14% |
| 64k/1k  | 16   | 415.6 tok/s  | 422.3 tok/s  | +1.75%     | +2.12% | +1.58% | 0.28% |
| 64k/1k  | 64   | 507.8 tok/s  | 519.4 tok/s  | **+2.28%** | +2.78% | +2.08% | 0.02% |
| 128k/1k | 8    | 198.6 tok/s  | 201.6 tok/s  | +1.59%     | +2.62% | +0.88% | 0.05% |

Gains grow with longer prompts and with concurrency, since both put more tokens into each prefill step. 

### GSM8K (1,319 examples, 8-shot, chat template, multiturn)

| Run | Flexible extract | Strict match |
| --- | ---------------- | ------------ |
| baseline | 93.86% | 93.93% |
| this PR | 94.01% | 94.09% |
| baseline again | 94.69% | 94.62% |

The two baseline runs are identical code and differ by 0.83%. This PR lands between them, so there is no accuracy change either way.

## Update 17 September

#54845 landed a ROCm router kernel for the same three models while this was open. It covers up to 32 tokens while this PR starts at 2048. But they were checked in the wrong order: the low-M tier is consulted first and always returns, so this PR's kernel was never reached above 32 tokens.

Commit 2782fc4 checks this tier first and hands small batches back to the low-M kernel, so both keep their measured range. Also restores a logger #55899 removed, which this PR calls at model load. I verified on MI355X: at 32 tokens all three models use #54845's kernel, at 2048 and 8192 they use this one.

New TODO
- Numbers/Accuracy check above predate #54845 and need a rerun

export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1

title: [Bugfix][V1] Release in-process LLM resources on deletion
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #21073.

With `VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0`, deleting a directly constructed `LLM` did not release its GPU resources. The in-process engine and worker froze their object graph into Python's permanent GC generation, while deletion did not run the full engine teardown. References held by the engine and worker remained reachable, and the process-global CUDA graph pool could outlive the engine that created it. Together, these gaps blocked construction of another `LLM` in the same process.

This change:

- adds idempotent `LLM.shutdown()` and `LLMEngine.shutdown()` paths and calls them from the destructors;
- skips persistent GC heap freezing for the in-process engine and worker;
- runs the existing compiled-model cleanup finalizer before teardown;
- drops torn-down executor, worker, scheduler, and DP-group references before cache cleanup; and
- resets the process-global CUDA graph pool so a later engine cannot reuse a destroyed pool.

Multiprocess engines keep the GC-freeze optimization. The in-process path may spend more time scanning the engine object graph during cyclic GC, in exchange for making deletion reclaim its resources.

This is not duplicated by #54162 or #54246. Those PRs added weak compiled-model finalization and layer-level KV-cache cleanup, respectively, but current `main` with both changes still reproduces the bare-deletion failure. #45195 and #35676 clean up compiled-model hooks on the `VllmRunner` path; they do not route a directly constructed `LLM` through full shutdown.

title: [Feature] Improve engine rpc failure handling and shutdown
body:
## Purpose

Closes #58242.

A worker RPC error can leave unread replies that get consumed by the next call. This PR preserves reply correspondence where recovery is possible and propagates terminal failures through shutdown:

- Drain one reply from every selected worker before returning the first error. After a worker error, use `VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` as a shared collection budget, preserving any earlier deadline across SHM and socket reads.
- On incomplete receives, fail the executor and pending RPCs, reject queue reuse, and notify EngineCore.
- Complete utility futures when the receiver stops and fix the concurrent shutdown-address race.
- Preserve failed sleep state for explicit wake recovery, and protect Core cleanup from additional SIGTERM/SIGINT while retaining the manager's termination deadline.

Includes #56416 with original authorship preserved.

## Test Plan

CPU regressions cover reply collection, timeout/EOF handling, sleep/wake recovery, utility cancellation, and shutdown races.

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 VLLM_PLUGINS='' VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 \
```

title: [ROCm][DSv4.1][Perf] Fused router gate for gfx950
body:
## Purpose and measured status

Optimize the gfx950 BF16 router `X[M,7168] @ W[384,7168].T` plus sqrtsoftplus scoring, correction bias, and expert selection. The tested M values are all **33 distinct products** of `[1,2,4,6,8,16,32,64,128,256] × [1,2,3,4,5,6]`, through 1536; both top-k 6 and 8 are measured below.

The optimized operation beats the runnable unfused baseline at every measured size: **1.47–3.86× with cold rotating inputs**. **It does not reach the raw hardware roofline.** At M=1536/top-k6, the full operation takes **23.17 µs cold** versus **3.450 µs** for the ideal bandwidth/compute-only bound (**14.9%**). The analysis below identifies the remaining costs.

The original draft fails compilation at `tl.arange(0,384)`. The runnable baseline here is BF16→FP32 `torch.mm` (the gate GEMM operation used by GateLinear) followed by `fused_topk_bias(scoring_func="sqrtsoftplus")`.

## Implementation

- M=1–2 uses a vector GEMV; other batches use tiled BF16 MFMA with deterministic FP32 split-K partials.
- The second kernel fuses partial reduction, scoring, bias-aware ranking, normalization, and scaling. Larger batches use a single-wave Gluon selector; smaller batches use packed-key Triton top-k. This is a **two-kernel** implementation.
- Ranking keys retain the entire FP32 score and inverse expert ID. Equal computed ranks prefer the lower expert ID; output weights retain the unbiased score.
- Compensated `log1p` preserves small negative-tail scores without the slower general OCML path. A direct maximum handles top-k1, which otherwise fails to compile with the installed Triton `topk(k=1)`.
- M>768 uses larger MFMA32 tiles and an XCD-aware launch order. The supported token cap increases to 1536; input storage/device and ID dtype validation are enforced.

No serving/model dispatch is wired in this PR. No model-level speedup or evaluation result is claimed.

## Measurement protocol

Measured commit: `f894dba7781cda88aab4edb1fbc8012fc4c2b87f`. MI355X/gfx950, one GPU (physical GPU4), BF16 inputs, FP32 accumulation/output weights, int32 expert IDs, correction bias, renormalization, scaling=1.5. PyTorch `2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`, HIP `7.15.26333`, Triton `3.8.0`. Environment: `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1 ROCPROFILER_QUEUE_INTERPOSITION=0`.

Both arms measure the complete GPU operation using HIP graph replay. Compilation, allocation, random inputs, and copies are outside timing. Events surround 128 operations; three rounds alternate arm order with 15 samples each. Tables report medians; the JSON artifact retains p10/p90 and kernel source SHA256 `de8dd90626b18179a16bf49b0d3ff8298401f002901da3c71903a368368f0e99`. Correctness is checked before timing.

**Warm** reuses one input set. **Cold** rotates 128 independent input sets: gate weights alone occupy **672 MiB**, exceeding the 256 MB last-level cache. This defeats reuse between operations while preserving legitimate reuse inside each operation. Warm throughput is not evidence of HBM bandwidth. CUPTI is unavailable on ROCm; per-dispatch event timing was rejected because it inflated a no-op control from 1.684 to 8.52 µs.

## Roofline analysis

The dense MI355X specifications are **8 TB/s HBM**, **2.5166 PFLOP/s BF16 matrix compute**, and **256 MB LLC**. The higher sparse compute number is not applicable. Source: [AMD MI355X datasheet](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/instinct-tech-docs/product-briefs/amd-instinct-mi355x-gpu-brochure.pdf).

For N=384, K=7168, and k selected experts:

```text
F = 2*M*N*K
B_min = 2*(M*K + N*K) + 4*N + 8*M*k
AI = F / B_min
T_peak = max(B_min / 8e12, F / 2.5166e15)
TFLOP/s = F / latency_us / 1e6
Effective GB/s = B_min / latency_us / 1000
```

Bytes count each BF16 input and FP32 bias once and one FP32 weight plus int32 ID per selected expert. They exclude scratch and repeated tile loads. The FLOP count includes GEMM, but not nonlinear scoring, comparison, or reduction. Effective bandwidth is mathematical operation traffic, not measured HBM traffic.

Independent large-workload controls on GPU6 reached **6.533 TB/s** for a checked 1 GiB streaming read and **1.403 PFLOP/s** for 8192-square BF16 GEMM with FP32 output after sustained warmup. A live sample during GEMM recorded 1766 MHz SCLK/1399 W, versus the datasheet's boost conditions. These are measured calibration points, not proven ceilings for this router. Their illustrative bound is `max(B_min/6.533e12, F/1.403e15)`.

Representative top-k8 bounds and achieved full-operation throughput:

| M | AI, FLOP/B | Minimum MB | Peak bound, µs | Calibration bound, µs | Cold TFLOP/s | Effective cold GB/s |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 1.00 | 5.521 | 0.690 | 0.845 | 0.89 | 894.2 |
| 16 | 15.35 | 5.737 | 0.717 | 0.878 | 9.65 | 628.8 |
| 128 | 95.87 | 7.350 | 0.919 | 1.125 | 56.90 | 593.5 |
| 256 | 153.30 | 9.193 | 1.149 | 1.407 | 98.84 | 644.8 |
| 512 | 218.84 | 12.879 | 1.610 | 2.009 | 188.63 | 862.0 |
| 768 | 255.22 | 16.566 | 2.071 | 3.013 | 235.60 | 923.1 |
| 1024 | 278.35 | 20.252 | 2.532 | 4.018 | 253.45 | 910.5 |
| 1536 | 306.09 | 27.625 | 3.453 | 6.027 | 356.26 | 1163.9 |

The peak ridge is 314.575 FLOP/B, so the entire requested sweep is memory-bound in that ideal model (M1536/top-k8 reaches 306.09 FLOP/B). The calibration ridge is 214.76 FLOP/B, making its larger-M bound compute-dominated. Neither model captures launch/selection latency or limited workgroup residency.

**Small M:** a graph no-op measured 1.684 µs and a rotating ~5.5 MB read measured about 2.78 µs, already above the 0.69 µs bulk-bandwidth ideal. Two dependent launches, scalar/vector scoring, and wave communication are substantial fixed costs. These controls provide context; subtracting their latency from the operation would not be a valid measured speedup.

**Large M:** split-K trades extra traffic for occupancy. At M1536/S7, partial logits occupy 16.515 MB and add **33.030 MB of logical write+read traffic**. Final BM128/BN128 tiling issues approximately **132.121 MB of logical input loads**, despite only 27.525 MB of unique BF16 input data. Those repeated loads can hit cache; they are not an HBM-byte count.

Counter ablation at M1536, prior BM64/BN128/MFMA16 versus final BM128/BN128/MFMA32/XCD order:

| Counter/resource | Prior tile | Final tile |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| FetchSize beyond L2, KiB | 64,534.5 | 33,589.5 |
| WriteSize, KiB | 16,128 | 16,128 |
| L2 hit rate | 64.4% | 74.6% |
| MFMA utilization | 13.45% | 15.12% |
| VMEM latency, cycles | 807 | 710 |
| VALU instructions | 1,316,448 | 695,584 |
| Register spills / LDS bank conflicts | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

FetchSize is traffic beyond L2, not proof of off-chip HBM bytes on this LLC-equipped GPU. Counter collection perturbs cache/timing, so these counters are separate from the unprofiled latency tables. The ablation changes tiling, MFMA shape, and ordering together; it does not attribute the entire gain to ordering alone.

The final large tile uses 99,808 B (97.5 KiB) LDS and launches 252 useful CTAs at M1536, allowing only one resident CTA per CU. Lower memory latency and higher cache hit rate support improved locality; low MFMA utilization and limited residency remain consistent with a memory/dependency-latency bottleneck. **The raw roofline gap remains; it is not explained by missing matrix instructions or register spills.**

Further tests rejected no-split GEMM, a fully fused all-expert tile, explicit Gluon double buffering, prepared weights, wider tiles, and increased-residency configurations. They either slowed GEMM or increased partial-buffer/selection cost enough to lose end-to-end. Prepared weights additionally required a ~2.7 µs packing pass and 5.5 MB persistent storage. The final choice preserves the original contiguous weight input format.

## Validation and limits

```bash
HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=7 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py -k rocm_fused_router_gate -q
# 53 passed

HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4 .venv/bin/python -m \
  benchmarks.kernels.benchmark_rocm_fused_router_gate \
  --samples 15 --output final_benchmark.json
# 33 M values × 2 top-k values × 2 cache modes = 132 measurements
# Reference checks passed before timing

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/router/rocm_fused_router_gate.py \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_topk_softplus_sqrt.py \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rocm_fused_router_gate.py
# Passed
```

The full benchmark agrees with FP32 Torch reference expert IDs exactly and weights at atol=rtol=2e-5. Tests cover masked rows, empty inputs, bias/no bias, both normalization modes, int32/int64 IDs, ties, negative tails, invalid storage, and top-k1.

Additional selector checks passed 240 cases and a 300,001-logit scoring check (maximum relative error 1.95e-6 for logits≥-87). A separate 32-case generic top-k/tail probe preserved all selected expert sets and weights; four cases permuted nearly tied selected experts (reference score gaps≤4.17e-7). Auditing the computed ranks confirmed correct ordering for the kernel's own FP32 scores. This is not a claim of bitwise or batch-invariant equivalence across accumulation implementations. Extreme exponential subnormals can flush on this ROCm configuration.

**Model evaluation:** not run. There is no model callsite dispatching this kernel in this change, and the local checkpoint is inaccessible. Existing evaluation artifacts belong to another change and are not reused as evidence. Serving integration and an evaluation that actually exercises this kernel remain prerequisites for a model-level claim.

## Duplicate work and AI assistance

This updates the existing #57478 rather than opening a competing PR. The open-PR search for `fused router gate` identified this existing BF16 gate/selection work; the optimization is applied here. NVIDIA Mega-Gate work and selection-only ROCm changes do not provide this gfx950 BF16 projection implementation.

AI assistance was used (Codex, including parallel tuning/review agents; the original draft also disclosed Cursor). The human submitter must review the changed lines, understand the tradeoffs, and run the relevant tests before submitting this as ready.

title: [Perf][MoE] Skip top-k slots routed to non-local experts in TritonExp…
body:
## Purpose

Under EP with a full routing table on every rank (`MoEPrepareAndFinalizeNoDPEPModular`, DeepEP high-throughput), `TritonExperts.apply` aligns with `ignore_invalid_experts=False`: slots whose expert lives on another rank still get M-blocks in both `fused_moe_kernel` launches (the `off_experts == -1` branch writes zeros), and `moe_sum` adds the zeros back. At EP degree `ep`, `(ep-1)/ep` of the launched M-blocks do no useful work.

This PR aligns with `ignore_invalid_experts=True` when an `expert_map` is set and no LoRA context is active, and reduces with the existing pad-aware `moe_sum(input, output, topk_ids, expert_map)` (#48385) whenever `expert_map` is set. `fused_marlin_moe` already pairs the two.

Scope: dropped slots leave their workspace rows unwritten, so the skip requires a row-local activation quantization for the second GEMM (unquantized, static `a2_scale`, block-wise, or native dynamic per-token). Dynamic per-tensor activation scales (e.g. non-blocked online `--quantization fp8`) and LoRA keep the dense path. `TritonWNA16Experts` is unchanged.

## Test Plan
