title: [Bugfix][Logging] Fix three logging calls whose message is swallowed at runtime
body:
## Purpose

`logging` interpolates with `msg % args` inside `LogRecord.getMessage()`. When the format string and the argument count disagree it raises, the handler prints `--- Logging error ---` plus a traceback to stderr, and **the intended message never appears**. Three call sites in the tree do this.

**1. `vllm/v1/engine/tensor_ipc.py:149`**

```python
while tensors and (mid := next(iter(tensors))) < message_id:
    if sender.tensors.pop(mid):
        logger.warning(
            "Discarding %d stale tensors from sender %s",
            sender_id,          # one argument, two specs
        )
```

`%d` also receives the sender id, which is a `str`, so this raises `TypeError: %d format: a real number is required, not str`. The count the message wants is the size of the dict that `pop(mid)` returned, which is currently discarded by the `if`.

**2. `vllm/distributed/device_communicators/quick_all_reduce.py:175`**

```python
logger.warning(
    "Custom quick allreduce:",                       # format string, no %-spec
    f"Invalid quantization level: {regime_str}. "    # ...but here is an argument
    "Supported levels: "
    f"{list(QuickReduceRegime.__members__.keys())}",
)
return
```

Someone who sets an invalid `VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION` gets a logging traceback instead of the list of supported levels, and quick allreduce then silently stays off — exactly the case the warning exists for.

**3. `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/moriio/moriio_connector.py:1987`**

```python
logger.debug(
    "MoRIIO handshake listener received done recv for req",
    req_id.decode(),
)
```

Same shape: an argument with nothing to interpolate it into.

## Changes

- All three rewritten in the lazy `%s` form. For `tensor_ipc.py` the popped dict is bound to `stale` so its length can be logged, which is what the message has always claimed to report.
- `pyproject.toml`: add `PLE1205` and `PLE1206` to `[tool.ruff.lint] select`. The `G` (flake8-logging-format) rules already selected do **not** cover argument-count mismatches — `ruff check --select=G` passes on all three files above. `PLE1205`/`PLE1206` are report-only (no autofix), and the tree is clean for them after this change:

  ```
  $ ruff check --select=PLE1205,PLE1206 .
  All checks passed!
  ```

  `ruff check .` reports the same 133 pre-existing findings before and after this PR, so enabling the rules adds no new failures.

## Test

`tests/v1/test_tensor_ipc_queue.py` gains `test_receiver_reports_how_many_stale_tensors_it_discards`. It primes a `TensorIpcReceiver` with two tensors buffered under a stale `message_id`, asks for a tensor from a newer message, and asserts the rendered warning names the count and the sender. No GPU, no subprocess.

On current `main` it fails:

```
E   TypeError: %d format: a real number is required, not str
FAILED tests/v1/test_tensor_ipc_queue.py::test_receiver_reports_how_many_stale_tensors_it_discards
```

With this PR the whole file passes:

```
$ pytest tests/v1/test_tensor_ipc_queue.py
10 passed, 3 skipped in 24.93s
```

(3 skips are the CUDA-only cases; I ran this on a CPU-only host. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean on every changed file.)

I do not have AMD or MoRIIO hardware, so 2 and 3 are verified by reading plus the standalone stdlib repro below; 1 is covered by the new test.

```
>>> log.warning("Custom quick allreduce:", "Invalid quantization level: FP8")
--- Logging error ---
  File ".../logging/__init__.py", line 400, in getMessage
    msg = msg % self.args
TypeError: not all arguments converted during string formatting
Message: 'Custom quick allreduce:'
Arguments: ('Invalid quantization level: FP8',)
```

---

*AI assistance disclosure, per [contributing/README.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/docs/contributing/README.md#ai-assisted-contributions): this change was prepared with Claude Code. Every changed line was reviewed, the failure mode was reproduced against stdlib `logging`, and the new test was run both with and without the fix on a CPU-only host. Commit carries `Co-authored-by: Claude`.*

title: [Feature][KVConnector][DSv4.1] Encoder-only prefill with Mooncake P/D
body:
## Purpose

Implement encoder-only Prefill for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash P/D serving with the direct `MooncakeConnector`. This work builds on the asymmetric P/D proposal in RFC #57383 and the full-prompt, cache-hit-replay design in RFC #57738: P encodes the whole prompt through L0-L19 and produces the L20 Main KV/Indexer K, while D replays the adopted cache-hit tail through the full target and samples the first token. RFC #57738 analyzes NIXL pull as its initial path; this PR contributes a Mooncake-specific handoff and credits both RFCs for the design.

The initial Mooncake implementation adds the execution boundary, zero-token P completion, an explicit transfer profile, and connector readiness and region checks. H20 P/D integration checks and TTFT measurements are reported below. DSpark and CUDA graphs are not yet supported in this path; broader validation are planned.

## Implementation

- Add opt-in `KVTransferConfig.dsv41_encoder_only_prefill` on dedicated Mooncake producer and consumer roles. Keep full target weights on P in this first change; weight omission is separate work.
- On P, run L0-L19 normally, execute the L20 pre-mix and canonical compressor/Main-KV/Indexer-K writes, and skip L20 attention/FFN, L21-L39, final norm, LM head, sampling, and DSpark.
- Complete a cache-only P request after its full prompt is consumed, with no generated token. Each P worker returns an event-backed output; its executor synchronizes the GPU event before the scheduler may mark Mooncake blocks sendable. The Mooncake proxy sends `cache_only` and the shared `transfer_id`; incomplete and aborted requests remain non-sendable. D waits for Mooncake's transfer completion before replay.
- Select transferable groups from V4.1's configured Main-KV source and Indexer-K owner layer IDs. Fail if a required group is absent, mixed with D-local state, or duplicated. Bounded-replay SWA, compressor continuation, and draft groups remain local. Mooncake also rejects mismatched producer/consumer registered region sets.
- Restrict the first supported path to direct `MooncakeConnector` (not `MooncakeStoreConnector`), NVIDIA, MRV2, PP=1, no PCP or microbatching, bounded replay with a 128-token window, the 40-layer V4.1-Flash topology ending its global sources at L20, text-only requests, and no prompt logprobs. P currently requires `--no-async-scheduling` because async output placeholders do not yet model zero-token completion. D has a DSpark window check, but DSpark and CUDA graphs are not supported in this initial configuration.

Enable the new option in both server roles:

```json
{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","dsv41_encoder_only_prefill":true}
{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","dsv41_encoder_only_prefill":true}
```

Use the existing Mooncake proxy for these roles and pass `--no-async-scheduling` to P. The proxy's `cache_only` marker does not change conventional Mooncake requests when the option is off.

## Validation

### Environment and A/B setup

- Image: vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-0961bbae2894d574be790d219651824eb199318e.
- Hardware: two nodes with 8 NVIDIA H20 GPUs each; P used one 8-GPU node and D used the other.
- Baseline: the fixed nightly above.
- Candidate: the same fixed nightly with PR head `b576413489` applied as a runtime source overlay.
- Both arms included the same consumer-side release-only Mooncake pull fix now present in `760d90833e`. The baseline therefore was not a completely unmodified nightly. This fix is required because bounded replay can discard a short remote hit while Mooncake still has a release-only pull; an empty pull must release P blocks without reporting a receive completion to a D request that never entered `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`.
- Baseline and candidate were deployed in fresh pods with separate caches. Runtime source hashes were checked against the prepared source bundles.

### Server configuration

Both roles used MRV2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`), TP=1, PP=1, DP=8, expert parallelism, bounded replay, synchronous scheduling, no speculative decoding, and CUDA graphs disabled:

```text
vllm serve /data00/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
  --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash
  --trust-remote-code
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41
  --dtype bfloat16
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_ds_mla
  --block-size 64
  --tensor-parallel-size 1
  --pipeline-parallel-size 1
  --data-parallel-size 8
  --enable-expert-parallel
  --all2all-backend deepep_high_throughput
  --moe-backend humming
  --linear-backend humming
  --attention-backend FLASHMLA_SPARSE_DSV41
  --no-async-scheduling
  --enable-prefix-caching
  --swa-bounded-replay
  --no-disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager
  --max-model-len 33792
  --max-num-seqs 8
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90
  --safetensors-load-strategy lazy
  --api-server-count 1
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"NONE"}'
```

P used `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192` and the `kv_producer` Mooncake role. D used `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048` and the `kv_consumer` role. Both used the following role-specific `--kv-transfer-config`; the baseline omitted only `dsv41_encoder_only_prefill`:

```json
{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma","device_name":"mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3,mlx5_4"},"dsv41_encoder_only_prefill":true}
{"kv_connector":"MooncakeConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","kv_load_failure_policy":"fail","kv_buffer_device":"cuda","kv_connector_extra_config":{"mooncake_protocol":"rdma","device_name":"mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3,mlx5_4"},"dsv41_encoder_only_prefill":true}
```

Candidate P and D both set the new option, and its proxy added `cache_only=true` to P requests. `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` was set for node-local DP/EP process groups to avoid this NCCL version's virtual GPU-to-NIC topology failure; Mooncake continued to use RDMA between P and D.

DSpark and CUDA graphs are currently unsupported in this Mooncake encoder-only P/D configuration. DSpark was excluded from the measurements because this nightly's speculative cache-group numbering did not match the non-speculative producer. CUDA graphs were disabled in both arms because the nightly's DeepEP high-throughput dispatch performs a CPU count synchronization during capture. Future work will validate DSpark correctness and draft acceptance, CUDA graph execution, full model quality, and additional TP/PP topologies before expanding the support boundary.

### Correctness and benchmark

The correctness corpus contained 20 fixed, temperature-zero completion requests covering short prompts, 127/128/129-token boundaries, 4K/8K/8K+1/16K/32K prompts, and repeated prefixes. All 20 requests completed in both arms. Output text was exactly equal for 18/20 cases; the two differences were generation wording rather than a candidate semantic regression (both math outputs answered 391, and the candidate answered the Chinese capital prompt correctly where the baseline did not). This is a bounded integration check, not a replacement for a full model evaluation.

Performance used `vllm bench serve` through the same P/D proxy:

```text
--backend vllm
--dataset-name random
--random-input-len {4096,8192,16384,32768}
--random-output-len 1
--random-range-ratio 0
--num-prompts 32
--request-rate 0.2
--max-concurrency 4
--temperature 0
--ignore-eos
```

Each length first received 8 disjoint-seed warmup requests, followed by 32 measured requests. A/B used identical measurement seeds; each length used a different seed. P metrics confirmed zero prefix-cache hits and zero preemptions during all measured intervals.

| Input | Baseline Mean TTFT | Candidate Mean TTFT | Mean reduction | Baseline P99 TTFT | Candidate P99 TTFT | P99 reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4K | 1,597.54 ms | 970.32 ms | 39.26% | 2,494.57 ms | 1,371.39 ms | 45.02% |
| 8K | 3,246.51 ms | 1,757.22 ms | 45.87% | 5,359.65 ms | 2,815.44 ms | 47.47% |
| 16K | 7,124.47 ms | 3,383.92 ms | 52.50% | 10,856.65 ms | 5,279.80 ms | 51.37% |
| 32K | 20,626.11 ms | 8,391.67 ms | 59.32% | 21,579.17 ms | 11,100.91 ms | 48.56% |

Both arms completed all 128 measured requests and all 32 warmup requests with no failures, engine crashes, tracebacks, preemptions, or pod restarts. P99 has only 32 samples per length and should be treated as an observation from this run. This test measures fixed-rate TTFT, not maximum throughput, and does not cover DSpark or CUDA graphs.

### GSM8K accuracy

EvalScope 1.11.1 ran 200 zero-shot GSM8K samples per arm with batch size 8, temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95, seed 42, max_tokens 65536, and reasoning_effort high. Both arms used fresh pods and separate caches. The accuracy deployment increased max model length to 131072 for the generation limit; all other server settings above were unchanged.

| Arm | Correct | Accuracy | Succeeded | Errored |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline | 195/200 | 97.5% | 200 | 0 |
| Candidate | 193/200 | 96.5% | 200 | 0 |
| Delta | -2 | -1.0 pp | 0 | 0 |

Pairing by dataset sample index gave 193 samples correct in both arms, 5 wrong in both, 2 correct only in the baseline, and 0 correct only in the candidate (exact two-sided McNemar p=0.5). The two discordant outputs made alternate choices on ambiguously worded problems: "two times older" and "10 times more." Their responses addressed the correct prompts; no response mix-up, request failure, engine error, traceback, or pod restart was observed. This single stochastic run does not establish a statistically significant accuracy regression, but the observed -1.0 percentage-point delta is reported rather than treated as exact equivalence.

## Relationship to other work

Open PRs were checked by RFC number and by Mooncake/encoder-only/cache-only keywords. No other open PR implements this V4.1 execution boundary on direct Mooncake P/D. #55654 optimizes DSpark context-KV insertion, #56437 validates PP sharing, and #56227 supplies the merged bounded replay foundation; they are complementary, not duplicates.

If an RFC author (#57383/#57738) or maintainer lands a shared or NIXL-first implementation, this Mooncake path can be rebased/stacked on that work, retaining its connector-specific transfer profile, readiness handling, tests, corner cases, and eventual measurements. I am happy to coordinate that split rather than maintain duplicate generic model/scheduler code.

title: [Bugfix][MLA] Fix SM90 sparse MLA IMA on >16k-row steps by chunking plan/run
body:
## Purpose

Fixes a CUDA illegal-memory-access crash whenever a single scheduled step packs more than 16384 query rows on the SM90 sparse MLA backend (the GLM-5.3-Flash default), e.g. `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768` with a 28k-token prefill chunk, or 32k tokens scheduled across concurrent requests.

**Root cause (flashinfer 0.6.18.post1, the pinned version).** The SM90 batch-MLA plan hardcodes `max_total_num_works = 16384` and never checks it: the load-balancing schedule is `std::copy`'d into per-array regions sized for 16384 works, so a larger step silently overwrites neighboring schedule arrays, and the kernel then reads garbage `q_indptr`/`kv_indptr` (IMA in `BatchMLAPageAttentionHopper`). This backend feeds one varlen row per query token, so any step with more than 16384 scheduled tokens overflows. flashinfer 0.7.0 raised the limit to 65536 and added a hard error, but vLLM pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.18`. Small overflows (e.g. 16385 works) do not even fault — they run with a corrupted schedule.

**Fix.** When a step has more than `_MAX_PLAN_CHUNK_ROWS = 8192` query rows, plan and run the MQA as independent row chunks: the builder plans each chunk into its own `_SM90State` (a lazily grown pool), and `forward_mqa` runs each state's row range and concatenates. Each row is already an independent varlen query (causality is encoded in the top-k selection, `causal=False`), so chunking is exact. The bound is 8192 rather than 16384 so the work count stays provably under 16384 even with split-kv rows: works <= rows + total_kv_len / kv_len_limit, and `kv_len_limit` tracks total_kv_len / num_clusters. Steps at or under the limit keep the existing single-plan path unchanged, including CUDA-graph replay.

## Not a duplicate

- #56969 fixed a different OOB in this backend (mixed prefill/decode batches); it is in the tested tree and the crash still reproduces without this change.
- #55222 fixes the fp8 plan dtype and the indexer prefill workspace sizing; different call sites.
- #55626 reports a FlashInfer SM90 sparse-MLA IMA on H20 under TP+EP+MTP. Its stack is an async host sync point so it cannot be confirmed as the same bug, but a corrupted plan schedule is consistent with it.
- Searched open PRs for this backend, the plan work limit and schedule chunking; nothing else covers it.

## Testing

- Two new CPU wiring tests in `tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py` (chunked planning, chunked forward). The existing tests pass unchanged (`11 passed` total).
- Standalone flashinfer probe of this backend's exact plan/run call shape (rows x 1 token, kv_len=2048, heads=8, ckv=512, kpe=0, bf16) on H20: 16384 rows OK; 16385 rows runs but schedule corrupted; 20480 rows CUDA fault.
- Operator-level equivalence on H20 (real `BatchMLAPagedAttentionWrapper`, N=9000 rows, chunked 8192+808 vs single plan, per-row pseudo-random kv indices): **bit-identical outputs**, both for uniform kv_len=2048 and mixed kv_len in [512, 2176] (`max_abs_diff=0.0`). Chunking decomposes the plan/run only; per-row math is unchanged.
- Server A/B, GLM-5.3-Flash-FP8, TP=8 on 8xH20, MTP spec decode, 28201-token prompt:
  - without this fix, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`: OK (prefill chunks stay under the limit);
  - without this fix, `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`: IMA in `BatchMLAPageAttentionHopper`, engine dead;
  - with this fix, `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`: OK (28201-token prompt served in 1.71s; e2e requests pass).
  - The e2e tree is based on a Sep-17 main snapshot with the already-merged #57317 cherry-picked; upstream main has it. Note the FP8+MoE stack is not bit-stable across server restarts (greedy texts can flip between launches even on an unchanged tree), so equivalence is asserted at the operator level above, not via cross-launch text diffs.
- Upstream-main alignment (checked today): main still pins `flashinfer-python==0.6.18.post1`, and both touched files are byte-identical between main and the tested snapshot (last backend-file change is #56969 on Sep 15). The full test file, including the two new tests, passes on a checkout of today's main (`11 passed`; the engine e2e on that tree was not runnable in this image due to an unrelated `_moe_C` ABI bump in main, no nvcc available to rebuild).
- Backend-level repro on today's main tree (bypasses model loading): an unpatched-style single `plan` over N=20480 rows hits CUDA illegal address; the patched `build()` plans the same step as 3 chunks and all chunk runs complete with finite outputs.

## Notes

Each chunk state allocates its own 128 MiB workspace plus top-k index buffer, lazily on the first oversized step (~200 MiB each; two cover 32k tokens). Once the flashinfer pin moves to >= 0.7.0, the chunk limit can be revisited or removed.

AI assistance was used for this work.

title: [DSpark] Capture the full draft step as a decode CUDA graph
body:
## Purpose Even when the query forward replays a FULL CUDA graph, the DFlash/DSpark draft step still leaves two pieces of per-step host work on the decode hot path: 1. **Context K/V precompute** (`precompute_and_store_context_kv`) runs eagerly outside the graph, because the context shape varies from step to step. 2. **Attention metadata build** runs eagerly on every step solely to refresh the SWA builder's persistent GPU buffers; on the replay path, the built metadata itself is discarded. On uniform decode, both operations have fixed shapes and are capture-safe. This PR therefore captures the entire draft step (context K/V precompute, metadata refresh, query forward, and Markov sampling) as a single decode-step CUDA graph. **Before this PR:** **After this PR:** ## Validation Capturing the draft step must not change the speculator's proposals. The checks below therefore compare acceptance and accuracy against this branch's parent commit (`c723a831a8`), and serving performance against current main, with everything else held fixed. ### Setup - **Hardware / software:** 4× GB200, FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`. - **Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`). - **Speculative decoding:** DSpark with 5 speculative tokens and full decode CUDA graphs. - **Topologies:** - **DEP4:** MegaMoE backend with adaptive verification. - **TP4:** auto MoE backend with fixed verification. ### Acceptance and GSM8K accuracy Each pair runs the full GSM8K test set (1,319 identical 5-shot completion prompts) with greedy decoding, concurrency 32, a 1,024-token output cap, and strict answer extraction. Acceptance length is read from the engine's `vllm:spec_decode_*` counters over the whole run for DEP4. For TP4, it is aggregated from the engine's periodic SpecDecoding log windows over the steady state; the same method is used on both sides of each pair. | Configuration | Acceptance length, incl. bonus (parent → PR) | GSM8K (parent → PR) | | --- | ---: | ---: | | DEP4 | 3.411 → **3.385** | 1234 → 1227 / 1319 (93.56% → 93.03%) | | TP4 | 3.471 → **3.486** | 1227 → 1223 / 1319 (93.03% → 92.72%) | - The acceptance deltas are within ±1% and have opposite signs across the two topologies, and the per-position acceptance curves coincide. The captured draft step therefore does not change what the drafter proposes. - The GSM8K deltas are run-to-run noise: two repeats of the same DEP4 parent configuration scored 0.9219 and 0.9356 (an 18/1319 spread), which is wider than any delta in the table. - These results establish parity with the parent; they do not claim an accuracy improvement.
GSM8K server configuration Common flags: ```bash --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 \ --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 ``` DSpark is configured with 5 speculative tokens. - **DEP4:** `--data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --kernel-config '{"moe_backend":"deep_gemm_mega_moe"}'`, with adaptive verification enabled. - **TP4:** `--tensor-parallel-size 4`, with the auto MoE backend and adaptive verification disabled.
### Serving benchmark TP4, DSpark (5 speculative tokens, synthetic acceptance length 5.5), random dataset with 128 input / 1,024 output tokens. **Base** is `826e300cde` (main) and **PR** is `12b4c35c1b` (the same commit plus this PR's diff). CPU/step is the host time per engine step, measured with an injected per-step probe. | Concurrency | CPU/step | TPOT | ITL | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 6.80 → 4.53 ms | 1.29 → 1.07 ms (−17.1%) | 7.04 → 5.87 ms (−16.6%) | | 8 | 6.58 → 4.43 ms | 1.87 → 1.84 ms (−1.6%) | 9.94 → 9.94 ms (0.0%) | | 32 | 7.00 → 4.54 ms | 2.95 → 2.92 ms (−1.0%) | 14.74 → 14.65 ms (−0.6%) | | 64 | 7.16 → 4.64 ms | 4.05 → 3.93 ms (−3.0%) | 20.21 → 20.25 ms (+0.2%) | The PR cuts host time per step by about a third at every concurrency. At concurrency 1 the step is host-bound, so this carries through to a ~17% lower TPOT and ITL; at higher concurrency the GPU dominates and latency is roughly unchanged.
Serving benchmark configuration ```bash vllm serve --tensor-parallel-size 4 \ --attention-config '{"backend":"FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41","indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}' \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --no-enable-prefix-caching \ --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":5.5}' vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 1024 \ --ignore-eos --max-concurrency <1|8|32|64> ```
### Tests The captured draft step is also covered by: ```bash .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py -q ``` ## AI assistance AI assistance was used for this change: the implementation, the evaluation runs, and this description were produced with Claude Code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Sampler] Add DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) sampling
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #8581

DRY penalizes tokens that would extend a token sequence already present in the context, with a penalty that grows exponentially in the repetition length. It targets loops directly, which `repetition_penalty` (a flat per-token scale) does not. It is a standard sampler in llama.cpp, koboldcpp and text-generation-webui (designed by p-e-w, koboldcpp implementation by pi6am, per llama.cpp's credit line). It complements `RepetitionDetectionParams`, which stops a request once a loop is detected; DRY makes the loop less likely to form.

**A custom logits processor. It changes no existing vLLM file: 4 new paths, +1868/-0** against `5302d1fe40` (#56497, which turned the V2 sampler into a `list[LogitsProcessor]`). The four are `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/dry.py`, `vllm/v1/sample/dry_core.py`, `vllm/v1/sample/dry_utils.py` and `tests/v1/sample/test_dry.py`, per `git diff --stat 5302d1fe40 25a5ec7856`. No entry in `Sampler.logits_processors`, no `SamplingParams` field, no change to the OpenAI request schemas, and no sampler test double edited.

**No gpu<->cpu synchronization is added to the sampler hot path.** A live engine is clean in three modes under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error`, the strict mode of that check (`envs.py:646-650`: `warn` warns on each sync, `error` raises), and a fourth mode with no engine shows the checker itself armed; the two degenerate parameter regions that do synchronize are declared in the source rather than left to trip it.

It loads by FQCN, online or offline:

```
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \
    --logits-processors vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.dry:DryState
```

```python
LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct",
    logits_processors=["vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.dry:DryState"])
```

`--logits-processors` is `ModelConfig.logits_processors` (`config/model.py:370`, registered at `arg_utils.py:978`). A package may instead register `DryState` under the `vllm.logits_processors` entry-points group (`logits_processor/loader.py:34`), in which case no flag is needed. Neither route forces the V1 runner: custom logits processors are not in `VllmConfig._get_v2_model_runner_unsupported_features` (`config/vllm.py:2880`) at this base.

Parameters arrive in `SamplingParams.extra_args`, which is `vllm_xargs` on the OpenAI-compatible endpoints (`completion/protocol.py:226`, copied to `extra_args` at `:365`; the chat and responses schemas do the same at `chat_completion/protocol.py:482` and `:703`, `responses/protocol.py:290` and `:433`; `docs/features/custom_arguments.md`):

```
curl http://localhost:8000/v1/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct",
  "prompt": "Summarize the water cycle.",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "vllm_xargs": {"dry_multiplier": 0.8, "dry_sequence_breakers": ["\n", ":", "\"", "*"]}
}'
```

The recognized keys are `dry_multiplier`, `dry_base`, `dry_allowed_length`, `dry_penalty_last_n` and `dry_sequence_breakers`, written down once with llama.cpp's defaults in `_DRY_DEFAULTS` (`dry.py:74-80`). `dry_multiplier` defaults to 0.0, so a loaded processor is inert until a request sets it. Any other `dry_*` key fails the request (`dry.py:149-158`) instead of being ignored as a misspelling.

One default deliberately differs from llama.cpp: `dry_penalty_last_n` is `-1` here (scan the whole context) against llama.cpp's `64`. llama.cpp has no equivalent: libllama clamps a negative `dry_penalty_last_n` to 0 (`src/llama-sampler.cpp:3640`) and llama-server rejects one (`server-schema.cpp:153-155`, hard limits `[0, INT32_MAX]`). Every other default matches `common/common.h:243-259` at llama.cpp `ec928150`, the revision every llama.cpp line number here is against. Four validation rules also differ from llama.cpp's, three of them llama-server's and the fourth libllama's:

- A `dry_base` below 1.0. llama-server replaces it with the default (`server-schema.cpp:142-147`); this accepts it and warns, which leaves DRY inert (`dry.py:222-234`).
- An empty breaker array. llama-server rejects it (`server-schema.cpp:242-249`); this accepts it (`dry_utils.py:110-112`).
- Breaker count. llama-server has no cap; this rejects more than 64 (`dry.py:217-221`), since a previously unseen multi-character breaker costs a containment scan over the vocabulary.
- Breaker string length. libllama truncates to 40 bytes (`MAX_CHAR_LEN`, `src/llama-sampler.cpp:3642`, compared against `std::string::size()` at `:3665-3668`); this truncates to 40 code points (`dry_utils.py:110`).

### Implementation

Line numbers are against `25a5ec7856` on this branch, or against `5302d1fe40` for files this PR does not touch.

- `DryState` (`dry.py:98`) subclasses the V2 `LogitsProcessor` and is constructed by `build_custom_logits_processors` with `(vllm_config, LogitsProcRequestState)` (`logits_processor/loader.py:183`). The loader's processors are appended after `logit_bias_state`, `penalties_state` and `bad_words_state` (`sampler.py:69-74`), which is llama.cpp's chain order: `common/common.h:261-263` lists `COMMON_SAMPLER_TYPE_PENALTIES` then `COMMON_SAMPLER_TYPE_DRY`. Bad words ahead of DRY means that mask wins over DRY's edits. DRY only subtracts, so it cannot re-inflate a grammar-masked token, which `interface.py:99-103` requires of a processor.
- `validate_params` (`dry.py:138`) is the admission hook: a classmethod over `SamplingParams` that the frontend runs per request (`loader.py:204-209`, which wraps a `ValueError` into `VLLMValidationError`), so a bad argument fails the request before it reaches the sampler. It type-checks all five keys. `dry_multiplier` and `dry_base` get finiteness and non-negativity; `dry_allowed_length` and `dry_penalty_last_n` get a stricter integer check, a lower bound of 0 and of -1 respectively, and an upper bound, `_DRY_INT_MAX` (`dry.py:63`), which is llama-server's `INT32_MAX` cap, because without one an int64 numpy store raises `OverflowError` inside `execute_model`; `dry_sequence_breakers` gets a list-of-strings check and the 64-entry cap.
- The `dry_base >= 1.0` assert is gone from `apply`. The review named `validate_params()` or `use_dry()`; this is the `use_dry()` one, since `validate_params` only warns for such a base, per the parity note above. The invariant is documented on `use_dry` (`dry.py:389-401`), the predicate `add_request` gates the slot on (`dry.py:246`), which returns False for such a base and keeps it out of `dry_core`. The one assert left in `apply` is the draft-expansion check (`dry.py:300`).
- `add_request` (`dry.py:241`) reads `extra_args` through `_dry_args` (`dry.py:85`), stores the five parameters into per-slot numpy arrays, and gates the slot on `use_dry` (`dry.py:246`). Slots are recycled, so it clears the previous occupant's breaker entry (`dry.py:248`) whether or not the new request enables DRY.
- The tokenizer is loaded once in `__init__` with `cached_tokenizer_from_config` (`dry.py:129`), and llama.cpp's default breaker set is resolved there eagerly (`dry.py:133-135`), because `add_request` runs inside `execute_model`.
- Breaker masks are cached by `frozenset` of token ids, not per request slot: `breaker_ids` maps a slot to its set (`dry.py:119`) and `_breaker_masks` maps a set to one `[vocab]` bool device tensor (`dry.py:120`, built at `dry.py:273-291`). Every request that asked for the same breakers shares one mask and one host-to-device copy.
- `apply` (`dry.py:293`) takes its window widths from `ctx.seq_lens_upper_bound_np` (`dry.py:305`), so it does no device read. The interface supplies that host-side bound and documents it as exact when speculative decoding is not in use (`interface.py:86-89`), which is the condition this processor already requires. The field is not from this PR; it is in `5302d1fe40` at `interface.py:89`.
- Windows are gathered from the GPU-resident `req_states.all_token_ids` (`dry.py:324` and `:336-337`), so there is no per-step host copy of token history.
- Match lengths are computed as diagonal comparisons capped at `allowed_length + max_exponent`, which is exact because the exponent clamp maps every longer match to the same penalty. `_J_BUDGET` (`dry_core.py:117`) caps the j dimension, and is asserted below `2**15` so that the int16 run-length sum stays representable (`dry_core.py:122`); the scan is chunked against a separate byte budget, `_CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET` (`dry_core.py:130`, used at `:241`). The accumulator holds the penalty rather than the match length, so the charged entries go in with one `index_add_` (`dry_core.py:333`) and no post-scan `nonzero()`.
- Breaker strings resolve by llama.cpp's containment rule: every vocabulary token whose decoded text contains a breaker string is a breaker (`resolve_dry_breakers`, `dry_utils.py:91`). A single-character breaker resolves through a character index built alongside the vocabulary decode (`_VocabIndex`, `dry_utils.py:43`); only a multi-character one scans the decoded texts.

### Two deviations from the review comments

- The `frozenset` mask cache is bounded at `_MAX_CACHED_BREAKER_MASKS = 64` sets with FIFO eviction (`dry.py:69` and `:286-289`). `MAX_DRY_SEQUENCE_BREAKERS` (`dry.py:58`) bounds the length of one request's breaker list, not how many distinct sets clients can ask for, so the unbounded form holds one `[vocab]` bool on device per distinct set for the engine's lifetime. The host-side resolution cache is bounded the same way (`dry_utils.py:27` and `:126-128`).
- The tokenizer comes from `cached_tokenizer_from_config` (`dry.py:129`) rather than a bare `get_tokenizer`. It passes the config's `tokenizer_mode` (`tokenizers/registry.py:316-317`). `ModelConfig.__post_init__` replaces `"auto"` there with one of seven concrete modes for the architectures that need one, and leaves it `"auto"` for every other model, Qwen included (`config/model.py:693-712`); where it did replace it, a bare `get_tokenizer` would re-resolve its own `"auto"` default off the path instead (`registry.py:110-111`) and build the HF tokenizer, which is the wrong class for `deepseek_v32`. It is also the `lru_cache` entry the engine core's structured-output manager uses (`registry.py:305`, `v1/structured_output/__init__.py:79`), so the two share one tokenizer instead of building a second, and it returns `None` under `skip_tokenizer_init` (`registry.py:309-310`), which `_resolve_breakers` handles (`dry.py:237`).

### Known limitations

- No per-request refusal under speculative decoding. `validate_params` sees only `SamplingParams` (`interface.py:118-119`), so it cannot fail a request on the engine's configuration. `__init__` raises at startup instead (`dry.py:100-101`), echoing V1's own `STR_SPEC_DEC_REJECTS_LOGITSPROCS` (`v1/sample/logits_processor/__init__.py:44`, raised at `:204`). The consequence: one engine cannot serve both speculative-decoding and DRY traffic. Loading the processor on a speculative engine fails at startup, and not loading it leaves DRY unavailable there.
- Breaker resolution runs in the worker's `add_request`, inside `execute_model`, where the built-in form ran it in the frontend. `Sampler.add_request` calls it (`sampler.py:96`) from `GPUModelRunner.add_requests` (`gpu/model_runner.py:1156`), which `execute_model` calls at `:1646`. Measured on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct (vocab 151643, 151665 ids scanned), CPU only, rounded to the precision this box supports. The harness reports best-of, not a median: best of five for the init terms and for the scan-against-index comparison, best of fifty for the repeated-call figures, and a single run for each first-request figure. `__init__` decodes the vocabulary and builds the character index in about 555 ms (roughly 480 decode, 70 to 80 index) and resolves the default set there, so the default set costs 0.000 ms in `add_request`. A client's own set of single-character breakers costs under 1 ms on its first request and 0.006 ms after that; a set with two multi-character breakers costs about 10 ms, since it still scans the decoded texts. The character index is what makes the single-character case cheap: the same resolutions against the containment scan are about 20 ms for the default set and about 8 ms for the worst single character in that vocabulary (`" "`, in 53,131 tokens), against 0.31 ms and 1.9 ms through the index. The index costs 12.3 MiB of objects next to the 9.0 MiB of decoded texts already cached per tokenizer.
- Each worker rank loads its own tokenizer (`dry.py:129`). The frontend form needed one copy per engine.
- V2 model runner only. `DryState` subclasses the V2 `LogitsProcessor`, and the V1 loader requires its own (`v1/sample/logits_processor/__init__.py:151-152`), so an engine that has fallen back to the V1 runner fails at startup rather than ignoring DRY.
- llama.cpp additionally expands multi-token restart sequences for breakers; not implemented here. Containment resolution handles single-token breakers only.
- Two parameter regions fall back to a sequential scan in Python, which holds the GIL and has to bring the window to the host: a `dry_base` at or below `1.000001`, where the exponent clamp collapses to zero, and an `allowed_length + max_exponent` above the vectorized path's budget of 2048, which at the default `dry_allowed_length` means a `dry_base` below about `1.044`. That body is wrapped in `gpu_sync_allowed()` (`dry.py:355`), so `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK` does not fire on it silently.
- There is no early-out for a DRY request whose context never repeats: finding that out needs a device read, so such a request pays the full-width accumulator and `index_add_` on every step.

## Test Plan

- `pytest tests/v1/sample/test_dry.py`, included in the PR.
- `pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_thinking_budget.py`: the three sampler suites around the code the processor plugs into. This PR does not edit them.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` over the four files.
- A live engine under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` in `eager` and `cudagraph` modes, a `resolve` mode that counts vocabulary passes inside the engine process, a no-engine `detector` mode that checks the sync checker fires, and two `untouched-*` modes that compare token ids from an engine with the processor loaded against one without, on requests that set no `dry_*` key.

## Test Result

All local, on one RTX 5050 (sm_120) with torch 2.13.0+cu130. The unit suites and ruff ran at `25a5ec7856`; the engine runs and the timings ran at `7743467b97` and `ec74785c7a`, siblings of that head rather than ancestors. `dry.py` is the same blob at all three and the other three files differ only in comments and docstrings: AST-equal after a docstring strip, 4 of 4 paths, with a mutation control that fails. vLLM's test CI has not run, because the PR carries no `ready` label: `pre-run-check` fails unless a PR carries `verified`, `ready` or `ready-run-all-tests`, or its author has four merged PRs.

- `tests/v1/sample/test_dry.py`: **38 passed**. `test_gpu_sampler_flags.py`, `test_gpu_logits_processors.py` and `test_gpu_thinking_budget.py`: **29 passed**. Those three are byte-identical to `5302d1fe40` (`git diff --stat 5302d1fe40 25a5ec7856 -- <the three>` is empty), so they are a regression check rather than part of the change.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all four files under main's current config, which selects the pydocstyle `D` rules (`pyproject.toml:66-69`).
- The character index is checked against the containment scan it replaces, in two places. `test_breaker_index_matches_containment_scan` (`tests/v1/sample/test_dry.py:699`) is in the suite; out of tree, the same comparison over 20335 breaker inputs on the Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct vocabulary, 17829 of them every character that occurs in it, gives 0 mismatches.
- llama.cpp fidelity is checked in the suite. `test_worked_example` reproduces llama.cpp's own commented example from `src/llama-sampler.cpp`. `test_v2_matches_reference_fuzz` agrees with the sequential reference implementation, which shares no code with the vectorized path, over randomized histories at two chunk budgets. `test_differential_against_oracle` agrees with a brute-force reimplementation. `test_exponent_clamp_float32_semantics` and `test_double_pow_saturation` pin the float32 exponent clamp and the `std::pow(float, int)`-in-double behaviour that a naive port loses. `test_v2_disabled_and_gating` pins the disabled path, `test_peak_memory_bounded` bounds the scan's transient, and `test_breaker_mask_cache_is_bounded` pins the eviction above. An earlier revision also ran a differential against the llama.cpp binary with no disagreements, but that harness and its logs no longer exist and it is not offered as evidence.
- A live engine under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` on this code, four modes, **each exiting 0**: `eager` (`enforce_eager`, so compilation and capture can neither hide nor invent a sync), `cudagraph` (`cudagraph_mode=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`; the run captures twice, 51 piecewise and 2 full during CUDA graph memory profiling, then 51 piecewise and 35 full once the KV cache is sized), `resolve` (engine core in the same process) and `detector`. The three engine modes each run the same arms on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct: DRY at llama.cpp's default breaker set (`dry_multiplier=0.8`, `dry_base=1.75`, `dry_allowed_length=2`, `dry_penalty_last_n=64`), an unseen breaker set, a degenerate base, a DRY-off control, and five copies of the prompt in one batch. The harness asserts rather than prints its results: the DRY arm's text must differ from the control's on the same prompt, and all five batch rows must equal the batch-of-1 text. Both held in all three engine modes. Under `error` a detected sync raises, so exit 0 is the finding: no undeclared host-device synchronization on the path DRY adds.
- Two of those arms come with the harness's own qualification. The unseen-breaker arm matches the control byte for byte, since no match survives a sentence boundary, so it is path coverage for the request-time resolve and the mask build rather than evidence that DRY changed anything. The degenerate base, `dry_base=1.000001`, routes to the Python sequential fallback wrapped in `gpu_sync_allowed()` (`dry.py:355`), and that arm produces text with the check silent.
- `detector` is what makes the green result mean anything. With no engine, an undeclared `.item()` and an undeclared non-blocking copy from unpinned host memory both raise, and the same two syncs inside `gpu_sync_allowed()` are silent. **The checker is armed.**
- `resolve` counts the vocabulary pass in the process that makes it: once during engine init, 674.0 ms and 680.5 ms in the two runs, and 0 times while serving requests, one trip into `_vocab_index` and a cache hit. That is the same pass as the 555 ms figure above, measured inside a live engine rather than on its own in a CPU-only process, so this is the number that applies here. Resolving the default breaker set in `__init__` is what puts it there. A first DRY request still costs more than a later one in both runs (410.1 and 419.2 ms against 278.8 and 277.1 ms in eager, 300.7 and 319.4 ms against 106.8 and 106.7 ms in cudagraph), but breaker resolution is not that premium: an unseen set of three single-character breakers, which resolves and builds a new mask inside `execute_model`, came in at +4.5 and +0.6 ms over the later-request figure in eager, +1.7 and +1.9 ms in cudagraph. Two runs bound resolution and the mask build under 5 ms and do not separate them from the run-to-run spread. What the rest of the first-request premium is was not measured.
- Loading the processor does not move traffic that never asks for DRY. Two more modes, `untouched-eager` and `untouched-cudagraph`, build two engines each with identical `LLM` kwargs apart from `logits_processors` and with `seed=0` written out rather than left to the default, then compare token ids rather than text: three prompts with no `dry_*` key, the repetitive one, a prose one, and one carrying every character of the default breaker set, each sent alone, then all three batched, then alone again after a DRY request. **9 of 9 id sequences identical per mode, 18 of 18 across the two, both exiting 0.** The positive control is in the same run: the `dry_*` request diverges in the plugin engine while the same `extra_args` changes nothing in the engine without the processor, so the difference is the processor and not the dict. That second engine is sync-clean under the same armed check, and the only measured cost of loading the plugin is engine build time, +1266 ms eager and +904 ms cudagraph, the order of that 674 to 681 ms vocabulary pass.
- No serving path has been exercised. Every run above drives the offline `LLM` API or pytest, so `/v1/chat/completions`, `vllm_xargs` over the wire, concurrent and mixed batches, and end-to-end throughput are unmeasured.
- Two things are not measured on this code: step cost per batch size and a two-arm control over nine sampler suites against pristine main.
- This box has one 8 GB consumer card, so there is no large-model or throughput evidence here.

An older snapshot of this work, with its documentation and verification scripts, is published as a standalone patch pinned to an older base, for operators who want the feature before this is reviewed: https://github.com/sashko-zakharchuk/vllm/tree/dry-sampling-410f6da5c4/dry-patch . It predates the synchronization removal, the port onto #56497 and this processor form.

Per `AGENTS.md` section 1: AI assistance was used for this change and for this description. Test commands and their results are the two sections above, and every factual claim above names the command or file:line behind it.

On duplication: #8581 is the request, @NJX-njx claimed it in March 2026 and no branch followed. Four other DRY pull requests exist, all closed unmerged: #8546 (@alxiang, +151, 2024-09-17), #11368 (@AlpinDale, +456, 2024-12-20 to 2025-06-11), #16695 (@0xymoro, +212, 2025-04-16 to 2025-10-03) and #57620 (@sawsa307, 2026-09-18), which was opened and closed the same day as a check on the #56497 interface.

Compared with #57620: it is interface validation and says so, and the `dry_core.py` and `dry_utils.py` it carries are this PR's, credited under a `Co-authored-by` line. What is here is that same core in the same custom-processor form, with this PR's review comments applied. Speculative decoding raises at startup rather than warning once in `apply` and skipping the batch, which is what the review asked for; the breaker mask is keyed by breaker set and bounded at 64 with FIFO eviction rather than held per request slot; and the default breaker set resolves eagerly in `__init__` behind a character index rather than per request in `add_request`.

title: [Model] Support Ling 3.0 D-Spark serving
body:
## Purpose

This PR adds D-Spark speculative decoding support for
[Ling 3.0 Flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash)
using the official
[Ling D-Spark checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-dspark).

Key changes:

- Register `LingDSparkModel` and reuse the existing Qwen3 D-Spark runtime.
- Validate and normalize the Ling target/draft checkpoint contract.
- Expose the BailingMoeV3 auxiliary hidden states required by D-Spark.
- Use the checkpoint's D-Spark `block_size` as the default number of draft
  tokens while respecting an explicitly configured `num_speculative_tokens`.
- Give the Ling dense draft an independent 128-token KV-cache block instead of
  inheriting the target's KDA-expanded global block size.

Ling uses an MLA/KDA target with a dense MHA draft. KDA increases the target's
global attention block size, but applying the same token block size to the
dense draft produces a much larger MHA page and substantially reduces the
shared KV-cache capacity.

The Ling draft therefore uses a local 128-token KV-cache block. This override
is specific to normalized Ling D-Spark checkpoints; other Qwen3 DFlash and
D-Spark models continue to use the global cache block size.

The value 128 follows the model geometry. Per TP rank, with `H = 32 / TP`, the
draft MHA page is `128 × H × 128 × 2 (K/V) × 2 bytes`, equal to the KDA FP32
recurrent matrix `H × 128 × 128 × 4 bytes`. The complete KDA page is larger
because it also contains convolution state. Since regular MHA supports physical
page padding, the draft page can be padded to the aligned MLA/KDA target page
while retaining its logical 128-token block.

Example launch:

```bash
vllm serve \
  inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash \
  --served-model-name Ling-3.0-flash-dspark \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --reasoning-parser ling3 \
  --compilation-config \
    '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","max_cudagraph_capture_size":2048}' \
  --speculative-config \
    '{"method":"dspark","model":"inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-dspark","num_speculative_tokens":7}'

| Configuration | Correct | Accuracy |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Target-only reference | 1278 / 1319 | 96.8916% |
| Ling D-Spark | 1277 / 1319 | 96.8158% |
