title: [AuxOutput] Add Mooncake backend with keys-only R3 output
body:
## Summary Add a Mooncake backend on top of the AuxOutput implementation merged in #45635. This PR targets `main` and does not include the legacy commit stack. It promotes the validated implementation reviewed in aoshen02/vllm#7 upstream. Duplicate check: no open upstream PR implements this keys-only R3 storage backend. #57966/#57025 concern prefix omission/KV-offload compatibility, not publishing complete R3 to Mooncake for external retrieval. The fork PR is the earlier review copy, not a separate upstream proposal. ```text GPU worker R3 -> existing background writer -> Mooncake full blocks EngineCore -> clip accepted boundaries -> Mooncake boundary/tail objects TITO HTTP -> ordered aux_output_keys only trainer -> get(keys), concatenate -> complete R3 ``` - Reuse native Mooncake batch I/O, existing configuration/setup and background writer. SHM remains the default. - Return keys on the terminal TITO response, including stored partial tails; no inline R3 with Mooncake. Publication completes before exposing final keys. Requests with string stops publish incremental keys internally so API-side termination can deliver complete R3; HTTP still exposes keys only at completion. - Share full-block keys across instances and DP ranks using block hash and reset generation. P/D must use the same generation, model/R3 profile, hash configuration/seed, block size and Mooncake store. - No new RPC, ACK protocol, publisher thread, TTL registry or retry state. Retention is deployment-owned; missing/evicted objects fail explicitly. - EngineCore owns a separate client for boundaries finalized after Scheduler stop/length handling. Scheduler shutdown closes it; closing the Worker client in another process cannot release it. This does not delete remote objects. ## Validation Local tests: **128 distinct tests passed** across these suites/tests: ```bash python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q HF_HUB_CACHE= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_aux_output_keys_preserve_existing_output_wire_positions tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_terminal_aux_output_keys_survive_ipc_and_output_processing -q python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py::test_mooncake_decode_crosses_blocks_and_clips_terminal_output tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_request_output_collector -q ``` Commands used `/home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python`. A combined run initially had one missing offline default-model snapshot; rerunning that config test in the normal cache environment passed. Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy, passes. On this `main`-based branch, reruns passed **92 store/config tests + 34 TITO/IPC tests**, and all changed-file hooks. The new worktree initially lacked local FlashAttention extension links; collection passed after reusing the same installed extensions as the earlier worktree, without source changes. The additional command passed 3 tests (one store rerun and two collector cases). Tests cover the renamed `aux_output_keys` field through IPC, aggregation, streaming/non-streaming HTTP, absence of the old HTTP field, and client close. An attempted full OutputProcessor suite had 10 passes and 33 fixture errors in offline mode; an online retry confirmed HTTP 401 for the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` fixture. That full suite is **not** claimed passing. Slurm GB200 validation: two independent DP4/TP1/EP vLLM instances on two nodes, one shared Mooncake master, RDMA, async scheduling and prefix caching. Consumers run on the opposite node and fetch complete R3 using only returned keys. - 256K context, concurrency32 per instance: cold raw-data equality, hot prefix equality and fresh-client reads after requests finish pass (job30127). - MTP rejection and real stop clipping:32outputs match same-execution raw request/token-position data; fresh reads pass (job30130). - Forced preemption:88preemptions per instance,256requests total, all raw-position and fresh-reader checks pass, including local replay (job30144). Earlier runs with zero preemptions were rejected, not counted as coverage. - Matched SHM/Mooncake end-to-end throughput includes full cross-host retrieval and validation, two rounds,256K/concurrency32 per instance (jobs30115/30131): | Backend | Combined workload-span throughput | | --- | ---: | | SHM |115,758tokens/s | | Mooncake |115,038tokens/s | Difference **-0.62%**, including instance start skew. Averaging summed individual instance rates gives **-0.34%**. No material regression observed in these runs; two rounds are not a confidence interval or a precise intrinsic overhead estimate. Actual weights were **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base**, despite a0731served alias. GPU tests used a pinned-image Python port of the change, not a full target-revision rebuild. Correctness hooks were disabled for throughput measurements. RDMA results do not establish TCP stress reliability; high-key-count TCP reads previously encountered native transport resource exhaustion. The raw oracle checks accepted same-position provenance, not a specific replay version. These GPU runs precede the API-field rename; the rename was validated locally, not with another GPU throughput run. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation; five independent Claude audit rounds of the preceding implementation concluded APPROVE; this follow-up naming/lifecycle review was self-audited. Human line-by-line review and acceptance of the test evidence remain required before merge. ## Multi-turn scaling follow-up (2026-09-21) GB200, actual DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base weights, DP4/TP1/EP per deployment, 256K initial context, 32 concurrent conversations per deployment, four turns (16 generated tokens + 1024 appended input tokens per turn). Prefix caching, chunked prefill and async scheduling enabled. Full R3 is fetched and validated on another node every turn; timing includes retrieval, decoding and validation. Median request-turns/s over three repetitions: | Engine replicas / concurrent conversations | SHM | Mooncake, 4 readers/deployment | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 / 32 | 0.623869 | 0.750283 | +20.3% | | 16 / 128 | 2.410555 | 2.954281 | +22.6% | The single-reader control did **not** outperform SHM (0.618058 / 2.361755). Independent native reader clients reduce client-side serialization; this is not an unconditional backend speedup. Each additional reader costs 128 MiB of local transfer buffer. At four deployments, configured Mooncake capacity is 256 GiB versus 128 GiB SHM, so this is not an equal-memory-cost comparison. Backend order was Mooncake then SHM, not randomized; three repeats do not establish statistical significance. Synthetic fixed-token conversations measure serving performance, not model quality. Jobs 30153/30154 completed successfully. Across the 18 phases (including the single-reader control), all 5,760 request-turns passed shape/dtype, output-token and within-conversation cached-prefix R3 equality checks. No preemptions occurred in this performance run; preemption/raw-oracle coverage is reported separately above. This does not assert cross-run, cross-backend bitwise R3 equality. Reproduction configuration: pinned image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:95569a195dfe088c22983b08509e8e7156c26b356726147db4072600cba416ed`, image revision `2671fedfc7ae604761990603fc736c0c4f21de57`, with the archived source patch; Mooncake 0.3.12.post1, RDMA, shared master, reader `global_segment_size=0`, 128 MiB local buffers and 8 GiB per writer/publisher. Use 1 and 4 deployments, 32 HTTP threads/deployment, and 1/4 native reader clients as separate cases. Reset prefix cache before each repetition and exclude warmup; aggregate throughput by the whole workload time span. The Slurm recipe and raw logs are currently cluster-local, not a portable public benchmark. These frozen-image runs precede the latest mechanical cleanup; they are not a fresh GPU measurement of the final PR head. Latest cleanup removes repeated per-output block-size metadata, uses the Scheduler's authoritative hash granularity and shares output construction between backends. Changed-file pre-commit (including mypy) passes. Latest focused rerun: **107 passed, 173 deselected**: ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'mooncake or aux or routed_experts or store' -q --tb=short ``` ## Profiling follow-up (2026-09-22) Same frozen runtime and 256K/four-turn workload as above, one DP4 deployment, 32 concurrent conversations, cross-host RDMA retrieval with four native readers. Each backend has two unprofiled controls and one profiled run (Slurm 29958.60). Mean control throughput: **SHM 0.596435 vs Mooncake 0.743928 request-turns/s (+24.7%)**. Mean workload duration: 214.65s vs 172.07s; about 95% of the time saved is in the three warm/prefix-reuse turns. This compares complete delivery paths, not intrinsic RDMA versus shared-memory read speed. Mean per-request Mooncake costs over 192 warm requests in the two controls: | Stage | Wall time | | --- | ---: | | Native batch get, including lookup/transfer/wait | 526 ms | | Copy buffers to bytes and release handles | 36.5 ms | | Final bytes concatenation | 10.2 ms | | Whole get_concatenated, including the above | 578 ms | | Separate per-client lock wait | 1486 ms | SHM materializes R3, encodes NumPy/Base64 and sends it through HTTP; Mooncake returns keys and fetches raw bytes separately. Mean warm-request HTTP completion is 17.88s vs 4.26s; post-HTTP retrieval/decoding/checking is 1.84s vs 2.45s. Mooncake therefore adds post-HTTP work but saves substantially more on HTTP delivery. For 128 profiled requests, the client HTTP read chain consumes 97.49 vs 6.28 CPU seconds, JSON decoding 8.23 vs 0.77; SHM also spends 14.04 CPU seconds on Base64 decoding. HTTP body volume is 11.61 GB vs 0.89 GB, with Mooncake still fetching another 8.71 GB of raw R3. The dominant observed saving is avoiding the large Python HTTP/JSON/Base64 path, not eliminating data transfer or concatenation. Mooncake publication/flush waiting is higher; not every stage is faster. Profile timings are inclusive CPU totals, not additive request latency. Profiling reduces throughput by 11.8% (SHM) and 3.3% (Mooncake); the table and throughput comparison use unprofiled controls. Native API time is not pure RDMA wire time, and exported function profiles do not fully account for native CPU. The SHM after-control used a restarted, re-warmed server after a profiler-export failure. These two controls are not a confidence interval. All six phases passed 768 request checks and 576 cached-prefix R3 equality checks, with identical prefix-hit counts and zero preemptions. This retains the fixed-token/model-weight, memory-capacity and frozen-image limitations above; it does not establish model quality or cross-backend bitwise equality. Raw profiles, controls and recipes are archived cluster-locally. ## Independent Aux configuration (2026-09-22) AuxOutput now requires `VLLM_AUX_OUTPUT_MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`; KV retains `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`. There is no implicit fallback. Both variables may explicitly point to the same file. The existing config class and native setup are reused; no new RPC, thread or abstraction is introduced. Worker, EngineCore publisher and external helper readers use the same Aux factory. Ray propagates the variable, not the file; the path must be readable on each relevant node. KV-specific `enable_offload` does not restrict Aux initialization, including when both variables explicitly select the same file. The initial configuration-isolation commit touched five files (+90/-9). The follow-up below removes the standalone document and corrects its erroneous offload restriction; those initial counts do not describe the final PR. Validation: **159 distinct local tests passed** and changed-file pre-commit (including configured mypy) passed: ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/test_ray_env.py tests/test_ray_env_utils.py -q --tb=short /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -k config -q --tb=short ``` A new GB200 run (Slurm step 29958.61) passed **32 request-turns and 16 cached-prefix R3 equality checks** across two independent DP4 deployments and opposite-node RDMA readers. Both containers inherited a KV config path pointing to a nonexistent file; valid writer/reader configs were supplied only through the new Aux variable. Workload: 32K initial prompt, eight conversations per deployment, two growing turns, 16 output tokens, async scheduling and chunked prefill. Keys-only responses, full R3 shape/dtype, token counts and cached-prefix equality passed; each instance recorded 260096 prefix-hit tokens and zero preemptions. This freshly tests the config patch on the pinned-image Python port described above, not a rebuild of the current full PR head. It is not a throughput A/B, model-quality evaluation, concurrent KV-connector traffic test or full Ray-cluster test. KV compatibility and Ray environment propagation are covered locally. ## Audit fixes (2026-09-22) - Remove the Aux rejection of KV `enable_offload=true`; shared configuration remains valid. The field controls KV-specific load policy, not Aux storage. - Fix API-side string stops: publish accepted incremental keys internally for requests with string stops and accumulate them in OutputProcessor. Ordinary requests retain terminal publication; external HTTP still returns keys only at completion. This avoids finishing at the API before EngineCore sends keys. - Correct the Mooncake Worker test to exercise keys-only output, not only a swapped storage backend. Add a network-independent tokenizer regression that checks two-step R3 byte equality when the API stops and aborts EngineCore. - Remove `docs/features/aux_output_mooncake.md` and its code reference. Final local validation: **148 tests passed** (112 store/config/related Scheduler cases, 173 deselected; 36 TITO/IPC/collector cases). Changed-file pre-commit, including configured mypy, and `git diff --check` passed. ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'mooncake or aux or routed_experts or store' -q --tb=short HF_HUB_CACHE= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_aux_output_keys_preserve_existing_output_wire_positions tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_terminal_aux_output_keys_survive_ipc_and_output_processing tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_request_output_collector -q --tb=short ``` String-stop requests incur more small-object writes; that performance cost has not been measured. The GPU runs above predate these audit fixes and are not claimed as validation of the new string-stop path. No new GPU run was performed. ## Backend layout follow-up ```text aux_output_connector/ store.py Shared BlockObject, error and background writer shm.py ShmBlockObjectStore mooncake.py MooncakeBlockObjectStore and output publisher ``` Move the existing SHM implementation into its own module and update imports, type references and test patches. No new interface, RPC or thread. The split also removes a redundant `slot is None` guard in SHM `put`; it is not a class-name-only AST change. Two older Worker test fixtures now explicitly select the SHM backend. Validation: **107 store/config tests + 18 capture tests passed**; changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed. One additional capture test fails while importing the installed Humming dependency (`humming.dtypes.float4e0m3` missing). Running that test's original HEAD source reproduces the same failure; it is not counted as passing. No new GPU benchmark was run for this mechanical split. ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q --tb=short /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py -q --tb=short ``` ## Mooncake PD + R3 handoff (2026-09-22) Enable `MooncakeConnector` with the Mooncake Aux backend. P runs the full prompt with `max_tokens=1` and no R3 prompt cropping; D receives the same prompt and the normal KV-transfer parameters plus: ```json "aux_output_prefix": {"block_size": 4, "keys": ["

", "

"]} ``` The block size is the R3/hash granularity (4 in this test), not the KV page size. D reuses shared full-block keys directly. Scheduler sends only the key for an unaligned first-forward boundary; Worker restores that block's missing prefix and joins newly computed R3. Aligned starts require no restore read. No full-prefix import or republication is needed. P objects remain immutable; the caller must keep source objects available. The configuration-level KV connector/PD blacklist has now been removed for both Aux backends. This is not a claim that every connector/backend implements remote R3 handoff; this PR's tested handoff is Mooncake PD + Mooncake Aux. Identical keys retain the first published value. After a cache miss and recomputation, returned R3 may therefore differ from the latest execution. This is an explicit accepted limitation; no overwrite or version mapping is introduced. Fresh tail keys can also wrap slices of older full objects. Validation: - 117 store/config tests passed; changed-file pre-commit, including mypy, passed. - Slurm 30373, two GB200 nodes, independent DP4/EP4 instances, real RDMA KV transfer and a shared Mooncake Store: all five cases passed. - Prompts 1025/1027/1028/1029/4099; D started at 1024/1026/1027/1028/4098. Covered 2–5 prefill chunks, streaming/nonstreaming, immutable P keys, complete external readback and later local reuse without the manifest. - First handoffs matched raw GPU rows exactly. Repeated keys retained their bytes; repackaged tails were checked against current or previously validated same-position rows, consistent with the first-writer contract. - Actual weights: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base. Same pinned image/Python adapter as above; modified Aux modules match the candidate source. This is not a full target-revision rebuild, throughput benchmark, or model-quality evaluation. - The initial retry oracle incorrectly assumed every new tail key represented new computation. Its failure logs were retained; the corrected checker and successful explicit retry are archived with the job. Slurm was cancelled after that retry passed, releasing both nodes. ```bash HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q --disable-warnings ``` AI assistance was used for this follow-up. Human review and acceptance of the semantic tradeoff and test evidence remain required before merge. ## Shared-key PD simplification (2026-09-23) Remove instance/DP namespaces and full-prefix restoration: production net **-28 lines**, touching only the two Aux connector modules and existing tests. No Scheduler/ModelRunner changes, new RPC or background-thread removal. Same P/D generation is an explicit deployment requirement. - **113 store/config tests passed**, changed-file pre-commit (including mypy) and `git diff --check` passed. Command is the store/config command above. - Independent Claude Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3 multi-round audits concluded APPROVE. - New Slurm **30589**, GB200 17/18, native RDMA: five PD cases passed with prompts 1025/1027/1028/1029/4099, 2–5 prefill chunks, streaming/nonstreaming, shared full-key equality, immutable P objects and later local cache reuse. D first-forward positions were 1024/1026/1027/1028/4098, confirming KV loading. - First checker failed on a later reuse: it only allowed the immediately prior response's R3, excluding an older valid first-writer row at the same position. The corrected checker allows previously validated same-position rows for new repackaged tails, while checking old-key immutability. Independent Kimi review approved the correction; the explicit rerun passed all five cases. Original failure logs remain: the batch retains exit 1 from the first checker; the rerun checker exited 0. No production patch was needed for this failure. - Actual weights: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base; existing pinned-image adapter, with changed modules byte-identical to this candidate. Not a full PR-image rebuild, throughput A/B or model-quality evaluation. Resources have been released. AI assistance was used. Human review remains required before merge. ## Main merge and PD policy (2026-09-23) Merged main (`88aa0d287d`) without force-push. Removed the entire AuxOutput KV connector blacklist, rather than keeping backend/connector exceptions. Other compatibility checks (model runner, PP/DCP/PCP, etc.) are unchanged. Configuration/store tests: **231 passed**; merge-file pre-commit passed. This permits configuration; it does not supply SHM with cross-host object access. Matched PD vs PD+R3 throughput completed successfully (Slurm **30597**, GB200 17/18, 20m13s). Same nodes, order PD -> PD+R3 -> PD, two measured rounds per phase; 64 requests/round, concurrency32, 32768 input +128 output tokens. Both P/D use DP4/EP4, async scheduling and real Mooncake RDMA KV transfer. | Mode | HTTP output tokens/s | Including full R3 retrieval | | --- | ---: | ---: | | PD, pooled before/after | 232.506 | 232.506 | | PD+R3 | 230.966 | 230.590 | | Change | -0.66% | -0.82% | Startup/warmup excluded. Each of the six measured rounds recorded2097152 external-KV hit tokens and zero P/D preemptions. All384 measured requests passed token checks;128 R3 requests passed full key-readback size checks, fetching1.086GB total. Raw-position correctness is covered by the prior E2E, not by this throughput checker. Four reader clients fetch R3 after HTTP; thread slots remain occupied through retrieval, so HTTP throughput is not an isolated model-execution metric. Before/after baseline drift was0.12%. Actual weights remain DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base, using the established frozen-image adapter, not a full latest-main rebuild. No raw GPU trace hooks, no MTP; synthetic cold prompts at one workload point. Few repeats are not a confidence interval. Resources released; user allocation14/15 untouched.

title: [WIP][Model][ROCm][DCP] DeepSeek-V4 decode context parallelism
body:
## Purpose

Model-layer DCP support for DeepSeek-V4 (hybrid SWA + compressed KV), per RFC #57228. Builds on the merged Kimi-K3 DCP framework from #51705 + #53598 and transplants the validated mechanisms from the inactive #44573 w/ co-author credit to @baonudesifeizhai. Adds onto current main, with ROCm/AITER leg being validated on 8xMI355X.

**Draft / WIP**: opened early for visibility and design alignment, not yet ready for review. Currently only contains the foundations for the functionality.

- [x] ContextParallelLayout + Triton ownership helpers (interleaved token/slot ownership, logical block table addressing)
- [x] DSV4 DCP merge ops: sink-after-merge via the consolidated v1/attention/ops/dcp.py collectives, compressor softmax reduce
- [x] Compressor partial-stats kernel (per-rank online-softmax pooling)
- [x] Compressor finalize kernels (owner-masked insert: compressed KV + indexer K caches)
- [ ] Scheduler geometry: supports_context_parallel spec flag + logical_block_size composed with dcp_world_size_for_kv_cache_spec
- [ ] Metadata localization (SWA / indexer / compressed slot mapping)
- [ ] Attention wiring (gather-Q, sink-free local attend + LSE, merge) w/ C4A decode top-k localization fix

#44573 is the direct ancestor of this PR (inactive since June, NVIDIA-only, before DCP framework consolidation). This PR series is it susccessors on the current main, validated and meant for ROCm. No other open PR or issue implements DSV4 DCP (checked 2026-09-16).

title: [Frontend][Tracing] Add support for tracing aborted requests

## Purpose Currently, requests that are aborted or terminated due to errors do not emit their corresponding tracing spans, making it challenging to diagnose and troubleshoot issues in production environments. This PR enhances the tracing functionality by ensuring aborted requests generate trace spans and including the error that caused the abortion in the trace span. ## Test Plan 1. Start vLLM with tracing enabled: ``` export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT=grpc://0.0.0.0:4317 export OTEL_SERVICE_NAME="vllm-server" export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_INSECURE=true vllm serve Qwen3-0.6B --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --block-size 16 --max-model-len 4096 --otlp-traces-endpoint="$OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT" --disable-log-requests ``` 2. Send a request and manually abort it (e.g., using Ctrl+C): ``` curl --location --request POST 'http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions' \ --header 'Authorization: Bearer 123456' \ --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{ "messages": [ { "role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant." }, { "role": "user", "content": "Could you please introduce yourself?" } ], "top_p": 0.9, "temperature": 1, "max_tokens": 1000, "stream": true }' ``` ## Test Result ---

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Support bare call: and whitespace-free channel transitions in Gemma4 parser
body:
## Summary

Fixes #54256.

When serving Gemma-4 with reasoning and tool calling, the model frequently transitions directly out of reasoning (`<channel|>`) into emitting a tool call (`call:func{...}`) without re-emitting the optional `<|tool_call>` prefix. 

This PR ensures the Gemma4 parser handles bare `call:` transitions from both `CONTENT` and `REASONING` states, and fixes the offline fallback regex in `gemma4_utils.py` when `<channel|>` directly precedes `call:` without whitespace.

## Root Cause

1. In `vllm/parser/gemma4.py`, transitioning from `REASONING` to `CONTENT` on `THINK_END` left the FSM without a transition on `CALL_PREFIX` (`"call:"`). When the model dropped `<|tool_call>`, the tool call was silently dropped.
2. In `vllm/tool_parsers/gemma4_utils.py`, the fallback regex `r"(?:<call>|(?:^|\s)call:)(\w+)\{(.*?)\}"` required whitespace before `call:`, missing attached delimiters like `<channel|>call:...`.
3. Related to #53444 (which added `:` opener handling within `TOOL_PREAMBLE`, but still required `<|tool_call>` to reach `TOOL_PREAMBLE`) and #53363 / #53255 (empty `tool_calls` with `finish_reason="tool_calls"`).

## Fix

1. **`vllm/parser/gemma4.py`**:
   - Added `(ParserState.CONTENT, "CALL_PREFIX") -> ParserState.TOOL_NAME` transition emitting `EventType.TOOL_CALL_START`.
   - Added `(ParserState.REASONING, "CALL_PREFIX") -> ParserState.TOOL_NAME` transition emitting `(EventType.REASONING_END, EventType.TOOL_CALL_START)`.
2. **`vllm/tool_parsers/gemma4_utils.py`**:
   - Updated fallback pattern to `r"(?:<call>|(?:^|\s|<channel\|>|:)call:)([\w\-\.]+)\{(.*?)\}"`.
3. **Tests** (`tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_regex_and_bare_calls.py`):
   - Exercises the production `vllm.tool_parsers.gemma4_utils.parse_tool_calls` directly (no copied local regex constants), so regressions in the real tiered pattern are caught. Cases assert both the parsed function name and arguments:
     - Tier 1: canonical tag-wrapped calls, `<turn|>` closure, multiple sequential calls, `strict=True` ignoring fallback shapes
     - Tier 2: bare `call:` glued to `<channel|>` (no whitespace), colon-prefixed `<|tool_call>:call:...`, leading-whitespace bare call, fragmented `<call>` tag, hyphen- and dot-containing tool names, no-call -> empty
   - Retains the `Gemma4EngineToolParser` + offline `parse_tool_calls` integration cases.

## Verification

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_regex_and_bare_calls.py tests/tool_parsers/test_gemma4_tool_parser.py
```
- 67/67 tests pass (13 in `test_gemma4_regex_and_bare_calls.py` + 54 existing).
- Verified against live Blackwell GPU deployment.

## AI assistance

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to refactor the regression tests to exercise the production parser. All changes were reviewed line-by-line by the submitter.

title: [Bugfix][Core] Raise a fresh EngineDeadError per request instead of re-raising the shared instance
body:
### Purpose

Fixes #56943.

When the engine dies, `AsyncLLM.output_handler` logs the root cause once and then `OutputProcessor.propagate_error()` hands the **same** exception instance to every in-flight request's `RequestOutputCollector`. Each consumer's `raise output` prepends its own frames onto the shared `__traceback__`, and the OpenAI serving layer logs that accumulated traceback once per request (`logger.exception("Error in chat completion stream generator.")`). Log volume therefore grows quadratically with the number of in-flight requests: an incident log showed 93 ever-growing tracebacks (233 → 845 lines per traceback) totaling 41,340 ERROR lines in ~10 minutes for ~90 concurrent requests.

Fix: in `RequestOutputCollector.get()`/`get_nowait()`, raise a fresh `EngineDeadError() from None` when the collected output is an `EngineDeadError`:

- Each request then logs only its own constant-size traceback; the root cause is still logged exactly once by `AsyncLLM.output_handler`.
- `from None` keeps the shared instance out of the `__context__` chain that logging would also print.
- The message users see is unchanged: `EngineDeadError` always carries the standard "EngineCore encountered an issue. See stack trace (above) for the root cause." text (`_format_exception` never attaches per-incident args).
- Non-`EngineDeadError` exceptions still pass through as the same instance, so per-request error behavior is unchanged.
- New requests already fail fast with a fresh instance via `ensure_alive()`, so this makes the in-flight path consistent with the new-request path.
- This follows the existing precedent in `generate()`, which wraps failures into a fresh `EngineGenerateError() from e` instead of re-raising a shared instance.

The collector is the single choke point through which both consumers (`generate()` and pooling `collect()`) receive the error, so the fix covers all current and future consumers.

Note on the base: this branch is based on the fork's `main` (the fork could not be synced to upstream `main` with the available token scopes). I verified with `git merge-tree` that it merges cleanly into today's `main`, and the merged `vllm/v1/engine/output_processor.py` is byte-identical to applying the same patch directly on `main`. Happy to rebase if preferred.

### Test Plan

Added `tests/v1/engine/test_request_output_collector_errors.py`:

- `test_collector_raises_fresh_engine_dead_error`: a shared `EngineDeadError` whose `__traceback__` was pre-grown by 10 re-raises is put into collectors; both `get()` and `get_nowait()` must raise a *fresh* instance whose traceback is shorter than the accumulated one, with `__suppress_context__` set.
- `test_collector_reraises_request_error_instance_unchanged`: non-`EngineDeadError` exceptions are still re-raised as the same instance.

### Test Result

Standalone reproduction of the collector mechanics (this machine has no full vllm dev env; CI will run the new unit tests):

```
shared error pre-grown to 10 tb entries
fixed:    get_nowait() : 3 fresh errors, constant tb depth 3
fixed:    await get(): 3 fresh errors, constant tb depth 4
control:  shared instance tb depth grows per consumer [12, 14, 16]
control:  ValueError re-raised as the same instance (unchanged behavior)
```

i.e. before the fix each consumer re-raising the shared instance grows its traceback by one consumer round per request; after the fix every consumer gets a constant-size traceback and the shared error stays out of the logged chain.

Related: vllm-ascend companion fix vllm-project/vllm-ascend#16570 (a model wrapper that amplified the same storm with extra frames), reported in vllm-project/vllm-ascend#16567.

title: [Kernel] Resubmit PR 48666 - Gemma4 FP8 KV FA4 head dim 512 backend selection
body:
## Purpose Re-submit https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48666 due to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52987. Flagged by CI for perf regression, but the regressed perf is resulting from Model emitting special token. The model emits the special token because plain serving with [RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic](https://huggingface.co/RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic) before https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48666 uses Triton, but #48666 upgraded to FA4 wrongly because the FA4 FP8-KV kernel does not support bidirectional attention (mm-prefix). After https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56305, serving without `--language-model-only` can use the `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN` composite backend: causal text uses FA3/FA4 per layer, while an actual mm-prefix request uses Triton. Therefore, `--language-model-only` is no longer needed. There's also a silent upgrade after unifying FA4 globally for all layers after https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42175. The correct table of kernels to be used when serving `vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic --kv-cache-dtype fp8`: | Serve mode | Before PR #48666 | After PR #48666, before this PR | After this PR | |---|---|---|---| | None (multimodal-prefix enabled) | head dim 256: **TRITON_ATTN**
head dim 512: **TRITON_ATTN** | head dim 256: **FA4 (wrong)**
head dim 512: **FA4** | **TRITON_FLASH_ATTN** composite:
head dim 256 causal: **FA3**
head dim 512 causal: **FA4**
mm-prefix: **TRITON_ATTN** | `FA3` is used for the head-dim 256 R-SWA layers even without mm-prefix because forcing FA4 with FP8 KV cache on SM90 causes output corruption. The config if-else guards are included in separated commits. ## Test Plan Same as the latest https://github.com/vllm-project/perf-eval/blob/main/workloads/gemma_4_31b_it_h200.yaml. ```bash vllm serve RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic \ --tensor-parallel-size 1 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \ --reasoning-parser gemma4 \ --tool-call-parser gemma4 \ --enable-auto-tool-choice ``` ```bash vllm bench serve \ --backend openai \ --base-url http://127.0.0.1:18000 \ --model RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic \ --dataset-name random \ --num-prompts 512 \ --max-concurrency 128 \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --ignore-eos \ --num-warmups 128 ``` CI runs this configuration for three repetitions; the before/after comparison below reports one run for each revision. ## Test Result Before, using `TRITON_ATTN`: ``` ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Successful requests: 512 Failed requests: 0 Maximum request concurrency: 128 Benchmark duration (s): 958.75 Total input tokens: 4194304 Total generated tokens: 524288 Request throughput (req/s): 0.53 Output token throughput (tok/s): 546.84 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 1512.00 Peak concurrent requests: 134.00 Total token throughput (tok/s): 4921.59 ---------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 31806.59 Median TTFT (ms): 16375.95 P99 TTFT (ms): 140616.45 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------ Mean TPOT (ms): 195.10 Median TPOT (ms): 209.39 P99 TPOT (ms): 219.68 ---------------Inter-token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 195.10 Median ITL (ms): 85.68 P99 ITL (ms): 1172.52 ================================================== ``` After, using `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN`: ``` ============ Serving Benchmark Result ============ Successful requests: 512 Failed requests: 0 Maximum request concurrency: 128 Benchmark duration (s): 662.32 Total input tokens: 4194304 Total generated tokens: 524288 Request throughput (req/s): 0.77 Output token throughput (tok/s): 791.60 Peak output token throughput (tok/s): 1652.00 Peak concurrent requests: 134.00 Total token throughput (tok/s): 7124.39 ---------------Time to First Token---------------- Mean TTFT (ms): 26563.93 Median TTFT (ms): 14289.54 P99 TTFT (ms): 151069.14 -----Time per Output Token (excl. 1st token)------ Mean TPOT (ms): 129.67 Median TPOT (ms): 139.23 P99 TPOT (ms): 144.40 ---------------Inter-token Latency---------------- Mean ITL (ms): 129.67 Median ITL (ms): 76.59 P99 ITL (ms): 672.11 ================================================== ``` `TRITON_FLASH_ATTN` improves output throughput from 546.84 to 791.60 tok/s (1.45x). `--language-model-only` is not required to reach the FA3/FA4 causal path after this PR. ---

title: [Bugfix][Model] MiMo: keep fused fp8 qkv_proj pairing state across weight-loading calls
body:
## Purpose
`XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL` (and V2.5) produce degenerate output when using `--load-format fastsafetensors` or `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` when testing on Mi355x.  This issue should be platform-agnostic. 

## Root cause

MiMo's fused fp8 `qkv_proj` arrives as two checkpoint tensors (`weight` and `weight_scale_inv`) that must be sharded together, so `MiMoV2Model.load_weights` paired them in a dict and flushed only when both members arrived in the *same* call.

`AutoWeightsLoader._groupby_prefix` (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:260-274`) groups the stream with `itertools.groupby` on the first name component and calls a child's `load_weights` **once per contiguous run of `model.*`**. Any pair that straddles a group boundary therefore never flushes and both parameters are left uninitialised — zeros/NaN for the fp8 weight and `-inf` for its scale:

Instrumented load (`mimo_v2.py`), TP=2:

| loader | `layers.0.self_attn.qkv_proj.weight` | `…weight_scale_inv` |
|---|---|---|
| default | correct | correct |
| `--load-format fastsafetensors` | `sum=0` | `sum=-inf` |
| `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` | `sum=0`/`NaN` | `sum=-inf` |

`eager` fragments heavily because `safetensors.torch.load` returns a Rust `HashMap` (not file order). Nothing errored because weights tracking is disabled for quantized models (`default_loader.py:435-438`), hence gibberish tokens instead of a load failure.

## Fix

MiMo's fused fp8 `qkv_proj` arrives as two separate tensors — the weight and its scale — which have to be sharded together, so the loader holds the first one until the second shows up. That holding area was a local variable, and a local variable only lives for one call of `load_weights`; when the loader runs more than once (fastsafetensors, eager), a pair can be split across two calls, both tensors are dropped, and the attention projections are left empty.

Keep the holding area on the model instead (`mimo_v2.py`, and the same spot in `mimo_v2_mtp.py`), so a pair still completes no matter which call each half arrives in. Nothing in the loader itself is changed, so no other model is affected.

## Test Plan
Start serving with this, change model id to `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` and add `--load-format fastsafetensors` or `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` when testing the different case. 
```
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 \
vllm serve XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --max-model-len auto \
  --generation-config vllm \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}' \
  --tool-call-parser mimo \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice \
  --reasoning-parser mimo
```

Test with lmeval, change model id to `XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5` for the mimo v2.5 test. 
```
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions \
  --model_args model=XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=32,max_retries=10,max_length=32000,timeout=60000 \  
  --gen_kwargs '{"max_tokens":16000,"until":[]}' --batch_size auto \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 25 --apply_chat_template
```

## Test Result

| case | result |
|---|---|
| MiMo V2.6, default loader |  gsm8k @ 25 shots (~0.97)  |
| MiMo V2.6, `--load-format fastsafetensors` | gsm8k @ 25 shots (~0.97) |
| MiMo V2.6, `--safetensors-load-strategy eager` | gsm8k @ 25 shots (~0.97) |
| MiMo V2.6 + MTP spec-decode, fastsafetensors | gsm8k @ 25 shots (~0.97) |
| MiMo V2.5, fastsafetensors | gsm8k @ 25 shots (~0.97) |

title: Fix: Calculate ITL using exact token delta from usage stats (#27485)
body:
## Purpose
Fixes the Inter-Token Latency (ITL) calculation bug in the `openai-chat` benchmarking backend. Fixes #27485, which the stale bot closed as `not_planned` on 16 June after 90 days of inactivity. The bug is still present on main; numbers below.

Previously, the benchmark assumed each SSE chunk contained exactly one token. When servers batched tokens under load, ITL was incorrectly inflated. This PR passes `continuous_usage_stats: True` and calculates ITL using the exact token count delta provided by the server.

- Ensures TTFT is only recorded once, and only on a chunk that carries a token.
- Calculates correct ITL by dividing the chunk time delta by the exact number of tokens generated in that chunk.

Measuring this also surfaced a second counting error, independent of batching: the role-only opening chunk is currently counted as a token transition, adding one spurious interval per stream.

**Duplicate Check:** I have verified this does not duplicate existing work. PR #42661 attempted a similar fix but has been inactive, failed CI, and did not correctly handle the delta logic across all fallback scenarios. This implementation is fresh and comprehensively tested.

*Note: This PR was developed with AI assistance.*

## Behaviour notes

Rebased onto current main. #54708 and #55508 are preserved; their 18 tests in `test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py` are untouched and green.

Two visible changes:

1. **TTFT moves later for streams opening with a role-only chunk.** Main records TTFT on any chunk with a non-empty `choices`, including `delta: {"role": "assistant"}`. This branch waits for content, reasoning or a tool call.
2. **`latency - ttft == sum(itl)` holds.** A first token-bearing chunk can carry more than one token. Its extra tokens are recorded as zero-length intervals, which keeps the count at `output_tokens - 1` without charging prefill time to inter-token latency. Measured across 300 requests at concurrency 64, on both clients: 300 of 300 satisfy the identity, maximum residual 0.

For servers that do not send `continuous_usage_stats`, timing still comes from chunk arrivals as it does today, apart from the role-only change above.

The same change is applied to `benchmarks/backend_request_func.py`, a second copy of this client with the identical bug. It backs `benchmark_serving_structured_output.py`, which reaches the same function through `--backend openai-chat`. #55508 did the same.

## Test Plan

Unit tests in `tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func.py`:

- `test_openai_chat_itl_uses_continuous_usage_token_deltas`: per-token ITL from the usage delta.
- `test_openai_chat_final_usage_does_not_double_count_fallback_timing`: a trailing usage chunk adds no spurious interval.
- `test_openai_chat_latency_invariant_holds_with_continuous_usage`: pins #55508's `latency - ttft == sum(itl)`.
- `test_openai_chat_usage_with_tokens_satisfies_first_chunk`: a usage chunk reporting `completion_tokens > 0` satisfies #54708's check.
- `test_legacy_openai_chat_itl_uses_continuous_usage_token_deltas` and `test_legacy_openai_chat_final_usage_does_not_double_count_fallback_timing`: the same two behaviours against `benchmarks/backend_request_func.py`.

```bash
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func.py -v
pytest tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py -v   # upstream's, untouched
ruff check vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func.py
ruff format --check vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func.py
```

## Test Result

```text
test_endpoint_request_func.py          8 passed
test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py   18 passed
ruff check                             All checks passed!
ruff format --check                    2 files already formatted

git diff upstream/main --stat -- tests/benchmarks/test_endpoint_request_func_timing.py
(empty)
```

One assertion changed during the rebase. `test_openai_chat_itl_uses_continuous_usage_token_deltas` asserted `latency == 0.8`, the trailing usage chunk's arrival. That predates #55508, which deliberately stopped trailing usage chunks extending latency. It now asserts 0.75.

### End-to-end

`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B` on one RTX 3080. Client: `vllm bench serve --backend openai-chat --num-prompts 300 --random-input-len 256 --random-output-len 256 --max-concurrency 64`. Three runs per condition, alternating, after a discarded warm-up. Only `vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py` changed between runs; same server process throughout.

300 requests of 256 output tokens should give 300 x 255 = 76,500 intervals.

| run | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 76,349 | 76,500 |
| 2 | 76,544 | 76,500 |
| 3 | 74,339 | 76,500 |

This branch is exact in all three runs, 255 per request for all 300 requests. main is wrong in both directions:

- **Over-counts.** 108 of 300 requests recorded 256 intervals. The role-only opening chunk is counted as a token transition.
- **Under-counts.** A batched chunk carrying N tokens yields one interval. In run 3, 256 of 300 requests were affected and 2,161 intervals were lost, down to 235 on the worst request.

Those errors partly cancel, which is why mean and median are not a signal here: within-condition spread on median ITL reached 1.03 ms against a 0.58 ms between-condition difference, so no latency claim is made. The interval count is the result.

Mean TTFT was 271 ms on this branch against 235 ms on main, consistent with the role-only chunk no longer setting TTFT.

That run covers `vllm/benchmarks/lib/endpoint_request_func.py`. The copy in `benchmarks/` was checked by driving `async_request_openai_chat_completions` directly against the same server, 300 requests at concurrency 64, with `len(itl) == output_tokens - 1` asserted per request:

| | intervals | requests passing |
|---|---|---|
| main | 74,900 | 0 of 300 |
| this branch | 76,500 | 300 of 300 |

76,800 output tokens in both; main loses 1,600 intervals.

title: [Spec decode] Support variable-length decode for Kimi-K3 adaptive ver
body: ## Summary Make Kimi-K3's MLA and KDA decode paths capturable as FULL varlen CUDA graphs so they work under adaptive DSpark verification (#47808), which schedules ragged per-request draft budgets and requires device-sourced query lengths. Before this change K3's `FLASHINFER_MLA` reported `UNIFORM_BATCH`/`UNIFORM`, and the decode builders derived per-request query length from a measured/averaged count, so a graph captured on a uniform dummy did not match ragged replay. ## Changes **FlashInfer MLA** (`flashinfer_mla.py`) - Promote `_cudagraph_support` to `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` and `query_len_support` to `QueryLenSupport.VARLEN`. - On the causal spec-decode path, pass `cum_seq_lens_q` + `max_q_len` to `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla` (flashinfer #3238); assert this path runs on trtllm-gen and does not return LSE (mutually exclusive with DCP). - Flatten non-causal and DCP decode rows by mapping each row to its request with `searchsorted` on the device query offsets instead of `repeat_interleave(uniform_len)`. - Carry `query_start_loc_device`, `cum_seq_lens_q`, and `max_query_len` on the decode metadata; set `cum_seq_lens_q` only when `max_query_len > 1`. **MLA common** (`mla_attention.py` + subclass builders) - Thread a promised `max_query_len` through `MLACommonMetadataBuilder._build_decode` (clamped to `reorder_batch_threshold`) and the `flashmla`, `flashattn_mla`, `rocm_aiter_mla`, and `dots3_note` builders. **KDA** (`kda_metadata.py`) - Promote `KimiK3KDAMetadataBuilder` to `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS`. - Route every active decode through the spec path by masking on `is_prefilling` rather than draft count. - Return `True` from `supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch`. **KDA RecoverSSM** (`kda_metadata.py`, opt-in via `--use-replayssm`, off by default) - Make RecoverSSM co-exist with the adaptive path so it can drop the KDA spec-decode SSM state from `num_spec+1` slots to 1 per request (kernels already in #51855): - Restore `self.layer_names` on the builder so RecoverSSM's commit context can resolve the per-layer forward context (the GDN base does not retain it; inert when RecoverSSM is off). - Demote spec rows whose `query_len` exceeds `num_spec+1` out of the RecoverSSM path instead of raising. Adaptive's cost-table profiler probes token counts past the cudagraph limit by even-splitting them over the capped request slots, producing eager dummy rows longer than RecoverSSM's `num_spec+1` verify buffers; real captured/serving decode rows are always `<= num_spec+1`, so they are unaffected. **Mamba-hybrid model state** (`mamba_hybrid.py`) - Prefer the batch's promised `max_query_len`, and classify spec-decode rows off `is_prefilling` rather than `num_scheduled_tokens == draft_count + 1`. **K3 DSpark draft** (`dspark_mla.py`) - Build the confidence head when the config enables it, load its weights (skipped only when the draft did not build one), and expose `compute_confidence`. Related Issue: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/51867 ## Test plan - [x] Updated the MLA backend metadata tests for the new `_build_decode` signature (`test_mla_backends.py`, `test_rocm_aiter_mla_mtp_split.py`). - [x] Adaptive DSpark spec decode on Kimi-K3 (TP8, fp8 KV). - [x] RecoverSSM + adaptive on Kimi-K3: boots and serves through full-graph capture; validated against the base-adaptive checks (accuracy/coherence artifacts were overwritten by later runs and are being regenerated). ## Validation Kimi-K3 (target) + `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` (draft), TP8 on 8×B300, FP8 KV cache, `attention_backend=FLASHINFER_MLA`, `num_speculative_tokens=7`, `enable_adaptive_verification=true`. (Numbers below are RecoverSSM off; it is opt-in.) ### Accuracy — lossless vs. no-spec (GSM8K, in-tree runner, 1319 questions, 5-shot, temperature 0) | max-concurrency | no-spec | adaptive | |---|---|---| | 16 | 0.949 | 0.949 | | 64 | 0.951 | 0.949 | | 128 | 0.948 | 0.948 | Adaptive matches no-spec within run-to-run noise (invalid-response rate ~0.1% in every run), i.e. adaptive verification is lossless at temperature 0. ### Coherence (MTBench, 80 prompts, temperature 1) Adaptive: 80/80 successful requests, 0 failed, ~19.5K generated tokens; no repetition or degeneration in the saved completions. ### Speculative-decoding health (speed_bench, temperature 1, c16) Acceptance rate 28.95%, acceptance length 3.03, per-position acceptance decaying 74.5% (pos 0) → 6.9% (pos 6) — non-zero at every position, confirming the draft + confidence head + varlen verification path is exercised end to end. ### RecoverSSM (opt-in) health Adaptive + RecoverSSM serves through full-graph capture with healthy acceptance length (2.4–2.9 across c1–c256), confirming the RecoverSSM verify/commit path is exercised end to end; matches base-adaptive accuracy/coherence. ## Benchmarking Pareto sweep of the varlen decode path: 16 configurations × 9 concurrency levels = 144 serving runs. Configurations are fixed draft length K=1..7 plus adaptive, each with and without RecoverSSM. Kimi-K3 (target) + `Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark` (draft), TP8 on 8×B300, FP8 KV cache, `attention_backend=FLASHINFER_MLA`, `draft_sample_method=probabilistic`, `num_speculative_tokens=7` for adaptive. `speed_bench` qualitative, `--speed-bench-output-len 2048`, `--max-model-len 16384`, prompt count scaled with concurrency. Axes: per-user token rate (`1000 / median TPOT`) vs aggregate output throughput. Overlaying both families lets a non-RecoverSSM point appear to overtake a RecoverSSM one it never competes with, so each family is also plotted with its own frontier. ### RecoverSSM, adaptive off vs on | c | off | on | gain | |---|---|---|---| | 64 | 2248.6 | 2349.4 | +4.5% | | 128 | 2241.5 | 4454.7 | +98.7% | | 256 | 2222.9 | 4887.9 | +119.9% |

title: [ROCm][CI] Expand single-GPU coverage on MI355 DPX
body:
Move single-GPU CI coverage to MI355 DPX, including all main-CI `mi355_1` suites except the suite that failed its first DPX run in [build 90270](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90270/table). Include focused fixes for the observed kernel-reference and cold-cache loading failures. Remove the DPX-specific skips, xfails, tolerance increases, and unused `is_dpx()` / `VLLM_DPX_CI` plumbing originally introduced by this PR.

| Source queue | Main-CI suites moved | Main-CI shards moved |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `mi300_1` | 30/51 (58.8%) | 40/79 (50.6%) |
| `mi355_1` | 44/46 (95.7%) | 62/69 (89.9%) |

- Block INT8 MoE's reference now truncates activation quantization like the production C++ and Triton implementations. Preserve round-to-nearest for existing whole-token reference callers and add exact fractional-value regression cases.
- MXFP4 skinny GEMM's independent FP32 reference is rounded to the declared BF16 output type before comparison. Correct BF16 rounding reproduces both old DPX failure counts exactly; tolerances and pass-rate thresholds are unchanged.
- Reduce one large-K skinny-GEMM test's M from 128 to 64 so the raw operation needs 96 CUs rather than 192 on a 128-CU DPX device. It retains the same 24 K-shards and multi-pass LDS readback regression coverage.
- Discover nonstandard root-level safetensors filenames when the Hub's standard metadata API rejects them, reading headers without downloading weights. This fixes TinyLlama GPTQ cold-cache initialization, which otherwise constructs unquantized layers before encountering checkpoint `qweight` tensors. Preserve offline/gated cache fallback.

- Guard native DPX jobs with a nonblocking lock per render device in the shared host-local cache. A second participating job fails before workspace preparation or test execution; CPU-only and non-DPX jobs bypass the guard. This protects cooperating runners while the cluster allocation issue observed in [AMD-CI build 13342](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13342/list) is investigated.
- Use AMD-SMI diagnostic options supported in Linux guests, preserving the existing probe timeouts and failure handling.

Guard validation: 23 local process cases passed, including an eight-process race admitting exactly one workload, device aliases, independent devices, queue bypasses, and lock retention through teardown. A separate check verified inherited lock lifetime after wrapper termination. Six real AMD-SMI probes, guest-parser checks, shell syntax, and pre-commit passed. Lock tests use synthetic device nodes; live cross-pod mount sharing remains unverified.

Investigation, implementation, validation, and this description were AI-assisted.

title: [Performance][Hardware][RISC-V] Use a 16-column RVV tile for narrow-M attention GEMMs
body:
## Purpose

The RISC-V RVV CPU attention kernel currently drives every output tile with an
8-column (`LMUL_256`) B-row load and one accumulator per row. For the narrow-M
shapes that dominate decode and GQA (`m_size <= 4`), that shape has too little
independent work to keep the core busy and re-issues the same scalar A loads twice
as often as necessary.

This PR adds a 16-column micro kernel that keeps **two independent 8-lane (m2)
accumulator chains per row** and calls it from the macro kernel when
`N % 16 == 0 && mb <= 4`. `M >= 8` (prefill) keeps the existing Mx8 tile.

Single file, no API change, no new symbol outside `csrc/cpu/cpu_attn_rvv.hpp`:

```text
 csrc/cpu/cpu_attn_rvv.hpp | 155 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++-
 1 file changed, 154 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

### Motivation

`gemm_macro_rvv_fma_Mx8_Ku4` is used by both attention phases via `TileGemmRVV`
(`BLOCK_SIZE_ALIGNMENT = HEAD_SIZE_ALIGNMENT = 32`), so `N` is a compile-time 32
and `M` is `q_head_num` for the iteration:

- decode / GQA: `M` is small (typically 1-4), `K` is `head_dim` (QK) or the
  token count in the block (PV);
- prefill: `M` is 8-16.

With `mb <= 4` the existing kernel issues, per k step, one 8-column B load and
then only `mb` scalar-broadcast `vfmacc.vf`. The scalar A loads (`flw`) are
therefore re-issued once per 8 output columns even though the same `a[i][k]`
value feeds the whole 16-column row width that the block already holds, and the
per-row dependency chain is a single accumulator.

### What changed

1. **New micro kernel** `gemm_micro_rvv_fma_Mx16_Ku4<M, kv_cache_t>`
   (`M` in `[1,4]`, `K` unrolled by 4 plus a tail loop). Each row keeps two
   `fixed_fp32x8_t` accumulators, `accl<i>` for output columns `[0,8)` and
   `acch<i>` for `[8,16)`. Register budget at VLEN=128: `4 * m2` accumulators
   (16 regs) + 2 `m2` B rows (4 regs) = 20 of 32.
2. **Macro kernel dispatch**: when `N % 16 == 0` and `mb <= 4`, step `n` by 16
   and call the new kernel; otherwise fall through to the unchanged 8-column
   path. `mb == 8` (prefill) still uses `gemm_micro_rvv_fma_Mx8_Ku4`.
3. Corrected the now-stale section comment describing the N step.

Nothing else changes: paged KV layout, stride contract, mask / softmax / alibi /
softcap semantics, OpenMP structure, and the QK/PV public API are untouched.

### Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched open issues and PRs for RISC-V RVV attention work before opening this:
`gh pr list --state open --search "rvv in:title,body"` returns only the
capability-detection and transcendentals/INT4-GEMM changes by `HakureiPOI` and
`velonica0` (#51132, #52933, #52858, #48487, #53069, #52934). None of them touch
`gemm_macro_rvv_fma_Mx8_Ku4` or the attention tile shape; this change is
confined to the tile geometry of the attention GEMM and is orthogonal to all of them.

## Why two 8-lane chains, and not one wider one

The obvious alternative — one 16-element (`LMUL_512`) accumulator per row and a
single 16-element B load — was implemented and measured, and is **clearly
worse**. Three variants were compared on the target machine (details under
"Test Result"):

| variant | per-row accumulators | B-row load | speedup at M=1, K=256 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mx8 baseline | 1 x m2 | 1 x m2 (8 cols) | 1.00x |
| **this PR** | **2 x m2** | **2 x m2** | **1.49-1.56x** |
| LMUL_512 variant | 1 x m4 | 1 x m4 (16 cols) | 1.11-1.13x |
| LMUL_512 load only | 2 x m2 | 1 x m4 (+ `vget` split) | 1.10-1.13x |

Widening a vector register does not create an independent dependency chain — it
makes one chain longer over more lanes. What helps here is having two independent
accumulator chains per row, which the core can overlap. Note that the register
accounting is identical for both designs (20 of 32), so the wider tile buys no
register headroom either.

`M >= 8` is deliberately left on the Mx8 tile: `4` rows x `m4` would need 32
accumulator registers, and prefill shapes are not the bottleneck.

The kernel comment in the patch states this mechanism explicitly, so the code and the
measured result agree; an earlier draft of the rationale attributed the gain to the
wider B access, which the measurements above do not support.

## Test Plan

**Bit-identical to the existing kernel.** For a fixed output element, `k` still
ascends in steps of one and every step is a single `vfmacc.vf` into the same
element, so the FP32 accumulation order is unchanged; the 16-column tile only
changes which accumulators live side by side. The claim was checked empirically
rather than argued:

- the kernel from this patch was compiled against the real
  `csrc/cpu/cpu_types_riscv_defs.hpp` (`RVVI` / `LMUL_*`) at the target VLEN,
  together with the unmodified `gemm_micro_rvv_fma_Mx8_Ku4`;
- sweep `M in {1,2,3,4,8,16} x N in {8,16,24,32,64} x K in
  {1,3,4,7,31,64,128,255,256} x accumulate in {0,1}` = 540 cases;
- result: **540/540 byte-identical** (`memcmp` of the full output tile) versus
  the Mx8 kernel, and within `1e-4` relative of a scalar reference.

The code inside this patch is the code that was compiled for that test (the kernel
body is textually identical apart from line wrapping and comments).

**Existing tests already exercise the new path.** In
`tests/kernels/attention/test_cpu_attn.py`,
`test_varlen_with_paged_kv_normal_rvv` parametrizes `num_heads` over `(4, 4)`,
`(8, 2)`, `(9, 3)` and `SEQ_LENS` contains `q_len = 1` decode batches, so both
the narrow-M (`mb <= 4`, new tile) and the wide-M (`mb == 8`, unchanged tile)
dispatch are covered, across `HEAD_SIZES = [96, 128, 512]` and
`block_size in {96, 128}`.

## Test Result

**Correctness — 540/540 byte-identical, 0 differences.**

```text
=== sweep-A: 540 shape cases, 88128 elements ===
sweep-A bit-exact: 0 diffs
```

Reproduced identically at **VLEN=128 and VLEN=256**, with an extended sweep
(`M in {1..9,12,16,17} x N in {8,16,24,32,64} x K in {1,3,4,7,31,64,96,128,255,256,512}`
= 1320 further cases) also at 0 diffs. Register-spill check on the compiled
kernel (`-S`): the Mx16 tile emits `2 x M` vector stores, all of them to `C`,
and **no** vector store or load through the stack pointer, for `M in {1,2,4}`.

**Performance.** Measured on the target SoC, single core pinned, 400 warmup
iterations, 25 samples per round, rotating variant order, median reported, three
independent processes. Kernel-level, `N = 32`, `-O3`, GCC 15.1, VLEN=128:

| shape | speedup vs Mx8 (3 runs) |
| --- | --- |
| M=1 K=256 | 1.563 / 1.543 / 1.485 |
| M=2 K=256 | 1.423 / 1.425 / 1.340 |
| M=1 K=128 | 1.199 / 1.258 / 1.474 |
| M=2 K=128 | 1.134 / 1.290 / 1.369 |

## AI assistance disclosure

AI assistance was used to prepare this change, via the **Yuansheng** tool
(`yuansheng@isrc.iscas.ac.cn`), credited in the commit as a `Co-authored-by:`
trailer. The human submitter has reviewed every changed line, understands the
implementation end-to-end, and is accountable for it in review.

---

title: [Security] Widen int32 pointer arithmetic to int64 in CUDA kernels
body:
## Summary

- Widen 32-bit integer pointer offset arithmetic to 64-bit in CUDA kernels to prevent cross-user data disclosure when `num_tokens * stride` overflows `2^32`
- Applies the established fix pattern from `451227cb3f` (activation_kernels.cu): cast `blockIdx.x` to `int64_t` before multiplying by stride/dimension
- Covers LayerNorm, LayerNorm-quant (FP8), MoE routing, and AllSpark W8A16 GEMM kernels

## Affected kernels

| Kernel | File | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| `rms_norm_kernel` | `layernorm_kernels.cu` | High -- confirmed exploitable with PoC |
| `rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High -- FP8 quantized path |
| `fused_add_rms_norm_static_fp8_quant_kernel` (both specializations) | `layernorm_quant_kernels.cu` | High |
| `moeSoftmax` / `moeSigmoid` / `moeTopK` | `topk_softmax_kernels.cu` | Moderate |
| AllSpark W8A16 GmemTile / ComputeTile | `allspark_qgemm_w8a16.cu` | Low (defense in depth) |

## Root cause

CUDA built-in `blockIdx.x` is `unsigned int` (32-bit). When multiplied by a 32-bit `hidden_size` or stride, the product wraps at 2^32, causing a kernel block to read/write another user's hidden state within the same batch. With `hidden_size = 8192`, the overflow triggers at ~524,288 tokens.

## Fix pattern

```cpp
// Before (32-bit overflow)
scalar_t* out_row = out + blockIdx.x * hidden_size;

// After (64-bit safe)
const int64_t token_idx = blockIdx.x;
scalar_t* out_row = out + token_idx * hidden_size;
```

For host-side code, `int input_stride` is widened to `int64_t input_stride` to match the kernel parameter change.

- [x] Pre-commit hooks pass (clang-format, typos, etc.)
- [ ] Existing LayerNorm kernel tests pass
- [ ] Existing MoE kernel tests pass
- [ ] CI build succeeds on CUDA targets

title: [MRV2] Validate MRV2 entrypoint logits processors
body:
## Purpose

MRV2 skipped frontend validation for auto-discovered logits processors, allowing invalid parameters to reach workers. Discover and validate these plugins at admission while preserving pooling's intentional skip.

## Reproducer

A temporary reproducer registers an entry-point-only processor whose `validate_params()` rejects the request, constructs the normal frontend validator, and separately verifies the pooling skip.

```python
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest.mock import patch

from vllm.exceptions import VLLMValidationError
from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams
from vllm.v1.engine.input_processor import InputProcessor
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor import loader
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.interface import (
    LogitsProcessor,
)


class RejectingPlugin(LogitsProcessor):
    validation_calls = 0

    @classmethod
    def validate_params(cls, sampling_params):
        cls.validation_calls += 1
        raise ValueError("plugin rejected request")

    def apply(self, logits, ctx):
        return logits


class EntryPoint:
    name = "rejecting"
    value = "reproducer:RejectingPlugin"

    def load(self):
        return RejectingPlugin

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name


def build_validator(runner_type):
    processor = SimpleNamespace(
        model_config=SimpleNamespace(
            logits_processors=None,
            runner_type=runner_type,
        ),
        vllm_config=SimpleNamespace(use_v2_model_runner=True),
    )
    return InputProcessor._build_logits_processors_params_validator(processor)


loader._cached_load_v2_logitsprocs.cache_clear()
with patch.object(loader, "entry_points", return_value=[EntryPoint()]) as discover:
    validator = build_validator("generate")

    try:
        validator(SamplingParams())
    except VLLMValidationError as exc:
        generation_outcome = f"rejected: {exc}"
    else:
        generation_outcome = "accepted invalid request"

    print(f"generation_discovery_calls={discover.call_count}")
    print(
        f"generation_validation_calls="
        f"{RejectingPlugin.validation_calls}"
    )
    print(f"generation_outcome={generation_outcome}")


# Verify that pooling models retain their intentional plugin skip.
loader._cached_load_v2_logitsprocs.cache_clear()
with patch.object(
    loader,
    "entry_points",
    side_effect=AssertionError("pooling unexpectedly loaded plugins"),
) as discover:
    validator = build_validator("pooling")
    validator(SamplingParams())

    print(f"pooling_discovery_calls={discover.call_count}")
    print("pooling_outcome=plugin skipped")
```

### Output on main

```text
generation_discovery_calls=0
generation_validation_calls=0
generation_outcome=accepted invalid request
pooling_discovery_calls=0
pooling_outcome=plugin skipped
```

### Output on this branch

```text
generation_discovery_calls=1
generation_validation_calls=1
generation_outcome=rejected: plugin rejected request
pooling_discovery_calls=0
pooling_outcome=plugin skipped
```

## Test Plan

```text
.venv/bin/python /tmp/repro_mrv2_plugin_validation_full.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_logits_processor_loader.py tests/v1/engine/test_input_processor_trace_replay.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_logits_processors.py -q --tb=short
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/sample/logits_processor/loader.py
```

Results:

- deterministic admission reproducer: invalid request accepted on main and rejected on branch
- targeted CPU/H100 suite: 20 passed

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) assisted with root-cause analysis, the patch, and test execution.

title: [Kernel] Mamba2: Pin SSD Triton configs under batch-invariant mode
body:
## Purpose

Under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` the Mamba2 SSD kernels (`_bmm_chunk_fwd_kernel`, `_chunk_cumsum_fwd_kernel`, `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel`, `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel`, `_state_passing_fwd_kernel`) still pick their tile configuration by autotuning. The autotune keys exclude batch and sequence length, so one process is consistent with itself, but the choice is made by timing and can differ between processes, for example a trainer rescoring a rollout and the inference engine, or two engine restarts. The tile changes the reduction order and therefore the bits: on GB200 with chunk size 64 and 8 heads, `BLOCK_SIZE_H` 2 versus 8 or 64 in the chunk cumsum gives different fp32 prefix sums and 59 to 351 of about one million output elements differ.

This PR pins each of the five kernels to one of its existing candidates under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. The pin is applied to the autotuner right after each kernel definition, so the candidate lists are not touched and default mode autotunes exactly as before. #55627 and #55905 build on this: they compare decode bits against prefill bits from these kernels, so the tile has to be fixed rather than timed.

Not a duplicate: #54993 and #55627 change how Mamba2 prefill and decode run, not the kernels' autotune selection. #48213 adds CPU-tuned candidate lists for the Triton CPU backend; since this PR leaves the lists alone, the two do not overlap.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_batch_invariance.py
VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba2_ssd_batch_invariance.py tests/kernels/mamba/test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py
```

The new file checks the pin helper, that each pinned tile is one of the kernel's candidates and that under `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1` each kernel exposes exactly that one configuration, and that the rows of a prefix do not depend on the tokens that follow.

## Test Result

GB200, Triton 3.7.1. Default mode: 7 passed. With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: 101 passed, the new tests plus the existing SSD correctness suite on the pinned tiles. Default-mode outputs are unchanged by construction (same candidate lists, keys and kernels), so no model evaluation is attached; the batch-invariant mode is exercised end to end by #55627 and #55905. pre-commit passes on the changed files.

## AI assistance

AI tools assisted with the implementation, tests and documentation. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

title: [XPU] Preserve non-contiguous strides when pinning CPU tensors for UVA view
body:
## Purpose

When obtaining an XPU accelerator view from an unpinned CPU tensor, the previous implementation invoked `cpu_tensor.contiguous()` before pinning the memory. This operation converted non‑contiguous strided views (e.g., the transposed weight‑scale tensor `scale_kn.t()`) into contiguous ones, discarding their original stride patterns. Later, applying `.t()` on these contiguous copies produced non‑contiguous tensors again, which triggered extra implicit `.contiguous()` copies during GEMM execution and degraded performance.

## Changes

- Modify the XPU‑specific `get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor` to allocate pinned memory via `torch.empty_strided` using the original tensor's size and stride, instead of first making the tensor contiguous.
- Add a new test `test_non_contiguous_strided_view` under `tests/kernels/core/test_uva.py` to validate both pinned and unpinned non‑contiguous strided views.

title: [Kernel] Fuse strided GDN RMSNorm gating on SM103
body:
## Summary

Fuse Qwen GDN RMSNorm and strided SiLU gating into one Triton kernel on NVIDIA SM103.

The fast path:

- consumes the three-dimensional projected `z` view directly instead of reshaping/materializing it;
- performs the FP32 RMS reduction, weight scaling, and SiLU gate in one launch;
- supports hidden dimensions 64, 96, 128, 192, and 256 with dimension/row-count-specific launch configurations;
- keeps the existing compiled/native path as the fallback for unsupported devices, dtypes, layouts, dimensions, group norms, gate order, and activations.

The GDN scan and output projection GEMM are unchanged.

## Why this is not duplicate work

I repeated open-PR searches for `RMSNormGated GDN` and `strided RMSNorm gated` before submission.

- #47842 removes an output reshape/copy on ROCm. This PR targets NVIDIA SM103 and optimizes the RMS reduction plus strided SiLU gate itself. It leaves ROCm on the current path.
- #36469 unifies two RMSNormGated module classes but does not add this kernel.
- #38798 ports RMSNormGated into vLLM IR but does not optimize projected strided GDN gates.
- #40921 fixes Dynamo tracing in the existing input guard.
- #46998 is already merged and forms part of the current-main compiled baseline used below.

No open PR was found that implements an SM103 strided RMSNormGated kernel.

## Dispatch and fallback

The optimized path requires:

- NVIDIA compute capability 10.3;
- BF16 contiguous CUDA `x` and BF16 `z`/weight on the same CUDA device;
- three-dimensional `x` and shape-matched `z` with contiguous hidden dimension;
- hidden size in `{64, 96, 128, 192, 256}`;
- no group norm, norm-before-gate, and SiLU/Swish activation.

Dimensions 192 and 256 use the fast path only up to 131,072 rows, where the measured speedup remains at least 18%. Larger configurations retain the compiled native path. Every failed guard follows the existing implementation.

## Correctness

The test matrix covers:

- hidden sizes 64, 96, 128, 192, and 256;
- token counts 1, 17, and 257;
- non-compact projected `z` strides;
- FP32 reference math and BF16 output;
- NaN/Inf checks;
- unsupported hidden sizes, non-CUDA inputs, and large-row fallback;
- FakeTensor output layout;
- Qwen output-projection routing;
- the existing FLA layernorm and Qwen GDN integration suites.

Focused result on B300/SM103:

```text
1580 passed, 14 warnings in 409.72s
```

Across the benchmark matrix, relative L2 error versus the compiled native implementation is `5.05e-6` to `6.98e-6`. The production D=128 case is `5.82e-6` with maximum absolute difference `0.015625`.

## Operator performance

Hardware: NVIDIA B300, compute capability 10.3. Source baseline: official main `5b29c958c`. Runtime: Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 13.2 environment.

Command:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python \
  benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_gdn_rmsnorm.py --production-shape
```

| Shape | Compiled native | Existing CUDA | PR | Speedup vs fastest baseline |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| D64, T2048, H64 | 40.67 us | 44.16 us | 15.36 us | 2.65x |
| D96, T2048, H64 | 48.64 us | 54.37 us | 23.52 us | 2.07x |
| D128, T2048, H64 | 48.96 us | 64.61 us | 25.57 us | 1.91x |

D192/D256 at 262,144 rows measured only 1.08x, so the runtime guard intentionally falls back above 131,072 rows.

## Full-model trace

Model: Qwen3.5-122B-A10B NVFP4 compatibility checkpoint, TP1, BF16 activations, FlashInfer GDN backend, VLLM_CUTLASS MoE backend, 8K prefill + one output token.

| Metric | Current main | PR | Delta |
|---|---:|---:|---:|

| GDN norm/gate GPU time | 3.366 ms | 2.501 ms | -0.865 ms (-25.7%) |
| Total GPU busy | 187.674 ms | 185.632 ms | -2.042 ms |

Current main emits 24 reduction kernels plus 36 pointwise/gate kernels. The PR emits one `_fused_gdn_rmsnorm_gated_kernel` per GDN layer.

NCU on the production D=128 specialization reports:

duration:             68.640 us
DRAM throughput:      70.87%
