title: [DSv4.1] Integrate Mega-Gate from DeepGEMM
body:
## Summary

Integrate DeepGEMM Mega-Gate into the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 DeepGEMM MegaMoE path, fusing the gate GEMM and expert selection. Prepare routing metadata once per model forward and reuse it across layers. Preserve hash routing for V4, image routing bias for V4.1, draft-layer expert counts, MTP warmup, and decoder auxiliary-state capture.

Two integration fixes are included:

- Let CMake FetchContent update an existing DeepGEMM checkout when its pinned revision changes. Previously, finding `csrc/python_api.cpp` skipped the update entirely and could rebuild 2.6.1 without `bf16_mega_gate` despite the new pin.
- ~~Clear padded hidden-state rows in place before Mega-Gate. NaN padding can trigger the kernel's finite-score assertion, later surfacing as a CUDA launch failure or NCCL error. `masked_fill_` avoids allocating a separate hidden-state tensor; valid rows are unchanged. Regression cases cover NaN padding for both main/draft and text/image routing.~~ Removed, fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/11

Update (17 Sep 2026)
- Since Mega-Gate underperforms for M<=16 (as LL-GEMM is very efficient), we only dispatch Mega-Gate for M>16

## Accuracy: full GSM8K

The final in-place implementation was evaluated locally through Vigil on **4× GB200**, using real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` weights, the current repository checkout, CUDA 13.1, and PyTorch 2.13.0. No engine overrides beyond TP4, EP, and the MegaMoE backend were supplied; CUDA Graphs remained enabled.

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Questions | 1319 |
| Correct | **1194** |
| Accuracy | **90.5231%** |
| Invalid responses | **0** |
| API failures | **0** |
| Worker errors | **0** |
| Evaluation time | 161.79 s |


## Kernel benchmark: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Gate

Measured on a **single NVIDIA GB300 (SM103)** with BF16 inputs `[M, 5120]`, BF16 gate weights `[384, 5120]`, **top-k=6**, `sqrtsoftplus`, normalization, and routed scaling factor **1.5**. **M is the number of token rows processed on one GPU**, not serving request concurrency.

The baseline is `GateLinear + fused_topk_bias`, using its normal shape-dependent dispatch. Mega-Gate fuses the gate GEMM and expert selection. The updated DeepGEMM pin allows non-finite padding scores, eliminating the separate hidden-state padding clear; existing input staging discards padded routes.

**Mega-Gate achieves 1.18–1.31× routing speedup for M ≥ 32, with no meaningful speedup for M ≤ 16.** Speedup is baseline latency divided by Mega-Gate latency.

| Tokens M | GateLinear + top-k (μs) | Mega-Gate (μs) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.640 | 8.096 | 0.820× |
| 2 | 6.848 | 8.032 | 0.853× |
| 4 | 6.752 | 8.032 | 0.841× |
| 8 | 8.064 | 8.224 | 0.981× |
| 16 | 8.256 | 8.256 | 1.000× |
| 32 | 10.112 | 8.304 | 1.218× |
| 64 | 10.353 | 8.448 | 1.225× |
| 128 | 11.200 | 8.896 | 1.259× |
| 256 | 11.488 | 9.696 | 1.185× |
| 512 | 13.520 | 10.720 | 1.261× |
| 1024 | 16.000 | 12.448 | 1.285× |
| 2048 | 18.913 | 15.872 | 1.192× |
| 4096 | 27.729 | 22.944 | 1.209× |
| 8192 | 46.752 | 35.745 | 1.308× |

**Method:** FlashInfer CUPTI timing of CUDA-graph replays with cold L2, 25 warmups, three rounds with alternating implementation order, and 100 samples per round. Values are medians of the round medians. Allocation, compilation, graph capture, input generation, routing metadata preparation, expert input staging, expert execution, and communication are outside the timed region. These measurements do not establish an E2E serving speedup.

**Correctness:** Expert IDs matched exactly at every batch size; routing weights matched with `rtol=1e-3, atol=1e-4`. Synthetic inputs and separated correction biases avoid ambiguous top-k boundaries. An additional 48 CUDA-graph replay cases passed with NaN/Inf padding across text, image, and hash/image routing.

**Versions:** vLLM `ef50fde183`, DeepGEMM `40d109bf`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA toolkit `13.1`, FlashInfer `0.6.18`, and CUPTI Python `13.0.1`.

## Related work and AI assistance

This updates the existing Mega-Gate PR rather than opening another implementation. Open-PR searches for `56266 in:body` and `Mega-Gate` were checked before reopening. Dependency/API changes overlap intentionally with #56876; that PR supplies the dependency update, while this PR adds the Mega-Gate routing integration. The upstream Mega-Gate implementation is tracked in https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/432.

OpenAI Codex assisted with the port, dependency alignment, conflict resolution, build-cache and padding fixes, compilation, debugging, and validation. Dependency/API changes adapted from #56876 are attributed in the commit history.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Replace torch.topk in DSA candidate block selection
body:
## Summary

`select_candidate_blocks` picks the top-k blocks per row with `torch.topk`, which runs a multi-pass radix select (`computeBlockDigitCounts`, `computeBlockwiseWithinKCounts`, `gatherTopK`). That does two things this caller does not need:

- **It orders the results.** The only consumer is `_candidate_flags_kernel`, which does `flags[block] = 1`. Nothing downstream reads the ranking or the scores — only the *set* of selected block ids matters.
- **It scans the whole padded workspace.** The logits workspace is padded to `max_model_len`, so `nblocks` is `max_model_len / block_size` no matter how short the context is. Past a row's end every block scores `-inf` and can never win a slot, but `torch.topk` has no way to express a per-row extent, so it reads all of it.

This PR replaces that select on ROCm with a Triton kernel:

- Each score and its index are packed into one order-preserving `int64` key, so `tl.topk` returns both at once and the separate `_store_candidates_kernel` pass disappears. The float bits are sign-transformed so IEEE order becomes unsigned order, and the index rides inverted in the low bits so ties resolve to the smaller index, matching `torch.topk`.
- Each row is bounded by its own `end`, which is the part `torch.topk` cannot do. At 4K context in a 256K workspace this skips ~98% of the columns.
- Decode rows are `batch * next_n`, only 1–640, which is too few to fill the GPU one program per row. Rows are split across programs and merged, with the split size computed **on device** from each row's live extent — a host-side bound would need a sync, and sizing from the padded width instead measured 6.3x → 2.0x at low concurrency.

**The CUDA path is unchanged**; the new kernel is behind `current_platform.is_rocm()`.

## Not a duplicate

Checked open PRs touching this area:

- **#57858** is the only other open PR touching `candidate_blocks.py`, but it optimizes **prefill consumer-layer scoring** (`candidate_mqa_logits`, scoring only candidate columns). The producer-side block select this PR rewrites is untouched there. The two are complementary. Note #57858 also flips `_store_candidates_kernel`'s NaN handling (`!=` → `>`); the ROCm path here bypasses that kernel entirely, so the behaviors do not collide.
- **#48726** (LiteTopk) is the indexer's *token* top-k, a different kernel and stage.
- **#50470**, **#46172**, **#56944** touch `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py` only (AITER dispatch, indexer optimization, prefill row sharding), not block candidate selection.

No open PR optimizes `select_candidate_blocks`.

## Correctness

The new path must select the same block *set* as the existing path. Verified against the unchanged path across 27 configurations — contexts 512 to 262144, rows 1 to 640, ragged per-row ends, non-zero `row_ks` starts, `row_repeat` decode grouping, `topk_blocks > nblocks`, and NaN scores:

```
27 cases, 0 mismatches
```

Two cases this caught during development, both now handled:

- `torch.topk` ranks NaN *highest*, and `_block_scores_kernel` can emit NaN during warmup, so keys force NaN above `+inf`.
- When `nblocks < topk_blocks` the internal `K_PAD` shrinks below the output width, leaving tail columns unwritten; they are now `-1` filled.

## Tests

```
$ pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_candidate_mask.py -q
9 passed, 14 warnings in 4.23s

$ pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py
exit=0 (no failures)
```

## Kernel performance (MI355X)

Full `select_candidate_blocks`, CUDA-graph timed, swept over the decode shape space: concurrency 1–128 x spec-decode depth 1–5, `max_model_len=262144`, `block_size=8`, `k=64`. All 120 points are faster.

| context | median | range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | 4.16x | 3.97–5.08x |
| 16384 | 3.99x | 3.27–4.70x |
| 65536 | 2.94x | 1.64–3.15x |

Representative points (microseconds):

| context | conc | next_n | rows | before | after | speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4096 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 47.55 | 11.20 | 4.24x |
| 4096 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 58.00 | 13.96 | 4.16x |
| 4096 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 293.54 | 67.86 | 4.33x |
| 16384 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 59.19 | 14.31 | 4.14x |
| 16384 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 299.65 | 91.67 | 3.27x |
| 65536 | 32 | 1 | 32 | 60.31 | 19.30 | 3.13x |
| 65536 | 128 | 5 | 640 | 330.51 | 185.83 | 1.78x |

These shapes are TP-independent: the DSA indexer is replicated across ranks (`index_n_heads` is not divided by `tp_size`, unlike the main attention heads), so TP2 and TP4 run identical selections and one sweep covers both.

## Notes

The kernel is still well above the bandwidth roofline (~45x at the largest shapes, more at small ones where it is latency-bound on two launches), so there is headroom left. `TILE=512` is a compromise: 1024 would take 65536-context from 2.36x to 2.79x but drop 4096-context from 23.8x to 14.4x. A context-aware tile choice could get both.

Benchmarks used uniform context per batch; heavily ragged batches are bounded by their longest row.

## End-to-end serving

Measured on MI355X TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, dspark MTP (5 speculative tokens, acceptance pinned at 3.51 so acceptance variance cannot contribute). Both arms are the **same build** differing only by an env toggle on the selection path, run concurrently on separate 4-GPU sets, after a warmup pass over every shape so Triton JIT and graph capture are paid before measurement.

**There is no measurable end-to-end difference, and none should be expected.** Output throughput, ISL 4096 / OSL 128:

| concurrency | baseline tok/s | this PR tok/s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 259.4 | 257.1 |
| 8 | 1287.7 | 1282.4 |
| 32 | 1068.9 | 1070.3 |
| 128 | 1253.8 | 1254.8 |

Repeating a single configuration three times shows run-to-run spread of 1112–1191 tok/s on baseline and 1142–1166 on this branch, with the sign of the difference flipping between repeats. The noise floor is several percent, while the expected effect is about 0.2%: the selection saves roughly 45 us per step against a 14.6 ms inter-token latency. The kernel win is real but it is a sub-1% slice of step time, so it cannot show up above noise in serving throughput.

Median ITL, the most stable metric here, is unchanged (14.59-14.64 ms baseline vs 14.61-14.73 ms this branch).

This PR should therefore be read as removing a hotspot that is prominent in kernel traces and cutting its cost 2-5x, not as an end-to-end throughput win.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change.

title: [Mypy] Fix mypy typing for Zamba2 models
body:
## Purpose

**Depends on W-model PR [#58254](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58254), which builds on V-model PR [#58251](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58251). Merge order: Q → U → V → W → Z.** This branch starts at W's `cb71508394`. Its diff against upstream `main` includes the pending dependencies; after those merge, rebasing onto `main` will leave only the Z-specific changes.

Continue the incremental mypy rollout tracked by [#26533](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26533) by removing `r"vllm/model_executor/models/[zZ]"` from the mypy exclusions and fixing typing in `zamba2.py`, the only selected file.

The Z-specific changes touch two files. Zamba2's LoRA output projection is constructed within each dimension-type branch so the merged projection receives `list[int]` and the ordinary projection receives `int`. The MLP's `num_hybrid_layers` annotation is corrected from `dict[int, int]` to `int`, matching its callers and use in `range`.

The same projection classes receive the same constructor arguments, and model computations are unchanged. No casts or typing suppressions are added.

## Reproducer

On the base revision `cb71508394` (the W-model branch), first remove `r"vllm/model_executor/models/[zZ]"` from `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, then run:

```bash
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 \

```

Base (`cb71508394`):

With the Z typing fixes:

Runtime checks used the existing Python 3.12 environment and imported the Z branch's source files:

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu

# 1 passed.
```

Total: **3 distinct tests passed**, covering Zamba2 registry import, its declared ReplaySSM support, and the model-architecture configuration for `Zyphra/Zamba2-7B-instruct`.

Full model inference, GPU validation, and model-quality evaluations were not run because the NVIDIA driver is unavailable; the checkout also lacks the compiled `vllm._C` extension. The hybrid-model generation suite was inspected but not run. These results establish registry and configuration coverage, not numerical model-output validation.

title: [ROCm] Enable Hisparse on ROCm : Sparse MLA Hot-Buffering
body:
# [ROCm] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA hot-buffering on gfx950

## Purpose

Enables HiSparse (#53781) on AMD ROCm, verified on gfx950 (MI350X, CDNA4).

HiSparse keeps the bulk of the sparse-MLA KV cache in pinned host memory and
pulls only the indexer-selected rows back just in time, so long-context agentic
sessions stop getting preempted. #53781 landed it CUDA-only.

**Draft.** bf16 KV is complete and benchmarked; `fp8` KV plus HiSparse still
faults on ≥16k prefills (last bullet under Limitations). That is being fixed,
and this PR stays in draft until it is.

## Changes

### 1. Route HiSparse attention through the int64-safe Triton kernel (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`)

HiSparse points attention at
`PagedCacheView.attention_cache`, a view over the **whole multi-layer KV slab**,
so the row indices it emits scale with the total block count rather than with
one layer's page table. Off HiSparse the same model emits a max row index of 33;
on HiSparse it reaches 7.5 million. AITER's decode kernel computes
`row_index * row_width` in int32, so on GLM-5.3 (`row_width=576`) it wraps above
row 3,728,270 and answers with approximately zero — no NaN, no assert, no
kernel error.

The backend already carries a Triton ragged path that promotes the slot index to
`tl.int64`, so it is immune past that point. Under HiSparse it becomes
unconditional: `use_hisparse_triton_attn` is set from
`isinstance(index_group, HiSparseMLAIndexGroup)` at construction, and the prefill
call additionally passes `allow_aiter_opus=False` so the dispatcher inside
`rocm_sparse_attn_prefill` cannot fall back into the OPUS ASM kernel, whose KV
addressing width is likewise unverified. No flag, no env var — HiSparse on ROCm
is always on the int64 path.

### 2. ROCm backend wiring (`rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`)

Every CUDA HiSparse backend consumes a **dense** `[tokens, topk]` index tensor
plus `valid_counts`; AITER's tuned decode kernel consumes a **ragged** flat list
plus an indptr. Bridging that is the bulk of the diff:

- `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` accepts an `index_group_builder` and registers with
  it, which is what makes `mla_attention.py:575` pick up `hisparse_cache` and
  drive KV mirroring.
- Decode: `convert_decode_logical_to_physical_topk` → dense physical top-k →
  compacted to ragged → attention runs against `physical_kv_cache` (the hot
  buffer) instead of the paged KV cache.
- Prefill: mirrors the CUDA guard, staging host rows via `stage_prefill_rows`
  when the context is not fully resident. This is not optional — once a context
  has been offloaded, `all_context_pages_resident` is False and
  `index_group.py:232` asserts outright.
- AITER's persistent work-stealing metadata is disabled under HiSparse: its
  buffers are sized in `build()`, but HiSparse rewrites the indptr at forward
  time from resolver counts. Correctness first; noted as a perf follow-up.

One new Triton kernel, `compact_topk_to_ragged_triton`. The existing
`fetch_id_to_ragged_triton` was not reusable: a mid-row `-1` must *drop out*
rather than displace a valid entry.


### 3. HIP kernel port (`csrc/`)

The four fused HiSparse cache ops now build and run on ROCm. Mechanical:
vectorized copy widths, `__nv_bfloat16` → `hip_bfloat16`, and warp-primitive
shims added to `csrc/cuda_compat.h`. No algorithmic change; CUDA codegen is
unaffected.

### 4. Config gate (`vllm/config/vllm.py`)

Opens HiSparse for ROCm, with `fp8_ds_mla` (the 656-byte packed row) rejected by
name rather than failing deep in a kernel. Every other platform keeps the
existing rejection.

## Platform-neutral fixes

These are in shared code and affect CUDA too.

**`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/index_group.py` — event record does not
survive nested `torch.compile`.** `self.logical_topk_ready.record(...)` is
traceable, so Dynamo lowers it to a `torch.ops.streams.record_event` node whose
event lives in a process-global side table. `reset_user_object_tracking()`
clears that table on compile entry. vLLM nests compiles
(`CustomOp.maybe_compile` wraps `forward_native`), so an inner compile firing
during an outer graph's execution wipes the entry that graph's node depends on.
Replaced with an opaque custom op keyed by an integer group handle, so the event
never becomes a graph input. CUDA appears not to have hit this only because its
call path reaches `set_logical_topk_ready` from outside the compiled region.

**`vllm/distributed/.../hisparse/worker.py` — mirror guard for unbracketed
runs.** Warmup and profiling runs execute the model with the connector disabled,
so `start_step`/`finish_forward` never bracket them and `_per_layer_mirrored` is
never cleared between passes. The second warmup pass then trips
`RuntimeError: HiSparse layer 0 mirrored twice.` Added a `_step_in_flight` flag
so mirroring is skipped outside a real step. The double-mirror check is
unchanged inside a step.

**`vllm/v1/worker/worker_base.py` — layout query runs outside the config
scope.** `get_supported_kv_cache_layouts` is an RPC that calls
`get_current_attn_backends(self.vllm_config)` with no config set, but a
backend's supported set can depend on the config — HiSparse changes how ROCm
sparse MLA addresses pages. Wrapped in `set_current_vllm_config`.

**`vllm/v1/hisparse/runtime.py` — `cudaGetLastError` is absent on ROCm.**
`release_pinned_state` clears the sticky error flag after a failed unregister,
but ROCm's `torch.cuda.cudart()` exposes only `cudaError`,
`cudaGetErrorString`, `cudaHostRegister`, `cudaHostUnregister`. The handler
would itself raise `AttributeError` and mask the real error. Guarded with
`getattr`; the clear is best-effort cleanup, so skipping it is correct rather
than degraded.

## Required AITER fix (out of tree)

**This branch does not run on stock AITER.** With HiSparse enabled, gfx950 takes
a `Memory access fault` inside AITER's 1-stage fp8-blockscale MoE,
`fmoe_fp8_blockscale_g1u1`. It is not a HiSparse bug, but HiSparse is what makes
it fire, so it gates this PR.

AITER Issue: [ROCm/aiter/issue#]()

**[ROCm/aiter#5764](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5764)** backs the tail
with real memory at the `per_1x128` launch site, returning a view with the
original shape so no observable value changes. It makes the over-read harmless
rather than removing it. **Every number in this PR was produced with that patch
applied.**

## ROCm-specific workarounds

**Imported IPC events are capped at 32 record/wait cycles on ROCm.** The 33rd
raises `hipErrorInvalidValue` even with the two sides fully serialized, so it is
a resource limit and not a race. HiSparse's shared host pool records one per
step, so any run decoding past 32 steps at TP>1 would fail. On ROCm the worker
falls back to a local-event handshake plus a TP barrier
(`HiSparseConnectorWorker.sync_host_writes`), which orders the same writes
without an interprocess object.

## Test Plan

Hardware: 8× MI350X (gfx950, CDNA4), ROCm 7.2.3, AITER 0.1.21.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_hisparse_kernels.py
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_hisparse.py
```

Plus GSM8K via `lm_eval`, a needle-in-a-haystack probe under sustained offload,
and the agentic throughput sweep — all three below, with GLM-5.3 on gfx950.

## Test Result

| Suite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `test_hisparse_kernels.py` | 16 passed, 76 skipped | **41 passed** |
| `test_rocm_aiter_mla_sparse_metadata_sync.py` | 4 passed | **4 passed** |
| `test_sparse_mla_backends.py` | 84 passed, 688 skipped | **100 passed, 687 skipped** |
| `test_sparse_mla_backends.py -k hisparse` | 15 passed, 15 skipped | **32 passed, 2 skipped** |
| `test_hisparse.py` (e2e) | skipped (CUDA-gated) | **2 passed** |

## Model Evaluation

GSM8K, 200 questions, 5-shot, greedy (`temperature=0`), seed 42. GLM-5.3, TP4,
full 78-layer model, gfx950. Production serving config: 32k context, fp8 KV
cache, cudagraphs enabled. HiSparse arm adds a 128 GiB pinned host pool.

Model Runner V2 is forced in **both** arms — HiSparse enables it implicitly, and
comparing against an MRV1 baseline reintroduces a confound.

| Arm | Accuracy (run 1 / run 2) | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| HiSparse **off** | 0.905 / **0.915** | 1171 / 1212 |
| HiSparse **on** | 0.890 / **0.925** | 200 / 233 |

On AITER's int32 decode kernel, the identical configuration scored
**0.000–0.005** — near-zero attention for every row above the wrap point. (These
GSM8K numbers were taken with the block-count cap that preceded the Triton
routing; both avoid the overflow, and the Triton path is the one that ships.)

The throughput gap above is real but misleading as a verdict on HiSparse: GSM8K
prompts are short and concurrency is low, so nothing is ever under memory
pressure and the indexer is pure overhead. The benchmark below is the one that
answers the question.

**Accuracy while the host path is actually live.** GSM8K above runs below
HiSparse's offload watermark, where every page stays GPU-resident and no host DMA
happens at all — so it does not exercise the feature. A needle-in-a-haystack
probe on 8× MI350X (GLM-5.3, TP=8, `--max-model-len 80000`, 256 GiB host pool)
loads the pool with long-generation holder requests until KV usage sits just
under the watermark, then measures with short probes alongside them:

| | |
|---|---|
| needle accuracy | **60/60 = 1.000** |
| by depth (10/30/50/70/90%) | 12/12 at every depth |
| host→device **during the probe window** | **245.4 GiB** |
| KV usage during window | min 0.775, mean 0.836 |
| preemptions | 0 |

A 25-probe run at a lighter load agrees (25/25, 9.2 GiB moved), as does a control
below the watermark where nothing offloads (25/25). The 245 GiB figure is a delta
across the probe window, not a cumulative counter.

## Throughput

The workload from the GLM-5.3 hybrid-offloading blog post, which is what HiSparse
was built for: OpenHands-style agentic conversations, 13 turns, first turn ~74k
tokens and later turns 753, output pinned to 220. GLM-5.3, **TP4 on 4× MI350X**
(the blog ran TP8 on H200), `--max-model-len 131072`,
`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 32768`, 128
conversations, sequential arms, a fresh server per point.

**Every arm runs bf16 KV, a deviation from the blog's fp8** — forced by the fp8
limitation below. It roughly doubles KV bytes and so lowers absolute throughput
for all arms alike; the comparison between arms is unaffected.

Throughput is logical total tokens/s per GPU; interactivity is `1000 / mean TPOT`.

| arm | conc | reqs | interactivity | tok/s/GPU | TPOT ms | TTFT med |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no offloading | 1 | 28 | 50.6 | 3444 | 19.8 | 276 |
| no offloading | 8 | 223 | 5.5 | 2753 | 182.5 | 15069 |
| no offloading | 16 | 448 | 4.4 | 2265 | 228.3 | 86827 |
| CPU offload 512 GiB | 1 | 28 | 49.0 | 2978 | 20.4 | 278 |
| CPU offload 512 GiB | 8, 16, 24 | — | **crashed** | | | |
| **HiSparse 512 GiB** | 1 | 28 | 21.3 | 1499 | 46.9 | 665 |
| **HiSparse 512 GiB** | 8 | 224 | 8.0 | **4129** | 125.5 | 1754 |
| **HiSparse 512 GiB** | 16 | 435 | 3.3 | **4141** | 298.7 | 1620 |
| **HiSparse 512 GiB** | 24 | 661 | 1.9 | 3330 | 526.4 | 1360 |
| hybrid 384+128 GiB | 1, 8, 16 | — | **crashed** | | | |

The shape matches the blog. The no-offload baseline **degrades** as concurrency
rises (3444 → 2753 → 2265) because 74k-token contexts get preempted and
re-prefilled; HiSparse climbs and then holds (1499 → 4129 → 4141), and at
concurrency 16 delivers **1.83× the baseline's throughput** with TTFT median 54×
lower (1.6 s vs 87 s). HiSparse loses at concurrency 1, as expected: with no
memory pressure the indexer is pure overhead.

The trade is visible in the interactivity column: at concurrency 16 HiSparse's
per-token latency is worse (299 ms TPOT vs 228 ms), because it keeps far more
requests in flight instead of preempting them. That is throughput/latency
exchange, not a free win — but the first
token arrives in 1.6 s rather than 87 s, which for an agentic workload is the
number that is felt.

Two arms crash, and neither crash is in code this PR touches:

- **CPU offload** dies in `swap_blocks_batch` / `hipMemcpyBatchAsync`
  (`cache_kernels.hip:223`) at concurrency ≥ 8, with 27 GB already staged. That
  is the generic `OffloadingConnector` DMA path, unmodified here.
- **hybrid** (`MultiConnector` wrapping both) dies seconds after the first
  request at every concurrency, although each connector passes **alone** at the
  identical configuration. Under investigation; not a blocker for HiSparse
  standalone.

So on ROCm today HiSparse is not merely faster than CPU offloading — at
concurrency ≥ 8 it is the only offload arm that runs at all.

## Limitations

- **HiSparse cannot use AITER's tuned ASM sparse decode kernel on ROCm** until
  its row offset is widened to 64 bits; it is prebuilt assembly and out of tree.
  The Triton ragged path is correct but not equally tuned.
- **`fp8_ds_mla` is not supported on ROCm** and is rejected with a clear error.
  bf16 and standard fp8 rows work — the HiSparse runtime is dtype-generic
  (`row_width` is a constructor parameter).
- **Gated on [ROCm/aiter#5764](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5764)** (see
  above). Stock AITER faults in `fmoe_fp8_blockscale_g1u1` whenever HiSparse is
  enabled on gfx950.
- **`fp8` KV plus HiSparse faults on prefills at or above ~16k tokens**, even
  with the AITER fix above applied. **Being fixed — this PR stays in draft until
  it is.** It is the *interaction*: the same configuration with `auto` KV passes
  16k and 74k, and fp8 with HiSparse off passes both. bf16 KV is the workaround
  and is what the benchmark above uses.

  It is an **async ordering bug**: under `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3
  AMD_SERIALIZE_COPY=3 HIP_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` all of 1k/4k/16k/32k pass, where
  the unserialized run fails hard at 16k. Rank 0 dies by silent host SIGSEGV —
  no traceback, no `Memory access fault` — immediately after an AITER
  `per_1x128` MoE dispatch; the other ranks are victims parked in a barrier.
  Narrowing which synchronization is missing is in progress.
- **AITER's persistent work-stealing decode path is disabled under HiSparse.**
- **`MultiConnector` combining HiSparse with `OffloadingConnector` crashes** on
  ROCm (see above). Each connector works alone. It presents with the same
  signature as the fp8 fault above, so the two are plausibly the same race;
  being investigated together.
- **MTP under HiSparse on ROCm is untested.**
- Verified on gfx950 only. Other CDNA targets are untested.

---

*AI assistance was used in preparing this change.* All changes reviewed by the
submitter.

title: [Mypy] Fix mypy typing for Whisper models
body:
## Purpose

**Depends on V-model PR [#58251](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58251), after U [#58239](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58239) and Q [#58046](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58046). Merge order: Q → U → V → W.** This branch starts at V's `68b92a6308`. Its diff against upstream `main` includes the pending dependencies; after those merge, rebasing onto `main` will leave only the W-specific changes.

Continue the incremental mypy rollout tracked by [#26533](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26533) by removing `r"vllm/model_executor/models/[wW]"` from the mypy exclusions. All three selected files are now checked: `whisper.py`, `whisper_causal.py`, and `whisper_utils.py`. The language constants in `whisper_utils.py` already pass without code changes.

The W-specific changes touch four files. They type Whisper's language-detection tokenizer and return value, narrow audio tensor leaves and encoder outputs, and correct causal attention backend class/optional types and the slot-mapping metadata contract. The shared `SupportsTranscription` interface is updated to accept `TokenizerLike` in both language-detection methods.

One documented `type: ignore[override]` preserves Whisper cross-attention's existing signature, which takes encoder states instead of self-attention metadata. Existing exceptions for processor access and dynamically constructed attention subclasses remain unchanged. No casts are added. Model computations remain unchanged for valid inputs; assertions make existing tensor requirements explicit.

## Reproducer

On the base revision `68b92a6308` (the V-model branch), first remove `r"vllm/model_executor/models/[wW]"` from `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, then run:

```bash
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 \
  --files $(git ls-files 'vllm/model_executor/models/[wW]*.py') \
  --hook-stage manual
```

Base (`68b92a6308`):

```text
Found 12 errors in 2 files (checked 3 source files)
```

With the W typing fixes:

```text
Run mypy for Python 3.12.................................................Passed
```

## Test Plan

Validation on `cb71508394`:

```bash
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
# Full-repository check passed.

for version in 3.10 3.11 3.13; do
  pre-commit run "mypy-$version" \
    --files $(git ls-files 'vllm/model_executor/models/[wW]*.py') \
    vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py --hook-stage manual
done
# All three checks passed.

pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only 68b92a6308 HEAD)
# All applicable hooks passed on the four-file W-specific diff.

git diff --check 68b92a6308 HEAD
# Passed.
```

Runtime checks used the existing Python 3.12 environment and imported the W branch's source files:

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu

HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python --no-managed-python \
  python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_whisper.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/generation/test_voxtral_realtime.py \
  tests/models/test_registry.py -q --tb=short --maxfail=3 \
  -k 'test_parse_language_detection_output or buffer_preserves or (test_registry_imports and (Whisper or Voxtral))'
# 7 passed.

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python --no-managed-python python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_whisper.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py \
  -q --tb=short --maxfail=2 -k whisper
# 9 passed.
```

Total: **16 distinct tests passed**. These cover language-detection parsing, Whisper/Voxtral registry imports, realtime buffering, Whisper encoder-window truncation, and common processor consistency for both Whisper model entries.

Full model inference, GPU/ROCm attention validation, and model-quality evaluations were not run because the NVIDIA driver is unavailable; the checkout also lacks the compiled `vllm._C` extension. Runtime validation covers CPU utilities, buffering, registry imports, and processors.

## Duplicate-work check

Reviewed issue #26533 and its comments, open PRs referencing that issue, and open PR searches for mypy and Whisper mypy. No matching W-model typing rollout was found. Q, U, and V are explicit dependencies. The other Whisper results cover compilation, transcription features, or separate bug fixes.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with the typing fixes, interface and call-site review, validation, local stack setup, and this PR description.

title: [Bugfix][DCP] Preserve interleave for per-slot KV connectors
body:
## Purpose

Fix DCP KV-cache interleave handling for KV connectors that transfer cache rows
using their own per-slot geometry.

Currently, DCP interleave normalization assumes that the external transfer unit
is a complete local vLLM KV-cache block. This is correct for the existing Nixl
P/D path, but is incorrect for connectors whose transfer layout is based on
individual cache rows or slots.

This PR:

- Adds a connector capability for preserving the configured
  `cp_kv_cache_interleave_size`.
- Keeps the existing default behavior for connectors that do not opt in.
- Propagates the capability through `MultiConnector`.
- Preserves the existing Nixl block-level alignment behavior.
- Only preserves the configured interleave when all child connectors in a
  `MultiConnector` support it.

No existing issue is linked. This is a focused extension of the current DCP
connector behavior and does not replace the existing Nixl-specific normalization
logic.

## Test Plan

Added a configuration unit test covering a KV connector that preserves the
configured DCP interleave size.

Commands run:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/test_config.py -k 'dcp_interleave' -q

.venv/bin/python -m py_compile \
  vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/base.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/multi_connector.py \
  tests/test_config.py

.venv/bin/python -m ruff check \
  vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/base.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/multi_connector.py \
  tests/test_config.py

.venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check \
  vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/base.py \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/multi_connector.py \
  tests/test_config.py

git diff --check

Repository pre-commit hooks were also run during commit.
### Test Result
The targeted unit tests passed:
```bash
5 passed, 284 deselected, 15 warnings in 1.75s
```
Ruff, formatting, Python syntax compilation, git diff --check, and all
pre-commit hooks passed.

The test was run with VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu because the local environment
does not expose a supported GPU platform. Without this override, pytest reached
the teardown phase but the local PyTorch accelerator cleanup triggered a
platform-related segmentation fault. No test assertion failed.

No documentation update is required.

AI assistance was used during implementation, testing, and preparation of this
PR description. The patch has been reviewed by the submitting author.

title: [Bugfix][Transformers backend] Fix CUDA graph capture for dynamic-rope models
body:
## Purpose

A model with `rope_type: "dynamic"` served through the Transformers modeling backend cannot
start at all under CUDA graph capture. Engine startup dies during `determine_available_memory`:

```
File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py", line 386, in capture
    with torch.cuda.graph(
...
File ".../transformers/models/hunyuan_v1_dense/modeling_hunyuan_v1_dense.py", line 436, in forward
    position_embeddings = self.rotary_emb(hidden_states, position_ids=position_ids)
File ".../transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py", line 125, in wrapper
    dynamic_frequency_update(self, position_ids, device=x.device, **kwargs)
File ".../transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py", line 100, in dynamic_frequency_update
    if seq_len > max_seq_len_cached:  # growth
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing
Search for `cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported' ...

RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed.
```

Transformers wraps every RoPE `forward` with `@dynamic_rope_update`, which computes
`torch.max(position_ids)` and branches on it. Reading that value back to the host is illegal
inside a capturing stream, so the capture is invalidated and the engine never comes up. The
only workaround today is to give up CUDA graphs entirely (`cudagraph_mode=NONE`, or
`--enforce-eager`).

#23738 made `can_enable_torch_compile` return `False` for these models, which stops
`torch.compile` from tripping over the same branch, but CUDA graph capture is wrapped at the
model-runner level independently of whether the model was compiled, so the crash path was left
open. This PR closes it.

The observation that makes a fix possible: the update is frequently dead code. It only
recomputes `inv_freq` once positions grow past `max_seq_len_cached` (initialised to
`max_position_embeddings`), and only restores the original `inv_freq` after such a growth has
happened. vLLM never emits a position beyond `max_model_len`, so whenever the context is capped
at or below `max_position_embeddings` **both branches are unreachable** and the decorator is
pure overhead — overhead that happens to be fatal under capture.

This PR:

1. Adds `dynamic_rope_update_is_noop(vllm_config)`: `max_model_len <= max_position_embeddings`.
2. Removes the decorator from the decoder's RoPE modules when that holds
   (`remove_noop_dynamic_rope_update`), restoring the `@torch.no_grad()` that Transformers
   stacks on top of it.
3. Lets `can_enable_torch_compile` return `True` in exactly that case, since the reason it was
   returning `False` no longer exists once the branch is gone.

Two deliberate exclusions:

- **Encoders.** The sweep is scoped to `model.get_decoder()`, because `max_model_len` bounds
  decoder positions only — it says nothing about what an encoder/vision tower is fed.
- **`longrope`.** It reassigns `inv_freq` at any context length, so its modules keep the
  decorator.

One implementation note for reviewers: the decorator is identified by the *code object* of the
wrapper `dynamic_rope_update` returns, not by `forward.__wrapped__`. Transformers writes
`@torch.no_grad()` **above** `@dynamic_rope_update`, and `no_grad` also uses `functools.wraps`,
so `forward.__wrapped__` is the dynamic wrapper itself — unwrapping one level would silently
drop `no_grad` while leaving the update in place.

### Scope

This only helps when `max_model_len <= max_position_embeddings`. For a dynamic-rope model whose
context is genuinely scaled past the pretrained length, the update is live, the decorator stays,
and behaviour is unchanged — including the capture failure, which is correct, since the sync is
real there.

### Not a duplicate

- No open PR touches `can_enable_torch_compile` or `dynamic_rope_update` (searched
  `can_enable_torch_compile`, `dynamic_rope_update`, `"dynamic rope" in:title`, and open PRs on
  the Transformers backend).
- The only prior work in this area is #23738, which this PR completes rather than reverts:
  dynamic-rope models that *can* still rescale within `max_model_len` remain uncompiled, exactly
  as that PR intended.

## Test Plan

New CPU-only unit tests:

```bash
pytest tests/models/transformers/test_dynamic_rope.py -v
```

They assert observable behaviour through the public forward — whether an over-long
`position_ids` still rewrites `inv_freq` — rather than inspecting how the decorator is attached:

- the no-op predicate at and around the `max_position_embeddings` boundary;
- `can_enable_torch_compile` for default / dynamic / per-layer-type rope;
- the update is gone when it cannot fire, and the remaining forward is numerically identical and
  still runs under `no_grad`;
- the update is kept when rescaling is reachable, and for `longrope`.

The new test file is wired into the existing `:computer: (CPU) Basic Models Other` job in
`.buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml` — it is CPU-only and runs in seconds, next to the
`models/transformers/fusers/` tests already in that job. That edit is only there to satisfy
`check_test_tethering`; it appends one path and changes nothing about the tests already listed.

Lint:

```bash
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/utils.py \
    vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/base.py \
    tests/models/transformers/test_dynamic_rope.py
pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
```

End-to-end: serve HunYuan-MT2-7B (`rope_type: "dynamic"`, `max_position_embeddings: 262144`,
`factor: 1.0`) on TP2 with `--max-model-len 32768` and `cudagraph_mode: FULL`, before and after.
IFEval on both.

## Test Result

CPU unit tests:

```
13 passed in 4.03s        # tests/models/transformers/test_dynamic_rope.py
pre-commit: ruff check / ruff format / mypy-3.12 — all passed
```

End-to-end on HunYuan-MT2-7B, TP2, `--max-model-len 32768`, `cudagraph_mode: FULL`. Validated on
a v0.29.0 backport of this diff, not on main — v0.29.0's `can_enable_torch_compile` and the
`recursive_replace()` call site are byte-identical to the pre-change versions here.

**Before:** engine fails to start, with the traceback quoted under Purpose
(`cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported` at `modeling_rope_utils.py:100`, then
`cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated`, then `Engine core initialization failed`).

**After:** the decorator is dropped on both ranks,

```
(Worker_TP0) DEBUG [transformers/utils.py:445] Removed no-op `@dynamic_rope_update` from rotary_emb
(Worker_TP1) DEBUG [transformers/utils.py:445] Removed no-op `@dynamic_rope_update` from rotary_emb
```

capture completes and the server comes up,

```
Capturing CUDA graphs (PIECEWISE): 100%|██████| 19/19
Capturing CUDA graphs (FULL):      100%|██████| 19/19
INFO [v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:960] Graph capturing finished in 2 secs, took 0.12 GiB
INFO: Application startup complete.
```

and the model is compiled, where before it was refused outright
(`WARNING [vllm.py:2952] torch.compile is turned on, but the model ... does not support it`):

```
INFO [compilation/backends.py:1155] Dynamo bytecode transform time: 9.18 s
INFO [compilation/backends.py:393]  Compiling a graph for compile range (1, 2048) takes 13.59 s
INFO [compilation/monitor.py:53]    torch.compile took 28.64 s in total
```

### Accuracy

IFEval, baseline served with `cudagraph_mode=NONE` (the only configuration that starts without
this change) versus the patched server above:

| Metric | n | Baseline (`cudagraph_mode=NONE`) | With this change | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| prompt_level_strict | 541 | 72.6% | 72.5% | -0.1 |
| inst_level_strict | 834 | 79.3% | 79.1% | -0.2 |
| prompt_level_loose | 541 | 74.1% | 74.3% | +0.2 |
| inst_level_loose | 834 | 80.3% | 80.5% | +0.2 |

All four deltas are within 0.2pp, against a binomial 1-sigma of roughly 1.4-1.9pp at these
sample sizes, and they do not share a sign. The model's `generation_config.json` enables
sampling (`temperature: 0.7`, `top_k: 20`, `top_p: 0.8`), so exact agreement was never expected
once compilation and graph capture change kernel selection.

Note the two runs are not the same server config — they cannot be, since the baseline config
does not start. The comparison is `cudagraph_mode=NONE` without the fix versus `cudagraph_mode=FULL` with it.
Where the numbers can move at all is worth being precise about: removing the decorator is
bit-identical at the RoPE layer, which `test_removal_does_not_change_frequencies` asserts
directly. Any end-to-end difference comes from compilation and capture now being available for
this model, which is the same position every other compiled model is in.

AI assistance was used to write this change (Claude Code).

Closes #57890

title: [Docs] Add PR checklist skill for coding agents
body:
## Overview

(DISCLAIMER: I USED THE NEW SKILL TO HAVE GPT-6 AUTHOR THE PR DESCRIPTION BELOW, COMMIT THE CHANGES AND OPEN THIS PR. TREAT IT AS A REVIEWABLE EXAMPLE ARTIFACT. ALL CODE CHANGES WERE HAND WRITTEN WITH CARE BY ME.)

Add a `pr-checklist` skill for coding agents preparing, reviewing, or revising
vLLM pull requests. Integrate it with the agent contribution instructions and
the PR template.

## Claims

- Provide a structured review workflow covering design fit, compatibility,
  complexity, tradeoffs, validation, test quality, code clarity, and PR evidence.
- Distinguish validation performed for a contribution from tests maintained in
  the repository, emphasizing meaningful coverage rather than test volume.
- Include guidance for human-in-the-loop review and responding to prior feedback.
- Require agents to use the skill before submission through `AGENTS.md`.
- Restructure the PR template around Overview, Claims, Validation, and Details,
  with checklist and AI-assistance disclosure fields.

The intended benefit is better-prepared contributions and less avoidable
maintainer follow-up. This PR does not claim a measured reduction in review
rounds or review time.

## Validation

This change is documentation and agent instructions only. No serving-engine,
model, kernel, dependency, or runtime behavior is modified; runtime tests,
model evaluations, and performance benchmarks are not applicable.

### Diff and structure checks

```bash
git status --short
git diff -- AGENTS.md .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md
git ls-files --others --exclude-standard .agents/skills/pr-checklist
git diff --check
git diff --no-index --check /dev/null .agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md
wc -l AGENTS.md .agents/skills/pr-checklist/SKILL.md
```

- Reviewed the two tracked-file diffs and the complete new skill.
- Confirmed the proposed change consists of those three files; research data,
  scraping scripts, plots, and intermediate drafts are excluded.
- `AGENTS.md` has 159 lines and the skill has 153 lines, within the applicable
  instruction-document budgets.
- The tracked-file whitespace check produced no diagnostics.
- The new skill's whitespace check reports one trailing space on the helper
  inlining instruction. This remains in the proposed diff.
- No Markdown linter or documentation build was run.

### Current-skill behavioral smoke test

A fresh agent context read the current skill and applied it to four
hypothetical scenarios without executing tests or changing files:

1. **This documentation-only PR:** recognized runtime validation as not
   applicable and assessed workflow consistency and documentation.
2. **Reviewing another author's optimization PR:** requested missing
   configuration, correctness, and serving-performance evidence rather than
   skipping the PR-contents section.
3. **Re-review with an unresolved backend concern:** traced related paths,
   requested appropriate evidence, and identified a stale description.
4. **Intentional all-drafts-rejected regression test:** identified a conflict
   between the expected zero acceptance and the skill's nonzero-acceptance
   instruction. This remains an outstanding caveat below.

These are qualitative instruction-following checks, not automated regression
tests or evidence of real-world review-time savings.

## Details

### Motivation and research

The drafting process examined the latest 50 vLLM PRs reviewed by each of
`benchislett` and `mgoin`, ordered by the reviewer's latest submitted review.
The samples contain 97 distinct PRs and 342 nonempty authored review/comment

appropriate ownership and reuse, concise implementations, meaningful rather
than excessive tests, and claims supported by evidence.

A separate exploratory analysis measured additions and deletions under

reinforced that LOC is a coarse review aid, not a reliable standalone semantic
complexity classification. The skill's 50/250 bands are judgment-based
guidance, not validated predictive cutoffs.

The research artifacts are local preparation material and are not included

the human author with AI-assisted research and review.

title: [ROCm] Add V2 BF16 streamed PP transport
body:
## Summary

Add an opt-in V2 fixed-schema BF16 pipeline transport for ROCm on the V2 model runner:

- preallocate a bounded sender ring and order P2P sends on a dedicated stream
- receive full-size chunks directly into a fixed receive buffer
- bypass per-step metadata exchange for full `max_num_batched_tokens` chunks
- preserve the existing tensor-dict path for partial tails and unsupported schemas

The feature is disabled by default and selected with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_STREAMED_PP_TRANSPORT=1`. Supported envelope: V2 model runner, ROCm, **TP=1, PP>1**, contiguous BF16 `hidden_states`, and full `max_num_batched_tokens` chunks. Configurations with `PP=1` (for example TP8/PP1) reject the flag at worker startup; benchmarks below are TP1/PP8 only.

This PR is intentionally separate from #55032, which targets the V1 `PPTransport` path. V2 integrates with `PPHandler` and the V2 GPU model runner.

The first commit adds metadata-free async tensor P2P (`isend_tensor`) used by the transport ring.

## Tests

- `tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py`: V2 transport schema validation, ring drain, generic-send reap
- `tests/test_envs.py`: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_STREAMED_PP_TRANSPORT` parsing
- `tests/distributed/test_comm_ops.py`: metadata-free `isend_tensor` coverage
- Worker startup guards in `gpu_worker.py` reject unsupported topologies (`PP <= 1` or `TP != 1`) before model load

## Performance

Measured on 8 x MI355X, DeepSeek-V4-Pro tuned stack (OPUS sparse + FP8 WO_A, nightly pin `73029d4244`), **TP1/PP8 only**, prefix caching disabled. This transport does not apply to `PP=1` layouts such as TP8/PP1.

### C1 100K prefill (TP1/PP8)

| Arm | TTFT runs (ms) | Median TTFT | Input throughput |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Generic (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_STREAMED_PP_TRANSPORT=0`) | 2294.5 / 2278.3 / 2279.1 | 2279.1 ms | 43,877 tok/s |
| Stream (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_STREAMED_PP_TRANSPORT=1`) | 2198.9 / 2183.3 / 2183.9 | 2183.9 ms | 45,790 tok/s |

Delta: **median TTFT -95.2 ms (-4.2%)**.

### TP1/PP8 prefill concurrency

Fixed 8,192-token prompts, one output token, 10 requests per concurrency slot, `max-num-seqs=48`.

| Max concurrency | Generic total tok/s | Stream total tok/s | Gain |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 2817.27 | 2977.25 | +5.68% |
| 2 | 9329.89 | 9316.00 | -0.15% |
| 4 | 22459.09 | 22612.09 | +0.68% |
| 8 | 48709.24 | 49062.22 | +0.72% |
| 16 | 57937.44 | 61954.36 | +6.93% |
| 32 | 59968.76 | 64380.70 | +7.36% |
| 48 | 60701.55 | 65155.02 | +7.34% |

All 1,110 requests in each arm completed without errors.
### TP1/PP8 prefill concurrency — median TTFT

Same workload as above (8K input / 1 output, 10 prompts per concurrency slot).

| Max concurrency | Generic median TTFT (ms) | Stream median TTFT (ms) | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 898.6 | 898.8 | +0.0% |
| 2 | 1754.5 | 1756.8 | +0.1% |
| 4 | 1208.4 | 1193.0 | -1.3% |
| 8 | 1182.3 | 1164.0 | -1.5% |
| 16 | 2109.0 | 1959.3 | **-7.1%** |
| 32 | 4214.1 | 3916.0 | **-7.1%** |
| 48 | 6318.1 | 5877.8 | **-7.0%** |

From C≥16, median TTFT tracks the throughput gains (~7%), consistent with transport savings on the V2 runner (no V1 ~9K tok/s ceiling).



## Correctness

Greedy GSM8K 5-shot, 1319 questions, `temperature=0`, `max-concurrency=32`, TP1/PP8 on the tuned `main-tuned-v2` images:

| Arm | Accuracy | Correct | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Generic | 94.62% | 1248/1319 | 0 |
| Stream | 95.00% | 1253/1319 | 0 |

Both arms produced zero invalid responses. Stream transport does not introduce parse failures; the generic/stream delta (+5 correct) is within normal greedy run variance.

Reference on the earlier `fp8woa` tuned image (without V2 transport overlay): **1256/1319 = 95.22%**, invalid=0.

## AI assistance

title: [Bugfix] Finish a request that can never fit in the KV cache with an error instead of re-prefilling it forever
body:
## Purpose

When a running request cannot get blocks for its next prefill chunk and there is no other request to preempt, `Scheduler.schedule()` preempts the request itself and prepends it to the waiting queue. If admission let the request in although its real footprint exceeds the pool, the next step schedules it again from token zero (a preempted request whose Mamba groups get no prefix hit recomputes everything) and the cycle never ends: the KV usage gauge saw-tooths to ~100% every few seconds, no token is ever produced, the API server logs nothing (stats are only emitted on steps with output) and the client only sees its own timeout.

Observed on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (GDN + QSA + MTP, one RTX PRO 6000): a 249,950-token prompt cycled for 16 minutes (six full re-prefills in a 150 s sample) on a branch based before #53906, where the QSA ring buffer's 8-token block size dragged `cache_config.block_size` down and the align-mode Mamba managers took a fresh state block every chunk, so a request needed 1.9x the blocks the capacity estimate assumed. Any future accounting drift reproduces the same silent spin.

## Fix

Track a request that preempted itself twice with the running queue empty (`request.num_preemptions >= 2 and not self.running`): nothing else holds KV blocks, so it can never fit. Finish it with `FinishReason.ERROR` in `update_from_output`, the path already used for grammar compile failures, so the client gets a 500 immediately and the engine log names the request, its prompt length and the pool size. The second self-preemption is required rather than the first to stay clear of any transient one-off.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q
```

New: `test_request_that_never_fits_is_failed_not_respun` (single request larger than a 10-block pool, full-sequence admission mocked as optimistic like the hybrid layout above; the request must be finished with `FinishReason.ERROR` after exactly two self-preemptions, leaving nothing running or waiting).

## Test Result

`163 passed` on `main` (d2906091b), CPU. Live: with the guard in the serving branch, a request that cannot fit returns HTTP 500 within one re-prefill cycle instead of spinning until the client times out; on the fixed accounting no request has hit the guard across a full replay (0 guard errors, 8 of 8 prompts up to 261,802 tokens correct).

title: [Metrics] Add admission rejection metrics
body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #49445. Admission limits reject requests with HTTP 503, but operators cannot tell from metrics which queue cap fired (`max_num_queued_reqs` vs `max_num_queued_tokens`), and each rejection logged at INFO.

This adds `vllm:admission_rejections_total` (`reason` label, no `engine` label). The unit is one rejected frontend admission attempt; `n > 1` still increments by one. The counter is incremented in `check_admission` through `StatLoggerManager`, matching the sleep-state side door: this event never appears in `EngineCoreOutputs`.

Per-rejection diagnostic messages move from INFO to DEBUG now that the counter exists (requested on #49445 until metrics landed).

Not duplicating:
- #53936 (atomic `n > 1` admission) remains a separate core change.
- #54746 (shared occupancy) is a different feature.
- No other open PR implements `admission_rejections`.

## Test Plan

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/engine/test_admission_control.py
```

Existing admission tests now also assert Prometheus samples (success stays at 0, each reject reason increments once, request-cap-first, `n > 1` still +1). `vllm:admission_rejections_total` is listed in `EXPECTED_METRICS_V1`.

## Test Result

```
46 passed, 14 warnings in 4.71s
```

No model evaluation: metrics and logging only; admission decisions are unchanged.

title: [Bugfix] Account for PCP when validating DCP for GQA/MQA models
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51429.

`ParallelConfig` accepts `decode_context_parallel_size in (1, pcp, tp * pcp)` when prefill context parallelism is enabled, and `initialize_model_parallel` lays the DCP groups out over the PCP axis first. `ModelConfig.verify_with_parallel_config` then rejects that same topology for GQA/MQA models whenever `tensor_parallel_size <= total_num_kv_heads`, because it only counts TP-induced KV head replication as duplication for DCP to reclaim. So a topology one layer documents as valid cannot be started, and the error message (`Increase --tensor-parallel-size`) points at the wrong knob.

PCP replicates the full KV cache on every PCP rank (K/V are all-gathered across the PCP group), so a DCP group that spans the PCP axis always has duplication to reclaim. This PR:

- computes the DCP ceiling as `max(1, tp // num_kv_heads) * pcp` instead of `tp // num_kv_heads`, and only raises the "no duplication source" error when both TP and PCP contribute nothing;
- applies the query-heads-per-KV-head divisibility check to the TP-spanning part of DCP (`dcp // pcp`) rather than the whole DCP size, since ranks along the PCP axis hold identical query heads (the attention backends all-gather queries across the DCP group and run them against the local KV heads, which are the same on every PCP rank);
- mentions `--prefill-context-parallel-size` in the error messages.

Behaviour with `pcp == 1` is unchanged: the ceiling collapses to `tp // num_kv_heads` and the divisibility check to `num_q_per_kv % dcp`.

Note on reachability: in-tree PCP is currently MLA-only (`pcp_manager.py` raises for non-MLA models and no non-MLA backend sets `supports_pcp`), and this guard is skipped for MLA. So today the relaxed path is exercised by out-of-tree backends (we hit it on TPU, where PCP shards the KV cache and `dcp == pcp` is how the block accounting is kept consistent). The fix is still worthwhile as platform-independent config validation: `ParallelConfig` already accepts the topology, and the old message pointed at the wrong knob.

### Relationship to #51490

#51490 (by @mayuriphad) addresses the same issue and I'd be glad for either to land. This PR differs in that it:

1. also generalises the query-head divisibility check, which #51490 leaves keyed on the full DCP size. With that check unchanged, a model with 3 query heads per KV head still fails at `pcp = dcp = 2` even though no query heads are split along the DCP group.
2. adds the regression tests to `tests/test_config.py` next to the existing DCP config tests, and builds a real `ParallelConfig` in them so the test asserts that both validation layers accept the same topology.

I wrote the original issue and am the human submitter for this change; I have reviewed every changed line. AI assistance was used for this PR.

## Test Plan

CPU only, no GPU or model download needed.

pytest tests/test_config.py -k gqa_dcp -v

title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Derive num_speculative_tokens from a speculators draft config
body:
## Purpose

Refs #40382. The primary issue there, no Ampere attention backend for a non-causal `head_dim=256` draft, is already resolved on current main by #40394. This PR fixes the remaining `num_speculative_tokens` auto-detect gap.

Serving a speculators-format draft (Eagle3, DFlash, PEAGLE, ...) through `--speculative-config` with the target as the top-level `--model` fails to start unless the user also restates `num_speculative_tokens`, even though the draft config already declares it under `speculators_config.proposal_methods[0].speculative_tokens`.

The existing auto-detect path only runs when the speculator repo itself is the top-level `--model` and `maybe_override_with_speculators` handles it. With the target as `--model` and the draft supplied via `--speculative-config`, `SpeculativeConfig.__post_init__` loads the draft as a `SpeculatorsConfig` built from `transformer_layer_config`, so the proposal-method `speculative_tokens` count is dropped before `num_speculative_tokens` can default from it.

This carries the speculators proposal count into the draft config and defaults `num_speculative_tokens` from that count when the user did not provide an explicit value. A user-provided value still takes precedence, and the behavior is generic across speculators algorithms.

## Test Plan

Validated `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()`, the shared config-build path used by `vllm serve` and offline `LLM(...)` before engine startup. The repro uses target model `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, speculators draft `nm-testing/Llama3_2_1B_speculator.eagle3`, and omits `num_speculative_tokens`.

title: [torch.compile] Remove dead torch 2.9 Inductor monkeypatches
body:
## Summary

`vllm/env_override.py` carries four Inductor monkeypatches plus a `get_raw_stream` workaround that are gated on `is_torch_equal("2.9.0")` / `is_torch_equal("2.9.1")`. No supported install path ships torch 2.9:

- `pyproject.toml` build requires `torch == 2.13.0`; `requirements/cuda.txt`, `cpu.txt` and `xpu.txt` pin `torch==2.13.0`
- ROCm: `requirements/build/rocm.txt` pins `torch==2.11.0`, `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base` builds ROCm/pytorch `release/2.12`, and `docker/Dockerfile.rocm_base_gfx1250` sets `TORCH_VERSION=2.11.0`
- TPU: `docker/Dockerfile.tpu` starts from the `xla:nightly` image

So both gates are constant-false everywhere vllm pins a version, and the ~380 lines behind them can never execute. This PR removes them.

## What is removed

- `memory_plan_reuse_patched` (pytorch#165514 workaround)
- `get_graph_partition_signature_patched` (pytorch#165815 workaround)
- `should_partition_patched` and `_update_scheduler_patched` (vllm#26678 workaround)
- `_patch_get_raw_stream_if_needed` (vllm#30905 workaround)
- the `if is_torch_equal("2.9.0"):` block that installs them, and the now-unused `is_torch_equal` import
- `tests/compile/test_config.py::test_get_raw_stream_patch`, whose body only asserts under torch 2.9

## What is deliberately NOT touched

The `torch <2.12`, `2.10–2.12` and `>=2.11` gates further down the same file stay exactly as they are. ROCm images ship torch 2.11 and 2.12, so those patches are still live — the comment saying one "can be removed once torch >=2.12 is the minimum supported version" is not yet true for every supported platform.

No behavior change on any version vllm currently pins.

Found while auditing version-gated leftovers in popular open-source projects.

## AI assistance

Per the AI Assisted Contributions policy: the edit was applied and verified with AI assistance (Claude), from an analysis and a patch script written by me. The commit carries a `Co-authored-by:` trailer.

title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Recover locally invalidated pull peer metadata
body:
## Summary

Recover a pull peer whose **local NIXL metadata is missing**, while Prefill is
still alive with the same engine ID. Otherwise, the cached `_remote_agents`
entry and prepared dlists can keep later requests on the stale path.

- On receive failure, query local metadata existence without descriptors.
  A transfer failure alone is not treated as evidence that Prefill is dead.
- Defer native checks/cleanup until background handshakes and the affected
  peer's receive handles finish, including handles outliving request metadata.
- Reuse existing cleanup, so a fresh request can handshake again. Preserve
  healthy peers; never replay a failed request's old remote block IDs.

Only `nixl/pull_worker.py` changes production behavior. Tests extend the existing
connector suite and initialize the HMA fixture. No new router API,
configuration, push-mode behavior, or successful-path native metadata query.

## Related Work

Related to #49238. #50047 also cleans peer state, but on a broader
dead-peer/address-replacement basis. This patch requires positive local
metadata absence and handles unchanged producer identity. There is cleanup
overlap, not a claim that the two proposals are unrelated. This narrower scope
is explained in the [#49238 discussion](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49238#issuecomment-5552206777). @YannikHinteregger, I would appreciate
your feedback on the overlap with #50047 and whether consolidation is preferable.

#52232 is a separate, necessary HMA fail-closed fix and is **not included here**.
Recovery alone does not prevent a failed HMA request from generating invalid
output. The integration experiment tested both changes, with attribution to
Tyler Michael Smith, and a small API terminal-error follow-up. #54689 (TTL)
and NIXL #1987 (native UCX race) are outside this patch's scope.

## Validation

### Rebase onto main (2026-09-23)

Rebased onto `8d16ca6cc21931481f6c6f9ec0365874a80c6bb2` without conflicts.
Initialized the three recovery fields in main's new HMA `region_pull_worker`
test fixture after full-import testing exposed the omission. This rebase adds
no production-code changes to the September 20 version. Recovery runs from
`get_transfer_results()` (also covering the legacy `get_finished()` wrapper).
The failure override forwards the current failure set, metric flag, and boolean
handle-release result. Main's wait-for-all-reads and notify-only/full-cache-hit
behavior is preserved; the obsolete descriptor-fixture changes were dropped.

Executed in isolated H20 containers, with full vLLM Python imports:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Focused recovery tests, mocked NIXL boundary | 18 passed |
| Five connector files, `-m cpu_test` | 357 passed, 224 deselected |
| Same existing CPU cases on main, excluding recovery tests | 339 passed |
| Eight selected recovery/control cases on main | 3 expected assertion failures, 5 passed |
| Real NIXL UCX, 1 MiB CPU and GPU buffers | Both passed |

The 18 recovery cases are included in 357. The negative control replaces only
`pull_worker.py` with main's file; the tests and environment are otherwise the
same. The three failures are behavioral assertions, not import errors.

Runtime: NIXL 1.4.1, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Python 3.12.3. The rebased Python
checkout used native extensions from the existing vLLM
`0.29.1rc1.dev422+gd05da62e9` image, not a fresh CUDA build of main.
The native probe keeps the peer alive, deliberately removes local metadata,
observes the stale-read error, invokes patched cleanup, and explicitly reloads
the same agent's metadata for a byte-checked read. Healthy-peer reads still work.
Automatic handshake behavior is covered by pytest; this batch is **not** a new
model-serving/accuracy run, natural-disconnect reproduction, or NVLink/RDMA claim.

Pre-commit (including mypy), Ruff, `compileall`, and `git diff --check` passed.
Earlier setup/download failures and the pre-fix fixture failures are not counted

```bash

Real serving validation used isolated TP1 P/D, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731,
NIXL 1.3.2, fp8 HMA KV, eager mode, and `UCX_TLS=tcp,cuda_copy` with the existing

title: [Perf] DiffusionGemma: one-pass sampler statistics kernel
body:
## Purpose

Followup to https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57250 - helps decoding for diffusiongemma in both text and structured answer mode (the latter only at high concurrency, the former in all cases I've found).

A custom diffusiongemma Triton kernel: 

 - one program per logits row
 - does an online max and sum in one pass
 - draws Gumbel noise inline from Philox instead of materializing a noise tensor
 - writes the softmax once in the embedding dtype (only when self-conditioning will read it)

Replaces _compiled_sample_step's older process which was several fused kernels that performed:

 - Cast the logits to fp32 and divide every element by the request's temperature.
 - Draw a uniform random tensor the same size as the logits, turn it into Gumbel noise with two logs, add it to the scaled logits, and take the argmax of that for the sample.
 - Take the argmax of the scaled logits themselves for the committed token.
 - Compute log_softmax over each row, exponentiate it to get the probabilities, multiply the two and sum for the entropy.
 - Cast the probabilities to bf16 for the self-conditioning matmul.

(each of those is at least one read and often one write of a [4096, 262144] fp32 tensor at concurrency 32)

## Test Plan

tbd

title: [Bugfix] Honor safetensors index tensor assignments
body:
## Purpose

**Symptom:** loading a TP4 Qwen3.8 Flash Next AWQ checkpoint (222,747 tensors) produced wrong weights. The checkpoint reuses 33 official PLE shards, from which its index selects only 129 tensors — but those files also store 1,024 unindexed FP8 expert tensors, some carrying names the index assigns to *different* AWQ shards. Those stale tensors were loaded and silently overwrote the correct ones.

**Root cause:** a safetensors index assigns each tensor name to exactly one shard. `DefaultModelLoader` uses `weight_map` only to filter the shard *file* list, then hands those files to the standard safetensors iterator, which yields *every* tensor stored in each file. The per-file assignment is never enforced, so any checkpoint that intentionally reuses a shard containing extra tensors loads them.

**Fix:** treat `weight_map` as a per-file tensor allowlist. `_prepare_weights` now also returns the index's per-shard tensor sets, and the iterators drop tensors the index did not assign to that shard.

The allowlist is only built when it is actually needed: `get_safetensors_index_weights_by_file` compares each selected shard's stored tensor names against its index assignment and returns `None` unless some shard really does store unindexed tensors. Detection reads safetensors headers via `safe_open(...).keys()`, never tensor data, and returns as soon as the first mismatching shard is found. So ordinary sharded checkpoints — and checkpoints with no index at all — keep every existing loader path unchanged, including the accelerated backends.

Coverage per path:

- default/lazy and torchao: filtered inside `safe_open` before `get_tensor`, so unindexed tensors are never materialized.
- eager and multithreaded: the shard is decoded as a unit, so unindexed tensors are dropped immediately after decode and never reach weight loading. Correct, but without the memory saving of the lazy paths.
- A shard absent from the index raises rather than loading unfiltered.

`fastsafetensors` and `instanttensor` cannot filter within a shard at all. Rather than let them silently bypass the index, reused-shard checkpoints fall back to the filtered standard iterator with a warning. Ordinary indexed checkpoints are unaffected and keep using these backends.

**Duplicate-work check:** no open vLLM PR implements per-file index tensor filtering. Searched `safetensors index` and `model loader tensor filter`; nearby loader PRs address EP filtering or other formats, not this index contract.

**AI assistance:** OpenAI Codex assisted with implementation, tests, and PR preparation. I supplied the production reproducer, reviewed every changed line, and ran the tests below.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_filter_duplicate_safetensors.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py -vv

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_ep_weight_filter.py \
  -k EpFilterOnSyntheticMoeWeights -vv

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/model_loader/default_loader.py \
  vllm/model_executor/model_loader/weight_utils.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_filter_duplicate_safetensors.py \
  tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_registry.py
```

The regression builds two shards sharing a `main.weight`: the indexed shard holds `1.0`, the reused shard holds stale `99.0` plus an unindexed tensor. It asserts only `main.weight=1.0` and `ple.weight=2.0` are yielded, across `auto` and explicit `safetensors` load formats and default/lazy/eager strategies, plus a separate case for `enable_multithread_load` (sorted before asserting, since `as_completed` does not preserve file order).

Three further tests pin when filtering engages at all: an ordinary sharded checkpoint and a checkpoint with no index must both produce no allowlist, while the reused-shard checkpoint must produce the expected per-shard sets.

## Test Result

- `test_filter_duplicate_safetensors.py`: `12 passed`.
- `test_registry.py`: `6 passed`.
- Existing synthetic EP iterator regression: `5 passed`.
- Pre-commit on all changed files: passed (ruff, ruff format, mypy, SPDX).
- Negative control: with the allowlist built unconditionally, `test_prepare_weights_skips_filtering_for_ordinary_checkpoint` fails with `assert {...: {'main.weight'}, ...: {'ple.weight'}} is None`, confirming the test pins the accelerated-backend regression rather than passing vacuously.
- Real checkpoint: the equivalent change completed TP4 loading of the 222,747-tensor Qwen3.8 Flash Next AWQ model and kept all 1,024 unindexed FP8 expert tensors out of weight loading. That run predates this PR's shard-header detection; the isolated validation above was run on CPU without a GPU.
- No model compute path changed.

title: [Bugfix] Validate token budget after disabling chunked prefill
body:
## Purpose

Models with non-causal attention disable chunked prefill only after KV-cache specifications are collected in EngineCore. At that point, SchedulerConfig has already validated max_num_batched_tokens while chunked prefill was still enabled.

If max_num_batched_tokens is smaller than max_model_len, a prompt larger than the scheduling budget can therefore remain in the waiting queue indefinitely. This was reproduced with HRM-Text-1B using max_model_len=4096 and the default max_num_batched_tokens=2048: 2048-token prompts completed, while 2049-token prompts never became schedulable.

Re-run SchedulerConfig.verify_max_model_len after disabling chunked prefill for non-causal attention. Invalid configurations now fail during engine startup with the existing actionable error instead of accepting requests that cannot be scheduled.

## Test Plan

- Add a CPU-only regression test with a non-causal KV-cache specification and an initially enabled chunked-prefill configuration.
- Verify that late disabling of chunked prefill revalidates the scheduling token budget.
- Run Ruff lint and format checks on both changed files.

## Test Result

```text
python -m pytest -q --confcutdir=tests/v1/engine tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_init.py
1 passed in 1.11s

ruff check vllm/v1/engine/core.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_init.py
All checks passed!

ruff format --check vllm/v1/engine/core.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core_init.py
2 files already formatted
```

Manual Ascend reproduction before this patch:

- max_model_len=4096, max_num_batched_tokens=2048
- 2048-token prompt: completed
- 2049-token prompt: remained waiting for more than 120 seconds
- Explicitly setting max_num_batched_tokens=4096 allowed 2049, 3000, 4000, and 4095-token prompts to complete

This validation is platform-independent; Ascend was used only to discover and reproduce the scheduler state.

title: [Perf] DiffusionGemma: constrained reads over the request's logprob_token_ids
body:
Adds a new `diffusion_constrained` property that allows us to reduce the amount of work needed when performing constrained diffusion (ie: structured answers). Experimental results: approx. 25% faster. Followup to #57250 ## Purpose By passing `logprob_token_ids` it means that you already know the possible answer set. `diffusion_constrained: true` allows us to save work - the unembedding is a GEMM over the K gathered rows of the tied embedding instead of all 262k, the sampler runs in K-space (Gumbel sample, argmax, entropy, convergence), and maps picks back through the set, and the self-conditioning soft embed multiplies K-space probs by the K embedding rows. Overall we save ~25% in my local experiments on a GB10.

The timings, warm engine, fresh prompts per arm, two runs of each arm shown as a range. Single-slot reads, one step, canvas 48:
