title: [BugFix][Core] Promote parked skipped_waiting requests under saturation
body:
## Purpose

Fix the promotion-starvation mechanism analyzed in #53130.

Requests parked in `skipped_waiting` (`WAITING_FOR_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_GRAMMAR` / `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` / `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ`) are only promoted while the waiting loop of `schedule()` traverses them, and that loop stops on the token-budget and `max_num_seqs` capacity checks. On steps where running requests consume the entire token budget (e.g. long chunked prefills) or occupy every request slot, the loop never reaches the parked requests, so:

- a parked request whose grammar has finished compiling is never promoted, and
- a parked request whose grammar compile **failed** is never detected and never terminated.

Under sustained saturation both conditions hold indefinitely: parked requests are stuck until a restart while the engine reports healthy (the incident in #53130). This matches "mechanism A" reproduced at the scheduler level by @Ddhjx-code, and implements the fix direction sketched by @kenhaesler in the same thread (sketch 5).

Change: after the waiting loop, promote the requests it left unvisited in `skipped_waiting`. Everything the loop did traverse has already had its promotion check and sits in `step_skipped_waiting`, so on a normal step the sweep does no work; only a starved remainder is visited, and only when starvation occurs. Promotion order is irrelevant to the sweep (it only advances state; scheduling order is still decided by the queue), so it uses a new `RequestQueue.iter_unordered()` that walks the underlying deque/heap without copying or sorting — `PriorityRequestQueue.__iter__` copies and re-heapifies the queue, which is not acceptable on the hot path under `--scheduling-policy priority`. Promotion is idempotent (state-gated by `_is_blocked_waiting_status`), and promoted requests stay in `skipped_waiting` so cross-queue FCFS/priority order (`_select_waiting_queue_for_scheduling`) is unchanged.

Companion: #55931 makes the grammar-future poll non-blocking (split out of this PR at review request); with it, each promotion check is O(1).

Out of scope: admission of new requests while the token budget is saturated is unchanged (inherent chunked-prefill semantics), as is the eviction/re-prefill feeder discussed in the issue.

**Not a duplicate**: #53321 adds a timeout for `WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ` only (orthogonal and complementary — it handles a status that has no promotion path, while this PR fixes the gates that starve promotion for all parked statuses). #45406 un-strands `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` requests stuck behind an unschedulable queue head — a different mechanism (scan aborted mid-loop) from this one (loop never entered).

## Test Plan

TDD: the regression tests were written first and fail on unmodified `main` for the expected reasons; they pass with this change.

```
pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py       # full scheduler suite
pytest tests/v1/core/test_request_queue.py   # new: iter_unordered on both queue types
```

New tests (CPU-only, no model load):

- `test_parked_grammar_promotion_when_token_budget_saturated[fcfs|priority]` — a mid-prefill request saturates the budget; a grammar-ready parked request must still be promoted (the `priority` variant exercises the sweep over a `PriorityRequestQueue`).
- `test_grammar_compile_failure_detected_when_token_budget_saturated` — same saturation; a failed compile must reach `FINISHED_ERROR` within one step.
- `test_parked_grammar_promotion_when_capacity_saturated` — same, with `max_num_seqs` saturated instead of the budget.
- `test_iter_unordered_yields_every_request_once[fcfs|priority]` — the new queue method yields every request exactly once without consuming the queue.

## Test Result

- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: **167 passed**, 1 failed — `test_async_scheduling_pp_allows_rescheduling_with_output_placeholders` fails identically on unmodified `main` and is unrelated to this change (rebased onto c55e15a44e).
- `tests/v1/core/test_request_queue.py`: **2 passed**.
- `pre-commit run`: all hooks passed.
- Model evals: not applicable — this changes scheduler liveness only; token sampling and outputs on the scheduled path are untouched.

title: fix(docker): build lmcache from source in KV-connectors images to match shipped torch ABI
body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53424

`INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true` images install LMCache from a PyPI wheel that is compiled against a single pinned torch ABI (torch 2.11 at the time of writing). When the vLLM image ships a newer torch (2.13 in v0.27.1), the wheel install **succeeds**, but its precompiled `lmcache/c_ops*.so` fails to load at runtime due to the C++ ABI mismatch, silently falling back to slow torch-baseline ops. Because the wheel install succeeds, the Dockerfile's source-build fallback never runs.

This PR makes the lmcache install path deterministic:

- `docker/Dockerfile` (KV-connectors stage): split `lmcache` out of the batched `--no-build` requirements install and install it separately with `--no-binary lmcache --no-build-isolation-package lmcache`, so uv builds the sdist against the torch version actually shipped in the image. The other connectors keep the existing wheel path.
- `.buildkite/scripts/install-kv-connectors.sh` (CI twin of that stage): same change, keeping image and CI installs consistent.

The apt build-deps block (`BUILD_PKGS`) now always runs for this stage since lmcache is always built from source; cleanup logic is unchanged.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

- Issue #53424 has no linked or referenced PR (checked via issue timeline cross-references and open PR search for "lmcache"/"53424").
- No other open PR touches `requirements/kv_connectors.txt`, the KV-connectors stage of `docker/Dockerfile`, or `.buildkite/scripts/install-kv-connectors.sh`.

## AI assistance disclosure

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude, via Hermes agent). The submitting author reviewed every changed line, verified the dependency-resolution behavior locally as described below, and understands the full diff end-to-end.

## Test Plan

- `bash -n .buildkite/scripts/install-kv-connectors.sh` passes.
- Flag semantics verified with uv in a clean container (torch installed, no GPU needed to observe artifact selection):
  - baseline `uv pip install 'lmcache==0.5.3'` selects the prebuilt wheel (`lmcache-0.5.3-cp312-cp312-manylinux_2_27_x86_64...whl`), which ships `lmcache/c_ops.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so`;
  - adding `--no-binary lmcache --no-build-isolation-package lmcache` forces the sdist (`lmcache-0.5.3.tar.gz`) source build (observed entering the c_ops compile step; that compile requires CUDA headers, so full compilation is exercised by the KV-connectors image build CI).
- `typos` hook clean on both changed files.
- The CI job building the KV-connectors image exercises both changed paths end-to-end.

## Test Result

- Wheel-vs-source selection confirmed locally: default → `.whl`; with new flags → source build started.
- `typos docker/Dockerfile .buildkite/scripts/install-kv-connectors.sh` → clean.
- Runtime confirmation of `c_ops` loading under matching ABI will come from the KV-connectors image build + GPU CI on this PR.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Drop -1 sentinels when building the ragged sparse-MLA indices
body:
## Purpose
The sparse MLA kernel (pa_sparse_prefill_opus) currently seg. faults when -1 sentinels happen within accessed region as there is no check for it.

 `combine_topk_swa_indices` reserves top-k columns from a position-derived count and writes `-1` wherever a candidate fails its validity test, and `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` copies the row prefix verbatim, sentinels included.
 
 ## The fix

Make the ragged index stream sentinel-free at the point it is built, so no consumer can dereference one. `build_ragged_indices_from_dense` now keeps only valid entries per row, and `indptr` counts those. Semantically identical, skipping an index and masking it out give the same attention result.

This is layout-agnostic: it does not matter whether the sentinels are leading, interior or trailing. Getting rid of 
"-1" indices should not cause any side-effects as they are supposed to be masked out anyway.

## Tests

GSM8K 5-shot shares a few-shot prefix, so with prefix caching on (the default)
it generates partial hits:

title: [Core][Sleep Mode] Add opt-in preparation of first-sleep backup buffers
body:
## Purpose

The first level-1 sleep can spend most of its time allocating pinned host buffers for weight backup. Applications that put the first sleep on a latency-sensitive path may prefer to pay that allocation cost during startup.

This adds `VLLM_SLEEP_PREPARE_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES` (default `0`, disabled). With CUDA and the CuMem sleep backend enabled, the worker prepares empty weight-backup buffers after warmup, before becoming ready. The first sleep still copies the **current** GPU weights, including updates made after preparation. Prepared capacity is consumed once; later sleeps use the existing allocator/cache behavior.

The budget covers the complete set of prepared weight buffers, conservatively rounding each allocation up to a power of two. Preparation is skipped if that set exceeds the budget. Allocation changes, reload, discard, level-2 sleep and shutdown cancel unused preparation. The change is limited to the allocator, worker lifecycle, configuration, documentation and tests; it introduces no new public RPC.

This trades earlier host-memory residency and longer startup for a shorter first sleep. It does not remove the allocation cost or speed up weight copying. The budget is per worker, **not** a process-wide or machine-wide pinned-memory limit; existing host cache and other allocations are outside it. Cancellation drops references without flushing the global host cache.

Error handling is deliberately conservative: `torch.OutOfMemoryError` and `MemoryError` cancel preparation and fall back to ordinary sleep; other exceptions release prepared references and propagate. In the tested PyTorch version, CUDA pinned-allocation exhaustion can surface as `torch.AcceleratorError` and fail startup. This option does not guarantee recovery from every allocation failure or an OS out-of-memory kill.

Related work checked: #55206 releases host cache after wake, and #57629 changes wake remapping order for unified memory. This PR instead prepares capacity before the first sleep. It neither implements nor depends on the graph offload/discard mechanisms in #56373 or #57899. No open PR implementing the same startup preparation was found in the duplicate-work search. If another policy clears the host cache later, this change does not replenish prepared buffers or avoid the next allocation cost.

## Test Plan

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/worker/test_sleep_mode_backend.py -q
python -m pytest tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py -q -s \
  -k 'prepared_sleep_backups or basic_cumem'
```

The unit tests cover disabled preparation, rounded budgets, partial allocation failure, unexpected error propagation, stale allocation identity/handles, cancellation and worker lifecycle hooks. The GPU test changes weights **after** preparation, disallows new CPU backup allocation during the first sleep, verifies the updated values after wake, and then exercises another sleep/wake cycle. Injected allocation exceptions do not emulate real host-memory exhaustion.

For the model experiments, both the unchanged baseline and this candidate used one H20, FP16, TP=1, the V2 runner, no `torch.compile`, FULL graph capture sizes `[1, 2, 4, 8]`, synchronous scheduling, `max_model_len=256`, `max_num_seqs=8`, `max_num_batched_tokens=256`, prefix caching disabled, and `gpu_memory_utilization=0.8`. The candidate used `VLLM_SLEEP_PREPARE_BACKUP_MAX_BYTES=137438953472` (128 GB, with 1 GB = 2^30 bytes); the baseline used `0`. This is the configured budget, not measured physical pinned residency.

Each model/configuration had three independent startups and 20 level-1 sleep/wake cycles per startup. A separate local benchmark recorded startup, first sleep, and subsequent sleep/wake times without internal timing instrumentation. After every wake, the first generation and five subsequent generations were compared with the same process's initial token IDs: four fixed prompts, temperature 0, seed 42, `ignore_eos=True`, 32 generated tokens per prompt. These are controlled output-regression checks, not a broad accuracy evaluation. The benchmark script is separate from the tests included in this diff.

## Test Result

Local H20 validation: driver 580.126.09, Python 3.12.3, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130. Baseline: `e9f169d16b`. The native wheel was built from `97dc6b19d2`; a source comparison found no differences between these revisions in `csrc`, `cmake`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `requirements`, `setup.py`, `vllm/_custom_ops.py`, or `vllm/third_party`. These results are local validation, not upstream CI results.

- Unit tests: **29 passed**.
- CUDA allocator tests: **2 passed, 19 deselected**.
- Model comparisons: **18 independent startups, 360 cycles** across baseline and candidate; all controlled output checks passed.
- Targeted pre-commit checks passed.

Times below are seconds. Each cell is the median across three independent startups. For subsequent sleeps, each startup contributes the median of cycles 2–20. “Startup + first sleep” is summed per run before taking the median.

| Model (FP16, TP=1) | First sleep, baseline → prepared | Startup + first sleep, baseline → prepared | Subsequent sleep, baseline → prepared |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B | 0.618 → 0.059 | 16.209 → 16.275 | 0.057 → 0.057 |
| Qwen3-8B | 6.193 → 0.343 | 23.905 → 23.747 | 0.343 → 0.343 |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 | 21.899 → 1.160 | 48.201 → 48.150 | 1.159 → 1.159 |

The data supports moving the first allocation cost out of sleep; it does not demonstrate a comparable reduction in total startup-plus-sleep time or a subsequent-cycle speedup. Multi-GPU, unified-memory systems and real host-exhaustion recovery were not validated. Some model runs on both trees emitted multiprocessing semaphore-cleanup warnings at exit; they returned exit code 0 and are not described as warning-free runs.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, local experiment execution and review. The author is responsible for the submitted change; these results are not a claim that every test was personally executed by the author.

[Bugfix][DSv4.1] Use 64-token sparse-MLA pages on SM120
body:
## Draft — dependency and duplicate-work review required

Partially addresses #56461 / #56702. **Do not merge as a standalone complete SM120 fix.**

### Scope

The proposed change selects a 64-token sparse-MLA/indexer kernel page on SM120 and a 64-token SWA cache page instead of treating SM120 like SM100. The three backend declarations are in:

- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/sparse_mla.py`
- `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/nvidia/flashinfer_sparse.py`
- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`

The SWA allocation is in `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/attention.py`. Other architecture branches are intended to remain unchanged.

For DeepSeek-V4.1 ratio-1/ratio-2 layers, a 64-token kernel block yields 64/32-state indexer pages. The pinned DeepGEMM **SM120 FP8** path still rejects page32; allowing it is a separate dependency, not something this Python patch fixes.

### Duplicate-work check (2026-09-17)

Re-read #56461 / #56702 and checked open PRs referencing them and SM120 block geometry. Existing #56509 substantially overlaps this PR (including the SWA and backend declarations). I am keeping this PR draft and am not opening another geometry PR or claiming this one is non-duplicative. The two should be consolidated with the maintainers before further advancement; a smaller test suite or helper extraction alone is not a material reason to duplicate the fix.

The **separate** FP8 page32 kernel gap is now proposed as vllm-project/DeepGEMM#14. This is distinct from the vLLM geometry PRs.

### Required dependency integration

1. Merge/resolve the DeepGEMM FP8 page32 support, then update both `cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake` and `tools/install_deepgemm.sh` to the accepted fork commit. Both currently pin `a6bbb8000161c0dc3a85a0300a905f76898a7913`.
2. FlashInfer dual-cache prefill needs 32-token extra pages. Existing flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5174 already addresses this with tests; no duplicate PR is being opened.
3. The older deployed FlashInfer 0.6.18 needed a local `(8,1152)` decode specialization. Inspection of current FlashInfer main shows runtime top-k in the DSV4 decode launcher, so the old fixed-specialization workaround should not be proposed unchanged upstream.

### Corrections to the earlier description

- Withdraw the claims that default flags and explicit block sizes 128/256 have been verified. The actual serving experiment used **`--block-size 64`**; that does not establish the full manager-block/kernel-block compatibility matrix.
- The committed second change includes an early constructor block-size check. It is removed in the local working tree because validation needs to respect the manager/kernel block distinction and initialization order; that removal has NOT yet been pushed. This remains a review item, not a completed fix.
- Local test corrections also remain unpushed. The unrelated exploratory Triton implementation and its tests are not part of this PR and are not being added.
- Do not attribute the old image's `topk=1152` to DSpark without tracing its metadata. #56461 documents the image-prefix/window contribution; the earlier DSpark-only explanation was not established.

### Validation and provenance

An earlier **backport** of the geometry changes, together with a DeepGEMM 2.6.1 page32 backport and FlashInfer decode/prefill patches, started on 8x RTX PRO 5000 72GB (SM120) with TP8/EP, FP8 KV, DSpark K=5, `--block-size 64`, and `--max-model-len 262144`.

The recorded pod was Ready with no restarts at the end of that experiment. Pod-local `/v1/models` succeeded, and `/v1/chat/completions` returned `323` for `17*19`. This is only a short serving smoke test, not a precision evaluation, long-context validation, or proof of correctness of this PR head against current dependency pins.

The separately tested DeepGEMM fork patch has 72 added correctness cases and 10 existing cases passing on SM120; details and limitations are in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#14.

Submission-time `git diff --check` passed on the local vLLM branch/worktree diff. This update changes the PR description only; it does not assert that this PR head's unit tests, full pre-commit suite or current-main end-to-end run were rerun. Human review, applicable test reproduction, model evaluation and dependency-closed build validation are outstanding.

### Background: captured block-geometry failure

Archived log excerpt from the old serving image, with explicit `--block-size 64` (2026-09-17). Line numbers are those of the image, not this PR head; only grep/process/timestamp prefixes have been removed:

```text
File "/usr/local/lib/python3.12/dist-packages/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py", line 130, in init_attn_backend
```

title: [CI] Split (H200 MIG 35GB / MI355) Quantized Models into GPTQ Marlin, AWQ and Other Schemes jobs
body:
## What

Split `quantized-models-test` into three named jobs: GPTQ Marlin, AWQ, and Other Schemes. Each runs whole test files in a single pytest process, replacing the earlier five-way hash shard. One-file edit to `.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml`; no test bodies, parameters or markers change.

## Old

```text
(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantized Models   [quantized-models-test]
└── pytest models/quantization                         (one job, ~42–60m on recent main)
    mirror: (MI355) Quantized Models, same command
```

## New

| Buildkite job | key | whole coverage units | mirror |
|---|---|---|---|
| `(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantized Models / GPTQ Marlin` | `quantized-models-gptq-marlin` | `test_gptq_marlin.py` | none: every case skips on ROCm |
| `(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantized Models / AWQ` | `quantized-models-awq` | `test_awq.py` | `amd-quantized-models-awq`, same file |
| `(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantized Models / Other Schemes` | `quantized-models-other` | `test_fp8.py`, `test_fp8_per_channel.py`, `test_gpt_oss.py`, `test_mimo_v2_qkv_shard.py`, `test_modelopt.py`, `test_mxfp4.py`, `test_mxfp8.py`, `test_nvfp4.py`, `test_per_token_kv_cache.py` | `amd-quantized-models-other`, same files |

`quantized-models-test` is retired; its coverage is exactly the union of the three new jobs on the primary lane.

## Notes

- **Why named jobs instead of the hash shard:** those two files are the two largest units in the directory. The five-way shard also ran about 13 extra worker-minutes, because each replica repeated model loading and compilation that one process shares across cases. Keeping each file group in one process removes that duplication; only the per-job checkout and container start is added.
- **GPTQ Marlin stays one job and is at the 20-minute target, not under it.** The file measured 16–24 minutes whole across four recent `main` runs, at or above 20 in three of them, and a flat file cannot be divided without splitting it. The cost is in the test itself: each of its six cases starts two engines over 1–2B models, and `flaky(reruns=3)` can repeat a case. That is being raised with its owners separately.
- **Mirror-lane coverage:** the two mirror jobs claim every file except `test_gptq_marlin.py`, so the mirror no longer collects that file's six skip-only cases. Nothing that ran before stops running.
- Earlier validation comments describe the superseded five-way shard. AI assistance was used.

## Expected runtime and overhead

Predictions from per-file pytest time in the unsharded job on four recent `main` builds ([#89713](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89713), [#89666](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89666), [#90455](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90455), [#90426](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90426)); per-job overhead from the latest validation build [#90445](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90445).

| job (primary lane) | pytest (predicted) | running wall (predicted) | non-pytest overhead | main overhead cause |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GPTQ Marlin | 16–24m, median ~20m | ~17–25m | ~0.5–1m | checkout and container start |
| AWQ | 9–17m | ~10–18m | ~0.5–1m | checkout and container start |
| Other Schemes | 16–20m | ~17–21m | ~0.5–1m | checkout and container start |

- **Aggregate cost:** the three jobs run the same per-file work as the unsharded job, so the prediction is the unsharded total plus two extra job startups, about **+1–2 worker-minutes**, compared with +13 for the five-way shard.
- **Mirror lane:** both mirror jobs predicted well under the target, with aggregate cost within about a minute of the unsharded mirror job.
- **Critical path:** from a 42–60 minute single job to roughly 20 minutes, set by GPTQ Marlin.

title: [Feature] [KV Offload] Support sharing SimpleCPUOffload prefix caches across local DP replicas
body:
## Summary

Implement #58240. `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` currently keeps an independent CPU prefix cache 
in each DP replica. When a request is routed to another local replica, that replica recomputes
a prefix even though a completed CPU copy is available. This change adds an opt-in
`cpu_offload_shared=true` mode that lets local DP replicas reuse completed CPU prefixes.

This builds on [#37160](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/37160), which
introduced `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` and its private per-replica CPU cache.
This PR extends that connector with opt-in cross-DP publication and lookup; it
does not change the native offloader's per-replica semantics.

## Configuration

Add `cpu_offload_shared`, a JSON boolean in `kv_connector_extra_config`,
defaulting to `false`. Set it to `true` to share completed CPU prefixes with
compatible DP replicas in the same IPC namespace and distributed DP group.
Leaving it unset retains the existing private CPU pools.

The CPU capacity remains a per-worker budget: `cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank`
reserves each worker's write partition. Corresponding local DP peers can read
published entries from one another's partitions, while writes remain owned by
the worker that allocates the slot. For example, two local DP peers configured
with 8 GiB each expose a 16 GiB node-local region for published slots and
metadata; this is shared visibility, not a dynamically rebalanced write pool.

Pass the following to `--kv-transfer-config`:

```json
{
  "kv_connector": "SimpleCPUOffloadConnector",
  "kv_role": "kv_both",
  "kv_connector_extra_config": {
    "cpu_offload_shared": true,
    "cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank": 8589934592,
    "lazy_offload": false
  }
}
```

Shared mode requires the CPU backend, eager offloading (`lazy_offload=false`),
prefix caching, compatible model/KV layouts and reproducible prefix hashes.
It supports fixed MoE DP groups and TP, with `PP=DCP=PCP=1` and no LoRA or
elastic EP. Each TP coordinate shares its own KV shard with corresponding
local DP peers. Cross-node transfer requires a network-capable connector or tier.

## Implementation

Use the existing `SharedOffloadRegion` type, as established for native
`CPUOffloadingSpec` storage by
[#50094](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50094), and the DMA/`BlockPool`
interfaces for storage and transfers; the cross-DP publication index, locking
and reader reference semantics are new code in this PR. Each writer owns a
fixed partition, and the shared pool does not dynamically move free write slots
between workers. Lookup and pinning use `flock` on the metadata region's descriptor;
prefixes are published after all worker stores complete, and reader references
prevent slot reuse until peer loads finish. The workers use the existing DMA
backend for transfers.

The rebased base also includes the upstream prefix-cacheable-group handling from
[#56810](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56810). This PR consumes that
group eligibility behavior and adds cross-DP publication; it does not duplicate
the upstream hybrid-model bug fix.

| Production file | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/simple_cpu_offload_connector.py` | Parse and validate `cpu_offload_shared`; connect worker and scheduler handshakes. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_offload.py` (new) | Discover local DP peers, verify cache identity/layout, and allocate shared KV views per TP coordinate. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/shared_block_pool.py` (new) | Add shared hash publication, slot versions, locking and peer read references to `BlockPool`. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/metadata.py` | Define the worker-to-scheduler shared-pool handshake. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` | Attach the shared pool and synchronize scheduler lookup, allocation and completion handling. |
| `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/worker.py` | Allocate/pin shared CPU views, expose the handshake and release mappings on shutdown. |

Tests and documentation changed:

- `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py`
- `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py`
- `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`

## Why this is not a duplicate

The following open PRs address adjacent behavior, but none adds cross-DP CPU
prefix publication and peer loading for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`:

- [#53073](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53073) targets shared mmap
  startup ownership and cleanup. This PR targets completed-prefix visibility
  and safe peer reads after asynchronous DMA. It follows the mmap lifetime
  rules but adds a different metadata publication and reader-lifetime protocol.
- [#53474](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53474) targets node-local
  sizing and worker placement for native `OffloadingConnector`. This PR targets
  node-local prefix reuse for `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, including one pool
  per TP coordinate. The connectors, allocation path and target behavior differ;
  this PR has no code dependency on #53474.
- [#47324](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47324) targets a GPU
  load/compute stream race inside one worker. This PR targets host-side slot
  ownership when another worker reads a completed prefix. It does not implement
  the open PR's load-path stream-ordering fix; the two changes are complementary,
  and this PR adds separate cross-worker reader references.
- [#57418](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57418) targets concurrent
  requests waiting for the same in-flight load inside one engine. This PR
  targets completed CPU prefixes shared by different DP engines; it does not
  change connector-side coalescing of simultaneous loads.
- [#43483](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43483) targets routing a
  request to the DP rank that already owns a GPU prefix. This PR targets actual
  CPU KV publication and peer loading when routing selects another replica;
  routing-only ownership hints cannot provide that transfer.
- [#57422](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57422) targets inode-safe
  unlinking of existing shared mmap files. This PR uses the existing mmap
  lifetime model but adds cross-DP prefix metadata and reader references.
- [#54743](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54743) targets which KV
  groups receive offload configuration. This PR keeps the existing group
  eligibility rules and adds sharing only for groups already handled by
  `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`.
- [#52921](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52921) targets aligning
  scheduler and worker pool sizes across PP/speculative workers. This PR keeps
  the existing per-worker capacity calculation and adds node-local sharing
  after those capacities agree.

## Validation

The rebased source is `aeab9b0666ee14962901f20eadc08f983d8e6bb1`, based on
upstream `97dc6b19d2fe92b794b49e684677a2e1a8b2c540`.

On the rebased source, the focused scheduler, KV-event and connector suite passed
**87 tests** on the DGX Spark CUDA environment:

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py -q
```

The suite includes shared scheduler publication, reader pinning, delayed
publication, metadata mismatch rejection, non-prefix-cacheable groups and the
TP configuration acceptance test. Ruff and the applicable pre-commit checks pass.

The model validation used two DGX Spark hosts, each with one NVIDIA GB10
(SM121), CUDA 13.2, driver 580.173.02, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu132 and
FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1. Because only two physical GPUs were available, the
model tests used a diagnostic topology with two logical workers per GPU. This
is functional evidence, not independent-GPU performance evidence; PyTorch
requires NCCL processes to have exclusive GPU access.

For the TP2×DP2 diagnostic, the four logical workers were mapped as follows:

| Logical launch rank | DP | TP | Host | HTTP port |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| 0 | 0 | 0 | DGX Spark 1 | DP0 endpoint |
| 1 | 0 | 1 | DGX Spark 2 | Headless |
| 2 | 1 | 0 | DGX Spark 1 | DP1 endpoint |
| 3 | 1 | 1 | DGX Spark 2 | Headless |

The TP shard probe restored distinct TP0 and TP1 byte patterns through their
corresponding local DP groups and passed the all-shard publication barrier.
The full model run used DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DSpark K5 probabilistic
sampling, CUDA graphs, Rust frontend, RoCE and 2 GiB CPU/GPU KV capacity per
worker.

### Experiment setup

Use the same source commit and model weights for both modes. The launch below
shows the TP2×DP2 settings used for the TP shard and recovery probe. Run one
process for each logical launch rank in the table above: ranks 0 and 2 on the
first host, and ranks 1 and 3 on the second. Here `--nnodes 4` counts four logical
launches across two physical hosts; the DP size is 2.

Set `MODEL` to the
[DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731)
weights, then set `NODE_RANK`, `DP_RANK`, `DP_PORT` and the coordinator ports and
address for the deployment. Use distinct HTTP ports for DP0 and DP1, one shared
DP RPC port, and one shared TP master port. Logical ranks 1 and 3 are headless.
The host-specific network environment is intentionally omitted.

```bash
KV_CONFIG='{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_offload_shared":true,"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":2147483648,"lazy_offload":false}}'

PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:False \
.venv/bin/python -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve "$MODEL" \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port "$DP_PORT" \
  --data-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-rank "$DP_RANK" \
  --data-parallel-external-lb \
  --data-parallel-address "$HEAD_IP" --data-parallel-rpc-port "$DP_RPC_PORT" \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel --enable-ep-weight-filter \
  --nnodes 4 --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \
  --master-addr "$HEAD_IP" --master-port "$TP_MASTER_PORT" \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --trust-remote-code --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.47 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 2147483648 \
  --max-num-seqs 16 --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 64 \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["all"]}' \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune":false}' \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-caching-hash-algo sha256 \
  --enable-prompt-tokens-details --per-request-spec-decode-metrics detailed \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --kv-transfer-config "$KV_CONFIG"
```

Add `--headless` for logical ranks 1 and 3. For the private control, change only
`cpu_offload_shared` to `false`. Keep `expandable_segments:False` in both
connector runs because the upstream KV-connector guard rejects
`expandable_segments:True`.

External DP routing gives one configured endpoint port to DP0 and another to DP1
on the coordinator host; the TP followers are headless. Send case `i` to DP rank
`i % 2` for the cold phase and to `1 - (i % 2)` for the peer phase, preserving
the prompt and `cache_salt`. The port selects the replica; it is not part of the
prefix hash.
Between phases, wait for requests and stores to finish, then POST to
`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=true` on both endpoints for a cold run, or
`/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false` to clear only GPU caches before peer
replay. Check that both resets succeed before issuing requests. Confirm reuse
with the external CPU-prefix counters.

### Offload correctness and latency

The GPU DMA tests and TP2 shard probe restored distinct TP0/TP1 byte patterns
after peer loads and withheld publication until all TP workers completed their
stores.

#### Performance improvement test

The rebased-source one-shot test used 24 unique approximately 6K-token prefixes,
one in-flight request per endpoint and streaming `max_tokens=1` requests. Each
prefix was populated on its owner, GPU caches were reset, and the prefix was
requested exactly once from its local DP peer.

| Mode | Peer TTFT p50 | Peer TTFT p95 | External transfer | Local compute |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Private | 14.41 s | 15.11 s | 0 / 140,652 | 140,652 |
| Shared | 5.22 s | 7.13 s | 129,024 / 140,652 | 11,628 |

Shared peer TTFT was 63.8% lower in this rebased-source diagnostic run. All 24
peer requests had zero errors, empty outputs, replacement characters,
invalid controls or cold/peer output mismatches. This is a diagnostic result;
the topology with two logical workers per GB10 is not a production throughput
setup.

#### Concurrency stability test

The long-output workload used 16 fixed approximately 6K-token prompts and asked
for eight exact reference lines with `temperature=0`, `seed=0` and
`max_tokens=192`. Cold and peer phases used concurrency 4; C16, C32, C64 and
mixed-eviction phases each sent 64 requests.

| Mode | C16 p50 | C32 p50 | C64 p50 | Full campaign |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Private | 34.09 s | 39.21 s | 45.56 s | 288/288 exact |
| Shared | 32.40 s | 34.93 s | 44.34 s | 288/288 exact |

Both campaigns completed without request errors, token mismatches, empty
outputs, replacement characters or invalid controls. DSpark acceptance remained
between 99.2% and 99.3%. These repeated phases exercise queueing, local reuse and
output integrity; they are not used as the shared-mode performance comparison.

### Accuracy validation

The rebased-source GSM8K smoke used the same 200 five-shot questions,
`temperature=0`, `seed=0`, concurrency 32 and a 512-token output limit:

| Configuration | Correct / 200 | DSpark acceptance |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Private cold | 190 | 63.84% |
| Private peer | 192 | 63.92% |
| Shared cold | 191 | 64.56% |
| Shared peer | 191 | 63.57% |

All 800 requests completed without request errors, empty output, replacement
characters or invalid control characters. Shared and private scores are close in
this rebased-source smoke; this single round is not a statistical equivalence
claim. The TP2×DP2 recovery probe separately passed 8/8 cold and 8/8 peer
requests in both modes with token-exact output; private peer CPU hits were 0 and
shared peer CPU hits were 45,056 tokens.

## AI assistance

The implementation and analysis were assisted with AI and reviewed by human.

title: [Mypy] Fix mypy typing for Qwen and Qianfan models
body:
## Purpose

Address part of [#26533](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/26533) by fixing typing in the Qwen/Qianfan model family and removing `r"vllm/model_executor/models/[qQ]"` from the mypy exclusions. All 24 selected model files are now checked.

The changes cover optional configuration and multimodal fields, tensor/container and cache types, generic processing-info types (including ASR inheritance), MoE mixin attributes, and the realtime async-generator protocol.

Five documented, line-specific typing exceptions preserve existing runtime contracts: four incompatible speculative-drafter/MTP overrides and one instance-local override of a class-level LoRA mapping. No file-wide ignores or replacement exclusions were added.

The branch incorporates upstream `main` at `276db94fb2`. The conflict resolution preserves upstream's multimodal processor interfaces, typed dummy options, ASR position fix, tensor video timestamps, and vision caches. The remaining diff against that revision touches 23 files.

## Reproducer

On upstream main, first remove the Q-model exclusion from `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py`, then run:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --files \
  $(git ls-files 'vllm/model_executor/models/[qQ]*.py') --hook-stage manual
```

The initial baseline was 297 errors in the selected Q-model files on the original base, `7c877062ac`. This is a historical result, not an error count for current main.

## Validation

Rechecked after merging upstream `276db94fb2`:

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main HEAD)
# All applicable hooks passed, including mypy for Python 3.10.

for version in 3.11 3.12 3.13; do
  .venv/bin/pre-commit run "mypy-$version" --files \
    $(git ls-files 'vllm/model_executor/models/[qQ]*.py') \
    vllm/model_executor/models/interfaces.py --hook-stage manual
done
# All passed on all 24 Q-model files plus interfaces.py.
```

Runtime checks used the existing Python 3.12 environment with an editable, precompiled vLLM installation:

```bash
export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-qQ-uv-cache
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu
export VLLM_CACHE_ROOT=/tmp/vllm-qQ-runtime-cache
export HF_HOME=/tmp/vllm-qQ-hf-cache

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python --no-managed-python python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_vl_mrope.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_omni.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_qwen3_asr_mrope.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen2_5_omni_embed.py \
  tests/entrypoints/speech_to_text/transcription/test_qwen3_asr_sanitize_prompt.py \
  -q --tb=short --maxfail=3
# 151 passed.

uv run --no-project --python .venv/bin/python --no-managed-python python -m pytest \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_omni.py \
  tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_qwen3_vl.py \
```

title: [ROCm][Test] Fix DPX/MI355 gfx950 test failures in NPS2 partition mode
body:
## Summary

ROCm MI355 GPUs in DPX mode use NPS2 partitioning — each physical GPU is split into 2 logical partitions (~144 GiB each). When multiple test pods run on the same physical node simultaneously (bin-packing scheduler), tests encounter GPU memory and hardware-specific failures. This PR fixes 3 categories of failures validated by a 400-job DPX stress test.

## Changes

### 1. GPU memory teardown — `tests/basic_correctness/`

**Problem:** On DPX nodes with bin-packing, a prior test leaves ~11 GiB residual GPU memory. The next `test_deep_sleep_*` test tries to initialize with `gpu_memory_utilization=0.92` × 144 GiB = 132.48 GiB but only 132.47 GiB is free — failing by 10 MB.

**Fix:** New `gpu_memory_cleared` opt-in fixture in `conftest.py`. Only activates on `gfx950`, waits for GPU to drop below 8% usage. Tests that need clean state explicitly request it via parameter — **no overhead on other tests** (not `autouse`).

```python
# conftest.py
@pytest.fixture()
def gpu_memory_cleared():
    if current_platform.is_rocm() and "gfx950" in (current_platform.get_device_name() or ""):
        wait_for_gpu_memory_to_clear(devices=[0], threshold_ratio=0.08, timeout_s=30)
    yield

# test_mem.py — 4 tests opt in
def test_deep_sleep(gpu_memory_cleared): ...
def test_deep_sleep_lora(gpu_memory_cleared): ...
def test_deep_sleep_async(gpu_memory_cleared): ...
def test_deep_sleep_fp8_kvcache_mrv1(monkeypatch, gpu_memory_cleared): ...
```

Same fixture added to `tests/models/language/generation/conftest.py` for hybrid model tests (`mamba-130m` Engine OOM on MI355).

### 2. GPTQ kernel not compiled for gfx950 — `tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py`

**Problem:** The GPTQ kernel (exllama/marlin) is not compiled for gfx950. At model load time, `qweight` key is missing from `RowParallelLinear`, causing `ValueError`.

**Fix:** Skip `test_auto_gptq_quantization_method` on gfx950.

### 3. Tensorizer numerical mismatch — `tests/model_executor/.../test_tensorizer.py`

**Problem:** After tensorizer serialization/deserialization, `test_deserialized_encrypted_vllm_model_has_same_outputs` asserts exact output match. gfx950 produces a valid but lexically different output due to attention numerical precision differences from gfx942/NVIDIA.

**Fix:** `xfail(strict=False)` for gfx950 — test still runs and counts as expected failure.

## Test Plan

Validated by 400-job DPX stress test on MI355 cluster:

| Build | Failures | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Before any fix | 71 | GPU partition collisions + all the above |
| After infra fixes | 4 | Only pre-existing GPTQ + tensorizer |
| **After this PR** | **1** | Only unrelated GPTQ test file |

- [x] `tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py` — `test_deep_sleep_*` pass on gfx950 DPX
- [x] `tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py` — mamba-130m passes
- [x] `tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py` — GPTQ tests skipped on gfx950
- [x] `tests/model_executor/.../test_tensorizer.py` — marked xfail on gfx950
- [x] No regression on gfx942 (MI300X SPX) — all conditions gated on `"gfx950"`

title: support rl feature : weight checker
body:
## Purpose

In the RL training loop (`start_weight_update → update_weights* →
finish_weight_update`) the trainer pushes Actor weights into the rollout
inference engines. Before the loop starts we need to confirm that
`weight_checker` actually lands: that the update reached every engine, every
tensor, and was not corrupted or partially written. Otherwise a silent
weight-update failure turns into off-policy training.

`weight_checker` computes a **per-tensor SHA-256 checksum** of the model
weights, so a caller can save the pre-update digests, randomize the weights,
let the trainer transfer them back, and verify byte-for-byte that the result
matches what it started from.

RFC: #52689

## Design: three actions, no server-side state

One development endpoint, `POST /weight_checker`:

| Action | Request | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `checksum` | `{"action":"checksum"}` | `{"checksums": {name: hex_str}}` |
| `reset` | `{"action":"reset"}` | `{"status":"reset"}` |
| `compare` | `{"action":"compare","baseline":{name: hex_str}}` | `{"match": bool, "mismatches": [str]}` |

* `checksum` hashes every covered tensor (parameters plus persistent buffers)
  and returns the digests; it stores nothing.
* `reset` overwrites exactly the covered tensors with random values, in place,
  so that a later `compare` can prove the weights really changed.
* `compare` diffs the current digests against a **caller-supplied** baseline
  and returns `match` plus the fully rank-qualified names that differ.

**Why the baseline is not kept on the server.** `vllm serve` can run more than
one API server process behind one listening port (data parallelism with
`--api-server-count`, SO_REUSEPORT). Requests are dispatched by the kernel, so
the `checksum` that creates a baseline and the `compare` that follows a weight
transfer are very likely served by *different* processes. A process-local
baseline silently disappears and the verification turns into a false negative
(HTTP 400 / `baseline_created: true` again). Keeping the endpoint stateless
makes the check correct on every API process and removes the "one-shot
baseline / serialize concurrent clients" caveats. The caller already holds the
digests, because `checksum` returns them.

An earlier revision of this PR stored the baseline in `app.state` with a
`snapshot` action. That design is what reviewer feedback and the DP findings
below invalidated, so it has been removed; RFC #52689 is being updated to
match.

## Coverage

* Keys are rank-qualified —
  `dp{dp}:pp{pp}:pcp{pcp}:tp{tp}:ep{ep}:{tensor_name}` — so shards of the same
  logical weight cannot collide, and a duplicated key is rejected.
* A single request covers every engine that the frontend it reaches manages
  (each engine covers its own workers). The engine fan-out gathers over
  `core_engines`, so it is correct for both internal and external load
  balancing.
* In a multi-frontend deployment (`--data-parallel-external-lb` with more than
  one local engine per frontend) each frontend only knows its own engines, so
  checking the whole group requires sending the action to **every** API server
  and merging the results. The docs say this explicitly.

## Test Plan

`tests/entrypoints/serve/dev/rlhf/state_transitions/test_weight_checker.py`

| Test group | Covered | Priority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API (single engine, real small checkpoint) | `checksum` returns 64-hex digests and is stable across calls; `compare` without `baseline` is 400; `compare` reports changed and missing tensors; repeated `compare` with the same baseline keeps working; invalid/missing action is 400 while `/health` stays up; `reset` changes the weights and `reload_weights` restores them | P0 |
| TP2 / DP2 / EP | real checkpoint across TP=2, DP=2, EP; rank-qualified key inventory; `checksum → reset → reload → checksum` equality and a final `match: true` | P1 |

## Test Result

test tp use qwen3-0.6b，test ep use qwen3-30b

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Reserve encoder graph memory without decoder graphs
body:
## Purpose

While following up on the [MRV2 feedback on my earlier PR](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54905#issuecomment-5769718464), I revisited CUDA graph memory accounting in the V2 runner. This led me to a missing case similar to the encoder graph memory accounting I previously worked on in #41714, but in a different runner and configuration.

MRV2 can capture encoder CUDA graphs independently of decoder graphs. With `cudagraph_mm_encoder=True` and `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, the encoder still captures graphs, but the Worker skips graph memory profiling. The V2 profiler also returns early based on decoder-only checks. Consequently, automatic KV-cache sizing does not reserve memory for those encoder graphs.

This PR:

- Allows the Worker to profile MRV2 encoder graphs when decoder graphs are disabled, excluding `enforce_eager`.
- Uses the runner's existing encoder/decoder capture predicate in the V2 profiler. The pre-bootstrap decoder configuration check remains necessary because the decoder manager has not been initialized yet.
- Preserves MRV1 behavior: MRV1 does not perform encoder capture when decoder graph mode is `NONE`, so it should not reserve memory for that case.
- Adds regression coverage for KV-budget subtraction, an uninitialized decoder manager, encoder capture without decoder descriptors, and cleanup on capture failure.

No kernels, capture sizes, batch-size limits, pool-sharing policy, or memory-estimation formulas are changed. This concerns normal multimodal generation, not the separate `--mm-encoder-only` deployment mode.

## Related Work / Duplicate Check

I checked #49224 and its comments, open PR references to that issue, and open/merged PRs for encoder graph memory, `cudagraph_mode=NONE`, and MRV2 profiling.

- #53306 introduced the existing MRV2 graph profiler and closed #49224. This fixes a remaining eligibility case; it does not reimplement that profiler or claim to fix the original issue in full.
- #57865 changes retained-workspace/released-graph accounting. At `12b5ceefaf7f`, both its Worker and V2 profiler still skip profiling for decoder `NONE`.
- #51590 changes MRV1 capture-footprint measurement. At `5d28d0504e9b`, its Worker still requires decoder graphs to be enabled.
- #54061 adds capture tracing, not this memory-reservation fix.
- #56922 enables graphs for the separate encoder-only runner, not this regular MRV2 KV-budgeting path.

The first two open accounting PRs overlap files with this change, but address different failures. This PR deliberately leaves their accounting-policy changes out of scope.

## Test Plan

Validation used a fresh Python 3.12 environment and a standard editable installation with the official CUDA 13.0 wheel for the exact main-base commit `a6c47fbbf4187e8ae5396ebdcf93234db617a4ad`. Both baseline and fixed sources used the same dependencies and CUDA binaries. All 18 installed extension files matched that wheel by SHA256; loaded-library paths were also checked. There are no C++/CUDA changes in this PR.

The focused suites were run both through the environment-verification wrapper and directly with pytest. The direct command, with temporary/cache directories configured outside the repository, was:

```bash
../encoder-cg-matched-20260922/.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_worker.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_encoder_cudagraph.py -q \
  --basetemp=../encoder-cg-matched-20260922/pytest-direct \
  --junitxml=../encoder-cg-matched-20260922/pytest-direct.xml
```

The regression subset was also run against an unmodified main worktree using the final tests and `--import-mode=importlib`.

Model checks use NVIDIA B200, BF16, TP=1, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, and the actual Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct weights at revision `66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3`. Configuration: `max_model_len=2048`, `max_num_seqs=2`, `max_num_batched_tokens=1024`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.12`, prefix caching disabled, FLASHINFER encoder attention, and one image/no video per prompt.

The model harness observes the real profiling/capture returns, KV budget, temporary-pool release, production recapture/replay, and generated token IDs. A separate check runs the repository's `vllm bench throughput` with actual multimodal requests, rather than a synthetic kernel timing loop.

<details>
<summary>Multimodal benchmark configuration</summary>

The local invocation uses a read-only wrapper that asserts one image per request before calling the unchanged benchmark CLI. Its standard-install equivalent is:

```bash
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 \
  .venv/bin/vllm bench throughput \
  --backend vllm-chat --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct \
  --revision 66285546d2b821cf421d4f5eb2576359d3770cd3 \
  --dtype bfloat16 --seed 0 \
  --dataset-name random-mm --enable-multimodal-chat \
  --dataset-path synthetic-random-mm \
  --num-prompts 32 --num-warmups 4 \
  --random-input-len 32 --random-output-len 16 --random-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-base-items-per-request 1 \
  --random-mm-num-mm-items-range-ratio 0 \
  --random-mm-limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --random-mm-bucket-config '{(224,224,1):0.5,(448,448,1):0.5}' \
  --max-model-len 2048 --max-num-seqs 2 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.12 --no-enable-prefix-caching \
  --mm-processor-cache-gb 0 --mm-encoder-attn-backend FLASHINFER \
  --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image":1,"video":0}' \
  --mm-processor-kwargs '{"min_pixels":3136,"max_pixels":200704}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"NONE","cudagraph_mm_encoder":true,"encoder_cudagraph_token_budgets":[512,1024,2048],"encoder_cudagraph_max_vision_items_per_batch":2}'
```

The nonempty synthetic dataset-path marker avoids the current CLI fallback to text-only `random`; the random multimodal dataset does not read that path. The local run uses the pinned downloaded snapshot instead of fetching weights.

</details>

## Test Result

Tested base: `a6c47fbbf4187e8ae5396ebdcf93234db617a4ad`.
Tested PR head: `7ac8ba13be40e48b81984a73fcfd217f2102d52e`.

- Focused CPU/GPU suites: **92 passed**, including real graph allocation/capture/replay tests.
- Unmodified submission-base negative control: **4 failed, 14 passed** in the selected subset. The four failures are the Worker admission, the two V2 profiler admission cases, and the previously skipped encoder capture-error path. All pass with the fix.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and the manual Python 3.12 mypy check passed.
- `uv pip check`: all 228 installed packages are compatible.

Tested-base real-model checks:

| Configuration | Graph reservation | Production capture increment | Replay / outputs |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Unmodified base, encoder ON / decoder NONE, budget 1024 | 0 MiB | 262 MiB | 2 graph hits |
| Fixed, same graph configuration | 260 MiB | 258 MiB | 2 hits, tokens identical to base |
| Fixed, budgets 512/1024/2048, max vision items 2 | 534 MiB | 530 MiB | 4 hits, including a concurrent pair; tokens identical to base |

Both fixed runs released their temporary encoder profiling pools completely before production recapture and had zero replay misses. In each run, the KV budget equals requested memory minus the observed forward-profile non-KV footprint minus the graph reservation. In the matched-environment single-budget comparison, the forward-profile footprint was identical: KV budget changed from 14,439,960,146 to 14,167,330,386 bytes, exactly the 260 MiB reservation.

The full nine-configuration model matrix was rerun on this submission revision and matched wheel:

| Fixed configuration | Applied graph reservation | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Encoder ON, decoder NONE, compilation enabled | 260 MiB | Pass |
| Encoder ON, decoder NONE, compilation disabled | 228 MiB | Pass |
| Both graph types disabled, compilation enabled | 0 MiB | Pass |
| Both graph types disabled, compilation disabled | 0 MiB | Pass |
| Encoder and decoder graphs enabled | 708 MiB | Pass |
| Decoder graphs only | 448 MiB | Pass |
| Encoder ON, reservation opt-out | 0 MiB (260 MiB measured) | Pass |
| Eager | 0 MiB | Pass |
| Encoder budgets 512/1024/2048, max vision items 2 | 534 MiB | Pass |

All generated smoke-test token IDs matched the baseline, including the concurrent pair. Temporary encoder pools were released in every profiled configuration, and every enabled encoder graph run had zero replay misses.

The matched-environment multimodal benchmark completed four warmup and 32 measured image requests per run, with concurrency capped at two. Both runs processed 5,856 prompt tokens and generated 512 output tokens. The wrapper confirmed that every request actually contained one image.

| Source | Elapsed | Requests/s | Output tokens/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Unmodified submission base | 4.0719 s | 7.8588 | 125.74 |
| Fixed | 3.8608 s | 8.2884 | 132.62 |

Both CLI runs exited successfully and emitted the same NCCL process-group shutdown warning at exit. These are single short runs checking successful multimodal processing, not evidence of a statistically significant speedup or performance equivalence. This PR fixes a demonstrated memory-reservation omission, not a reproduced OOM or throughput bottleneck.

AI assistance was used for implementation, validation, and drafting.

title: [Bugfix][MiMo] Fix ViT attention-sink semantics and omni wrapper packed_modules_mapping
body:
## Purpose

Two fixes in `mimo_v2_omni.py`:

**1. ViT attention sink (`sinks_bias_key0=True` → `False`).** #49815 wired the learned vision sinks into the window-attention path. It chose the key-0 form to match the released HF `modeling_mimo_v2.py`, which adds `sinks[h]` to the logit of each sequence's first key. MiMo-V2.6's technical report (§2.2) describes *sink-augmented* SWA and cites a formulation where the sink is an extra logit that only enlarges the softmax denominator. Xiaomi's own SGLang integration runs the ViT on FA3 with `sinks=s_aux`, which is that denominator form.

The key-0 form is a no-op on uniform inputs, because every key and value is identical. So all patch tokens of a flat-colour image come out identical, and the image is misread. With MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL, a solid green 448×448 PNG gives "a close-up of a person's eye" on current main, versus "a solid, uniform green square" from Xiaomi's hosted API. The denominator form is already supported by `context_attention_fwd` via `sinks_bias_key0=False`.

**2. `packed_modules_mapping` on `MiMoV2OmniForCausalLM`.** `SupportsQuant` sets up quantization on the omni wrapper, which declares no `packed_modules_mapping`. The inner `MiMoV2FlashForCausalLM` mapping is therefore never used when resolving `ignored_layers`. A checkpoint that dequantizes a dense MLP to BF16 and lists `gate_proj`/`up_proj` in `ignored_layers` still gets `Fp8LinearMethod` on the fused `gate_up_proj`. Its BF16 weights are then loaded without scales, and the model emits NaN on every request. Stock MiMo is unaffected, since its layer-0 MLP is FP8 and not ignored. The wrapper now carries the inner model's mapping.

## Not a duplicate

Searched open PRs and issues (`gh pr list --state open --search "mimo sink"`, `"mimo_v2_omni"`; `gh search issues "mimo sink"`). The only related open work is #57804/#57795/#57806, which route the *language-model* attention-sink bias in `mimo_v2.py` through `weight_loader` for RL weight reload. They do not touch the ViT sink semantics or the omni wrapper's `packed_modules_mapping`, and this PR does not touch `mimo_v2.py`.

## Test Plan

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed file: clean.
- Served MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL (TP8) and MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL (TP4) on the `vllm/vllm-openai:mimo-v26` image, with and without this change mounted over `mimo_v2_omni.py`. Sent the same OpenAI chat requests to both (synthetic 448×448 PNGs, a COCO photo, OCR and diagram images, text), `temperature` 0 and 1, and compared against Xiaomi's hosted API via OpenRouter.
- Ran Xiaomi's HF `modeling_mimo_v2.py` on the same weights and inputs with both sink forms.
- Fix 2: served a MiMo-V2.6-Pro checkpoint with experts, `qkv_proj` and layer-0 MLP dequantized to BF16 (listed in `ignored_layers`), with and without this change; checked the load log for `Fp8LinearMethod` and requested logprobs.

## Test Results

Same weights, pixels and prompts, B300, TP8 for Pro and TP4 for Flash, `temperature=0`:

| input | main | this PR | Xiaomi API |
|---|---|---|---|
| solid green | "close-up of a person's eye" | "I see a solid, uniform green square." | "a solid, uniform green square" |
| solid white | "close-up of a person's face" | "The image is completely blank and white." | "completely blank and white" |
| left white / right black | "left: black, right: white" | "left: white, right: black" | same |
| photo, two cats on a pink couch | correct | correct, identical wording to API | — |

Also checked with no regressions and small gains: OCR ("Invoice #4827 Total: $1,309.55"), arrow direction, colour grids, and 8-colour stripes, where main drops cyan. The HF reference code reproduces main's outputs exactly with the key-0 sink, and the fixed outputs with the denominator sink.

Fix 2: a BF16-dequantized MiMo-V2.6-Pro hybrid returns NaN logits on main (`17*23` with logprobs → HTTP 400 "Out of range float values: nan"), and `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel` is selected despite no FP8 active weights. With this PR, no `Fp8LinearMethod` remains and it answers "391" with finite logprobs.

Related: #49815, which introduced the key-0 form.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Claude): the investigation, the A/B runs and the change were done by AI agents under my direction. I reviewed every changed line and the evidence above, and I can answer questions about the change.

title: [PCP][DCP] Enable PCP+DCP on sparse-MLA models
body:
## Purpose

Enable DCP to run alongside PCP on sparse-MLA models, so a deployment can shard the KV cache for decode and still split prefill query work across ranks.

This change:

- gives the sparse indexer a DCP-gathered prefill path: this rank's KV shard is all-gathered across the DCP group
- gives the FlashMLA-sparse backend the matching prefill path, with a rank-major gathered KV workspace and a PCP-invariant chunk plan every rank derives identically without communicating;
- replicates prefills too short to fill all `2*PCP` chunks when DCP is on, which keeps the per-region row count identical on every rank — the invariant the gathered layout rests on;
- adds a MoE all-reduce fast path for steps whose rows are all PCP-replicated, replacing an unconditional all-gather + reduce-scatter that duplicated every decode row `PCP` times;
- relaxes the PCP CUDA graph restriction for PCP+DCP to everything up to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, keeping only `FULL` over mixed batches rejected;

fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53573
Additionally
- fixes a pre-existing kernel/reference divergence: the top-k index kernel applied the block-table bound to prefill-workspace rows, while `_triton_convert_reference_impl` has always specified that only `-1` is invalid there. The existing test missed it because `token_indices[6, 150:160]` is an empty slice on a 128-column tensor;

## Test Plan

- NVIDIA GB200 x4
- GLM-5.3, NVFP4 weights
- TP=1, PCP=4, DCP=4

## Test Result

GSM8K, 1319 questions, TP1+PCP4+DCP4, `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`. Seven runs across the

| Run | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 0.830 | 0.000 |
| PCP4DCP4| 0.832 | 0.000 |


## Benchmarks

Prefill, 32768 in / 1 out:

| Layout | TTFT ms | P99 TTFT ms | vs tp4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| tp4 | 5512.1 | 8141.1 | 1.00x |
| pcp4 | 3278.1 | 4814.0 | 1.68x |
| pcp4dcp4 | 3326.8 | 4888.7 | 1.66x |

Decode, 1 in / 1024 out:

| Layout | TPOT ms | out tok/s | vs tp4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| tp4 | 18.6 | 3412.7 | 1.00x |
| dcp4 | 28.4 | 2236.8 | 0.66x |
| pcp4dcp4, PIECEWISE (this PR) | 86.7 | 735.9 | 0.22x |
| pcp4dcp4, with FULL decode graphs and moe deduplication   https://github.com/PatrykSaffer/vllm/compare/patryk/pcp-dcp-sparse-mla...patryk/pcp-dcp-full-cg-no-duplication | 32.6 | 1944.1 | 0.57x |



Why pcp4dcp4 decode is slower than dcp4 decode:
CudaCommunicator.__init__ enables custom all-reduce, torch symm-mem and FlashInfer fused all-reduce for tp groups only, so that per-layer all-reduce runs on NCCL ring.
followup is to enable it, sth like https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56157/changes/590e9b7e185df741e5aabbecfed351dd3470c04f

title: [Bugfix][Quantization] Do not select DeepGEMM with float32 scales on SM12x
body:
Fixes #57486. Reported and diagnosed by @ivanusto, who also found the MoE half and handed the patch
over.

## Problem

The 120 family has no working float32-scale path — its DeepGEMM kernels read packed UE8M0 scales.
With `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=0` the oracle resolves to `FLOAT32`, and vLLM still selects DeepGEMM:

- **linear**: `should_use_deepgemm_for_fp8_linear()` considers only dtype and N/K multiples.
- **MoE**: `_valid_deep_gemm()` never consults the format. `DeepGemmExperts` does read the oracle,
  but only to compute `use_ue8m0 = scale_fmt == FLOAT32_CEIL_UE8M0`, so on SM12x with E8M0 off it
  resolves False and float32 scales still reach the grouped kernels.

Per #57486, that yields NaNs on DeepGEMM `ad1f1726` (up to 22% of outputs) and a hard `RuntimeError`
since `a6bbb80`.

## Fix

One predicate, consulted by both selection sites. On the 120 family, DeepGEMM is only selected when
the resolved format is not `FLOAT32`; every other family is untouched.

**The oracle is deliberately left alone.** `DeepGemmQuantScaleFMT.from_oracle()` also drives scale
*layout* for non-DeepGEMM consumers — `QuantFP8` (`input_quant_fp8.py:67`) and four sites in
`fp8_utils.py` — and `FLOAT32` is the correct answer for them, including when DeepGEMM is simply
absent. Making the oracle return UE8M0 on SM12x would fix selection by mis-describing layout
elsewhere, so this gates at selection time instead.

## Verification

GB10 (sm_121, cc 12.1, driver 580.95.05, CUDA 13.0), `main` at `bf13ecc2f7`:

```
E8M0=1  oracle=UE8M0    scale_fmt_ok=True   linear_gate=True    <- unchanged, DeepGEMM still used
E8M0=0  oracle=FLOAT32  scale_fmt_ok=False  linear_gate=False   <- was True; kernel no longer reached
```

Family isolation, oracle forced to `FLOAT32`:

```
family 90  -> True    family 100 -> True    family 120 -> False
```

so Hopper's `FLOAT32_CEIL_UE8M0` path and the 100 family keep their current behaviour.

ruff (repo-pinned 0.14.0) and mypy clean.

## Scope

I verified the *selection* change on hardware. @ivanusto then ran the branch end-to-end on GB10
with DeepGEMM built from the fork at the `a6bbb80` pin: E8M0 on is `torch.equal` with main across
five shapes, and E8M0 off no longer reaches the kernel from either selection site. That run also
turned up a third site — the grouped-GEMM warmup calls
`m_grouped_fp8_gemm_nt_contiguous` directly, so `_valid_deep_gemm()`'s check never applied to it and
startup still failed after dispatch had already moved to Triton. Fixed here; the scale format is now
checked in `_fused_moe_grouped_gemm_may_use_deep_gemm` as well.

Tests are in `tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py`: the device-family matrix for the
shared gate, and one asserting the warmup predicate consults it before touching the module.

## Out of scope

Two more consumers take the FLOAT32 oracle to sm120 kernels that only accept int scales at
`a6bbb80`, both found by reading rather than running (@ivanusto's note):

- `BatchedDeepGemmExperts` — `_supports_current_device()` is just `is_deep_gemm_supported()`, and it
  feeds `fp8_m_grouped_gemm_nt_masked`, whose sm120 branch requires `kInt` scales. Only reachable
  with a batched activation format such as DeepEP low latency.
- `DeepGemmFP4Experts` — listed for family 120 and derives `use_ue8m0` from the scale format, so it
  sends float32 activation scales with E8M0 off.

Neither of us can exercise those configurations, so they're named rather than patched.

title: [Bugfix][MRV2][Spec Decode] Honor dynamic K in autoregressive speculators, 1.2~1.3x kernel perf improvement
body:
## Purpose

MRV2 did not propagate `SchedulerOutput.num_spec_tokens_to_schedule` to autoregressive speculators, causing unnecessary draft forwards and stale draft tokens.

This PR fixes the issue

## Test

Acc covered in current unit test

Perf can be seen in this AI generated script

```py
from functools import partial
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch
import triton

from vllm.v1.spec_decode.dynamic.utils import build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch import InputBatch, InputBuffers
from vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.autoregressive.speculator import (
    AutoRegressiveSpeculator,
)

MAX_K = 5
MAX_BATCH_SIZE = 48
HIDDEN_SIZE = 4096
NUM_REQS = (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 48)
DYNAMIC_K_SCHEDULE = [(1, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, 3)]


class SyntheticSpeculator(AutoRegressiveSpeculator):
    """MRV2 proposer whose model forward is replaced by a matmul."""

    def load_draft_model(self, target_model, target_attn_layer_names):
        raise NotImplementedError("This benchmark does not load a model")

    def __init__(self, device: torch.device) -> None:
        # Deliberately skip the real constructor: it allocates model-related state.
        self.num_speculative_steps = MAX_K
        self.max_num_reqs = MAX_BATCH_SIZE
        self.max_model_len = 8192
        self.dp_size = 1
        self.dp_rank = 0
        self.pcp_manager = None
        self.eplb_state = None
        self.use_fused_multi_step_decode = True
        self.prefill_cudagraph_manager = None
        self.decode_cudagraph_manager = None
        self.speculative_config = SimpleNamespace(
            uses_dynamic_speculative_decoding=lambda: True,
        )

        self.input_buffers = InputBuffers(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device)
        self.hidden_states = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.last_token_indices = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )
        self.current_draft_step = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
        self.sample_src_positions = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )
        self.idx_mapping = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
        self.temperature = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device=device)
        self.seeds = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
        self.draft_tokens = torch.zeros(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_K, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
        )

        self.weight = torch.randn(
            HIDDEN_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.src = torch.randn(
            MAX_BATCH_SIZE, HIDDEN_SIZE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device
        )
        self.dst = torch.empty_like(self.src)
        self.count_steps = False
        self.steps = 0

    def _synthetic_forward(self, num_tokens: int) -> None:
        torch.mm(self.src[:num_tokens], self.weight, out=self.dst[:num_tokens])
        self.src, self.dst = self.dst, self.src
        if self.count_steps:
            self.steps += 1

    def _prefill(self, num_reqs: int, num_tokens: int, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        self._synthetic_forward(num_tokens)
        self.draft_tokens[:num_reqs, 0].zero_()

    def _generate_draft(
        self, num_reqs: int, num_tokens_padded: int, *args, **kwargs
    ) -> None:
        self._synthetic_forward(num_tokens_padded)


def count_forwards(speculator: SyntheticSpeculator, run) -> int:
    speculator.steps = 0
    speculator.count_steps = True
    run()
    speculator.count_steps = False
    return speculator.steps


def main() -> None:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("CUDA is required")

    device = torch.device("cuda")
    speculator = SyntheticSpeculator(device)
    target_buffers = InputBuffers(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device)
    target_hidden_states = torch.randn_like(speculator.hidden_states)
    temperature = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, device=device)
    seeds = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    last_sampled = torch.zeros(MAX_BATCH_SIZE, dtype=torch.int64, device=device)
    dense_schedule = build_dynamic_sd_schedule_lookup(
        DYNAMIC_K_SCHEDULE,
        vllm_max_batch_size=MAX_BATCH_SIZE,
        vllm_num_speculative_tokens=MAX_K,
    )

    print("batch  sched_k  buggy_ms  fixed_ms  speedup  forwards(buggy->fixed)")
    for num_reqs in NUM_REQS:
        batch = InputBatch.make_dummy(num_reqs, num_reqs, target_buffers)
        common_args = dict(
            input_batch=batch,
            attn_metadata={},
            slot_mappings={},
            last_hidden_states=target_hidden_states[:num_reqs],
            aux_hidden_states=None,
            num_sampled=torch.ones(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
            num_rejected=torch.zeros(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
            last_sampled=last_sampled,
            next_prefill_tokens=target_buffers.input_ids,
            temperature=temperature,
            seeds=seeds,
            dummy_run=True,
            skip_attn_for_dummy_run=True,
            is_profile=True,
        )
        dynamic_k = dense_schedule[num_reqs]

        # Buggy: model_runner omitted runtime K, so propose() used max K=5.
        buggy = partial(speculator.propose, **common_args)
        # Fixed: model_runner passes the scheduler-selected runtime K=3.
        fixed = partial(
            speculator.propose,
            **common_args,
            num_speculative_tokens=dynamic_k,
        )

        buggy_steps = count_forwards(speculator, buggy)
        fixed_steps = count_forwards(speculator, fixed)
        assert dynamic_k == 3
        assert buggy_steps == MAX_K
        assert fixed_steps == dynamic_k

        buggy_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(buggy)
        fixed_ms = triton.testing.do_bench(fixed)
        print(
            f"{num_reqs:>5}  {dynamic_k:>7}  {buggy_ms:>8.3f}  "
            f"{fixed_ms:>8.3f}  {buggy_ms / fixed_ms:>7.3f}x  "
            f"{buggy_steps}->{fixed_steps}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

And we can get

```bash
batch  sched_k  buggy_ms  fixed_ms  speedup  forwards(buggy->fixed)
    1        3     0.151     0.115    1.306x  5->3
    2        3     0.148     0.115    1.286x  5->3
    4        3     0.149     0.115    1.298x  5->3
    8        3     0.148     0.115    1.282x  5->3
   16        3     0.151     0.115    1.315x  5->3
   32        3     0.150     0.114    1.306x  5->3
   48        3     0.149     0.115    1.287x  5->3
```
